## Codebase Patterns
- Missing authorization scope is a request-shape error, not a normal denial: `policy.Decide` returns `ReasonDeniedScopeRequired` for non-self actions whose `policy.Resource.Scope.OrganizationID` is empty, and `policy.Authorize` maps that to typed `apierr.ScopeRequired()` / `E_SCOPE_REQUIRED` (HTTP 400). Route resolvers should still provide explicit organization scope; this path catches missing path/query scope and resolver wiring mistakes before they collapse into misleading cross-tenant `E_FORBIDDEN`.
- Error-contract stories are a coordinated public-contract change: add the stable code in `internal/errors` (constant, `codeDescriptions`, `AllCodes`, `ExitCode`), add the backend taxonomy entry and typed constructor in `internal/controlplane/apierr`, add the deterministic HTTP mapping in `internal/controlplane/apienvelope.StatusForCode`, and pin all three with tests plus an envelope redaction/docs-link assertion. Do not surface these codes through ad hoc string literals.
- Auth error-contract split (BE-0514/BE-0513 pattern): missing/no-usable authentication material maps to `401 E_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` through `apierr.AuthenticationRequired()`; supplied-but-rejected credentials from `auth.ErrInvalidCredentials` map to `401 E_AUTH_INVALID` through `apierr.AuthInvalid()` with the fixed public message "the supplied credentials are invalid". Legacy typed `apierr.Unauthenticated(...)` still renders `E_AUTH` for older internal call sites, but new middleware invalid-token paths should assert `E_AUTH_INVALID`.
- Admin unpathed mutation endpoints that target a tenant selected by request data should expose `organization_id` in the query string so `RequireAuth` authorizes the real target before the handler reads the body. The body may repeat `organization_id` for typed clients but must match the query target; body-only cross-tenant targets are validation failures. Store-backed admin job starters should verify the target organization, insert the durable job, and append the allowed audit event in one `Store.Write` transaction so no import/reconcile job exists without its audit trail.
- HTTP response collection fields should stay shape-stable for agents: render empty lists as `[]`, not `null`. Normalize nil slices at the projection chokepoint before calling `apienvelope.WriteData`; BE-0287 pins this for `POST /v1/admin/dokploy/reconcile` `data.failures`.
- Auth error-contract split (BE-0513 pattern): missing/no-usable authentication material maps to `401 E_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` through `apierr.AuthenticationRequired()` with the fixed public message "authentication is required", no hint, and the standard docs URL. `httpapi.writeAuthError` is the chokepoint: `auth.ErrNoCredentials` takes the required-auth branch, `auth.ErrInvalidCredentials` takes the invalid-auth branch, and dependency errors pass through typed. Update tests based on the credential condition, not just the test name "unauthenticated".
- Preview environment state-machine stories use the same audited transition shape as the other resource state machines: `preview_environments.status` has the lifecycle table `pending -> provisioning/deleting/failed`, `provisioning -> ready/deleting/failed`, `ready -> deleting/failed`, `deleting -> deleted/failed`, `failed -> provisioning/deleting`, and `deleted -> terminal`; `PreviewEnvironmentRepository.Transition` locks the tenant-scoped `(organization_id, project_id, id)` row, rejects invalid edges with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` before any write, updates `status` plus `deletion_scheduled_at` when entering `deleting`, and appends a redacted `preview_environment_events` row with actor/request/previous/next/reason metadata in the same transaction. The legacy `ScheduleDeletion` helper also routes through `Transition` so it cannot bypass the lifecycle timeline.
- Quota reservation state-machine stories use a pure `ReservationStatus.CanTransitionTo` table plus an atomic repository `Transition` method: lock the tenant-scoped reservation row, reject impossible edges with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` before any write, update `quota_reservations.status` and `settled_at`, and append the matching `quota_reservation_events` row in the same transaction with actor/request/previous/next/reason metadata. Redact free-text reason text before persisting event message/metadata.
- Admin Dokploy reconcile mutation endpoints (BE-0286 pattern, POST `/v1/admin/dokploy/reconcile`) stay org-rooted for policy: `organization_id` is taken from the query parameter or defaults to the principal home org so `RequireAuth` authorizes `admin.reconcile` against the real target before the handler runs. The JSON body may repeat `organization_id` for typed clients, but it must match the query target; cross-tenant body-only targets are rejected before the runner port is called. Add the runner as a route-option dependency to avoid sweeping every existing `NewHandler` test call site.
- Admin Dokploy drift list endpoints (BE-0283 pattern, GET `/v1/admin/dokploy/drift`) use an unpathed admin route with query-scoped targeting: `organization_id` defaults to the principal home org, while optional `project_id`, `environment_id`, `service_id`, `status`, and `limit` filters are mirrored into `policy.Scope` by the resolver before `admin.reconcile` authorization. The handler validates hierarchy shape (`environment_id` requires `project_id`; `service_id` requires both project and environment) before store access. The store-backed `DriftFindingReader` verifies the target organization and any supplied parent resources tenant-scoped, then delegates to `DriftFindingRepository.List` whose SQL uses constant optional predicates so caller input never alters the statement shape.
- Drift finding state-machine stories use an explicit `drift_findings.status` lifecycle (`open -> resolved`, with `resolved` terminal) in addition to the existing `resolved_at` / `resolved_by_actor_id` stamps. `DriftFindingRepository.Transition` locks the tenant-scoped row, rejects invalid edges with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` before any write, updates the resolution columns for terminal resolution, and appends a redacted `drift_finding_events` row with actor/request/previous/next/reason metadata in the same transaction. The legacy `MarkResolved` helper also writes the lifecycle event so it cannot bypass the timeline.
- Bare-id job retry endpoints (BE-0277 pattern, POST `/v1/jobs/{job_id}/retry`) reuse `jobIDResolver` so policy is evaluated against the persisted job's owning scope before the mutating handler runs. The store-backed retry path leaves terminal source rows immutable and inserts a fresh queued clone for `failed`, `cancelled`, or `dead_letter` sources only; it scopes the caller's `idempotency_key` as `retry:<source_job_id>:<caller_key>`, copies non-secret payload refs, adds `retried_job_id` / `retry_requested_by`, appends a redacted `job.retry` audit event in the same transaction, and returns the queued retry job with `202 Accepted`. `succeeded`, `queued`, `running`, and `retrying` sources are stable conflicts; cross-tenant/unknown source ids remain tenant-scoped `E_NOT_FOUND`.
- Bare-id job cancel endpoints (BE-0280 pattern, POST `/v1/jobs/{job_id}/cancel`) reuse `jobIDResolver` so action `job.cancel` is authorized against the persisted job's owning scope before mutation. The store-backed cancel path calls `JobRepository.Transition(..., JobStatusCancelled, ...)` inside `Store.Write`, so queued/running/retrying jobs follow the shared state-machine bookkeeping, terminal jobs fail with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION`, and cross-tenant/unknown ids remain tenant-scoped `E_NOT_FOUND`. Append the redacted `job.cancel` audit event in the same transaction as the lifecycle event and return the cancelled source row with `202 Accepted`.
- Break-glass session state-machine stories use explicit `break_glass_sessions.status` plus the existing time/revocation stamps: `active -> revoked|expired`, with `revoked` and `expired` terminal. `BreakGlassRepository.Transition` locks the tenant-scoped session row, rejects invalid edges with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` before any write, updates status/revocation columns, and appends a redacted `break_glass_session_events` row with actor/request/previous/next/reason metadata in the same transaction. Customer-facing revoke routes through this transition path while preserving the existing public conflict response for duplicate revocation attempts.
- API key state-machine stories use explicit `api_keys.status` plus the existing lifecycle stamps: `active -> revoked|expired`, with `revoked` and `expired` terminal. `APIKeyRepository.Transition` locks the tenant-scoped key row, rejects invalid edges with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` before any write, updates status, stamps `revoked_at` for revoked transitions, and appends a redacted `api_key_events` row with actor/request/previous/next/reason metadata in the same transaction. Customer-facing revoke should call the transition path before appending its separate audit event so lifecycle timeline and audit timeline commit atomically.
- Project state-machine stories use the same audited transition shape as environment/service state machines: `projects.status` has the lifecycle table `pending -> active/deleting`, `active -> suspended/deleting`, `suspended -> active/deleting`, `deleting -> active/deleted`, `deleted -> terminal`; `ProjectRepository.Transition` locks the tenant-scoped project row, rejects invalid edges with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` before any write, updates status, and appends a redacted `project_events` row with actor/request/previous/next/reason metadata in the same transaction.
- Bare-id job read endpoints (BE-0274 pattern, GET `/v1/jobs/{job_id}`) should authorize against the persisted job row's owning scope, not an org-root placeholder: the resolver reloads the tenant-scoped job through `store.JobReader.GetJob`, mirrors `ProjectID` / `EnvironmentID` / `ServiceID` into `policy.Scope`, then the handler performs the same tenant-scoped read for the response. This preserves project/environment/service-scoped grant containment while unknown or cross-tenant ids still collapse to the repository's `E_NOT_FOUND` path.
- Job list endpoints (BE-0271 pattern, GET `/v1/jobs`) use an organization-root route with optional query filters `(project_id, environment_id, service_id, status, limit)`: `jobListResolver` mirrors supplied filters into `policy.Scope` before auth, the handler validates hierarchy shape before store access (`environment_id` requires `project_id`, `service_id` requires both), and `store.JobReader` verifies filtered parents tenant-scoped before delegating to `JobRepository.List` with a constant SQL statement whose optional predicates never interpolate caller input.
- Environment state-machine stories use a pure `EnvironmentStatus.CanTransitionTo` table plus an atomic repository `Transition` method: lock the tenant-scoped environment row, reject impossible edges with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` before any write, update `environments.status`, and append the matching `environment_events` row in the same transaction with actor/request/previous/next/reason metadata. Redact free-text reason text before persisting event message/metadata.
- Service state-machine stories use a pure `ServiceStatus.CanTransitionTo` table plus an atomic repository `Transition` method: lock the tenant-scoped service row, reject impossible edges with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` before any write, update `services.status`, and append the matching `service_events` row in the same transaction with actor/request/previous/next/reason metadata. Redact free-text reason text before persisting event message/metadata.
- Preview delete endpoints (BE-0268 pattern, DELETE `/v1/projects/{project_id}/previews/{preview_id}`) should stay parent-project scoped: route through `projectIDResolver` with action `preview.delete`, handler forwards principal org + path project/preview ids plus optional `If-Match`, store service verifies the tenant-scoped parent project and preview row before side effects, rejects stale/already-scheduled state, calls `PreviewEnvironmentRepository.ScheduleDeletion`, enqueues `delete_preview_environment`, and appends a redaction-safe `preview.delete` audit event in the same transaction. Return `202 Accepted` with the scheduled preview snapshot and ETag because teardown is durable but worker-driven.
- Provisioning job state-machine stories use a pure `JobStatus.CanTransitionTo` table plus an atomic repository `Transition` method: lock the tenant-scoped job row, reject impossible edges with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` before any write, derive lease/attempt/timestamp bookkeeping from the target status, and append the matching `provisioning_job_events` row in the same transaction with actor/request/previous/next/reason metadata. Redact free-text reason/error summaries before persisting event message/metadata.
- Deployment state-machine stories use a pure `DeploymentStatus.CanTransitionTo` table plus an atomic repository `Transition` method: lock the tenant-scoped deployment row, reject impossible edges with `E_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` before any write, update lifecycle timestamps/error fields, and append the matching `deployment_events` row in the same transaction with actor/request/previous/next/reason metadata. Redact free-text reason/error summaries before persisting event message/metadata.
- Worker Dokploy import jobs (BE-0502 pattern for `import_dokploy_resource`) are organization-scoped only and use a typed payload `(organization_id, yalla_organization_id, dokploy_organization_id[, assignment_dokploy_org_id])`. The worker reloads the Yalla organization from Postgres, rejects stale desired versions before scanning Dokploy, then delegates classification/apply to `migrateimport.Importer` through a store-backed repository adapter. Each imported project/environment/service row and its `dokploy_refs` mapping are inserted in the same transaction, so replay after partial success classifies existing refs as `skip_already_imported` and creates only missing descendants. Scanner/Dokploy failures stay retryable unless cancellation interrupted the context; malformed/cross-tenant/stale desired state is `worker.Terminal`.
- Worker service reconciliation jobs (BE-0501 pattern for `reconcile_service`) use one service-scoped payload `(organization_id, project_id, environment_id, service_id[, engine])`, reload the service and all dependent desired state through tenant-scoped repositories, verify payload scope plus `DesiredVersion`, reject deletion-scheduled services, resolve the parent environment `dokploy_refs` row, call typed Dokploy `EnsureService`, persist the service ref idempotently, render effective variables through the variables resolver, call typed `SyncVariables`, then ensure each desired `service_domain` with idempotent per-domain refs. A job already marked `succeeded` is a no-op; retryable upstream errors stay plain so the durable queue can persist a redacted `error_summary`.
- Worker preview teardown jobs (BE-0500 pattern for `delete_preview_environment`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed scoped payload `(organization_id, project_id, environment_id, preview_id)`, load the `preview_environments` wrapper and wrapped `environments.kind=preview` clone through tenant-scoped repositories, verify payload scope and preview-row `DesiredVersion`, resolve the clone's `environment` `dokploy_refs` row, call the typed Dokploy `RemoveEnvironment` intent only when an upstream mapping exists, then delete the mapping and hard-delete the preview wrapper in one transaction. A job already marked `succeeded` is a no-op; a replay after cleanup treats a missing preview wrapper as success and does not issue another Dokploy call. Retryable upstream errors stay plain so the durable queue can persist a redacted `error_summary`; stale/cross-tenant/malformed desired state is `worker.Terminal`.
- Worker preview create jobs (BE-0499 pattern for `create_preview_environment`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed scoped payload `(organization_id, project_id, environment_id, preview_id)`, load the `preview_environments` wrapper and wrapped `environments.kind=preview` row through tenant-scoped repositories, verify payload scope and preview-row `DesiredVersion`, reject deletion-scheduled previews before any Dokploy call, resolve the parent project Dokploy ref, call the typed Dokploy `EnsureEnvironment` intent for the wrapped clone, and persist exactly one `dokploy_refs` row as `yalla_kind=environment` / `yalla_id=<wrapped environment_id>`. A job already marked `succeeded` is a no-op replay; a crash replay with an existing ref fetches the upstream environment and leaves the mapping table unchanged. Retryable upstream errors stay plain so the durable queue can persist a redacted `error_summary`.
- Worker backup restore jobs (BE-0498 pattern for `restore_backup`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed scoped payload `(organization_id, project_id, environment_id, service_id, backup_id)`, load both the parent service and `service_backups` row through tenant-scoped repositories, require the backup row to be enabled and already `succeeded`, reject stale desired versions and deletion-scheduled services before any Dokploy call, resolve the service-kind-specific Dokploy service ref, then call the typed Dokploy `RestoreBackup` intent. A job already marked `succeeded` is a replay no-op and must not issue another upstream POST; retryable upstream errors stay plain so the durable queue can persist a redacted `error_summary`.
- Worker backup run jobs (BE-0497 pattern for `run_backup`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed scoped payload `(organization_id, project_id, environment_id, service_id, backup_id)`, load both the parent service and `service_backups` row through tenant-scoped repositories, reject stale backup versions plus disabled/running/deletion-scheduled state before any Dokploy call, resolve the service-kind-specific Dokploy service ref, mark the backup row `running` before calling the typed Dokploy `RunBackup` intent, then project the result to `succeeded` or `failed`. Replays of an already-succeeded backup row are no-op and must not issue another upstream POST; retryable upstream errors stay plain so the durable queue can persist a redacted `error_summary`.
- Worker variable sync jobs (BE-0496 pattern for `sync_variables`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed scoped payload `(organization_id, project_id, environment_id, service_id[, engine])`, load the service through the tenant-scoped repository, verify payload scope and `DesiredVersion`, resolve the service-kind-specific Dokploy service ref, fetch all four variable scopes in one read transaction, merge them with `internal/controlplane/variables.Resolver` and the configured secrets provider, render deterministic dotenv content, and call the typed Dokploy `SyncVariables` intent. The typed client maps application to `/application.saveEnvironment`, compose to `/compose.update`, and database engines to `/<engine>.saveEnvironment`; fake Dokploy request recording must redact the entire rendered `env` field because it contains plaintext effective values.
- Worker domain sync jobs (BE-0495 pattern for `sync_domains`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed scoped payload `(organization_id, project_id, environment_id, service_id)`, load the service through the tenant-scoped repository, verify payload scope and `DesiredVersion`, resolve the service-kind-specific Dokploy service ref, list desired `service_domains`, and call the typed Dokploy `EnsureDomain` intent once per desired row. Persist mappings as `dokploy_refs` rows with `yalla_kind='service_domain'`, `yalla_id=service_domains.id`, and `dokploy_resource='domain'`; replays pass `ExistingID` to `EnsureDomain` and must not insert duplicate domain mappings. Retryable upstream errors stay plain for the durable queue to persist redacted `error_summary`; malformed/stale/cross-tenant desired state is `worker.Terminal`.
- Worker project teardown jobs (BE-0494 pattern for `project.delete` / PRD alias `delete_project`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed scoped payload `(organization_id, project_id)`, load the project through the tenant-scoped repository, verify payload scope and `DesiredVersion` against the persisted row, resolve the `project` `dokploy_refs` row, and call the typed Dokploy `RemoveProject` intent. A job already marked `succeeded` is a replay no-op; a prior upstream deletion is idempotent because the typed Dokploy client treats remove 404 as success. Like environment/service delete jobs, project delete jobs do not reject `deletion_scheduled_at` because scheduled deletion is the expected lifecycle path.
- Worker environment teardown jobs (BE-0493 pattern for `environment.delete` / PRD alias `delete_environment`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed scoped payload `(organization_id, project_id, environment_id)`, load the environment through the tenant-scoped repository, verify payload scope and `DesiredVersion` against the persisted row, resolve the `environment` `dokploy_refs` row, and call the typed Dokploy `RemoveEnvironment` intent. A job already marked `succeeded` is a replay no-op; a prior upstream deletion is idempotent because the typed Dokploy client treats remove 404 as success. Like service delete jobs, environment delete jobs do not reject `deletion_scheduled_at` because scheduled deletion is the expected lifecycle path.
- Worker teardown jobs (BE-0492 pattern for `service.delete` / PRD alias `delete_service`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed scoped payload `(organization_id, project_id, environment_id, service_id)`, load the service through the tenant-scoped repository, verify payload scope and `DesiredVersion` against the persisted row, resolve the service-kind-specific `dokploy_refs` row, and call the typed Dokploy `RemoveService` intent. A job already marked `succeeded` is a replay no-op; a prior upstream deletion is also idempotent because the typed Dokploy client treats remove 404 as success. Unlike runtime-control jobs, delete jobs do not reject `deletion_scheduled_at`; scheduled deletion is the normal lifecycle path.
- Worker runtime-control jobs (BE-0488/BE-0489/BE-0490/BE-0491 pattern for `service.restart` / PRD alias `restart_service`, `service.stop` / PRD alias `stop_service`, `service.start` / PRD alias `start_service`, and `service.rollback` / PRD alias `rollback_service`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed payload parser carrying `(organization_id, project_id, environment_id, service_id)`, load the service through the tenant-scoped repository, verify payload scope against the persisted row, refuse stale `DesiredVersion` and `deletion_scheduled_at` before any Dokploy call, resolve the concrete service Dokploy ID from the service-kind-specific `dokploy_refs` row, and call a typed Dokploy runtime intent such as `RestartService`, `StopService`, `StartService`, or `RollbackService`. Keep accepting PRD underscore aliases (`restart_service`, `stop_service`, `start_service`, `rollback_service`, etc.) for compatibility with manually seeded jobs. Jobs with `Status == succeeded` should be no-op replays and must not issue another Dokploy POST; retryable upstream errors stay plain so the durable queue can persist a redacted `error_summary`.
- Worker deployment jobs (BE-0487 pattern for `service.deploy` / PRD alias `deploy_service`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed payload parser that includes `deployment_id`, load the deployment and parent service through tenant-scoped repositories, verify payload scope against the persisted deployment row, resolve the concrete service Dokploy ID from the service-kind-specific `dokploy_refs` row, mark the deployment `running` before calling `DeployService`, mark it `succeeded` only after a succeeded upstream deployment, and return retryable errors while the upstream deployment is still pending/running or unavailable. Replays of already-succeeded deployments are no-op and must not issue another Dokploy POST; retryable upstream failures leave the deployment running without `finished_at` so the durable queue can retry. The existing API enqueues `service.deploy`; keep accepting the PRD `deploy_service` alias for compatibility.
- Worker child ensure jobs (BE-0482/BE-0483/BE-0484 pattern for `ensure_project`, `ensure_environment`, and `ensure_application_service`) extend `worker.Provisioner` with a typed payload parser, validate the job scope fields against payload IDs, load the source-of-truth row through the tenant-scoped repository, check `DesiredVersion` before Dokploy calls and again before persisting refs, resolve the parent Dokploy ID from tenant-scoped `dokploy_refs`, call the typed Dokploy client through mapper-produced intents, and persist exactly one child `dokploy_refs` row. Replay should read the existing child ref, call the typed client with `ExistingID`, and leave the mapping table unchanged; malformed/stale/cross-tenant/missing desired state are `worker.Terminal`, retryable Dokploy errors stay plain, and queue-level tests should verify persisted `error_summary` stays redacted. Service-kind-specific jobs must also verify the source-of-truth `services.kind` before calling Dokploy and persist the matching Dokploy resource kind (`application`, `compose`, or `database`). `ensure_database_service` additionally validates the concrete engine in the durable job payload because the current `services` row stores only the broad `database` kind.
- Worker provisioning jobs are implemented through `internal/controlplane/worker.Provisioner`: parse `provisioning_jobs.payload` into a typed schema, mark malformed/stale/cross-tenant desired state with `worker.Terminal`, load source-of-truth state from Postgres before Dokploy calls, and persist resolved upstream IDs through tenant-scoped `dokploy_refs`; replay should verify an existing ref instead of inserting a duplicate mapping.
- Repository tenant-isolation tests for a **project-scoped preview lifecycle wrapper with Insert + GetByID + ListByProject + Update + ScheduleDeletion + DeleteByID, database-owned version/timestamps, and soft-delete state visible on read paths** (BE-0480 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/preview_environment_repository_tenant_isolation_test.go for preview_environments). Seed two complete Organization -> Project -> source Environment + preview-kind wrapped Environment chains, use overlapping-looking DisplayName/ChangeRef fixtures, assert ListByProject renders only the caller's stable page and returns a non-nil empty slice for `(orgA, projB)`, assert Get/Update/ScheduleDeletion/Delete using orgA with orgB's `(project_id, preview_id)` return typed `E_NOT_FOUND`, byte-compare both orgA and orgB bystanders after failed cross-tenant writes, and explicitly schedule deletion on orgB to prove soft-deleted preview rows remain tenant-scoped on both list and direct-id read paths. Add a global-PK collision probe across tenants because `preview_environments.id` is globally unique even though all normal reads/writes are tenant-scoped; the conflict must leave the prior owner byte-identical and create no row for the requester.
- Repository CRUD-and-invariants tests for a **project-scoped preview lifecycle table whose row points at both a preview-kind environment clone and a source environment, carries soft-delete lifecycle state, and exposes Insert + GetByID + ListByProject + Update + ScheduleDeletion + DeleteByID** (BE-0479 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/preview_environment_repository_invariants_test.go for preview_environments). The table is tenant-scoped by direct `(organization_id, project_id)` predicates and composite FKs to `environments (organization_id, project_id, id)`, uses `penv_` IDs via `domain.KindPreviewEnvironment`, and adds a trigger to enforce that the wrapped environment row has `kind='preview'` because a FK cannot express referenced-row-body predicates. It keeps status/deletion state out of customer metadata Update, and uses ScheduleDeletion (`status='deleting'`, `deletion_scheduled_at=COALESCE(..., now())`) for API teardown while preserving hard DeleteByID for worker cleanup after Dokploy teardown. Forward-applicable to future project-scoped lifecycle rows that wrap a concrete hierarchy resource with worker-owned status: test row shape/default status, deterministic `(created_at,id)` list ordering, optimistic conflicts, soft-delete lifecycle, hard-delete cleanup, constraint conflicts, referenced-row-body trigger conflicts, rollback, nil-Tx guards, and database-owned version/timestamps.
- Preview create endpoint/service pattern (BE-0262): parent-scoped preview API routes use `projectIDResolver`, a thin HTTP handler, and `store.PreviewEnvironmentService`. The store unit of work verifies the path project exists under the principal org, reloads the source environment tenant-scoped, requires `source.ProjectID == projectID` before auth/quota/job/audit side effects, creates a real `environments.kind='preview'` clone plus the `preview_environments` wrapper in the same transaction, reserves both `environments` and `preview_environments`, enqueues `create_preview_environment` with the preview id through the current `JobEnqueuer` port, and audits `preview.create` against `domain.KindPreviewEnvironment`. Wrong-project or cross-tenant source ids should collapse to typed `E_NOT_FOUND`.
- Repository CRUD-and-invariants tests for `service_backups` / PRD `backup_schedules` (BE-0477 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/service_backup_repository_invariants_test.go): this is a service-scoped desired-state leaf table with worker-projected run state. The repository surface is Insert + GetByID + ListByService + Update + MarkPending + DeleteByID; every query predicates on `(organization_id, service_id[, id])`. Insert treats `RetentionCount == 0` as omitted and normalizes it to the stable default 7, while negative/out-of-range retention still relies on the DB CHECK and maps to typed `E_CONFLICT`. Update must only write customer policy fields `(display_name, schedule, retention_count, enabled)` and preserve worker state `(status, last_run_at, last_succeeded_at)`; MarkPending is the narrow worker-signal transition and should bump version via trigger. DeleteByID is hard delete with optional If-Match, returning the deleted row snapshot. Forward-applicable to future service-scoped policy rows with worker-owned status columns: test default normalization, deterministic list ordering, optimistic conflicts, timestamp/version triggers, CHECK/FK conflicts, rollback, nil-Tx guards, and preservation of worker-owned columns during customer updates.
- Repository tenant-isolation tests for a **service-scoped hard-delete leaf table with Insert + GetByID + ListByService + Update + DeleteByID and optimistic version triggers** (BE-0476 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/service_domain_repository_tenant_isolation_test.go for service_domains). Seed two full Organization -> Project -> Environment -> Service chains, use overlapping-looking but globally unique (hostname, path) fixtures, assert ListByService returns only the caller tenant's stable page and a non-nil empty slice for a cross-tenant service_id, assert Get/Update/Delete using orgA with orgB's service/domain ids return typed E_NOT_FOUND, and byte-compare both orgA and orgB bystanders after failed cross-tenant mutations so missing organization predicates show up as version/updated_at drift. For service_domains specifically, an empty create path is intentionally normalized by the service layer to "/" and the database allows it; do not treat blank path as a DB CHECK conflict in repository constraint tests.
- Repository CRUD-and-invariants tests for a **tenant-scoped service leaf table whose public surface is Insert + GetByID + ListByService + Update + DeleteByID, whose row has database-owned version/created_at/updated_at, and whose parent link is the composite `(organization_id, service_id)` FK** (BE-0475 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/service_domain_repository_invariants_test.go for service_domains). The reusable shape is: seed the Organization -> Project -> Environment -> Service chain with existing helpers, insert through the typed repository rather than raw SQL, assert version=1 and created_at==updated_at on INSERT, assert Update bumps version and advances updated_at while preserving created_at and identity fields, assert matching If-Match succeeds while stale If-Match on Update/Delete returns typed `E_CONFLICT`, assert DeleteByID returns the final row and removes it, and cover CHECK/FK/UNIQUE violations, transaction rollback, parent cascade, deterministic ListByService ordering, and nil-Tx guards. Forward-applicable to future service-scoped leaf tables with hard-delete lifecycle and optimistic concurrency.

- Repository CRUD-and-invariants tests for a **TABLE WHOSE *_repository.go + PRIMARY *_test.go ALREADY EXIST FROM A PRIOR (NON-PRD) SUBSYSTEM STORY, AND WHOSE LIFECYCLE HAS A CLAIM PROTOCOL (Claim + Complete + Release + Find — three writes, one read) DRIVEN BY AN UPSERT WITH AN ON-CONFLICT TARGET ON A NON-PK UNIQUE TUPLE (organization_id, principal_id, idempotency_key), AND WHOSE ROW BODY CARRIES A MULTI-COLUMN COMPLETION-CONSISTENT CHECK** (BE-0469 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/idempotency_repository_invariants_test.go for idempotency_keys). The TestIdempotencyRepositoryClaimDuplicateIDIsConflict probe MUST force the collision through caller-supplied ids on different (principal, key) tuples; a regression that switched the ON CONFLICT target to (id) would swallow the collision and silently rewrite a peer row. TestIdempotencyRepositoryCompleteCoercesNilBodyToEmpty pins both the application-layer coercion AND the database-side non-NULL empty-bytea storage. The pending-side of the CHECK is pinned by TestIdempotencyRepositoryClaimMintsRowShape (a fresh Claim must leave all three completion columns NULL); the completed-side by TestIdempotencyRepositoryCompleteRowShape (after Complete, all three must be non-NULL AND a raw-SQL re-load must byte-equal the returned struct, AND created_at + expires_at must NOT have drifted across the Complete UPDATE -- only the four completion columns transition). TestIdempotencyRepositoryCompleteHonoursExplicitNow uses a specific 2024 timestamp far from time.Now() so a regression that ignored the arg and wrote time.Now() would fail with an obvious delta. This is a structurally distinct invariant from BE-0467 (audit_events) where ALL timestamps are server-side via DEFAULT now() and a caller-supplied OccurredAt must be discarded. (d) The id minter newIdempotencyID emits `idk_<32hex>` (16 bytes of crypto/rand entropy hex-encoded — 4 + 32 = 36 chars total). The row-shape probe MUST pin BOTH the prefix AND the total length so a regression that shortened the entropy or reformatted the prefix surfaces here. Test-local mintIdempotencyID(t, suffix) follows the established per-file suffixed-helper pattern (`idk_`+t.Name()+`_`+suffix) so parallel tests that need a deterministic caller-supplied id (to force a PK collision) cannot collide. The invariants file fills the Release gap with TestIdempotencyRepositoryReleaseRejectsNilTx so all three mutating methods (Claim / Complete / Release) have a pinned nil-tx guard. - Repository tenant-isolation tests for a **TABLE WHOSE SCHEMA LANDED IN AN EARLY MIGRATION, WHOSE TYPED REPOSITORY + INVARIANTS TESTS LANDED IN THE IMMEDIATELY PRIOR PRD STORY, AND WHOSE ROW BODY HAS NO CUSTOMER-MUTABLE COLUMN (Insert + Get + List + Delete only, NO Update / NO state-transition surface) AND CARRIES TWO UNIQUE CONSTRAINTS — ONE GLOBAL across tenants AND ONE PER-TENANT** (BE-0466 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/dokploy_ref_tenant_isolation_test.go for dokploy_refs). (b) The GLOBAL UNIQUE leg (e.g. dokploy_refs UNIQUE (dokploy_resource, dokploy_id)) demands a dokploy_refs-specific cross-tenant probe not present in any prior tenant-isolation file: orgA Inserting at a (resource, dokploy_id) ALREADY OWNED by orgB must surface as typed apierr.Conflict AND leave orgB's row byte-identical — this is the cross-tenant mirror of the same-tenant duplicate-target Conflict pinned in the BE-0465 invariants file, with the added byte-identity invariant. (c) GetByXxxTarget (e.g. dokploy_refs.GetByDokployTarget(orgID, resource, dokploy_id)) is a SECOND tenant-scoped read surface beyond the per-id Get — and because the (resource, dokploy_id) tuple is GLOBAL-UNIQUE, the row DOES exist for orgB's foreign-target call, so the tenant predicate is the ONLY thing hiding it. The cross-tenant test is structurally load-bearing: a regression that dropped the organization_id predicate from GetByXxxTarget would surface a successful read of orgA's row from orgB's caller (worst-case cross-tenant data leak). This file must also include a SANITY clause that calls GetByXxxTarget(orgA, resource, alphaDokployID) and expects success; without it the entire test could silently pass if the repository broke for both tenants. (d) Delete is *Tx-bound and returns NotFound via the tag.RowsAffected() == 0 path (not via pgx.ErrNoRows). The cross-tenant probe must run inside an s.Write closure and assert BOTH typed NotFound AND orgA's row byte-identity after — a regression that dropped the organization_id leg from the DELETE predicate would surface as either tag.RowsAffected() == 1 (orgB's call returns nil and orgA's row vanishes — the worst-case data-loss bug) OR as an orgA bystander column drift. The closest sibling (BE-0464 job_attempts) has no Delete surface, so this is a BE-0466-unique probe. - Repository tenant-isolation tests for a **TABLE WHOSE TYPED REPOSITORY IS THE NARROWEST IN THE STORE PACKAGE — APPEND (write) + ListByOrganization (read) ONLY, with NO GetByID, NO Update, NO Delete (row removal reachable only through organizations ON DELETE CASCADE on tenant teardown), AND WHOSE PRIMARY KEY IS GLOBAL (no UNIQUE on (organization_id, id) because the id minter emits 128-bit-entropy opaque tokens that are globally unique by construction)** (BE-0468 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/audit_repository_tenant_isolation_test.go for audit_events). Subspecies of the BE-0466 (dokploy_refs) tenant-isolation pattern with five load-bearing deltas that collapse the surface back to the narrowest viable cross-tenant shape: (a) the GetByID / GetByXxxTarget / Delete cross-tenant probes from BE-0466 are STRUCTURALLY ABSENT (no such methods exist on the repository), so the file header MUST document this as load-bearing so a future reader does not mistake the absence for a coverage gap. The BE-0466 9-probe shape collapses to a 7-probe shape: Append-bystander-byte-identity / Append-bystander-row-count-invariance / Append-cross-tenant-id-collision-Conflict-with-orgA-byte-identity-and-no-foreign-column-echo / ListByOrganization-cross-tenant-returns-only-own-rows-byte-identical + orgA-COUNT-invariance / ListByOrganization-above-cap-limit-clamping-is-tenant-scoped / ListByOrganization-unknown-tenant-empty-and-preserves-real-tenants-COUNT / organizations DELETE cascade is tenant-scoped (3-row orgB pool spanning the decision/metadata spread, plus post-cascade ListByOrganization probe). (b) The cross-tenant id-collision Conflict probe is the load-bearing audit-events-specific contribution: orgA writes a row carrying distinctive business columns (alpha_distinctive_* strings, a unique IP, a unique user-agent, a unique metadata key/value pair) and orgB attempts an Append with the SAME id under its own tenant; the PRIMARY KEY (id) global UNIQUE makes this a Conflict regardless of organization_id, AND the Conflict payload must echo ONLY the supplied id (which orgB has) and never any foreign column from orgA's row (action, resource_kind, resource_id, reason, request_id, correlation_id, ip_address, user_agent, or metadata values). A regression that widened the conflict resolution by organization_id (e.g. an ON CONFLICT (organization_id, id) DO UPDATE clause) would silently allow orgB to mint a row carrying orgA's id under its own tenant — the worst-case audit-log correlation-corruption shape. The not-foreign-substring assertions (containsValue against each distinctive value) are the second-line defence behind the apierr.Conflict code probe. (c) The above-cap-limit-clamping-is-tenant-scoped probe is the load-bearing read-side contribution: a regression that dropped the organization_id predicate from ListByOrganization but kept the LIMIT clause would surface here as a returned-row count well above orgB's seeded count (min(alphaSeed + bravoSeed, auditEventListMaxLimit) instead of just bravoSeed). The test seeds orgA's pool ABOVE the cap (auditEventListMaxLimit + 5 = 205 rows via raw-SQL INSERT — a 205-row Append-loop through the store would multiply the transaction setup cost too much for a single probe) and orgB's pool at a small fixed count (4); orgB's ListByOrganization with an above-cap limit request (1000) must resolve to exactly 4 rows, NOT the 200 cap. (d) assertAuditRowByteIdentical is structurally distinct from the application-level assertAuditEventByteIdentical in audit_test.go: the AuditEvent struct comparator would silently round-trip a metadata jsonb byte drift (the marshalled bytes differ but the unmarshalled map equals) or a sub-second occurred_at rewrite (the application struct's time.Time has Go-native nanosecond precision but the database column's microsecond precision can mask a rewrite within the same microsecond). The raw-row helper compares the persisted bytes exactly as the database stores them — the second-line defence the BE-0468 acceptance criteria require. (e) The unknown-tenant-empty-and-preserves-real-tenants-COUNT probe is the cross-tenant variant of the BE-0467 List-unknown-org-returns-empty: the invariants file seeds a single tenant and asserts the empty slice; the BE-0468 file seeds TWO real tenants and asserts BOTH (i) the empty slice for the phantom org-id AND (ii) BOTH real tenants' per-org COUNT(*) is unchanged after the read. A regression that silently auto-vacuumed orphan rows or counted rows owned by ANY tenant into a global cache would surface here. New helpers introduced (per-file Audit-suffix already established by BE-0467 to avoid store_test collisions): assertAuditRowByteIdentical (raw-row byte-level snapshot comparator), twoTenantAuditFixture + seedTwoTenantAuditFixture (two-organization fixture, NARROWER than the BE-0466 dokploy_refs equivalent because audit_events has no project/environment/service parent chain), itoa (tiny local int-to-string converter for the raw-INSERT seed loop in the above-cap-limit-clamping test — keeps the import graph free of strconv at this site). REUSED verbatim from sibling audit_test.go: auditEventFixture, appendAudit; from audit_repository_invariants_test.go: rawAuditRow, loadAuditRowByID, countAuditRowsForOrg, mintAuditID; from schema_test.go: seedOrg; from store_test.go: newStore; from organization_variable_tenant_isolation_test.go: containsValue. NO migration added. Forward-applicable to any future tenant-isolation story whose table has the (Append, ListByOrganization) narrow surface and a global PRIMARY KEY: a future security_events / system_audit / webhook_events table would inherit the same template, including the cross-tenant id-collision Conflict + foreign-column-no-echo invariant and the above-cap-limit-clamping-is-tenant-scoped invariant.

- Repository tenant-isolation tests for an **APPEND-ONLY CHILD table whose ONLY public mutation surface is Append() inside a *Tx, anchored by a composite FK (organization_id, deployment_id) to a tenant-scoped parent table with ON DELETE CASCADE, whose row body has NO version column AND NO updated_at column AND NO Update/Delete surface (BEFORE UPDATE trigger rejects every UPDATE at the SQL level), AND whose tenant teardown is reachable only TRANSITIVELY via parent-deployment-cascade OR parent-organization-cascade** (BE-0460 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/deployment_event_tenant_isolation_test.go). GOTCHA: when two tenants need to share a row "shape" in the cascade test, the suffixes MUST be per-tenant-unique because mintDeploymentID hashes `t.Name() + suffix` and the GLOBAL PRIMARY KEY on deployments(id) means two tenants cannot share an id even though every OTHER column is per-tenant unique — a naive same-suffix-for-both-tenants call trips mapWriteError's generic "a deployment with this idempotency key already exists" message which LOOKS like an idem-key conflict but is actually an id collision. Forward-applicable to any tenant-isolation story whose table carries a global PRIMARY KEY AND a per-tenant UNIQUE on a different column AND lifecycle triggers (e.g. future BE-0461 provisioning_jobs).
- Repository CRUD-and-invariants tests for a **TENANT-SCOPED LIFECYCLE-BEARING table whose Insert is caller-id (no per-row id minting in the repository), whose only public state-transition surface is a single Cancel() with optimistic-concurrency disambiguation, and whose row body carries a lifecycle CHECK (terminal-status <-> finished_at) plus a bump_version trigger** (BE-0457 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/deployment_repository_invariants_test.go). Structurally distinct from BE-0455 (quota_reservations — the repository mints qres_<token> ids and has no Update/Cancel surface) in three load-bearing ways: (a) the test must mint deployment ids itself (DeploymentService.Create owns domain.NewID(domain.KindDeployment); the repo does NOT mint). A test-local mintDeploymentID(t, suffix) helper using `"dep_"+t.Name()+"_"+suffix` avoids global PK collisions across parallel cases without a shared atomic counter — every *_test.go under internal/controlplane/store/ shares one package, so t.Name() is the natural disambiguator. (b) The terminal-status-on-Insert probe leverages the deployments_finished_consistent CHECK: Insert's INSERT column list omits finished_at, so any terminal Status passed in violates the CHECK by construction (status terminal AND finished_at NULL). This is the one-line proof that this surface can only mint non-terminal rows; no separate trigger test is needed. (c) Cancel exercises THREE disambiguation legs against the SAME *Tx — nil expectedVersion + terminal row -> apierr.Conflict (no current_version attached), non-nil expectedVersion + version mismatch -> apierr.ConflictStale (current_version attached, verified via apierr.CurrentVersionOf), unknown id -> apierr.NotFound. The cross-tenant Cancel probe MUST include a byte-identity assertion on the foreign-tenant row (status unchanged, finished_at still NULL, version not bumped) — without it, a regression that scoped the UPDATE by id alone and disambiguated by organization_id would silently mutate the foreign tenant's row before failing the lookup. The 31-test shape (Insert: row-shape / status-default / non-queued-status-persists / dup-id / dup-(org,idem) / blank-id / blank-requested_by / blank-idem / unknown-source / terminal-without-finished / unknown-org / cross-tenant-service / nil-tx / rollback; GetByID: persisted-row / unknown / cross-tenant; FindByIdempotencyKey: present / missing / cross-tenant; Cancel: queued / running / matching-version / stale-version-ConflictStale / terminal-row-Conflict / unknown-NotFound / cross-tenant-NotFound-with-byte-identity / nil-tx; ListByService: reverse-chronological / empty-non-nil-slice / cross-tenant-empty) leaves the BE-0458 tenant-isolation file to add the bystander byte-identical proof + organization-delete-cascade probes. Helpers reused: seedOrg/seedProject/seedEnvironment/seedService (schema_test.go), newStore (store_test.go). New helpers introduced (unique to this file): rawDeploymentRow, loadDeploymentRowByID, countDeploymentRowsForOrg, mintDeploymentID, runInsertDeploymentOrFail, seedQueuedDeployment, seedRunningDeployment, deploymentTxRollbackSentinel.
- Repository tenant-isolation tests for a **TENANT-SCOPED EVENT-LIKE LEDGER table whose ONLY public mutation surface is an unbounded INSERT (no UNIQUE on (organization_id, resource) — only PRIMARY KEY (id) and a composite-FK target UNIQUE (organization_id, id)), whose ONLY read aggregate is a SUM filtered by tenant + resource + status + expires_at predicates, and whose row body carries nullable timestamp/text columns** (BE-0456 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/quota_reservation_tenant_isolation_test.go). Structurally distinct from BE-0454 (quota_usage — partial UNIQUE (organization_id, resource) and the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING / SELECT FOR UPDATE primitive) in three load-bearing ways: (a) the bystander byte-identity assertion must cover the nullable job_id and settled_at columns (rawQuotaReservationRow declares them *string/*time.Time; the per-file stringPtrEqualQR/timePtrEqualQR/fmtStringPtrQR/fmtTimePtrQR helpers MUST get a per-file QR suffix because store_test already exposes QP-suffixed variants from BE-0451 and a stringPtrEqual variant from BE-0440); (b) the same-resource-in-two-tenants positive-direction pair is INSERT-and-both-persist (no conflict at all — no UNIQUE constraint to defeat) instead of LockUsage-and-both-succeed; (c) a NEW cross-tenant probe is mandatory — global PRIMARY KEY collision across tenants must surface as typed apierr.Conflict (yerr.CodeConflict) AND leave the prior owner's row byte-identical AND insert no row for the requester; this guards against a regression that swapped the INSERT for an ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (a copy-paste of quota_policies' upsert pattern). The 7-test shape (insert-bystander-byte-identity across active+settled peers / insert-row-count-invariant / same-resource-two-tenants-both-persist / global-PK-collision-cross-tenant-conflict with byte-identical prior-owner / SumActiveReservations-tenant-scoped (10-vs-300 chosen so a cross-tenant fold shows as 310) / SumActiveReservations-on-empty-tenant-returns-zero-even-when-others-have-rows / organization-delete-cascade-is-tenant-scoped) leaves the BE-0455 invariants tests (status / time / resource predicate filters, CHECK / DOMAIN / FK violations, row-shape, id-provenance, rollback, nil-tx) untouched. - Repository CRUD invariants test file for a **TENANT-SCOPED COUNTER table whose ONLY public mutation surface is an INSERT...ON CONFLICT (organization_id, resource) DO NOTHING + SELECT...FOR UPDATE primitive (LockUsage), with NO per-row Update/Delete, NO version column, NO service_id pointer, and a database-managed used_value mutated by an EXTERNAL code path (quota.Checker, not the repository), set_updated_at trigger fires BEFORE UPDATE only** (BE-0453 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/quota_usage_repository_invariants_test.go). Structurally distinct from BE-0451 (quota_policies — INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE upsert) in four load-bearing ways: (a) the second-call byte-identity proof must anchor updated_at TOO — ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is not an UPDATE and the set_updated_at trigger must not fire (a regression that switched to ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE with even a no-op SET would silently bump updated_at and a missing anchor would let that slip past); (b) the peer-row proof is a SAME-TENANT-DIFFERENT-RESOURCE check (UNIQUE (organization_id, resource) isolates rows by resource within a tenant); (c) the row-already-exists-with-non-zero-value leg has no policies analog — pre-seed via raw SQL at a sentinel value (e.g. used_value=17, id=`qu_seed_<resource>`) and prove BOTH the seeded id AND the seeded used_value survive a LockUsage call (this is the ONLY way to prove the discarded INSERT's minted prefix id does not replace the row's id — a regression to ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET id=EXCLUDED.id would be a catastrophic data-loss path that typed reader projections would not catch); (d) the DOMAIN-violation test casts an arbitrary string to the typed Resource (e.g. `store.QuotaResource("not-a-resource")`) to bypass Go's compile-time check and exercise the DOMAIN quota_resource CHECK at the database layer — surfacing as yerr.CodeConflict through mapWriteError. The 8-new-test shape (row-shape, second-call-byte-identity, peer-row-byte-identity, persisted-used-value, unknown-org-Conflict, unknown-resource-Conflict, tx-rollback, nil-tx-Internal) leaves the pre-existing TestQuotaRepositoryLockUsageCreatesAndReturnsCounter in quota_repository_test.go alone as the load-bearing two-call-idempotency probe. Helper symbols introduced: `lockUsageOrFail`, `loadQuotaUsageRow`, `countQuotaUsageRowsForOrg`, `rawQuotaUsageRow`, `quotaUsageTxRollbackSentinel`. Reused symbols from sibling files: `seedOrg` (schema_test.go), `seedQuotaUsage` (usage_test.go), `newStore` (store_test.go) — note `seedQuotaUsage` is the ONLY way to set used_value to a non-zero value through a test fixture because the repository surface has no equivalent (LockUsage cannot increment).
- Repository tenant-isolation tests for a **DUAL-SCOPE ledger-style table whose ONLY mutation surface is an INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE upsert and whose row body is observable EXCLUSIVELY through typed resolvers (no per-id Get/Update/Delete, no ListByParent)** (BE-0452 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/quota_policy_tenant_isolation_test.go). quota_policies has TWO scope_kind values ('plan_default' with NULL organization_id; 'organization' with non-NULL) anchored by partial unique indexes (e.g. `quota_policies_org_resource_idx (organization_id, resource) WHERE scope_kind='organization'`) and NO version column — so the byte-identical-bystander anchor reduces to the trigger-managed updated_at ALONE. The 9-test shape diverges from BE-0440 (project_grant, ListByParent-only) and BE-0436 (api_key_scope, per-id Get + per-id mutations) in four load-bearing ways: (a) cross-tenant projection is proved through EVERY resolver leg independently — one test per resolver method (EffectiveLimit per-resource tenant-scoped; ListEffectiveLimits count isolation; ListOrganizationUsage two-CTE-leg isolation) — because each resolver has its own WHERE clause and a regression dropping any one leg leaks a different column; (b) a NEW plan-isolation leg is added: orgA on 'starter' must not see 'pro' plan defaults even though both rows live in the SAME table with NULL organization_id — the plan column is the second tenant boundary on the plan_default scope and a missing plan predicate is a distinct regression surface from a missing organization_id predicate; (c) the byte-identical-bystander proof is observed via a RAW-SQL load of the underlying quota_policies row (reusing BE-0451's loadOrganizationPolicyRow + rawQuotaPolicyRow), because the typed reader projections deliberately omit id/created_at/updated_at/scope_kind/plan — a regression that stamped correct-looking limit_value and enforcement_mode onto the peer's row would slip past every typed-resolver projection if asserted only via EffectiveLimit; (d) ListOrganizationUsage has TWO independent tenant-predicate legs (one in the policies CTE on organization_id, one in the usage CTE on organization_id) — they need INDEPENDENT proofs because either leg dropping alone leaks a different column (limit_value vs used_value), so the file has BOTH a "policies-CTE leg isolated" test (orgA has an override, orgB has overrides on different resources, no counters) AND a "usage-CTE leg isolated" test (both tenants have a quota_usage counter on the SAME resource with DISTINCT used_value). NO per-id Get => NO (Code, Hint) existence-leak projection: the cross-tenant probe surfaces as an EMPTY projection (resolver returns ok=false, or len(rows)==0), NOT a typed apierr.NotFound — the empty-slice / ok=false IS the existence-indistinguishability proof. The shared-conflict-tuple fixture for the Upsert-UPDATE bystander test MUST be built via upsertOrganizationPolicy (not seedOrgPolicy raw SQL), because using the repository to build the fixture both proves the partial unique index lets the peer row land at all AND aligns baseline.updated_at timestamps so a wrong-row UPDATE shows up as sub-second drift. The corollary "same-resource-in-two-tenants-both-succeed" test is the load-bearing positive-direction pair — without it, a regression that resolved the conflict by (resource,) alone would have prevented the bystander INSERT, and every byte-identical assertion in the UPDATE-branch test would silently pass against a non-existent row. Helper naming caveat: nullable-column helpers MUST get a per-file suffix (stringPtrEqualQP / fmtStringPtrQP) — BE-0440's project-grant file already defines a stringPtrEqual variant in store_test and same-named helpers collide at compile time. Forward-applicable to any future dual-scope ledger-style table (a hypothetical KindFeatureFlagDefault + KindFeatureFlagOverride pairing, or KindPriceTier defaults + organization overrides, would inherit this template).
- Repository tenant-isolation tests for a **multi-table resource FAMILY whose physical realization is one table per scope in the Organization -> Project -> Environment -> Service hierarchy AND whose row body carries SECRET-BEARING columns (value plaintext + sealed-secret tuple)** (BE-0450 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/{organization,project,environment,service}_variable_tenant_isolation_test.go). Mirrors the BE-0449 per-scope split of the invariants tests: when the family is hierarchical with diverging mutation surfaces (organization variant exposes per-key GetByKey + DeleteByKey + UpdateMutable on top of the bulk Upsert + DeleteByXxxExceptKeys pair; project/environment/service variants expose ONLY the bulk pair), ship one *_tenant_isolation_test.go per physical table. The project/environment/service files converge on a uniform 8-test shape: ListByX-correct-across-tenants, ListByX-cross-tenant-scope-returns-empty, ListByX-isolates-shared-key, Upsert-INSERT-bystander-byte-identical, Upsert-UPDATE-bystander-byte-identical, DeleteByXExceptKeys-clear-all-bystander, DeleteByXExceptKeys-keep-subset-bystander, Upsert-same-key-in-two-tenants-both-succeed. The organization file ADDS four per-key tests that have no analog in the other three: GetByKey-cross-tenant-returns-NotFound (with error-surface no-value-echo), DeleteByKey-on-orgA-bystander (plus second-DeleteByKey-on-now-gone-key-returns-NotFound-no-value-echo), UpdateMutable-on-orgA-bystander (Version bumps on orgA, orgB stays byte-identical), UpdateMutable-cross-tenant-key-returns-NotFound-no-value-echo-bystander-byte-identical. THE LOAD-BEARING DIVERGENCE from the BE-0448 grant tenant-isolation template is the byte-identical-bystander projection: variables MUST anchor BOTH Value AND the (SecretProvider, SecretKeyID, SecretCiphertext) tuple AND the IsSecret flag, because variables carry secret-bearing columns that grants do not — a regression that stamped orgA's payload onto orgB's row or that re-sealed orgB's row with orgA's secret bytes would otherwise slip past every identity-column check. bytes.Equal (stdlib) is the right SecretCiphertext compare helper; no custom one needed. Helper REUSE strategy across the family: organization/environment/service tenant-isolation files reuse newXVariableID / upsertXVariable / listXVariablesOrFail defined in their sibling BE-0449 invariants files (same store_test package); the project file DEFINES its own newProjectVariableID(f, org, label) / upsertProjectVariable / listProjectVariablesOrFail because project_variable_repository_invariants_test.go inlines its helpers (no shared symbols to reuse). The project helper signature takes f + org because f.Project requires an org to synthesise the id — the org/env/service helpers use a factory-counter-only or fake-parent scheme. Picking the wrong helper shape at call sites is the most common compile failure when porting tests across the family. Each file defines getXVariableFromListOrFail and assertXVariableByteIdentical with distinct names to avoid same-package collisions across store_test. The containsValue substring helper for the error-surface no-value-echo assertions is defined in the organization file (only organization-scope per-key methods can RETURN errors with message/hint text); env/service/project paths surface their failures via FK Conflict or PK Conflict, both of which are invariants-file legs (not tenant-isolation legs). The "Upsert-same-key-in-two-tenants-both-succeed" test is structurally necessary as the positive-direction pair for the bystander byte-identical proofs — without it, a regression that resolved the conflict on (scope_id, key) alone would still pass every bystander check (the bystander INSERTs first, the peer Upsert then hits PK uniqueness or no conflict at all). OrganizationVariableRepository.ListByOrganization returns a NIL slice on no-rows (unlike its project/environment/service siblings which use make([]T, 0)) — the tenant-isolation contract is "len == 0", not "non-nil"; the org-scope test documents this divergence in a comment and DOES NOT assert non-nil. Forward-applicable to any future multi-table secret-bearing family at this hierarchy.

A PRD note that reads "Database table: <name>" can refer to such a family (variables = 4 scope tables, quota_* = 3 ledger tables) — when the family is hierarchical, ship one *_repository_invariants_test.go per physical table rather than collapsing into a single mega-file, because per-scope mutation surfaces diverge (organization_variables uniquely exposes UpdateMutable + DeleteByKey on top of the bulk-replace surface; project / environment / service variables expose only the bulk Upsert + DeleteByXxxExceptKeys pair). - Repository CRUD invariants test file for a **tenant-scoped child table whose ONLY mutation surface is an INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE upsert PLUS a bulk DELETE-by-exclusion (no per-id Get, no per-id Delete, no traditional UPDATE), with a database-managed version column, optional nullable scoping pointers, and a composite FK to a parent (organization_id, project_id) -> projects** (BE-0439 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/project_grant_repository_invariants_test.go). Two structural divergences from BE-0435 (api_key_scope_repository_invariants_test.go) are load-bearing: (1) the Upsert ON CONFLICT branch must be tested with a DIFFERENT caller-supplied id AND a DIFFERENT caller-supplied principal_kind to prove BOTH the caller-id-is-ignored guarantee AND the cross-kind-smuggling-impossible guarantee — the principal_kind column is NOT part of the scope tuple, so an existing row stays at its current principal_kind even when the caller passes a different kind for the same principal_id; a single Role-only update test would silently pass while a regression that promoted principal_kind to a SET clause still went undetected. (2) The Upsert rollback proof reduces to ListByProject-only because the repository exposes no per-id Get for grants — ListByProject is the ONLY observation surface for a grant row, so it is the load-bearing leak channel a partial commit would surface through, and an absent Get assertion is a deliberate file boundary, not a gap. Insert duplicate-id test must use a DIFFERENT principal_id so the ON CONFLICT (org, proj, principal, env, svc) branch does NOT match and the PRIMARY KEY (id) uniqueness violation is exercised — otherwise the upsert path silently swallows the duplicate id. DeleteByProjectExceptIDs has TWO codepaths in the repository (len(keepIDs)==0 -> unconditional DELETE; len>0 -> DELETE WHERE id NOT IN (ANY $3::text[])), so BOTH must be exercised independently — the empty-keep test must additionally use a fresh seed after the nil-keep clear AND assert the empty-slice ([]string{}) form is identical to nil at the wire (the repository documents nil and empty as identical, so a regression that diverged them would surface here). ON DELETE CASCADE from projects is the project-grant analogue of api_key_scope's ON DELETE CASCADE from api_keys: use raw `DELETE FROM projects WHERE id=$1` (NOT the repository's ScheduleDeletion, which is a SOFT delete and would NOT trigger CASCADE) and observe via ListByProject. Helper `newProjectGrantID(f, label)` synthesises a `pgrnt_<token_n>` id by rewriting f.Project's `prj_<token_n>` prefix — the testutil.Factory only stamps known domain prefixes and there is no f.ProjectGrant, so prefix-rewriting is the cleanest way to mint factory-unique ids without reaching into domain.NewID(domain.KindProjectGrant). The sibling project_grant_test.go's `seedProjectGrant` raw-SQL helper is kept intentionally separate: that file's tests exercise the read path against rows the schema (not the repository) inserted, so a regression that broke INSERT would still let the read tests pass — by contrast THIS file's `upsertProjectGrant` exercises the repository's INSERT path, so the two seed surfaces are complementary, not duplicates.
- Repository CRUD invariants test file for a **tenant-scoped table whose mutation surface spans FOUR distinct UPDATE paths (Update / UpdateDisplayName / ScheduleDeletion / Restore) PLUS Insert, with a database-managed version column AND a nullable soft-delete column (deletion_scheduled_at)** (BE-0437 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/project_repository_invariants_test.go): this is the BE-0425 organization template extended with the second-UPDATE-path projection (UpdateDisplayName must run the dual-anchor AND prove the path-specific WHERE/SET isolation — the row's slug must be untouched since the SET clause is `SET display_name = $3` only) and the BE-0431 inverse-soft-delete projection (Restore must dual-anchor AND clear deletion_scheduled_at back to NULL — the trigger fires on any UPDATE so a forgotten `SET deletion_scheduled_at = NULL` clause would still pass the version/timestamp anchors, making the "deletion_scheduled_at is nil after Restore" assertion the load-bearing one). - Repository tenant-isolation test file for a **tenant-scoped child table with a database-managed version column, a composite FK to a parent api_keys row, and NO secret-bearing column** (BE-0436 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/api_key_scope_tenant_isolation_test.go). The BE-0430 membership_tenant_isolation_test.go shape is the closest template; four substitutions are mandatory: (a) the cross-tenant indistinguishability probe uses the SAME (Code, Hint) anchor pattern, but on a single id column rather than a composite key — both the cross-tenant scope id and an unknown scope id under the prober's tenant must render byte-identical typed NotFound; (b) the byte-identical-bystander assertion carries TWO independent trigger anchors (api_key_scopes_set_updated_at AND api_key_scopes_bump_version) instead of memberships' one (memberships_set_updated_at + role_version-only-via-UpdateRole). The api_key_scopes table has NO secret-bearing column (the scope text itself is the customer-facing capability string), so the BE-0434 raw-secret_hash probe has no analogue and the byte-identical-bystander assertion alone covers every observable column. Helpers seedAPIKeyForScopes / newAPIKeyScope / insertAPIKeyScope are reused from api_key_scope_repository_invariants_test.go in the same store_test package — sibling-file test name collisions (e.g. TestAPIKeyScopeRepositoryListByAPIKeyIsTenantScoped from BE-0435) MUST be checked with `grep '^func Test'` on the sibling invariants file before adding new test names. Future tenant-scoped child tables with a version column and no secret-bearing column (variables.value when is_secret=false, future per-scope capability tables, scoped grant link tables not yet sharded out) should reuse THIS file as the template; if the row body carries a secret-bearing column add the BE-0434 raw-column probe on top.
- Repository tenant-isolation test file for a **tenant-scoped table with FOUR distinct mutation paths (Update / UpdateDisplayName / ScheduleDeletion / Restore), a nullable soft-delete column (deletion_scheduled_at), and a count surface the quota layer reads (CountByOrganization)** (BE-0438 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/project_tenant_isolation_test.go): this is the BE-0436 api_key_scope_tenant_isolation template extended with three projections api_key_scopes had no analogue for — (a) UpdateDisplayName needs its own OnOrgADoesNotTouchOrgB / CrossTenantBystanderIsByteIdentical pair because no other repo file proves the cross-tenant invariant on this surface; (b) the byte-identical-bystander helper carries DeletionScheduledAt as a fourth observable column on top of (version, updated_at, slug, display_name), so a cross-tenant ScheduleDeletion that stamped a peer nil→non-nil OR a cross-tenant Restore that cleared a peer non-nil→nil is caught even when triggers happened to look untouched (same-second match); (c) one composite SoftDeletedRowIsTenantScopedOnReadPaths test proves cross-tenant invisibility across ALL THREE read surfaces (Get / ListByOrganization / CountByOrganization) AND owner-tenant visibility across the same three in a single fixture — the projections collapse into one test because the SAME WHERE organization_id filter is what isolates the row on every read surface.
