- Repository tenant-isolation test file for a **tenant-scoped grandchild table whose ONLY read surface is a parent-scoped ListByProject (no per-id Get, no per-id Delete), with TWO mutation paths (Upsert with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE PLUS DeleteByProjectExceptIDs whose len(keepIDs)==0 and len>0 codepaths must each be exercised), a database-managed version column, optional nullable scoping pointers (environment_id, service_id), and a composite FK to a parent (organization_id, project_id) -> projects** (BE-0440 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/project_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go). This is the BE-0436 api_key_scope_tenant_isolation template adapted for a grandchild table whose conflict target itself includes (organization_id, project_id) AND a multi-column scope tuple. Five projections api_key_scopes had no analogue for are load-bearing here: (a) the byte-identical-bystander proof is observed through ListByProject (the only read surface) — there is no per-id Get like api_key_scopes had, so a helper getGrantFromListOrFail must scan the list response for the bystander id and fatal on absence; the implementation favours correctness over efficiency because the bystander lists are 1-2 rows by construction. (b) the byte-identical-bystander assertGrantByteIdentical helper must compare TWO nullable *string pointer columns (environment_id, service_id) in addition to the scalar columns — pair-helper stringPtrEqual / fmtStringPtr emit "<nil>" vs quoted string for failing assertions so nullability and value drift surface side-by-side; api_key_scopes had no pointer columns, so this is the first tenant-isolation file with a *string comparison. (c) the load-bearing worst-case fixture is the shared-scope-tuple fixture (both tenants own a grant row with the SAME (principal_id, environment_id, service_id) tuple on their OWN projects) AND the Upsert UPDATE-branch bystander test re-upserts with a DIFFERENT role + a fresh caller-supplied id to BOTH fire the ON CONFLICT branch on orgA AND prove the caller-id is ignored — a regression that resolved the conflict by scope-tuple alone (without organization_id and project_id in the conflict target) would have UPDATEd orgB on the peer-trigger fire. (d) DeleteByProjectExceptIDs needs TWO bystander tests because the repository has two SQL codepaths (one unconditional DELETE for nil/empty keepIDs, one DELETE WHERE id NOT IN ANY for non-empty keepIDs); the len>0 test must seed orgB grants whose id is NOT in keepIDs so a regression that dropped the tenant predicate would have deleted them through the "NOT IN ANY" branch. (e) ListByProject cross-tenant projectID returns an empty non-nil slice, so the cross-tenant indistinguishability projection is len==0 + non-nil + unknown-projectID-under-own-tenant yields the SAME empty-non-nil shape (NOT the Code+Hint NotFound shape from api_key_scopes / projects, because grants are read through a list path, not a per-id Get). Helpers seedOrg / seedProject / newProjectGrantID / upsertProjectGrant / listGrantsOrFail are reused from project_grant_test.go and project_grant_repository_invariants_test.go in the same store_test package — sibling-file test name collisions (TestProjectGrantRepo* in project_grant_test.go, TestProjectGrantRepository* in project_grant_repository_invariants_test.go) MUST be checked with `grep '^func Test'` on BOTH sibling files before adding new test names; this file uses the TestProjectGrantRepository* prefix (matching the invariants file convention) with unique suffixes (...OnOrgADoesNotTouchOrgB, ...IsolatesSharedPrincipal, ...InTwoTenantsBothSucceed). The file's docstring MUST call out which legs are already proved elsewhere (cross-tenant FK Conflict, duplicate-PK Conflict, ON DELETE CASCADE, tx-rollback, nil-Tx guards in BE-0439; ListByProject ordering and basic cross-tenant empty-list property in project_grant_test.go) and which are NEW HERE (byte-identical bystander on version + updated_at + role + pointer columns across BOTH Upsert branches AND BOTH DeleteByProjectExceptIDs codepaths, indistinguishability of cross-tenant vs unknown projectID at the list path, per-tenant scope-tuple coexistence, shared-principal_id read isolation) so a future reader does not look for missing tests where the proof is intentionally elsewhere.
- Repository tenant-isolation test file for a **tenant-scoped great-grandchild table with a composite (organization_id, project_id, environment_id) FK to environments, all SIX mutation surfaces of the projects template (Insert / GetByID / ListByEnvironment / Update / ScheduleDeletion / Restore), a database-managed version column, a nullable soft-delete column (deletion_scheduled_at), AND a per-parent UNIQUE (environment_id, slug) — NOT per-organization** (BE-0446 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/service_tenant_isolation_test.go). This is the BE-0438 project_tenant_isolation template extended with TWO load-bearing projections that have no analogue in the projects/environments tenant-isolation files: (1) `Restore CrossTenant bystander byte-identical` requires TWO baselines on the peer tenant — a live peer (DeletionScheduledAt nil) and a soft-deleted peer (DeletionScheduledAt non-nil) — because a regression that mis-handled the WHERE clause on Restore could clear a peer's stamp from non-nil to nil ONLY when the peer had a stamp to clear; a single state would silently pass a regression that only mis-fired in the other direction. The OnOrgADoesNotTouchOrgB Restore test seeds orgA→ScheduleDeletion (so Restore has something to undo), reads orgB live baseline, runs Restore on orgA, asserts orgB live bystander; THEN ScheduleDeletion(orgB), re-ScheduleDeletion(orgA), reads orgB soft-deleted baseline, runs Restore(orgA) again, asserts orgB soft-deleted bystander. The cross-tenant Restore test only needs the soft-deleted-peer baseline because its hostile probe touches the bystander row at most once. (2) The composite FK key surface widens to FOUR identity columns (id, organization_id, project_id, environment_id) — every GetByIDReturnsCorrectRowAcrossTenants assertion verifies all four anchors are DISTINCT between the two tenants (not just (id, organization_id)) so a WHERE-on-id-only mistake that collapses both lookups onto the same row is caught even if both tenants happen to be on the same project_id or environment_id by fixture accident. The `assertServiceByteIdentical` helper extends `assertEnvironmentByteIdentical` with environment_id and adds a Restore-direction error message to the DeletionScheduledAt switch (`cross-tenant Restore (or ScheduleDeletion-clear) cleared a peer tenant's soft-delete stamp`). Seed strategy: use raw-SQL `seedOrg`/`seedProject`/`seedEnvironment` for parents (they return testutil.* types directly) and `insertService` (repo path) for the target services rows — avoids the `projATuple`/`envFromStore` conversion needed in BE-0442 because that file's targets WERE environments and it had to feed `store.Project` into `f.Environment`. The shared-slug fixture works because UNIQUE is (environment_id, slug) — two tenants always have distinct environment_ids so they CAN legitimately share service slug text, making the WHERE-filter the only isolation and the byte-identical-bystander projection load-bearing. The file's docstring MUST call out which legs are already proved elsewhere (cross-tenant NotFound at the typed-error level by service_test.go `TestServiceRepoGetByIDIsTenantScoped`/`TestServiceRepoListByEnvironmentIsTenantScoped`, service-layer cross-tenant by `serviceservice_update_test.go` `TestServiceServiceUpdateCrossTenantIsNotFound`, Restore tenant-scope by `service_restore_test.go` `TestServiceRepositoryRestoreIsTenantScoped`) so a future reader does not look for missing tests where the proof is intentionally elsewhere.

- New customer-data resource = full vertical when it is the FIRST story for that table (BE-0435 pattern, api_key_scopes migration 0033, store/api_key_scope.go, api_key_scope_repository_invariants_test.go): this story is allowed to land migration + repository + first-pass tests because no prior story touched the table (no migration, no repo, no port, no handler, no wiring). The migration declares the table tenant-scoped at the database via the composite FK pattern established by project_grants / environment_grants — and when the parent table never exposed UNIQUE (organization_id, id) (api_keys was such a table) the SAME migration adds the constraint to the parent so the child's composite FK has a target; this is a safe additive change because the parent's PK already makes id unique and the new UNIQUE merely pairs it with organization_id. Repository follows the membership.go / project_grant.go pattern: stateless struct, *Tx for mutations with nil-Tx -> typed apierr.Internal, Querier for reads, pgx.ErrNoRows -> apierr.NotFound, mapWriteError for constraint-violation -> apierr.Conflict, tag.RowsAffected() == 0 -> apierr.NotFound on Delete. Tests combine CRUD + row-shape invariants in one file since no prior tests exist; tenant-isolation byte-identical-bystander proof is deferred to the paired BE-0436 (tenant-isolation) story that always follows.
- Test fixture caveat for api_keys-related seeding (BE-0435 learning, internal/controlplane/store/api_key_scope_repository_invariants_test.go seedAPIKeyForScopes): testutil.Factory.APIKey stamps a per-FACTORY prefix `yk_<token[:8]>`, NOT a per-key prefix. Two keys minted from the same factory get the same Prefix value, which collides with the api_keys_prefix_key UNIQUE constraint when two are inserted in the same test. Always derive the persisted prefix as `key.Prefix + "_" + key.ID` (or similar per-row salt) — never use `key.Prefix + "_" + label` because the same label is reused across orgs in tenant-isolation fixtures and the label is not unique.
- Repository for a **global identity table** with no organization_id and no version column (BE-0427 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/user.go): follow OrganizationRepository's shape (Get-by-own-id, scanX helper, nil-Tx guard → apierr.Internal) but drop the optimistic-concurrency If-Match path entirely; add a separate GetInOrganization(organizationID, userID) that JOINs against memberships so tenant-scoped reads return NotFound (the same shape an unknown id produces) for non-members and cross-tenant requesters. Delete uses RowsAffected() == 0 → apierr.NotFound (mirrors api_keys.Revoke). Conflict mapping for citext UNIQUE columns goes through mapWriteError with a non-sensitive user-facing message.
- Test-helper naming caveat at package store_test (BE-0427 learning): every *_test.go file under internal/controlplane/store/ shares the same package, so duplicate top-level helpers (`seedUser`, `seedMembership`, `seedOrg`, ...) collide at compile time — grep `func seedX` before adding a helper. seedUser already exists in apikey_test.go and returns only the user.ID; tests that need the full row should add a distinct seedUserRow helper that returns testutil.User.
- Tenant-isolation tests for a **global identity table** (BE-0428 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/user_tenant_isolation_test.go): byte-identical-snapshot proof for a table that has no organization_id and no version column. The BE-0426 organization template still applies, but three substitutions are mandatory: (a) drop the stale-If-Match/Update-with-mismatched-version test — there is no version column on the row, so optimistic-concurrency leak surfaces do not exist at this layer (session-token revocation lives on memberships.role_version and is covered by membership_test.go). (b) Add a CONFLICT-PATH BYTE-IDENTICAL test that snapshots BOTH the conflicting target AND the bystander — because the citext UNIQUE constraint on email fires AFTER the UPDATE row is locked and the BEFORE-UPDATE trigger has run, a regression where the trigger stamps updated_at before the constraint rolls back the write would surface on EITHER row; in BE-0426 there is no equivalent "global UNIQUE column outside the WHERE-id" surface to test. (c) Replace "list-by-parent must NotFound for cross-tenant parent ids" with "GetInOrganization-with-unknown-id and GetInOrganization-with-non-member-id produce indistinguishable NotFound shapes (same Code, same Hint)" — the membership join replaces the parent-id-WHERE filter, and existence-leak via Code/Hint divergence is the analogous failure mode. The DELETE-cascade test should snapshot BOTH userB AND userB's memberships count (asymmetric across tenants: the deleted user's memberships in EVERY tenant cascade away via memberships.user_id ON DELETE CASCADE, while bystander users in any tenant keep theirs). Document the deliberate ABSENCE of list-by-parent and soft-delete tests in the file's package-doc comment so a future reader does not look for a missing test (mirrors BE-0426's "tenant-root tables have no ListByParent" note).
- Repository CRUD invariants test file for a **composite-key tenant-scoped link table** with a database-managed version column (BE-0429 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/membership_repository_invariants_test.go). The BE-0427 user_repository_invariants_test.go shape is the closest template, but four substitutions are mandatory because the row has no own-id, has a (organization_id, user_id) composite primary key, and carries role_version + the memberships_set_updated_at trigger: (a) the duplicate-Insert Conflict test asserts on the PK collision (a second Insert with the same (org, user) pair) instead of the citext-UNIQUE-email collision — the schema has no UNIQUE column outside the PK that an INSERT could violate; (b) the existing membership_test.go's UpdateRole case already asserts the role_version atomic +1 increment, so the invariants file's UpdateRole test is dedicated to the timestamp dual-anchor (updated_at refreshed by the BEFORE-UPDATE trigger, created_at preserved) — do NOT duplicate the role_version increment here; (c) NO Delete-cascades-to-children test (the membership row is the SINK of two ON-DELETE-CASCADE FKs from users and organizations, not a SOURCE — cascades INTO memberships are proved in the parent table's invariants file, e.g. TestUserRepositoryDeleteCascadesToMemberships in user_repository_invariants_test.go); (d) the local rollback sentinel type MUST use a distinct name from user_repository_invariants_test.go's `errSentinel` because every *_test.go file under internal/controlplane/store/ shares the same store_test package — `membershipTxRollbackSentinel struct{}` is the canonical naming choice. The Insert-returns-row-with-timestamps test additionally asserts (a) role_version == 1 (the schema default that backs session-token revocation in BE-0020 auth), (b) Email + UserDisplayName populated from the JOINed users row (Insert returns OrganizationMember, not raw Membership — the httpapi layer renders the joined shape directly), and (c) created_at.Equal(updated_at) on the fresh row (the trigger has not fired yet). Forward-applicable to BE-0431/0432 (service_accounts CRUD + tenant-isolation) and BE-0433/0434 (api_keys CRUD + tenant-isolation) — both are tenant-scoped tables with their own version-tracking columns, so the rule "split the version-increment assertion (canonical CRUD test) from the timestamp-dual-anchor assertion (invariants test)" should also apply.
- Repository CRUD invariants test file for a **tenant-scoped table whose only customer mutation is an idempotent lifecycle flip** (BE-0431 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/serviceaccount_repository_invariants_test.go). The BE-0427 user_repository_invariants_test.go and BE-0429 membership_repository_invariants_test.go shapes are the templates, but three substitutions are mandatory because service_accounts has no generic Update and no version column — only Insert + Disable (COALESCE-idempotent): (a) the trigger-dual-anchor test drives through the **lifecycle mutation** (Disable) instead of a generic Update — created_at preserved, updated_at moves forward via the BEFORE UPDATE trigger, plus the lifecycle field (disabled_at) is set and IsDisabled() flips true; (b) the idempotent-second-call semantics are NOT re-asserted here (they belong in the canonical CRUD test in serviceaccount_test.go); (c) the rollback-leaves-zero-footprint test asserts BOTH Get-is-NotFound AND CountByOrganization == 0 (the quota reader is the second observable surface a half-written row could surface through, and a future refactor that switched Insert to a SAVEPOINT or autonomous transaction would silently inflate it without ever surfacing on Get). - Repository tenant-isolation test file for a **composite-key tenant-scoped link table** with NO own id, NO version column independent of role_version, and NO soft-delete column (BE-0430 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/membership_tenant_isolation_test.go). The BE-0428 user_tenant_isolation_test.go shape is the closest template, but four substitutions are mandatory because the link table is keyed by (organization_id, user_id) and the load-bearing cross-row failure mode is "the SAME user is a legitimate member of two tenants, and a WHERE-on-user-only mutation scrubs/bumps the WRONG tenant's row": (a) every byte-identical-snapshot test seeds the SAME user_id into BOTH tenants with deliberately distinct (role, role_version) tuples — a WHERE-on-user-only mistake would return one row for both Get calls and the disjoint role_version values would catch it even when the role values coincide; (b) the UpdateRole bystander test snapshots the OTHER tenant's row (not the unrelated user's row) — the BE-0428 "different user, different tenant" framing is too weak for a link table, because the disjoint-id check that user identity gets for free here is the WHOLE THING the test is proving; (c) the duplicate-Insert Conflict bystander test snapshots BOTH the conflicting target tenant's row AND the SAME-user-different-tenant bystander row — the PK collision fires AFTER any row-level CHECKs and the BEFORE-INSERT triggers, so a regression that ever touched the wrong row would leak through updated_at on either side; (d) the cross-tenant-NotFound-vs-unknown-pair indistinguishability test must run for BOTH Get AND GetMember (the JOIN-bearing read) — divergence in either Code or Hint is an existence leak surface, and the JOIN-bearing path is a separate code path from the bare-row Get. The List isolation test takes TWO shapes that must both run: (i) disjoint-user-base count isolation (orgA has 1 member, orgB has 3, List(orgA) returns 1 — proves the WHERE-organization_id filter is present at all); (ii) shared-user-row isolation (Ada is a member of BOTH tenants, List(orgA) returns ONE row containing only orgA's view of Ada, List(orgB) returns ONE row containing only orgB's view of Ada — proves the JOIN does not produce a row-per-(membership × every memberships row for the same user_id) duplication). Document the deliberate ABSENCE of soft-delete tests (memberships has no deletion_scheduled_at) AND the cross-table cascade tests (cascades INTO memberships from users/organizations are proved by the parent-table tests TestUserRepositoryDeleteCascadesToMemberships and TestTenantHierarchyCascadeDelete, not here) in the file's package-doc comment. CRITICAL SEED-VALUE GOTCHA: the memberships_role_check CHECK constraint on memberships restricts role to {owner, admin, member} ONLY — the broader {owner, admin, developer, viewer, ci, support} set is the GRANTS-table role enum (project_grants/environment_grants), not memberships. Tests that seed "developer" or "viewer" into memberships will fail with `new row for relation "memberships" violates check constraint "memberships_role_check" (SQLSTATE 23514)`. Forward-applicable to BE-0432 (service_accounts tenant isolation: a tenant-scoped table with an organization_id COLUMN and an own id, so the BE-0426 organizations template is the closer fit — but the "same logical entity across two tenants" angle does not apply to service_accounts the way it does to memberships, because a service_account row has no shared-identity column the way memberships shares user_id with the global users table) and BE-0434 (api_keys tenant isolation: same shape as service_accounts).
- Repository tenant-isolation test file for a **tenant-scoped row with its own id, organization_id COLUMN, NO version column, NO generic Update, and NO soft-delete column** — only Insert + Disable lifecycle flip (BE-0432 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/serviceaccount_tenant_isolation_test.go). The BE-0428 user_tenant_isolation_test.go and BE-0430 membership_tenant_isolation_test.go shapes are the templates, but four substitutions are mandatory because service_accounts has its OWN id (no shared-identity column the way memberships shares user_id with the global users table) and the load-bearing cross-row failure mode is "two tenants happen to share a slug (UNIQUE (organization_id, slug) permits this by design) and a WHERE-on-slug-only or WHERE-on-id-only mutation swaps the WRONG tenant's row": (a) every byte-identical-snapshot test seeds BOTH tenants with service accounts holding the SAME slug via a `seedServiceAccountWithSlug(t, db, f, org, label, slug)` helper that overrides the factory's slug — a WHERE-on-slug mistake would resolve to whichever row the planner found first and the per-tenant id assertion would catch it (the BE-0430 "same user, distinct role/role_version tuples" framing translates here to "different ids, SAME slug"; the inverse is the only cross-row leak surface a tenant-root-with-its-own-id table exposes); (b) the Disable bystander test is the analogue of BE-0430's UpdateRole bystander — Disable is the only mutation beyond Insert, so the BE-0428 generic Update test does not apply; the trigger dual-anchor (created_at preserved + updated_at refreshed) PLUS the lifecycle field (disabled_at == nil) on the bystander row catch any WHERE-on-slug-only Disable that ever matched the wrong row; (c) the duplicate-Insert Conflict bystander test snapshots BOTH the conflicting target tenant's row AND the same-slug-different-tenant bystander row AND a post-state CountByOrganization == 1 for each (since the trigger is BEFORE-UPDATE only, a rolled-back INSERT that resolved its UNIQUE check against the cross-tenant row would have no trigger anchor — Count is the second observable surface a row landing in the wrong tenant could leak through, mirroring the BE-0431 invariants-file Count-after-rollback rule); (d) the cross-tenant-NotFound-vs-unknown-id indistinguishability test must run for BOTH Get AND Disable (the only two NotFound-emitting paths the repository exposes) — divergence in Code or Hint is an existence leak surface, and the mutation path is a separate code path from the read; afterward, re-read the foreign tenant's row and assert disabled_at == nil so the cross-tenant Disable probe did not silently flip the lifecycle. The List isolation test takes TWO shapes that must both run (mirrors BE-0430): (i) disjoint-fixture count isolation (orgA=1 SA, orgB=3 SAs, gotA must contain only saA's id, gotB must contain exactly {saB1, saB2, saB3} — proves no JOIN scrambled which rows land where); (ii) shared-slug-row isolation (saA and saB both with slug "shared-ci-slug", List(orgA) returns exactly one row with id=saA, List(orgB) returns exactly one row with id=saB — proves a SELECT disambiguating by slug instead of by organization would have either swapped or merged the two rows). One additional CountByOrganization-specific test seeds three tenants (orgA=2, orgB=3, orgC=0 empty bystander) and asserts the three distinct counts; this is the quota-layer leak surface (Count is the read the quota engine consults to enforce per-organization limits, so a leak inflates one tenant's effective quota with another's usage). Document the deliberate ABSENCE of soft-delete tests (service_accounts has no deletion_scheduled_at — only disabled_at, which the byte-identical Disable snapshot treats as the analogue) AND the deliberate ABSENCE of generic-Update / DELETE / cascade tests (Disable is the only mutation; the api_keys.service_account_id cross-tenant FK leak proof lives in serviceaccount_test.go's TestServiceAccountAPIKeyCannotCrossTenantBoundary; the cascade-on-org-delete proof lives in TestServiceAccountBelongsToOneOrganization and TestTenantHierarchyCascadeDelete) in the file's package-doc comment so a future reader does not look for a missing test (mirrors BE-0428/BE-0430's deliberate-absence note). Note on apierr.NotFound message vs Hint: NotFound("service_account", id) Newf-builds a Message containing the caller-supplied id verbatim, but never sets Hint — so the cross-tenant-vs-unknown-id indistinguishability check MUST compare Code and Hint only (Message would diverge by caller input, which is not a leak). - Repository CRUD invariants test file for a **tenant-scoped row with its own id, organization_id COLUMN, NO version column, THREE distinct UPDATE paths (UpdateMutable / Revoke / RotateCredential), an additional UPDATE-but-not-mutation-state path (TouchLastUsed), and a secret-bearing row body (secret_hash + globally-UNIQUE prefix)** (BE-0433 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/api_key_repository_invariants_test.go). After the burst, the test builds two maps (expected: the closed set of synthesized request_ids; observed: the set of request_ids on captured events) and reports both missing-in-observed (a dropped emission OR a cross-write that overwrote one emitter's RequestID with another's — both surface here) AND unexpected-in-observed (a spurious event OR a cross-write that produced a new request_id under contention). Asserting on the SET (not just the count) is what catches the cross-write regression — a recorder that swapped two emitters' RequestIDs under a race would pass the count assertion but fail the set diff. Forward-applicable to every verification story whose contention burst's contract is "every emitter's identifying field is preserved on its recorded event": build expected/observed sets keyed on the emitter-unique identifier, then diff both ways. Three BE-0394-specific extensions to the chaos-classification template, all forward-applicable to ANY future chaos-Postgres / chaos-network-partition / chaos-rate-limit sibling whose subject is the store layer or any pgxpool-backed dependency: (1) `NEW IN-PROCESS FAKE NETWORK ENDPOINT FOR PGX` — unlike BE-0393's dokployfake (which exists as a long-standing HTTP test double under internal/controlplane/dokploy/dokployfake), there was no fakepg before this story. The minimal viable shape is a TCP listener on 127.0.0.1:0 that does NOT speak the Postgres wire protocol — it accepts the TCP connection (so pgx's dial completes successfully — important: graceful FIN, NOT RST via SetLinger(0), because RST races the dial on some kernels and surfaces as `connection reset by peer` on connect rather than the production failure mode of "dial succeeds, handshake fails") and then closes the conn, so pgx observes EOF on its startup-handshake read. The fake exposes a FIFO Fault queue (only DisconnectFault for now), a Host()/Port()/Addr() trio for DSN construction, an AcceptedConnections() counter so the harness can assert pgx made >=1 TCP attempt per op (a regression that short-circuited pgx without ever attempting a network connect would otherwise pass silently), Close() (idempotent), New(testing.TB) for tests inside the testing package, and NewServer() error for worker-goroutine constructors that cannot satisfy testing.TB. Forward-applicable to every future chaos-Postgres sibling: add SQLErrorFault (writes an ErrorResponse before closing — would require pgproto3 dependency from pgx), LatencyFault (delays the close), AuthFailFault (writes a FATAL ErrorResponse during startup). (2) `CLASSIFIER-WRAP CONTRACT, NOT END-TO-END CALLSITE WRAP` — unlike BE-0393's chaos test which exercises real production methods on the typed Dokploy client (c.GetDeployment, c.EnsureOrganization, c.RemoveService) so the test asserts on errors the client's PRODUCTION wrapping chokepoint already produced, BE-0394's chaos test exercises raw pgxpool ops (Pool.Ping, Pool.Acquire, Pool.Begin, Pool.Exec, Pool.Query) and EXPLICITLY wraps the resulting pgx error through apierr.StoreUnavailable inside the runtime member before asserting the contract. This is because the store layer does not currently route every call site through a single classifier chokepoint the way the Dokploy client does — store call sites return raw pgx errors and the wrapping happens at handler-shim boundaries. The chaos contract therefore pins the wrapper's behaviour given realistic pgx-derived errors, not every call site's wrapping behaviour. Forward-applicable to any verification story whose subject lacks a single production classifier chokepoint: assert the wrapper given realistic causes, not the production path. When a future story (BE-04xx) adds a store-layer classifier chokepoint, the chaos test can switch to invoking that chokepoint instead — the scenario table and the redaction/dependency/code assertions stay identical. (3) `ASYMMETRIC REDACTION CONTRACT — PASSWORD AT EVERY LEVEL, USERNAME AT WRAPPER ONLY` — pgx's connect error formatter intentionally includes the DSN username in error messages (for operator debuggability) but redacts the password. The chaos test's chaosPostgresSecretMarkers (cause-chain scan) therefore lists ONLY the password sentinel; the wrapper-envelope assertion (chaosPostgresEnvelopeMarkers) lists BOTH the password and the username sentinel because apierr.StoreUnavailable's rendered message is static ("the Yalla datastore is temporarily unavailable") and MUST NOT echo ANY pgx cause-chain content. The runtime member walks errors.Unwrap chain for the password marker AND asserts the wrapper envelope's rendered Error() string for both markers. Forward-applicable: any future chaos test whose subject is a wire-protocol library that includes debug info in errors should split the redaction contract into chain-level (real secrets only) + envelope-level (anything pgx-style libraries might leak into debug strings). The sentinel-literal approach (chaosPostgresSentinelPassword="yallachaossecret_DO_NOT_LEAK_42") keeps the assertion meaningful: if the wrapper EVER started embedding the cause's message, the sentinel would surface and the gate would trip on the first observation. Per-iteration setup cost is bounded by chaosPostgresConnectTimeout=750ms (per-attempt pgx connect deadline) which is strictly less than chaosPostgresOpTimeout=2s (per-op context deadline), so the burst (5 scenarios × 4 workers × 3 iterations = 60 iterations) completes in ~0.5s wall-clock.

(2) `TWO-ENTRY PRD PIN — `requiredLocalCommands` AND `requiredBackendCommands`` — unlike every prior verification-suite story (BE-0379..BE-0390) that pinned a single PRD command entry (BE-0379 in requiredLocalCommands, BE-0380..BE-0390 in requiredBackendCommands), BE-0391 pins BOTH: `go test -race ./...` in requiredLocalCommands AND `go test -race ./internal/controlplane/...` in requiredBackendCommands. (2) `CROSS-TENANT MATRIX TWIN` — the canonical-funcs list is a PAIR (TestPolicyMatrix + TestPolicyMatrixDeniesCrossTenant), not a triple (BE-0382) or a single (hypothetical), because the policy engine has TWO load-bearing matrix invariants: in-tenant decisions (Decide's main path: ReasonAllowedSelf / ReasonAllowedByRole / ReasonDeniedNoCapability per `builtinRoleCaps[role].has(required)`) and cross-tenant decisions (Decide's cross-tenant clause: ReasonAllowedSelf for CapSelf, ReasonAllowedBySupport for support's CapSupport bridging CapRead/CapSupport only, ReasonDeniedCrossTenant for everything else). The two matrices are STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL (same role × action cross-product, same engine, same fixtures) but differ in resource scope (resourceIn(orgA) vs resourceIn(orgB)) and in the expected-verdict switch. Forward-applicable to ANY future security-verification story whose invariant has a "happy path × foreign-scope path" dual: BE-0398 (tenant isolation), BE-0404 (break-glass), BE-0407 (service desired-state goldens). The cross-tenant variant's switch MUST encode the engine's exact cross-tenant clause — guessing it from intuition (e.g. assuming Support is always allowed cross-tenant) fails the matrix because the engine ALSO checks the required cap via `roleCaps.has(CapSupport) && (required == CapRead || required == CapSupport)`. Verify by tracing engine.Decide BEFORE writing the test's expected-verdict switch. The single-file shape is the BE-0354 dependency_scan pattern carried forward to the verification-suite family. (2) CLOSED EXEMPT SET WITH RATIONALE — every exemption in allowedPackagesWithoutUnitTests MUST carry a rationale that points to where coverage actually lives, not just a "thin entrypoint" hand-wave. The rationale is what makes a future review decide whether to keep, extend, or remove the entry; without it the set drifts. Current exempt set: cmd/yalla (Cobra entrypoint, behaviour in internal/cli), cmd/yalla-api (process wiring, behaviour in internal/controlplane/*), cmd/yalla-worker (loop wiring, behaviour in internal/controlplane/worker), internal/controlplane/jobs (doc.go placeholder). (5) PURE FUNCTION SPLIT — findPackagesMissingTests takes (root, exempt, ignored) and is called once by the runtime test against the real repo AND multiple times by the self-check with synthetic trees built via t.TempDir + mkFile helper. The self-check is what proves the walker doesn't false-positive on test-only dirs and doesn't false-negative on ignored subtrees. (6) CASE-SENSITIVE SUBSTRING CONSTANTS — `requiredSecuritySectionSubstrings` are matched verbatim against the doc, so a substring like "every Go package" will NOT match a sentence-start "Every Go package". When the doc text naturally starts a sentence with the substring, use the capitalised form in the constant. The first run caught this: the test failed with `missing required substring "every Go package"`; the fix aligned the constant with the doc, not the doc with the constant. The self-check fixture (synthetic SECURITY.md inside TestVerificationSuiteUnitTestsAnalyzerDetectsRegressions) must be updated in the same edit — if the synthetic fixture starts to fail, the test diagnostic explicitly says "fix the fixture, not the test" to prevent the wrong direction of fix. (7) NON-MAIN, NON-DOC-ONLY PACKAGE WITHOUT TESTS IS NEVER EXEMPT-WORTHY — prefer adding 2-3 small tests (e.g. internal/credentials IsNotFound + IsUnsupported + Store-interface compile-time pin) over expanding the exemption set. The exemption set is reserved for thin main-glue and `doc.go`-only placeholders. Adding the keyring_test.go tests took ~70 lines and was strictly preferable to a `internal/credentials` exemption entry, because the package has real classification logic (errors.Is over upstream keyring sentinels) that a future upstream rename could silently break. (8) PRD AS A VERIFICATION SURFACE — the prd.json's `verificationLoop.requiredLocalCommands` array is itself part of the contract. An AI agent reads the PRD before picking up a story; pinning the suite command there guarantees the agent sees it without needing to discover CI workflows or shell scripts. The matcher uses encoding/json with a partial struct (`{VerificationLoop struct{RequiredLocalCommands []string `json:"requiredLocalCommands"`}}`) so a future PRD schema extension doesn't break it. (9) CI MATRIX AS PART OF THE CONTRACT — pinning ubuntu-latest + macos-latest + windows-latest is what prevents a silent "we only test on Linux now" regression. The matrix dimension is a separate substring assertion per host so the failure diagnostic names the missing host explicitly. Forward-applicable to BE-0380 (repository integration tests — replace findPackagesMissingTests with findStoreTestsMissingTenantIsolation), BE-0381 (HTTP handler contract tests — replace with findHandlersMissingContractTest), BE-0382 (OpenAPI conformance — replace with findEndpointsMissingOpenAPI), BE-0383 (policy matrix), BE-0384 (quota concurrency), BE-0385 (job worker leases), BE-0386 (fake Dokploy contract), BE-0387 (redaction), BE-0388 (validator fuzz), BE-0389 (migrations from empty DB), BE-0390 (migration downgrade), BE-0391 (race detector), and every future P=1 verification-suite story. The pattern is the next-strongest form of the BE-0354 (dependency_scan) single-file multi-surface pattern, applied to a meta-contract whose subject is the test suite itself rather than a specific security control. The two pattern families share: (i) single file, (ii) closed substring/constant set per surface, (iii) self-check with synthetic fixtures driving every matcher. They differ in: (i) BE-0379-family stories have a `findPackagesMissingTests`-style repo walker as their primary matcher (the security-control family has no such walker; their primary matcher is an AST scan over package source); (ii) BE-0379-family stories pin the PRD itself (security-control stories generally don't); (iii) BE-0379-family stories use a closed exempt set with per-entry rationale (security-control stories use closed constant lists like `forbiddenSecretEnvFragments` but no per-entry rationale).
- Security-verification cross-package secret-confinement pattern, Dokploy-token instance (BE-0361 pattern, internal/release/dokploy_token_isolation_static_test.go + internal/controlplane/config/dokploy_token_isolation_test.go + SECURITY.md "## Dokploy Token Isolation" section + internal/controlplane/dokploy/AGENTS.md "Token isolation (BE-0361)" subsection; SEVENTH worked instance of the BE-0344 two-test template and FIRST cross-package instance — confirms the template scales from "this single function MUST honour rule X" (BE-0346) and "this directory MUST NOT import surface Y" (BE-0357 admin endpoints, BE-0349 SSRF) to "this scarce in-process secret MUST flow from source-of-truth package A through redaction package B into wire-emission package C with NO leak surface in customer-facing package D". Six load-bearing rules: (1) TRAILING-SELECTOR-NAME matching — when the field name is unambiguously the secret in the codebase ("DokployToken" is unique to the Config secret field, no other struct has a field of the same name), match by `SelectorExpr.Sel.Name == "DokployToken"` regardless of the receiver. This catches `config.DokployToken`, `cfg.DokployToken`, `c.DokployToken`, and any future-receiver shape alike, in ONE matcher rule, where the package-qualified-only variant would miss the `c.DokployToken` form a method using a `*config.Config` receiver would naturally write. The receiver-name freedom is the load-bearing rule: any closed list of qualifiers (`config.`, `cfg.`, …) is brittle to local-naming choices in a future refactor. (2) RETURN-FALSE-FROM-INSPECT to suppress double-counting when a matcher fires on a parent node whose children would ALSO match — `config.EnvDokployToken` is both a SelectorExpr (X=`config`, Sel=`EnvDokployToken`) and contains an inner `EnvDokployToken` Ident that the bare-Ident matcher would also flag. Returning `false` from the `ast.Inspect` callback after emitting the SelectorExpr diagnostic stops descent and keeps the count at 1. The self-check fixture `handler that reads config.EnvDokployToken is rejected` pins this — without the `return false` it would fail with `got 2, want 1`. (3) COUNT-AND-PIN-LOCATION instead of count-only — for invariants where the secret MUST appear at exactly one structural location (here, `c.token` in `client.go`'s Authorization header), the matcher returns the full set of `file:line:col` triples across every production file in the package, the test asserts `len == 1` AND the single hit's path-prefix equals the canonical file. A count-only assertion would let a future refactor move the line to a different file silently; a path-only assertion would let a duplicate slip in. The two assertions in series are strictly stronger than either alone. The constructor's `token: token` binding (a `KeyValueExpr.Key`, not a `SelectorExpr`) is NOT counted by construction — `ast.Inspect` walks the Key as an `Ident`, not a `SelectorExpr`, so the matcher's `SelectorExpr` pivot skips it for free. The self-check fixture `constructor binding token: token is NOT counted` pins this distinction. (4) COMPOSITE-LITERAL-FIELD-VALUE inspection for redaction-seam invariants — `(*Config).Redacted()` returns a `RedactedConfig{...}` composite literal whose `DokployToken` field value MUST be a CallExpr to the local `redact(...)` closure. The matcher uses `findMethodOnReceiver(file, "Config", "Redacted")` (a small helper that walks `file.Decls` filtering `FuncDecl.Recv.List[0].Type` against both `*ast.Ident` and `*ast.StarExpr` receivers), then walks the method body looking for ANY composite literal containing a `DokployToken` KeyValueExpr, then asserts the value is a CallExpr with `Fun.Name == "redact"`. Three orthogonal regressions fire one diagnostic each: missing method, missing field in the literal, bare-selector value instead of a call. The same pattern applies to ANY future "method M MUST stamp field F through helper H before returning" structural rule. (5) USES-FIRST gate for defence-in-depth log surfaces — `(*Config).LogValue()` MUST call `c.Redacted()` first AND MUST NOT touch `c.DokployToken` directly. The matcher walks the method body, tracking `seenRedactedCall` (set when a `c.Redacted()` CallExpr is found) and emitting a diagnostic for EVERY `c.DokployToken` SelectorExpr seen. The two diagnostics are independent — a method that called `c.Redacted()` but ALSO read `c.DokployToken` directly would fire one; a method that omitted the call but had no direct read would fire the other; a method that did both would fire both. Forward-applicable to any "MUST consult helper H before reading secret S" pattern (variables LogValue, future credentials redactor, etc.). (6) MARKER-PATTERN runtime gate at the projection seams — three table-driven tests in `dokploy_token_isolation_test.go` install a fixed `BE0361DOKPLOYTOKENMARKERXYZ` prefix on the Config.DokployToken field and assert the marker never appears in (a) the `json.Marshal(c.Redacted())` byte stream, (b) the `slog.JSONHandler` output under `slog.Any("config", c)`, and (c) the `c.String()` debug projection — for EACH of three fixtures: short-token (canonical), long-token (longer than the redactor's sentinel, longer than any reasonable line-buffered slog chunk so a partial-flush leak would still surface), and collision-prefix (token prefix collides with the projection's field name `dokploy_token`, so a regression that truncated at the field-name boundary would still trip the marker check). The marker is the leak detector — asserting on token bytes alone would false-positive whenever the value happens to equal a substring of the stable projection text. (7) GOLANGCI-LINT S1025 gotcha — staticcheck (under golangci-lint v2) flags `fmt.Sprintf("%s", x)` as redundant when `x` has a `String()` method, suggesting `x.String()` instead. For BE-0361 the intent of the runtime test was to PROVE that `fmt.Sprintf("%s", cfg)` doesn't leak, but since `fmt.Sprintf` with `%s` against a Stringer DELEGATES to `.String()`, calling `.String()` directly exercises the same code path and satisfies the linter. The test comment must explicitly document the equivalence so a future reader understands why the seemingly indirect "%s" check is actually identical to the direct Stringer invocation. The same gotcha applies to any future Stringer-surface security test.
- Security-verification package-confinement pattern, backup-encryption instance (BE-0362 pattern, internal/release/backup_encryption_static_test.go + internal/controlplane/backup/encryption_isolation_test.go + SECURITY.md "## Backup Encryption" section + SECURITY.md Required Verification Gates table row + internal/controlplane/backup/AGENTS.md "Backup encryption boundary (BE-0362)" subsection; EIGHTH worked instance of the BE-0344 two-test template and FIRST whole-package-confinement instance — confirms the template scales from "this single function MUST honour rule X" (BE-0346), "this directory MUST NOT import surface Y" (BE-0357 admin endpoints, BE-0349 SSRF), and "this cross-package secret MUST flow through one seam" (BE-0361 Dokploy token) to "this leaf package MUST NOT carry an entire data plane". Eight load-bearing rules: (1) IMPORT-WHITELIST-AS-FORBIDDEN-LIST — the backup package's only legitimate I/O is os.ReadFile on the operator-supplied status path, so the gate enumerates the symmetric/asymmetric cipher set (crypto/aes, crypto/cipher, crypto/des, crypto/rc4, crypto/rsa, crypto/ecdsa, crypto/ed25519, crypto/tls), the archive/compression set (archive/zip, archive/tar, compress/gzip, compress/zlib, compress/flate, compress/bzip2), the database driver set (database/sql, github.com/jackc/pgx/v5, github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool), and the process-boundary set (os/exec, net/http) as a closed forbidden map. The set is intentionally aggressive because the boundary contract is "no data plane", not "this specific library is bad"; a future contributor who needs one of these libraries must surface the design change in review, not slip it in. (2) INTERFACE-METHOD-COUNT-AND-NAMES — the read-only Reporter interface is pinned by name AND by its single method's name (Status). The matcher locates the InterfaceType named Reporter, rejects every field in iface.Methods.List whose len(Names)==0 (embedded interfaces would let any method through, e.g. embed io.Writer would silently expand the surface), and rejects every named method whose Name != "Status". A missing interface fires a separate "missing required interface" diagnostic — a future refactor that renamed Reporter to BackupSurface would silently disable the gate otherwise. (3) CALL-EXPR-SELECTOR write-seam scan — the package MUST NOT call package-qualified write/exec functions. The matcher walks every CallExpr, asserts call.Fun is a SelectorExpr whose X is an ast.Ident (package alias) and joins pkg.Name + "." + sel.Sel.Name to compare against forbiddenBackupWriteSeams (os.Create, os.CreateTemp, os.WriteFile, os.OpenFile, os.Mkdir, os.MkdirAll, os.Rename, os.Remove, os.RemoveAll, os.Symlink, os.Link, os.Truncate, os.Chmod, os.Chown, exec.Command, exec.CommandContext). os.ReadFile / os.Stat / os.Open are deliberately excluded — they are the legitimate read-only seams. (4) MARKER-PATTERN runtime evidence with FOUR encryption-shaped fixtures — a parameterised subtest installs the BE0362KMSMARKERXYZ prefix inside four payload shapes (kms-key-id with arn:aws:kms:, aes-wrap-blob with base64-shaped repeated bytes, restore-failed-message with multi-line bucket URL, pem-private-key with BEGIN/END markers) and asserts the marker never appears in (a) err.Error(), (b) every errors.Unwrap layer (TestFileReporterEncryptionMarkerSurvivesErrorWrapping walks the wrap chain — a regression that wrapped raw content inside a deeper %w would be caught), or (c) json.Marshal(Status) (defensive: the struct has no content field today, but a future Detail field would surface the operator's accidentally-seeded payload through every downstream projection). (5) FIXTURE-SHAPE diversity for redaction robustness — every fixture exercises a different class of regression a future "improvement" to the parse-error message might introduce; the marker is what makes the leak detector load-bearing across all four shapes, because asserting on the fixture's full content would false-positive whenever the content happens to share a substring with a stable error phrase (e.g. a fixture containing "is malformed" would trip the existing "backup: status file is malformed" message). (6) WRAP-ROBUST DOC SUBSTRINGS — when pinning Markdown content from a wrapped document (SECURITY.md and the runbook), choose substrings short enough to survive line wrapping. The first iteration used "Plaintext WAL must never" and "no read access" — both spanned line wraps in the source files ("Plaintext WAL must\n   never" and "**no** read access") and the test fired false positives. Fix: use "Plaintext WAL" and "read access" — same semantic, robust to Markdown wrap and to **bold** runs. The closed substring list still names every load-bearing fact (KMS-managed key for at-rest, read access for the no-access invariant, Plaintext WAL for the WAL ban, Auditability for restore audit events) without being brittle to formatting. (7) DUAL-DOC PIN — the gate pins TWO operator-facing documents: SECURITY.md (the public posture) AND docs/operations/backup-restore.md (the operator runbook). Each gets its own test function with its own heading constant and closed substring set. Pinning both prevents a future "tidy" pass from collapsing one without the other — the operator-facing runbook is part of the public contract because operators rely on it to discover the KMS rotation cadence, the no-read-access invariant, and the audit-event posture. (8) SELF-CHECK with KNOWN-GOOD AND KNOWN-BAD pairs for EVERY matcher — TestBackupEncryptionStaticAnalyzerDetectsRegressions feeds three pairs (imports, reporter-interface, write-seams) through every matcher. Each known-bad fixture must produce ≥N hits (N matches the synthetic regression count); each known-good fixture must produce zero false positives. The reporter-interface self-check has a THIRD synthetic — a renamed interface (Surface) — that proves the matcher fires a "missing required interface" diagnostic when Reporter is removed, not just when its method set widens. A self-check that only feeds known-bad through the matcher cannot catch over-tightening (a matcher that fires on legitimate code would still satisfy the bad-fixture assertions); a self-check that only feeds known-good cannot catch under-tightening (a matcher that fires on nothing would still satisfy the good-fixture assertions). Both pairs are load-bearing. Forward-applicable to ANY future security-verification story whose invariant is "this leaf package MUST NOT carry a data plane for cross-cutting concern X" — credential vaulting (the secrets package must not encrypt under a process-resident key), audit shipping (the audit package must not network out to a SIEM), rate-limit storage (the ratelimit package must not persist a token-bucket distributed store), backup restore orchestration (a future restore package's port shape), and KMS proxying (any future package that mediates KMS calls).

- Log-redaction fuzz harness, single-test runtime-only variant (BE-0359 pattern, internal/output/redact_fuzz_test.go + SECURITY.md "## Log Redaction Fuzzing" section + internal/output/AGENTS.md "Log redaction fuzzing (BE-0359)" subsection; FIRST worked instance of the single-test runtime-only shape called out in the BE-0344 pattern's closing line — applies to verification stories whose invariant is a runtime contract with NO static analog, e.g. log redaction fuzzing, idempotency replay, chaos tests for timeouts). Six load-bearing rules: (1) FUZZ-MARKER design — when proving a structural redaction rule scrubs the value-half of a transport pattern, bracket the fuzz-supplied value with a unique fixed marker (`"FUZZAUTHMARKERXYZ"`, `"FUZZQRYMARKERZYX"`) and assert the marker never appears in the redacted output. The marker is the leak detector, independent of the value's bytes. Asserting that the value-bytes do not appear false-positives whenever the value happens to equal a substring of the test's static suffix (e.g. `"example"` if the test constructs `Host: example.com`). The marker pattern is reusable for ANY future fuzz target that proves "structural rule X scrubs the value half of transport Y" — cookies, refresh tokens, future header/query patterns. (2) REGEX-VALUE-CLASS gotcha — Go's `regexp` `\s` is exactly `[\t\n\f\r ]`; vertical-tab (`\v`) is NOT in `\s` but form-feed (`\f`) IS. When constructing a fuzz value that must traverse a regex value class without being cut short, strip every character in the regex's exclusion set including every member of Go's `\s`. The first revision missed `\f` and a seed containing it ended the regex mid-value, surviving the marker bracket and producing a false-positive leak. (3) DEFENCE-IN-DEPTH interactions — when two structural rules can both fire on a fuzz value (e.g. a query value containing `AUTHORIZATION:` triggers the bearer regex which eats the rest of the URL), assert ONLY the safety property (marker absent), NOT cosmetic properties (non-secret params survive). Document the interaction in the test file so a future reader understands why the survival assertion is absent. (4) SENTINEL-OVERLAP scope-out — `Redactor.Redact` uses `strings.ReplaceAll(s, secret, Sentinel)`; if `secret` is a substring of `Sentinel` (e.g. `"REDA"` inside `"[REDACTED]"`), the second pass rewrites the freshly-inserted sentinel substring and the function is NOT idempotent. Skip these inputs in fuzz AND pin the exclusion in a regression test (`TestRedactor_FuzzScopeExclusionsAreReal`) so a future redactor fix (single-pass regex substitution that does not re-scan substituted text) deliberately breaks that test and forces a coordinated update to the fuzz scope, the SECURITY.md section, and the AGENTS.md note. (5) SEED-CORPUS vs `-fuzz` — `go test ./...` runs every seed in `f.Add` once, so the seed corpus is the regression net every commit exercises; `-fuzz` is operator-opt-in. When adding a new redaction rule, the worked pattern is: append a seed input to `redactFuzzSeeds` that triggers the new rule, add a fuzz target if the rule has a distinct structural shape, and update both the AGENTS.md and SECURITY.md sections at the same time. (6) `-fuzztime` SHUTDOWN quirk — `go test -fuzz=… -fuzztime=5s` with the default 16 workers sometimes reports `context deadline exceeded` at shutdown; this is a harness-internal timing quirk, not a real fuzz failure (no `testdata/fuzz/…` corpus file is written). Re-running with `-parallel=2` makes the shutdown cleaner. Forward-applicable to any future security-verification story whose invariant has no AST shape to gate (BE-0360 environment-variable redaction if the rule is purely "the variables service MUST pass every rendered value through the redactor before logging" with no AST shape; BE-0363 rate-limit bypass resistance; chaos-tests for timeouts; idempotency replay).

(2) The directory scan is bounded by a SINGLE small helper (`adminProductionFiles(t, root) -> []string`) that returns ONLY non-`_test.go` `.go` files plus the entry binary, sorted for deterministic diagnostics; test files are deliberately skipped because a future runtime regression test needs to mention the threat without tripping the gate. (8) The runtime evidence half is implicit (the existing `notFoundRecorder` returns the stable `yalla.error.v1` envelope for any `/debug/*` request) — same single-test-file shape as BE-0355 and BE-0356. Forward-applicable to: any future security-verification story whose invariant is 'no production source file under directory D may carry shape X', including future stories for forbidden environment-variable echoes, forbidden log-format strings, forbidden cipher-suite literals, or forbidden file-scheme URL literals.
- TLS and proxy header trust static-pin pattern (BE-0356, internal/release/http_server_hardening_static_test.go + SECURITY.md "## TLS Termination and Proxy Header Trust" section AND a new row in the Required Verification Gates table + internal/release/AGENTS.md "TLS and proxy header trust" subsection; FIRST instance of the BE-0355 single-test-file template applied to GO SOURCE FILES instead of declarative manifests; structural template for ANY future security-verification story whose invariant lives in (a) the construction shape of a typed struct literal in production Go code AND (b) the closed allow-list of string literals consulted in a designated function body). Six load-bearing rules: (1) The test file MUST use `package release_test` (NOT `package release`) so the canonical `projectRoot(t)` helper from release_test.go is in scope — the other static-pin tests in internal/release follow the same convention and a mismatched package gives an undefined-symbol build error at link time. (2) The struct-literal scan uses a package-qualified type selector helper (`isHTTPServerCompositeLit` matches a SelectorExpr with X=`http`, Sel=`Server`) so unrelated structs in the same source file are not scanned. Two closed sets ride on this matcher: `requiredHTTPServerFields = {ReadHeaderTimeout}` (every literal MUST include them, missing field = regression) and `forbiddenAPITLSStructFields = {TLSConfig, TLSNextProto}` (presence = regression). (3) The closed-set string-literal scan needs TWO ORTHOGONAL PASSES: a scoped pass on the named function body (`ClientIP` here — every `r.Header.Get(...)` literal must be in `allowedProxyHeaderLiterals` case-sensitively) AND a file-wide pass on every BasicLit in the file (no `forbiddenProxyHeaderLiterals` literal anywhere, case-insensitively). One pass is insufficient because a regression could land in a sibling helper added later; the file-wide pass catches that. Both passes share the same diagnostic prefix so operators see a consistent error format. (4) The scoped pass MUST also assert a required-identifier presence (`RemoteAddr` here — the fallback chain) AND emit a single 'missing function' hit if the named function is absent entirely, so the gate cannot pass silently when its target is removed by refactor. (5) SECURITY.md is the human-facing co-contract: the test pins (a) a verification-gate row in the Required Verification Gates table (with the `-run <Prefix>` selector — use a single shared test-function name prefix like `TestHTTPServerHardening` so one selector covers all four tests) AND (b) a dedicated section heading AND (c) a closed list of canonical substrings (operator expectations, the closed allow-list of headers BY NAME so a reader cannot mistake the policy, the load-bearing field name like `ReadHeaderTimeout`, and the test file path itself as the link to the enforcement). Watch line breaks in SECURITY.md substrings — a typed prose paragraph reflows and the apostrophe in `operator's` can land on its own line, breaking `strings.Contains`; either rewrap to keep the canonical phrase on a single line (preferred) or split into shorter pinned substrings. (6) The self-check sub-test feeds known-good AND known-bad synthetic fixtures through every matcher — for the struct-literal scan, every required field AND every forbidden field AND every forbidden call selector gets its own isolated regression fixture, plus a multiple-regressions fixture that confirms hits compose additively (e.g. missing-field + forbidden-field + forbidden-call = 3 hits). Forward-applicable to: any future security-verification story whose invariant is 'this typed struct literal in production code MUST/MUST NOT carry field X' or 'this named function MUST consult only allow-listed string literals' (e.g. middleware composition order pins, context-key allow-lists, telemetry attribute redaction key allow-lists, future proxy-trust expansions for X-Forwarded-Proto or RFC 7239 `Forwarded` if Yalla ever adopts them).
- Container image hardening static-pin pattern (BE-0355, internal/release/container_hardening_static_test.go + SECURITY.md "Container Image Hardening" section + internal/release/AGENTS.md "Container image hardening" subsection; structural template for ANY future security-verification story whose invariant lives in a non-Go declarative file — Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .github/workflows/*.yml, .goreleaser.yaml, Kubernetes manifests, OCI runtime spec). Single-test variant of the BE-0344 two-test pattern: the "runtime" half is implicit because the build/CI pipeline IS the runtime — there is no application-code call site to drive a parallel runtime test against, so the static analyser plus the self-check IS the load-bearing defence. Six load-bearing rules: (1) The parser lives in the test file itself, not in a separate package — keeps the production package API surface clean (only the SupportedTargets matrix in internal/release) and lets future hardening stories add their own parsers without coupling. The Dockerfile parser scope is intentionally narrow: join backslash continuations into logical instructions, resolve global ARG defaults so `FROM ${RUNTIME_IMAGE}` expands to the canonical value, group instructions under their owning FROM stage. Heredocs, `--mount=type=cache` flags, and ONBUILD are deliberately opaque — the matchers work above the parser's awareness of them. (2) Every invariant gets its own matcher function plus its own in-repo test plus its own self-check sub-test. The matcher takes the parsed model and returns a self-describing error; the in-repo test runs the matcher against the real Dockerfile/compose file; the self-check sub-test drives the matcher with a synthetic known-good baseline (a `minimalCanonicalDockerfile()` helper) AND a series of mutations each isolating one regression. (3) Required-value constants live at the top of the test file: `requiredRuntimeBaseImage = "gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot"`, `requiredNonrootUser = "nonroot:nonroot"`, `requiredCopyChown = "--chown=nonroot:nonroot"`, `requiredBuilderBuildFlags = {CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, -s -w}`. Closed sets for forbidden patterns: `forbiddenSecretEnvFragments = {TOKEN, PASSWORD, SECRET, API_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, SIGNING_KEY, DSN}` (case-insensitive substring on ENV key), `forbiddenRuntimePackageInstalls = {apt-get, apt install, yum install, dnf install, apk add, microdnf install}` (substring on runtime stage's joined RUN payload). The closed-set design is deliberate — it catches the secret-shaped fragments the project's config layer actually uses, not every possible English word that contains "key", so a future ENV that holds a non-secret hint does not false-positive. (4) SECURITY.md is the human-facing co-contract: the same test file pins (a) a verification-gate row in the Required Verification Gates table AND (b) a dedicated `## Container Image Hardening` section with literal substrings (`distroless`, `nonroot`, `Multi-stage build`, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-trimpath`, `Container image hardening`). A regression that drops either is caught as deterministically as a Dockerfile regression. (5) The postgres image pin regex `^postgres:\d+$` deliberately rejects variant tags like `postgres:16-bookworm` because the local integration-test stack must remain reproducible across local environments; if a future story needs a variant the regex must widen in lockstep with the fixture catalogue. (6) Builder stage vs runtime stage have ASYMMETRIC rules: builder stages may install packages (`apt-get install git` for the goreleaser-style git tag lookup is legitimate), the runtime stage may not. The matcher pins the asymmetry by walking only the runtime stage's instructions for the package-install scan and only the builder stage's instructions for the build-flag scan. The runtime stage is identified as the LAST stage (the unnamed final FROM); the builder stage as the FIRST stage with an `AS` name. Five test-fixture gotchas: (a) when SECURITY.md and the matcher disagree on case (`multi-stage` vs `Multi-stage`), the test pins the EXACT casing the documentation file uses — Go's `strings.Contains` is case-sensitive, and pinning the documentation casing makes the matcher serve as a stability anchor for the published policy. (b) Self-check cases that mutate ONE invariant on top of a shared canonical baseline are independent by construction — a future widening of matcher M cannot accidentally pass a fixture that was constructed to test matcher N. (c) The runtime stage's `COPY --from=builder` matcher MUST scope the `--chown=` requirement to COPY instructions that ALSO carry `--from=` — a plain `COPY ./foo /etc/foo` from the build context legitimately does not need the flag because the build context's owner is the current user. (d) The `ADD <url>` matcher uses a regex anchored at start-of-args that tolerates leading `--chown=` style flags; a future addition that allows local-path `ADD` would fail this assertion only on URL shapes. (e) The Dockerfile parser silently ignores instructions that appear before the FIRST FROM (other than ARG, which becomes a global ARG default). This is the Dockerfile spec behaviour; the test relies on it so `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7` parser directives and pre-FROM comments don't accidentally count as instructions in any stage. NOT applicable to verification stories whose invariant is a runtime contract WITH an application-code call site (request body size, JSON parser hardening, log redaction fuzzing) — those follow the BE-0344 two-test (static + runtime) shape because the runtime test has a real handler/repository call site to drive.
- Tamper-resistance three-wall verification pattern (BE-0353, internal/controlplane/store/{audit_tamper_static_test.go, audit_test.go::TestAuditUpdateBlockedByDatabaseTriggerWithRestrictViolation} + internal/controlplane/store/migrate/audit_immutability_static_test.go + internal/controlplane/store/AGENTS.md "Tamper resistance" subsection; structural template for any future append-only-table story whose immutability is enforced at the database trigger AND the Go repository surface — security events, key-rotation history, billing-ledger entries, fraud alerts, anything where "the record cannot change after write" is a load-bearing contract). The pattern is THREE static-time guards plus ONE runtime probe so a weakening of any one layer is caught by another. Five load-bearing rules: (1) MIGRATION-shape pin (parse the .up.sql via embedded fs and assert four regex shapes: function declared with `ERRCODE = '<sqlstate-name>'`, trigger declared with `BEFORE UPDATE ON <table> FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION <fn>`, the `CREATE TABLE` parenthesised body extracted and scanned for any forbidden column declaration, the `.down.sql` drops both the table AND the function — DROP TABLE alone leaves the function orbiting unused). The column-scan strips `--`-prefixed lines BEFORE matching so an in-body comment like `-- intentionally no updated_at column` does not trip the probe; the matcher anchors on `^(?:\s|,)*<column>\s+[a-zA-Z]` so a bare token mentioned in prose elsewhere does not match. (2) Go-SURFACE pin (parse the implementation .go via the existing mustParseFile helper, walk file.Decls, collect every FuncDecl whose receiver is the named type, and assert the set is exactly the allowed names AND each name does not start with a known mutation-verb prefix `{Update,Delete,Patch,Replace,Modify,Truncate,Remove}` — the verb prefix is a SECOND filter so a future allowed-set drift that re-admits a mutation-shape name still fails); also pin the struct declaration has no mutation-timestamp field `{UpdatedAt,ModifiedAt,RevisedAt,LastModifiedAt}` — the SQL column absence is the migration's job, the Go field absence is the surface's job, both must hold. (3) DML-SCAN pin (walk every non-test `.go` in the owning package, find every `*ast.BasicLit` of `token.STRING` kind, unwrap raw-string and double-quoted shapes, normalise whitespace and case, and reject any literal that contains a forbidden DML substring against the target table; only the carved-out INSERT shape inside the repository's own file is allowed — every other shape is a regression flagged with `file:line: forbidden DML against <table>: "UPDATE <table>" in literal`). The case-insensitive uppercase normalisation handles lowercase shapes that snuck in via copy-paste; the whitespace normalisation handles multi-line literals like `UPDATE\n  audit_events\nSET ...`. Comments are NOT scanned — the rule targets executable code paths and a SQL example in a doc comment is fine. (4) RUNTIME-wire pin (insert a fixture row, attempt every UPDATE shape an operator might try — by id, by tenant id, table-wide without WHERE, partial-column-rewrite, verdict-reclassification — and assert each rejection surfaces a `*pgconn.PgError` with `pgErr.Code == "<sqlstate>"` AND `strings.Contains(pgErr.Message, "<canonical phrase>")` AND the row's columns are byte-identical to the original after the attempted UPDATE; PG's `restrict_violation` is SQLSTATE 23001 NOT 38000 — 38000 is external_routine_exception, an easy typo because both classes start with a 3, verify the actual wire code by running once and reading the failure). Also assert the error message does NOT echo any caller input — the trigger function is value-free by design and a future log path that interpolates the rejected payload would surface here as a redaction regression. (5) SELF-CHECK pin (drive each matcher with synthetic known-good AND known-bad inputs in subtests so a future over-tightening that false-positives on real production code AND a future under-tightening that misses a real regression are BOTH caught — the self-check is the only safety net against "I weakened my own analyser without noticing"). Six asymmetries worth knowing: (a) `audit_events` allows direct SQL `DELETE FROM ...` because the design requires ON DELETE CASCADE to work for tenant teardown — so the DML-scan flags DELETE FROM at the Go layer (no app-side delete) but the runtime test does NOT assert DELETE is blocked at the DB layer (it isn't). The migration AGENTS.md section documents this asymmetry so a future reader doesn't try to "fix" it. (b) The wire SQLSTATE for the migration's `RAISE EXCEPTION ... ERRCODE = 'restrict_violation'` is 23001 (class 23 integrity_constraint_violation) — PG remaps the symbolic name to a numeric code at trigger compile time, the SQL pins the name, the runtime test pins the code, both must stay synchronised. (c) Mutation-verb prefix detection deliberately EXCLUDES `Set` and `Get` — too broad to flag without false positives across unrelated repositories — and the closed verb set lives in `isMutationSurfaceMethodName` as a helper rather than inline so adding a new verb is a single change. (d) The struct-field forbidden list does NOT include `UpdatedBy` / `LastEditor` — those are actor-attribution fields, not mutation timestamps; the rule targets writes-to-the-record, not metadata about who touched it. (e) The migration column-scan strips `--` line comments before matching but does NOT strip `/* */` block comments — PG accepts both, but `audit_events.up.sql` uses `--` exclusively and the simpler scanner is enough; if a future migration mixes styles, extend the scanner with the same upper-vs-lower test pattern. (f) The runtime test reuses the existing `auditEventFixture` / `seedOrg` / `appendAudit` helpers from `audit_test.go` so the new test is ~150 lines of mostly cases-and-assertions; the wire-error assertions live in a `*pgconn.PgError` `errors.As` extraction (NOT a string match on err.Error()) so a future error-wrapping change at the pgx layer that preserves the typed error still surfaces the assertion.
- Cryptographic-primitive rotation contract pin (BE-0351 pattern, internal/controlplane/secrets/{key_rotation_static_test.go, key_rotation_test.go} + internal/controlplane/store/migrate/secret_routing_idx_static_test.go + internal/controlplane/secrets/AGENTS.md "Key rotation" section; structural template for any future security-verification story over a long-lived cryptographic primitive that ships a rotation surface — JWT signing keys, webhook HMAC secrets, backup-target keys, mTLS issuance keys). Three load-bearing rules: (1) The cryptographic surface is pinned by a static AST analyser, not just by behavioural tests: parse the implementation file, locate the surface methods by name (`NewAESGCM`, `ActiveKeyID`, `KeyIDs`, `Open` for AESGCM), and assert each one's structural shape — `NewAESGCM` must take `[][]byte` (not a single key), `Open` must contain a range loop over the receiver's `keys` slice (not a single-key decrypt), `Open` must return the typed `ErrUnknownKey` identifier (not a string error). Behavioural tests catch the runtime regression but a static guard catches the silent refactor before the runtime test has a chance to fail. The self-check pins both directions of every analyser with synthetic regression sources. (2) The runtime test mirrors the operator runbook line-for-line as a three-phase rotation lifecycle: pre-rotation provider seals under k_old; mid-rotation provider boots with `[k_new, k_old]` and proves (a) old ciphertext still Opens via the retired key id, (b) new Seals reference the new active key id, (c) a fresh Seal under k_new does NOT decrypt under k_old's id (returns ErrInvalidCiphertext); re-seal step (the rotation worker's loop body) Opens under retired key then Seals under active and proves round-trip plaintext intact; post-retirement provider boots with `[k_new]` only and proves a row missed by the re-seal worker surfaces ErrUnknownKey (NOT ErrInvalidCiphertext, NOT a silent plaintext recovery). The runtime test reads as the runbook does so a future operator can compare the runbook against the executable contract. (3) The redacted-projection invariant is captured at runtime with a real `slog.NewJSONHandler` writing into a `bytes.Buffer`: `logger.LogAttrs(..., slog.Any("provider", provider))`, `json.Unmarshal` the result, assert `provider.master_keys == output.Sentinel`. The leak check substring-searches the JSON record for the FULL hex of every probe (k_old, k_new, plaintext, pre/mid ciphertext) — per-byte substring checks false-positive against the SHA-256-prefix key id (the 16-char id will collide with random 2-hex pairs in any 32-byte key at ~p=1/256 per byte). The same probes are checked against `fmt.Sprintf("%s", provider)` to pin the fmt.Stringer channel (panic messages). Both channels MUST also contain at least one accepted key id — the operator's only confirmation that a rotation took effect. (4) The store-layer routing index that the rotation worker depends on is pinned by a SEPARATE sealing trap in the migration package (the `migrations/` directory contains only .sql files — no Go package — so the trap lives in `internal/controlplane/store/migrate/secret_routing_idx_static_test.go` and reads each migration via `fs.ReadFile(embeddedMigrations, ...)`). The regex matcher tolerates harmless variations (`IF NOT EXISTS`, optional whitespace, multi-line) but pins the load-bearing parts: index name, table, column order `(secret_provider, secret_key_id)`, and `WHERE is_secret = true` partial-index predicate. A migration that drops the WHERE clause widens the index from "secret rows only" to "every row", which changes the index's purpose and breaks the worker's bounded lookup; the self-check exercises eight known-bad shapes to pin this. The `requiredVariableMigrations` slice is the canonical set of `*_variables` tables — adding a new variable table without adding it here silently reduces coverage.
- Inbound-hostname domain-takeover guard, symmetric to the SSRF outbound-URL guard (BE-0350 pattern, internal/controlplane/validate/{domain_takeover.go, domain_takeover_static_test.go, domain_takeover_test.go, AGENTS.md} + network.go Domain() call site + fuzz_test.go FuzzDomain seeds; second worked port of the BE-0349 two-test SSRF template into the validate package, but for a STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT threat: INBOUND hostnames the platform agrees to ROUTE traffic for, NOT outbound URLs the worker dereferences). Six load-bearing rules the new file added on top of the inherited BE-0349 template: (a) The takeover guard MUST live in a separate helper (`disallowedTakeoverHost`) and a separate static analyzer (`callsDisallowedTakeoverHost`) from the SSRF guard — they share the two-test template but check DISJOINT sets: a host that is legitimate to ATTACH (`myapp.example.com`) may still be illegitimate to FETCH if it resolves to a private IP, and vice versa. Reusing the SSRF helper would collapse both threat models into one, hiding which rejection class applies to which surface. (b) The guard's call site goes AT THE END of `Domain` (after the FQDN/label checks), not at the start. Single-label reserved names (`localhost`, `local`, `internal`, `lan`, etc.) and IPv6 literals (a single label after the `.` split) are rejected by the existing FQDN check BEFORE reaching the guard — so the test table for `TestDomainRejectsTakeoverTargets` restricts itself to inputs that actually pass through the helper today (IPv4 dotted literals, multi-label reserved exact-matches like `home.arpa`, suffix-match cases, shared-hosting eTLD bare forms). The single-label reserved names stay in `reservedTakeoverHostnames` as defence-in-depth (a future FQDN-check loosening must still trip the takeover guard) but the runtime regression table only asserts on what's actually reachable, so a missing call site is caught by a FAILING subtest rather than a silently-skipped one. Document the layering explicitly in the file's package-doc block AND in the test file's table-header comment, so the next reader doesn't add an unreachable case and then debug for an hour. (c) The reserved-name lists must DELIBERATELY EXCLUDE the RFC 2606 documentation-only suffixes (`.test`, `.example`, `.invalid`) from the SUFFIX walk while KEEPING them in the EXACT-MATCH map. Reason: those suffixes are not publicly routable so they cannot intercept real customer traffic — they are a squatting threat (bounded by the `service_domains` UNIQUE (hostname, path) constraint) rather than a takeover threat. The httpapi service-domains test fixtures across ~7 files (`api.canonical.example`, `domain-matrix-recognisable-needle.example`, etc.) use `.example` per RFC convention; adding `.example` to the suffix walk would break every one of those tests, and the cost is asymmetric: a real takeover defence would require migrating the fixtures whereas a softer squatting defence is bounded by the UNIQUE constraint and adds no value to either threat model. Document the omission AND the asymmetry in the helper's package-doc, the AGENTS.md section, and the test file's blocked-hosts table comment — so a future reader doesn't "fix" the omission and re-break the fixtures. (d) The wildcard interaction: `Domain` strips the leading `*.` BEFORE my helper sees the host. With wildcards enabled, `*.appspot.com` reduces to `appspot.com` which the exact-match map rejects — a wildcard makes the takeover STRICTLY WORSE (the bare suffix locks one routing entry, the wildcard locks every sub-tenant of that suffix) so the wildcard rejection is load-bearing and gets its own test (`TestDomainRejectsTakeoverTargetsForWildcard`). The helper ALSO defensively strips a leading `*.` itself so it remains correct for any future caller that passes the raw value. (e) The redaction backstop (`TestDomainTakeoverReasonsAreValueFree`) must plant the canary as a SUB-LABEL of a reserved-SUFFIX host (`canary + ".lan"`), NOT a reserved-EXACT-MATCH host (`canary + "appspot.com"` would not match the exact-match map). The suffix walk's `strings.HasSuffix(h, suffix)` reduces the entire host to the suffix-class reason without inspecting the canary — so a reason containing the canary proves the validator interpolated the value. The canary string itself MUST be picked to NOT collide with any word in the canonical reason set (no "domain", "namespace", "address", "literal", "hostname") — the BE-0343 redaction lesson is that substring redaction checks false-positive on stable classification phrases. (f) The FuzzDomain seed set added one entry per documented reject category PLUS an accept-branch re-derivation: `net.ParseIP(v) != nil` and `strings.HasSuffix(v, reservedSuffix)` MUST be false for every accepted host. The accept-branch re-derivation is what makes the fuzz target actually catch a regression of the takeover guard — without it, dropping the helper would let IPv4-literal seeds pass through to the accept branch without firing any assertion (the existing FQDN+label re-derivation accepts `8.8.8.8`).
