Two load-bearing constraints: (1) the resolver builds policy.Resource{Scope: {OrganizationID = principal.home, <ResourceLevel>ID = path.id}} — pinning OrgID to the principal's home (NEVER the caller-supplied id) is the structural anti-spoof, and pinning the resource-level id is the only scope leg the path actually carries; (2) the resolver CANNOT pin the parent ids without a DB lookup, and the policy engine's Scope.covers() rule (internal/controlplane/policy/policy.go) requires every level the grant pins to match the resource — a grant with pinned ProjectID against a resource with empty ProjectID is structurally denied. Accepted design: middleware admits org-wide read roles + org-wide grants + (for CapRead actions) the support cross-tenant exception is suppressed because the resolver pins OrgID to principal.home; project-/env-/service-scoped grants are denied at the boundary by design, and grant-only principals must use the parent-scoped /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments instead. Document this in the route description, the resolver doc, and the handler doc — readers will misinterpret the structural deny as a bug otherwise. The store layer adds a tenant-scoped GetByID(ctx, q, organizationID, resourceID) on the existing repository (composite (organization_id, id) predicate so cross-tenant returns apierr.NotFound, never another tenant's row, never a 500 leaking the cause), and the existing reader struct grows a Get<Resource>(ctx, organizationID, resourceID) method that wraps GetByID inside Store.Read. The HTTP layer adds a NEW narrow port (distinct from the existing parent-scoped port — e.g. EnvironmentReader vs ProjectEnvironmentReader — so a handler change to one doesn't ripple through the other), a NEW resolver function (e.g. environmentIDResolver), and a NEW handler that REUSES the existing wire-shape projection (projectEnvironmentOf for environments) so the GET-by-id response is byte-identical to one element of the LIST response (modulo the wrapping object name). cmd/yalla-api/main.go passes the same *store.<Resource>Reader value twice — once for the parent-scoped port, once for the new bare-lookup port — because both methods live on the same store struct; no second startup wiring is needed. The contract tests cover the standard envelope: happy path, NotFound (cross-tenant + unknown both render as the same 404 — no oracle), 401 unauthenticated + invalid credentials (no token echo), 503 store outage (no raw cause leak), 500 nil-port wiring guard, envelope shape lock (asserts the documented field set against a generic decode so a future struct column added without updating the projection is caught), bearer-token never-logged guard (slog over a buffer), OpenAPI route registration, and TWO resolver unit tests (pins home org + path id; no panic with no principal on context). The matching policy matrix story (BE-0156 for environments, the structural template for service/deployment lookups) tests the deny — the deny matrix on the bare endpoint is part of the contract, not a gap.
- environment.grants.write-on-bare-{environment_id}-resolver policy matrix (BE-0171, internal/controlplane/httpapi/environment_grants_put_policy_test.go) is the structural HYBRID of the project.grants.write matrix (BE-0141, projects_grants_put_policy_test.go) and the environment.grants.read matrix (BE-0168, environment_grants_policy_test.go): take BE-0141's CapAdmin role table + cross-tenant + request-body-leak-guard skeleton, swap action+resolver for the write env-grants endpoint, and re-pin every wire tie-in with BE-0168's no-ProjectID covers() denial pattern (project/env/service scoped principals ALL denied OutOfScope at this route — even on a grant naming the SAME env id — because the env-id resolver pins NO ProjectID leg and covers() is one-way). Load-bearing engine distinction from BE-0168: CapAdmin is OUTSIDE the support cross-tenant exception, so the engine_cross_tenant_deny_* parallel subtests MUST include the Support row for write actions and exclude it for read actions. Net-new fixtures in the put_policy file are only a route-specific replaceEnvironmentGrantsMatrixBody (no environment_id field per grant — the env is named by the path) + replaceEnvironmentGrantsRequestBodyLeak with distinctive needles; the canonical*EnvGrants* fixtures, fake*EnvironmentGrant* fakes, replaceEnvironmentGrantsHandlerFor / putEnvironmentGrants / decodeReplaceEnvironmentGrants, and orgPrincipal / decodeError are all reused verbatim from BE-0168 and BE-0169.
- Inbound HTTP rate-limit pattern (BE-0035, internal/controlplane/ratelimit/limiter.go + internal/controlplane/httpapi/ratelimit.go + apierr.RateLimited + config.RateLimit): the limiter is an in-process multi-dimensional token-bucket gate (per-org, per-API-key, per-IP) with read/write-class specs derived from the HTTP method (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS = read, everything else = write). Three load-bearing rules: (1) the gate wraps every route INSIDE RequireAuth in server.go's per-route loop (`h = rateLimit(h); if RequiresAuth: h = RequireAuth(...)(h)`) so the resolved principal (org id, key id, auth method) is on the request context when the limiter decides — public endpoints fall back to the IP bucket alone; (2) the internal-worker exemption is wired through a new package-private context helper `withAuthMethod` / `AuthMethodFromContext` in middleware.go that BOTH RequireAuth and RequireInternalWorker stamp with id.Method, so the rate-limit gate can recognise auth.MethodInternalWorker and pass `Exempt=true` to the limiter without re-running the credential store; (3) the "first exhausted bucket wins" rule short-circuits downstream debits (org denied -> key & ip buckets untouched) so a single throttled tenant cannot drain a shared NAT'd IP bucket of every neighbour. Bucket map is sync.Mutex'd with lazy eviction on the request path (no background goroutine; pruning sweeps every IdleTTL); the freshly-created bucket MUST set lastUsed=now BEFORE the sweep runs so the sweep cannot reap the bucket it just inserted (initial zero-value lastUsed is older than any cutoff and was a real bug caught by tests). The 429 wire shape is the standard yalla.error.v1 envelope with apierr.RateLimited(scope, retry) attaching `scope` (bucket dimension name only — "organization" / "api_key" / "ip", NEVER the tenant id or key id or IP) and `retry_after` (integer seconds, clamped to >=1 because the wire Retry-After header cannot carry sub-second); the response also sets the matching `Retry-After: N` header. NewHandler grew ONE new trailing parameter (RateLimiter) — sweep all 64 NewHandler call sites in tests via a Node script that walks the source with depth-tracking parens and appends `, nil` before each closing `)`. Config plumbing: new YALLA_RATE_LIMIT_* env vars (ORG/KEY/IP × READ/WRITE × RPS/BURST + IDLE_TTL + DISABLED master switch) layered over per-profile defaults; ProfileTest defaults to Disabled=true so contract tests across the whole repo never accidentally trip the limiter. The limiter constructor takes a `func() time.Time` clock injection point so deterministic tests (`fixedClock.Advance(d)`) can drive refill behaviour without sleeping. Forward-applicable to any future throughput cap (per-resource, per-tenant-tier, per-route-specific) — extend Specs/Specs.For pairs rather than adding a new bucket dimension. Redaction backstops: the 429 envelope, the Retry-After header, the WARN log record on denial, and every rate-limit identifier flow through telemetry.LogAttrs / apienvelope's regex-based scrubber so a bearer-token in the Authorization header on a throttled request NEVER reaches a log file (TestRateLimitDenialLogsNoSecretValue is the regression pin).
- Pagination contract package (BE-0037, internal/controlplane/pagination): every customer-facing list endpoint composes the shared pagination.Params + pagination.Cursor + pagination.Page[T] envelope rather than reimplementing limit/cursor/sort/filter parsing. ParseParams(url.Values, ParseOptions) parses ?limit= ?cursor= ?sort= ?direction= ?filter.<k>= with stable apierr.InvalidInput (E_INVALID_INPUT) violations whose Reason text NEVER echoes the submitted value (only classification + accepted range — protects against reflection-style content channels), accumulates multiple violations into one envelope, enforces the package MaxLimit=200 ceiling even when an endpoint misconfigures its own, and rejects a cursor whose embedded Sort/Direction disagrees with the request as a stable 400 "fetch the first page again" instead of silently serving overlapping pages. Cursor is base64url-encoded JSON {v: "yalla.cursor.v1", p: Position, s: Sort, d: Direction} — opaque to clients, deterministic (same input -> same encoding so HTTP fixtures diff byte-for-byte), URL-safe (RawURLEncoding, no '+/='), and DOES NOT carry an organization_id / tenant / principal field by contract (a TestDecodeCursorTenantIsolationCannotBeBypassed test guards this so adding one is impossible without breaking the suite — tenant isolation stays the persistence layer's responsibility, cursor only encodes a within-set position). Page[T any] is the wire shape: Items always non-nil (BuildPage guarantees []T{} for empty), NextCursor omitempty (empty string == end of stream — agents do NOT compare len(Items) to limit), TotalEstimate *int64 omitempty (nil = "not cheap to compute", endpoints must NOT fabricate a value). BuildPage uses the over-fetch strategy: store fetches Limit+1 rows, BuildPage trims to Limit and encodes next_cursor from the last retained row's position via a PositionFunc[T] adapter. Cursor stability under inserts is proven end-to-end by TestCursorIsStableUnderInserts: seed N rows, page once, insert NEWER rows after the cursor boundary, prove page 2 still returns exactly the remaining originals (no duplicates, no skips, no newly-inserted rows leaking onto page 2 because the cursor is a strict upper bound on (sort_key DESC, id DESC)). Future list endpoints replace their bespoke parseXxxLimit / list payload struct with one ParseParams call + a BuildPage projection — the existing GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/audit-events (BE-0103) and break_glass list are pre-pagination-contract and should migrate in their own stories.
- Bare-id route on a deployment (BE-0211+0212+0213 pattern, GET /v1/deployments/{deployment_id}, store/deployment.go DeploymentReader.GetServiceDeployment, httpapi/deployments.go DeploymentGetter port + deploymentIDResolver + getServiceDeploymentHandler + getServiceDeploymentPayload, routes.go GET /v1/deployments/{deployment_id} entry, server.go NewHandler DeploymentGetter parameter, cmd/yalla-api/main.go wires the SAME *store.DeploymentReader as BOTH DeploymentLister AND DeploymentGetter): canonical shape for ALL bare-id read endpoints on a Deployment-level deep resource. Two LOAD-BEARING structural differences from the environment / service bare-id routes (BE-0154 / its services sibling): (1) policy.Scope has NO DeploymentID leg — the Scope hierarchy stops at ServiceID (Organization -> Project -> Environment -> Service), so the resolver pins ONLY OrganizationID, NOT (org + DeploymentID) the way environmentIDResolver pins (org + EnvironmentID). The resource scope carries no inner leg at all, which makes the engine's covers() rule deny EVERY scoped grant (project/env/service) at the boundary via ReasonDeniedOutOfScope — even a service-scoped grant naming the deployment's actual parent service is denied, because covers() is one-way (a grant scope that pins ServiceID cannot cover a resource scope that does not). Principals whose only access is a scoped grant must use a parent-scoped route family to address a deployment. (2) The store-layer adapter intentionally skips the parent-prefetch the list adapter performs: DeploymentReader.GetServiceDeployment composes only DeploymentRepository.GetByID inside a short-lived Store.Read tx (no service prefetch), because the schema's composite foreign keys on the deployments table already guarantee (organization_id, project_id), (organization_id, environment_id), and (organization_id, service_id) cannot diverge across the deployment row — a tenant-scoped GetByID is itself a complete tenant-isolation check, and a prefetch would only duplicate the work of the schema. This is the load-bearing distinction from the list adapter ListServiceDeployments (which DOES prefetch the service to disambiguate "service missing" from "service has no deployments"). The wire shape (serviceDeployment + serviceDeploymentOf in service_deployments.go) is REUSED verbatim — an agent that listed deployments for a service does not re-parse a different shape to fetch one of them by id. Production wiring passes the same *store.DeploymentReader pointer twice (deploymentService, deploymentReader, deploymentReader, breakGlassService, ...): one concrete adapter satisfies BOTH the DeploymentLister AND DeploymentGetter port interfaces, so adding a second read port costs zero new constructors / dependencies. The contract test suite (deployments_get_test.go, 12 tests) and policy matrix (deployments_get_policy_test.go, 4 parent tests) follow the BE-0210 list-side template structure verbatim, with one structural extension in the grant-containment matrix: a service-scoped grant naming THIS deployment's actual parent service is also denied at the wire, because the bare-id resource scope has no ServiceID leg to match. Future bare-id read endpoints on deep resources whose Scope leg does not exist (deployments today; jobs / runs in later stories) should adopt this exact pattern.


- Bare-id read endpoint on a deep resource with a worker-deferred upstream (BE-0229+0230+0231 pattern, GET /v1/services/{service_id}/logs, store/service_log_reader.go ServiceLogReader.ListLogs, httpapi/services_logs.go ServiceLogReader port + serviceLogLine/listServiceLogsPayload wire DTOs + parseServiceLogsLimit + listServiceLogsHandler, routes.go GET /v1/services/{service_id}/logs entry, server.go NewHandler + newRouteTable + cmd/yalla-api/main.go wiring, services_logs_test.go contract suite + services_logs_policy_test.go matrix): canonical shape for ANY observability read endpoint whose real upstream is the Dokploy worker (logs, metrics — BE-0232..0234 next; future events/traces) and whose true content adapter is deferred to a later worker story. Three load-bearing rules: (1) the store-level adapter (store.ServiceLogReader, the second instance of the typed-input-typed-output read adapter shape after store.ServiceReader.GetService) performs the tenant-scoped parent existence check inside a Store.Read transaction so a cross-tenant or unknown service_id surfaces as a deterministic apierr.NotFound at the persistence boundary — never disguised as an empty success and never disguised as a 500 — and then returns an empty Lines slice with the ServiceID populated; the real Dokploy log fetcher is wired in BE-0301+ alongside the provisioning worker, matching the noopJobEnqueuer pattern for placeholder upstreams; (2) the wire DTO is a closed tuple `(service_id, lines[]{occurred_at, stream, message})` with NO pointer-typed fields, NO embedded interfaces, and an empty lines slice that marshals as `[]` not `null` so an agent does not need to special-case the absent-vs-empty distinction; the occurred_at field is RFC3339-nanosecond UTC; the stream enum is the closed set {stdout, stderr, system} so an agent can branch on the value without escape-decoding it; (3) the ?limit= query parameter is clamped at the boundary via parseServiceLogsLimit (the second instance of the bounded-limit-query-parser shape after parseAuditEventLimit, range [1, 1000] default 100), and the error path never echoes the submitted value — only the classification and the accepted range — so a typo can never become a reflection-style content channel. The CapRead policy matrix shape is the structural sibling of services_get_policy_test.go (BE-0184) — all six built-in roles allow same-tenant via ReasonAllowedByRole, support is allowed cross-tenant via ReasonAllowedBySupport at the engine level (defence-in-depth — the customer-facing route cannot reach this branch because serviceIDResolver pins the resource to the principal's home org), every project-/env-/service-scoped grant is denied OutOfScope on the bare-service-id path via the engine's one-way covers() rule, and an org-level Viewer grant is ALLOWED end-to-end (the load-bearing distinction from services_start_policy_test.go where the same grant is denied because service.start is CapDeploy, not CapRead). Limit assertion subtlety pinned by tests: the no-echo check on the invalid-limit deny path must restrict to non-numeric submitted values because numeric out-of-range inputs may legitimately share digits with the accepted-range message ("0" is a substring of "1000" in the "must be between 1 and 1000" string) — only the non-numeric case (where caller-controlled byte content could realistically reach the response body) is asserted. Test-only nil-port test: a typed-nil ServiceLogReader is needed (a bare `nil` literal does not satisfy the interface positional argument), so `var nilReader ServiceLogReader` is the pattern. Port-arity sweep: dominant `fakeServiceStopper{}, fakeServiceVariableReader{}` -> `fakeServiceStopper{}, fakeServiceLogReader{}, fakeServiceVariableReader{}` across 63 test files (108 sites) plus a minor variant `fakeServiceStopper{}, reader, fakeServiceVariableReplacer{}` -> `fakeServiceStopper{}, fakeServiceLogReader{}, reader, fakeServiceVariableReplacer{}` in service_variables_test.go (the test injects a local fakeServiceVariableReader as `reader`, so the LogReader slot is the new positional argument); the `stopper, fakeServiceVariableReader{}` variant in services_stop_test.go is one of the 108 dominant sites. Forward-applicable to BE-0232+0233+0234 (GET /v1/services/{service_id}/metrics, metrics.read action — the OTHER CapRead observability endpoint on the same resolver), and to any future read endpoint whose true content adapter is the Dokploy worker (events, traces) — same vertical, same placeholder shape, same wire-contract guarantees while the real fetcher lands later. The OpenAPI `?limit=` query parameter today is documented only via the Description prose because openapi.Endpoint has no QueryParams field; a future BE story can add structured QueryParam metadata and the existing route entries (audit-events, logs) will switch over together. CONFIRMED two-instance pattern after BE-0232+0233+0234: GET /v1/services/{service_id}/metrics mirrors the logs vertical one-for-one (store.ServiceMetricsReader with tenant-scoped GetByID, httpapi.ServiceMetricsReader port + listServiceMetricsHandler + parseServiceMetricsLimit + listServiceMetricsPayload, serviceMetricSample{name, occurred_at, value, unit} wire DTO with empty samples slice marshalling as [] not null, route on serviceIDResolver with action metrics.read, contract suite in services_metrics_test.go, policy matrix in services_metrics_policy_test.go); the metric-name closed set is the usage-metric ladder (http_requests, http_response_bytes, http_rps_peak_1m, latency_p95_ms, container_cpu_millicore_seconds, container_memory_mb_hours, storage_gb_month, build_minutes, …); the type-level doc explicitly disclaims billing authority (usage_counters + BE-0569/BE-0580 remain authoritative for invoiceable totals — this surface is a customer-visible read-through, not the billing oracle). New-arg mechanics: a Python ast-walking script (paren-depth-aware comma scanner, REVERSE call-order insertion so earlier offsets stay valid) injects the new ServiceMetricsReader / fakeServiceMetricsReader{} positional arg at slot 55 of newRouteTable and slot 57 of NewHandler across 33 test files / 63 call sites — reproducible recipe for any future newRouteTable / NewHandler signature growth. The third instance (events, traces, profiles, anything else under serviceIDResolver) can follow this template mechanically.


- POST create endpoint for a service-scoped child resource (BE-0250+0251+0252 pattern, POST /v1/services/{service_id}/backups, mirrors the service_domains POST trio BE-0238+0239+0240; clonable for BE-0264 previews, BE-0289 import previews, and any future bare-id child create): the store-layer composition is the canonical create-unit-of-work shape — ServiceXxxRepository.Insert (single-statement INSERT...RETURNING + mapWriteError mapping driver errors to typed apierr.Conflict whose message is value-free) + ServiceXxxService.Create orchestrator that opens a Store.Write Tx, runs the tenant-scoped parent existence check first (so a cross-tenant or unknown parent id surfaces as a deterministic apierr.NotFound, NEVER a 500 or silent success), runs an in-tx Authorize (defence-in-depth against grant-change races between the HTTP authorize and the desired-state write — the ONLY operation that runs in-tx Authorize; the in-transaction Authorizer is reserved for Create), runs the Insert, and Appends the immutable audit record — all inside the same *Tx so a row can never be persisted without its audit trail. Validation runs BEFORE the Tx is opened (validateCreateXxxInput against a shared validate.Collector so a request rejecting on more than one field surfaces every violation in one typed apierr.InvalidInput; submitted values NEVER appear in violation reasons). The customer-facing create pins any lifecycle status column to a fixed initial value (e.g. ServiceBackupStatusPending) so a customer cannot forge a 'succeeded' / 'completed' status through the public API surface — the worker is the authority for closed-taxonomy transitions; the status column is NOT in the createXxxRequest decoder shape and the validator overwrites in.Status in the validated struct. The audit Metadata records ONLY fields the application layer can prove redaction-safe by construction: structural identifiers (service_id), closed-taxonomy enums (status, certificate_type), and bounded primitives (retention_count, version, enabled flag rendered as "true"/"false"); caller-supplied free text (display_name, schedule, hostname even — schedule is a cron-style expression but is still caller-controlled bytes) is NEVER recorded verbatim, because a customer pasting a token into one of those fields is exactly the footgun a defensive convention avoids. The httpapi-layer composition is the canonical create-handler shape — createXxxRequest decoder (Enabled / boolean-default-true fields are pointers to preserve the absent-vs-explicit-false distinction at the JSON seam — `*bool` decoded; an omitted field collapses to the default at the handler boundary, an explicit `false` rides through unchanged; integer fields take their schema-side default when zero) + createXxxPayload + createXxxHandler that gates on RequireAuth + the typed-internal nil-creator guard + validate.DecodeJSON (strict, max-body-bytes, unknown-field rejection, no input echo on parse failure) + creator.Create + http.StatusCreated yalla.output.v1 envelope projecting through serviceXxxOf. Action is CapWrite (ActionXxxCreate -> CapWrite in catalog.go): owner / admin / developer allowed by role; CI / viewer / support denied via ReasonDeniedNoCapability — load-bearing distinction: a CapDeploy sibling action (e.g. ActionBackupRun, ActionDeploymentCreate) WOULD admit CI. The wire route uses serviceIDResolver (no parent_project_id leg pinned on the resource scope), so EVERY project-/env-/service-scoped grant is denied at the boundary via the engine's one-way covers() rule (ReasonDeniedOutOfScope); only an organization-wide write role or an org-level write grant reaches the handler. Cross-tenant: the resolver pins resource scope to the principal's home org id (never the path service's tenant), so cross-tenant service_ids hit the persistence layer with the home org id and surface as a deterministic apierr.NotFound — engine cross-tenant deny is pinned at the engine level (defence-in-depth: EVERY role including Support is denied cross-tenant for CapWrite — the support cross-tenant exception covers only CapRead / CapSupport). Contract test surface: success with full plumbing assertions (principal home org id forwarded, path service id forwarded, actor id forwarded, no caller-body org id trusted), boolean-default-true and explicit-false at the pointer seam, request_id propagation, validation failure propagated from creator as E_INVALID_INPUT (handler delegates validation to the store-layer orchestrator), strict-decode unknown-field rejection BEFORE creator runs, unauthenticated 401, role-deny 403 (handler never reached), cross-tenant 404 with principal home org forwarded, duplicate-id Conflict 409, store-unavailable 503, nil-creator typed Internal 500. Policy matrix test surface mirrors service_domains_create_policy_test.go one-for-one. Wiring footprint: adds ONE new positional arg (ServiceXxxCreator) to newRouteTable (~slot 57) and NewHandler (~slot 60); ~70 test files / ~120 call sites need a `fakeServiceXxxCreator{}` insertion via bulk substitution `fakeServiceYyyReader{}, fakeServiceZzzReader{}` -> `fakeServiceYyyReader{}, fakeServiceXxxCreator{}, fakeServiceZzzReader{}` (where Yyy is the sibling Reader and Zzz is the next port after the new slot in the signature); the special cases are the in-package contract-test helper for the new resource (`reader` -> `..., reader, fakeServiceXxxCreator{}, ...`) and any sibling test where the local `reader` variable is bound to a DIFFERENT port type that happens to share an adjacent slot (e.g. service_variables_test.go's `reader` is a ServiceVariableReader, NOT a backup reader, so its slot ordering needs a separate substitution). Re-runnable via a small Python script that pattern-matches and applies the three substitutions in order — see the BE-0232+0233+0234 description above for the ast-walking variant if a new arg needs to be inserted at a structural offset rather than between two named neighbours.

- Verb-on-child-resource endpoint pattern (BE-0253+0254+0255, POST /v1/services/{service_id}/backups/{backup_id}/run; sibling of the services_restart verb-on-parent shape, but adds a tenant-scoped child existence check; clonable for any future "trigger an action on a worker-driven child resource" endpoint — backup PATCH/DELETE, future preview-run, future deployment-retry triggers): the store-layer composition is the canonical run-unit-of-work shape — XxxRepository.GetByID (composite (org, parent, child_id) read; pgx.ErrNoRows -> apierr.NotFound(kind, child_id) — the kind/id NEVER contains the org or parent so the customer-facing message stays free of identifiers the principal cannot already prove they own) + XxxRepository.MarkPending (UPDATE...RETURNING flipping the worker-observable status column; the bump_version trigger from the resource's migration owns version, so MarkPending NEVER writes it itself — preserves optimistic-concurrency invariants for future If-Match callers) + RunXxxInput (plain-string actor/correlation seam — no policy/telemetry import in the store package) + XxxService.Run orchestrator (validate IDs before Tx; in Tx: parent-resource tenant-scoped Get -> child-resource tenant-scoped Get -> precondition 409s on closed-taxonomy state (enabled=false, status=running) -> in-tx Authorize (defense-in-depth against grant-change races; on the SAME *Tx as the write) -> MarkPending -> audit append with status_before/status_after metadata; ALL state mutations + audit commit atomically). The audit Metadata records ONLY closed-taxonomy enums (status_before/status_after) and structural identifiers (service_id); caller-controlled free text (display_name, schedule) is NOT recorded — Run does not mutate either and including them would expose a future redaction footgun. The httpapi layer is the canonical verb-handler shape — empty body, principal home org + path {parent_id} + path {child_id} forwarded to the runner, RequireAuth gates on the action's catalog mapping (backup.run -> CapDeploy), nil-runner guard runs after RequireAuth admits, 202 Accepted on success. Route entry's resolver is the bare-id resolver of the PARENT (serviceIDResolver), not the child — the resource scope pins to the parent's path identifier so scoped grants on parent siblings still get the engine's one-way covers() rule applied. The catalog mapping (CapDeploy vs CapWrite vs CapRead) is THE single load-bearing distinction in the policy matrix: CapDeploy widens the allow set to include CI (which holds CapRead+CapDeploy), so backup.run is allowed for CI keys even though backup.create (CapWrite) is denied — the policy matrix test pins this distinction at every grant scope (project-, env-, service-, org-level grants) AND at the engine's cross-tenant deny (CapDeploy is OUTSIDE the support cross-tenant exception, same as CapWrite). The bulk fake-fixture sweep for the new positional port follows the BE-0244 pattern: `perl -i -pe 's/fakePREVIOUS\{\},/fakePREVIOUS{}, fakeNEW{},/g' $(grep -rl 'fakePREVIOUS{}' internal/controlplane/httpapi/)` keyed on the immediately preceding port's bare struct literal — 71 files in the BE-0253 sweep — with two always-manual follow-ups: (a) the resource's own create-test helper that uses a local variable `creator` for the previous slot, (b) any wiring test that explicitly passes `nil` for the previous slot to reach the typed-internal guard.

- BE-0309 postgres is the FIRST database-engine clone of the BE-0301/BE-0307 per-service-type renderer-subtype pattern (internal/controlplane/dokploy/renderer_database_postgres_test.go; structural template for BE-0311 mysql / BE-0313 mariadb / BE-0315 mongo / BE-0317 redis). The subtype discriminator is neither the Builder (BE-0301/0303/0305) nor the ServiceType alone (BE-0307) but the Engine VALUE on a ServiceDatabase service. Four structural swaps vs the BE-0307 type-boundary clone: (1) Input helper collapses from two (per-builder) to ONE (databasePostgresInput) — databases do not vary by builder because the renderer's normaliseBuild() still runs but its output is not the subtype's identity. The fixture deliberately submits Role=RoleWeb + non-empty Domains + a CronSchedule so the "drops role+domains+cron" subtype-boundary assertion proves the renderer's drop semantics by observation, not by zero-value passive absorption. (2) The Drops* test becomes a single DropsRoleDomainsAndCron pin that asserts each of the three application/compose-only fields is dropped AND that none of their submitted values appear in Summary JSON / slog record / Summary.String() (the customer-submitted hostname "db.acme.example" and cron schedule "0 2 * * *" are the canonical leak candidates) — same no-leak structural barrier as the BE-0307 boundary, applied to a different drop surface. (3) The SubtypeBoundaryFromApplication shape gains an engine-label dimension: the renderer adds a new conditional yalla.engine label only for ServiceDatabase services (mirroring how yalla.role is conditional on a non-empty role), so the boundary test asserts BOTH yalla.service-type (must be "database") AND yalla.engine (must be "postgres") on the postgres case AND that yalla.engine is ABSENT entirely on the application case — the new label is the audit/observability surface that distinguishes a postgres database from a future mysql/mongo/redis database without re-reading the spec body. (4) RoleMatrix collapses entirely to a no-role tier-only matrix (database services have effectiveRole := "" set unconditionally in renderer.go); TierResourceDefaults pins that databases do NOT participate in the production-web 2-replica bump (the disjunction in defaultResources() is `(typ == ServiceApplication || typ == ServiceCompose) && role == RoleWeb` — ServiceDatabase is excluded by both conjuncts), so every tier defaults to one replica regardless. The production-code seam this story introduces is the validEngine() closed whitelist in renderer.go: BE-0309 ships only EnginePostgres = "postgres"; BE-0311..0317 EACH add one engine constant and one line to validEngine's switch — purely additive, no per-engine validation logic changes. The Render() engine validation expands from a single "required for database services" gate to a switch that ALSO rejects unsupported engines with a stable Reason "must be a supported database engine" (no value echo — the message text never names the rejected engine, so the BE-0311..0317 stories that add engines do NOT need to change the message). The ValidationFailures table includes an "unsupported engine" case keyed on "sqlite" — chosen because Yalla will never manage sqlite (file-based, no engine to provision), so the case stays stable across the entire BE-0309..0317 family even as the whitelist grows. The Determinism + RedactsAllVariableValues pins are direct ports of the BE-0307 shape. database.golden in testdata/renderer/ needs the +yalla.engine=postgres label added (regenerable via `go test -count=1 -run TestRenderGolden ./internal/controlplane/dokploy -args -update-golden` — the -update-golden flag is registered as a real *flag.Bool via init() in internal/testutil/golden.go, so it MUST be passed AFTER `-args`, not as a top-level go-test flag, or the binary errors out with "flag provided but not defined"). The worker-side acceptance criteria (dokploy_refs atomic write, quota reservation-to-conversion, fake Dokploy create/update/deploy/poll/failure/retry/replay) all defer to the later database worker story per the BE-0301 deferral pattern. Forward-applicable verbatim to BE-0317 redis (BE-0311 mysql, BE-0313 mariadb, BE-0315 mongo all landed: validEngine extended to `case EnginePostgres, EngineMysql, EngineMariadb, EngineMongo`; renderer_database_{mysql,mariadb,mongo}_test.go each pin their per-engine contract; the closed-set extension is one comma + one identifier per remaining sibling): each sibling adds ONE engine constant + ONE line to validEngine's switch + a per-engine test file cloned from renderer_database_postgres_test.go with the Engine constant swapped in databasePostgresInput's analogue and the engine label assertion updated. NOT applicable to non-database service types or to subtypes whose discriminator is the Builder or the ServiceType.

- Per-subtype quota dimension on the services Create unit of work (BE-0326 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/serviceservice.go ServiceService.Create + internal/controlplane/store/service_quota_applications_concurrent_test.go; structural template for BE-0327 compose_stacks, BE-0328 databases — every per-subtype dimension whose denominator is a SUBSET of the services table filtered by Kind): the create unit of work calls svc.quota.Reserve TWICE in the same *Tx for a service whose kind consumes a per-subtype dimension — first the existing QuotaResourceServices reservation (counts every service), then a conditional `if service.Kind == ServiceKindXxx { Reserve(QuotaResourceXxx) }` AFTER it and BEFORE the services.Insert. Order matters: the services reservation locks first so a tenant who exhausts the services dimension cannot acquire the per-subtype counter at all; the per-subtype reservation locks second so a tenant who exhausts ONLY the per-subtype dimension still gets a typed apierr.QuotaExceeded whose ExceededDetail.Resource names the per-subtype dimension specifically. Both reservations roll back together on any later failure (Insert, Enqueue, audit Append). Test pattern (clone of BE-0325): TWO quota_usage rows + TWO quota_policies seeded (per-subtype TIGHT at 5, services LOOSE at attempts*2 so the per-subtype dimension is the boundary that bites), assert detail.Resource == QuotaResourceXxx, assert BOTH active reservation tables == success count (because every winning Create reserved one of each). A second non-concurrent test exhausts the per-subtype dimension then proves a sibling-kind Create (compose / database for BE-0326) still succeeds — pins the per-subtype boundary as a regression barrier against a future refactor that drops the Kind guard. BE-0326 already lands the kind-guard inside ServiceService.Create at the same line where Reserve(services) returns nil; BE-0327 and BE-0328 each add ONE more conditional Reserve call right below the BE-0326 block (Kind == ServiceKindCompose / ServiceKindDatabase) and ONE more test file cloned from service_quota_applications_concurrent_test.go with the dimension constant + Kind constant + sibling-kind sanity-success cases swapped. NOT applicable to dimensions that span MULTIPLE service kinds with a non-trivial denominator (cpu_millicores / memory_mb / storage_gb — those count a numeric column on every kind and belong to a different per-numeric-resource pattern still to be designed).
- Per-Kind quota facet on environments (BE-0330 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/environmentservice.go + migrate/migrations/0025_environment_kind.{up,down}.sql + internal/controlplane/store/environment_quota_preview_environments_concurrent_test.go): structural template for ANY future per-Kind environment quota dimension (analog of the BE-0326/0327/0328 services per-Kind dimensions, now ported to the environments table). The FIRST per-Kind environment story lands the seam: a `kind` text column on environments with NOT NULL DEFAULT 'standard' and a CHECK constraint mirroring the closed Go enum one-to-one; a partial index on (organization_id, project_id) WHERE kind = '<minority-kind>' for the future sweeper; a `Kind` field on Environment, CreateEnvironmentInput, and CloneEnvironmentInput; a validateEnvironmentKind helper that normalises blank to the default member so legacy callers stay green; a closed `EnvironmentKind*` const set; and a conditional Reserve(QuotaResource<KindFacet>) on BOTH EnvironmentService.Create AND EnvironmentService.Clone (environments are the only resource with two create-shape entrypoints, both must be gated together). Subsequent per-Kind environment quota stories ship test-only — the seam is in place after BE-0330. The Reserve gates run in the SAME *Tx as Reserve(QuotaResourceEnvironments) and the desired-state write, so a tenant that exhausts either dimension cannot half-write an environment row whose other dimension passed. The default-on-blank Go validator MUST match the SQL DEFAULT so the migration is forward-compatible with in-process callers that predate the Kind field.

- Dimensional (magnitude-axis) quota dimension on a Create unit of work (BE-0331 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/projectservice.go QuotaReserver port + internal/controlplane/quota/quota.go Checker + internal/controlplane/store/serviceservice.go serviceCPUMillicoresByKind + internal/controlplane/store/service_quota_cpu_millicores_concurrent_test.go; structural template for BE-0332 memory_mb / BE-0333 storage_gb / and every future quota dimension whose allocation is a numeric magnitude per request rather than a +1 count). The FIRST dimensional story widens the load-bearing seam ONCE for the entire dimensional-quota family: the store-layer QuotaReserver interface gains a second method `ReserveAmount(ctx, tx, orgID, resource string, amount int64) error`, and the real adapter quota.Checker implements it as the canonical lock + sum-active + insert-reservation path with the amount parameterised. The count-axis convenience `Reserve(ctx, tx, orgID, resource string) error` is refactored to a one-line delegate `return c.ReserveAmount(...,1)`, so every prior count-axis call site is byte-identical and proves the new path is structurally compatible with the old. amount<=0 is rejected as Internal (wiring error — release is a separate path, not a negative reservation). The Checker validates amount, plan, resource, and limit BEFORE acquiring any row lock so a bad amount cannot block another tenant. The unit-of-work call site (ServiceService.Create) sources the per-request magnitude from a per-Kind constant map (serviceCPUMillicoresByKind: application=250, compose=500, database=500) via a `cpuMillicoresForServiceKind(kind)` helper — the map lives at the store layer so the dependency graph does not reach into the dokploy renderer's tier-aware defaults. The ReserveAmount call runs in the SAME *Tx as the count-axis Reserve calls, the desired-state write, the job enqueue, and the audit append; ordering is "every count-axis Reserve first, then the dimensional ReserveAmount" so a tenant who simultaneously exhausts a count dimension AND the dimensional dimension sees the count-dimension Resource surface in ExceededDetail (the LAST Reserve that fires produces the error). Three fakes (noopQuotaReserver in cmd/yalla-api/main.go, nopQuotaReserver in store/internal_test.go, recordingQuota in store/projectservice_test.go) need a one-line ReserveAmount addition to satisfy the widened interface; no other fakes exist because the concurrent tests use the real Checker. Test pattern: clone the BE-0326 concurrent test, replace the count-axis assertions with magnitude-axis ones — (1) policy LIMIT is a multiple of the per-Kind magnitude (cpu_millicores=1000 = 4 × 250-millicore apps); (2) expectedSuccesses = limit / per-Kind-magnitude; (3) detail.Requested is asserted to equal the per-Kind magnitude (NOT 1) — a regression hard-coding it back to 1 fails closed here; (4) detail.Reserved is expectedSuccesses × magnitude; (5) the active-reservations SUM(amount) assertion replaces / complements COUNT(*) — COUNT alone cannot tell whether the magnitude reached the reservation row Amount column, SUM(amount) closes the gap. A second non-concurrent test creates services across multiple kinds (application=250, database=500), exhausts the dimension exactly, then proves both a compose-kind request (would-reserve 500) and an application-kind request (would-reserve 250) are rejected — and that the two rejections report DIFFERENT detail.Requested values. The single equality check `composeDetail.Requested != appDetail.Requested` is the cheapest possible proof the per-Kind map actually fans out instead of collapsing to one constant. A SQL GROUP BY amount on quota_reservations confirms the magnitude distribution end-to-end (2 rows at 250 + 1 row at 500 for the canonical fixture). After BE-0331, EVERY future dimensional quota story (BE-0332 memory_mb, BE-0333 storage_gb, BE-0335 monthly_deployments) only needs a per-Kind/per-trigger magnitude helper and ONE ReserveAmount call site — the port is already widened and the real Checker implementation does not need to change again. The Reserve(...) call site convention stays for every count-axis dimension; ReserveAmount(...) is reserved for dimensions whose amount actually varies per request.
- BE-0332 memory_mb is the SECOND instance of the dimensional-quota template (BE-0331) and confirms the template clones without any port widening, Checker change, or fake update — only (a) a per-Kind magnitude map + helper in serviceservice.go (serviceMemoryMBByKind: application=512, compose=1024, database=1024), (b) one additional ReserveAmount call site inside ServiceService.Create AFTER the prior dimensional reservation, and (c) a structural clone of the concurrent integration test file with resource constant / magnitudes / limit swapped (service_quota_memory_mb_concurrent_test.go). Two load-bearing additions the template now records explicitly: (1) reservation order is part of the diagnostic contract — the LAST Reserve that fires produces the ExceededDetail.Resource surfaced to the caller, so a clone must seed the prior dimensional dimension(s) LOOSE in its concurrent test if it wants its own Resource to be the one that surfaces; a regression that reorders the reservations is detected by the clone test failing with the wrong detail.Resource (cpu_millicores instead of memory_mb, or vice versa). (2) The combined concurrent regression sweep across all dimensional tests requires `go test -race -parallel=2` (or lower) — two tests at 20 goroutines each saturate Postgres max_connections under default parallelism and surface as E_UNAVAILABLE instead of E_QUOTA_EXCEEDED. The per-test focused run remains green at full parallelism; this is a test-harness contention concern, not a code defect. Any future dimensional-dimension story (BE-0333 storage_gb / BE-0335 monthly_deployments / etc.) adds another concurrent test to the family and inherits both rules.
- Quota-dimension story whose call site is NOT yet wired (BE-0337 api_keys pattern, internal/controlplane/store/apikeyservice.go + internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0027_quota_resource_api_keys.{up,down}.sql + internal/controlplane/store/apikey_quota_api_keys_concurrent_test.go + cmd/yalla-api/main.go; structural template for BE-0338 members and ANY future dimension story whose owning Service.Create predates the QuotaReserver port — applies whenever a dimension story is the FIRST to wire its service-layer Reserve, distinct from the BE-0331..BE-0336 'call site already there' siblings whose owning unit-of-work already reserves the dimension). The minimum atomic delivery is FOUR change axes: (1) closed-set expansion — a new `NNNN_quota_resource_<name>.{up,down}.sql` migration that follows the BE-0326 backup_schedules template verbatim (DO block looking up the inline DOMAIN CHECK by `contypid = 'quota_resource'::regtype AND contype = 'c'` so the migration is robust to any Postgres-assigned constraint name, then `ALTER DOMAIN quota_resource ADD CONSTRAINT quota_resource_check CHECK (VALUE IN (...))` with the prior set + the new label; the .down.sql is structurally identical and narrows back to the prior set, accepting that any row carrying the new label fails the restored CHECK — that is the correct behaviour, silently dropping rows would lose audit-relevant state); plus the matching `QuotaResource<Name>` constant + membership-set entry in internal/controlplane/store/quota.go; plus updating the `valid` slice in internal/controlplane/store/quota_internal_test.go::TestQuotaResourceValid which pins `len(valid) == len(quotaResources)` — the test is a sealing-trap that catches a forgotten membership-set entry but ALSO fires on a forgotten valid-slice entry; both must change together. (2) Constructor port widening — the existing service struct grows a `quota QuotaReserver` field, the constructor parameter list grows the same port, the nil-guard switch grows a `case quota == nil` arm placed BETWEEN the last existing repo arm and the audit arm (the convention is store → parent repos → own repo → authz? → quota → jobs? → audit), and the Create unit of work grows a `svc.quota.Reserve(ctx, tx, key.OrganizationID, string(QuotaResource<Name>))` call placed AFTER every existence/parent-lookup check and BEFORE the desired-state Insert so a 404 on the parent is never disguised as a quota rejection AND a row-level conflict (slug, prefix, unique constraint) rolls the reservation back with the rest of the unit of work. (3) Constructor call-site fanout — three call sites change: cmd/yalla-api/main.go grows a `<name>Quota := noopQuotaReserver{}` placeholder (the real quota.Checker adapter is wired separately by a cross-cutting plan-resolver story; placeholder mirrors the projectQuota / environmentQuota / serviceQuota convention exactly), the in-package `package store` constructor-nil test grows a `nopQuotaReserver{}` local + a new `{nil quota, ...}` case wedged BETWEEN the last existing nil case and the audit case (positional ordering must mirror the constructor's nil-guard switch), and the `package store_test` integration-test helper grows the shared `&recordingQuota{}` (defined in projectservice_test.go — not a local `noopQuotaReserver{}`, which is only visible to cmd/yalla-api; the store_test package has its OWN allow-all fake hierarchy and the convention is to reuse `recordingQuota` for happy-path constructors). (4) Concurrent integration test — clone of the BE-0336 concurrent_deployments test with five structural simplifications when the owning service has no Authorizer / JobEnqueuer ports (api_keys is pure Yalla identity with no Dokploy mirror, so APIKeyService takes neither): no `atomicAuthorizer` / `atomicJobs` fakes need to be defined or counted; no `authz.calls == attempts` and no `jobs.calls == successes` assertions; the per-goroutine input loop calls `auth.Generate()` INSIDE the goroutine so every concurrent attempt mints its own unique (prefix, secret_hash) pair via crypto/rand (the prefix column is UNIQUE so a shared pair would deterministically conflict and mask the quota race); the parent-row seed is only an `organizations` row (no project/environment/service chain — api_keys live directly under the tenant); and the leaky-input candidates in the rejection-message scan use the resource-specific prefix (`key-%02d` / `req_apikeys_%02d` / `corr_apikeys_%02d`) so an echoed input still fails the message guard. The 'second test' sibling (TestXxxCreateAppliesXxxQuotaIndependentlyOfOtherDimensions) seeds ONLY the dimension under enforcement, exhausts it sequentially, asserts a SIXTH Create surfaces the dimension-specific rejection, and asserts no reservation row exists on TWO unrelated dimensions (services / projects) — the symmetry guard that catches a future regression that drops the Reserve call OR accidentally chose a different resource string. The whole pattern compiles + passes -race against a real Postgres without touching ANY of the 70+ httpapi fake-fixture call sites because the service's HTTP layer is owned by a separate seam (the api_keys handler already calls APIKeyService.Create with the same input shape; only the store-layer wiring changes). Pre-existing test failures gotcha: TestAPIKeyService* and TestEnvironmentService* / TestOrganizationVariableServicePatch* fail on HEAD due to testutil.Factory id-prefix vs ParseSlug drift — confirmed by stashing the BE-0337 changes and reproducing the identical 23-test set on the base commit. NOT introduced by this pattern, owed to a focused triage story before BE-0500+ verification stories run.

- Pure N-scope inheritance resolver (BE-0343 pattern, internal/controlplane/variables/{doc.go, resolver.go, resolver_test.go, AGENTS.md}; structural template for any future hierarchy-aware merge engine over org/project/env/service — feature-flag inheritance, domain-config inheritance, rate-limit inheritance). Five load-bearing rules: (1) The resolver package owns NO I/O — it defines a scope-agnostic ScopedVariable input shape and a Resolver that operates purely on in-memory tuples. The caller fetches inputs through the per-scope *Reader adapters (internal/controlplane/store) and converts store types into the resolver's input shape. This decouples the merge contract from persistence and lets unit tests use hand-built fixtures without a fake DB. (2) Collect ALL field violations across ALL scopes in one pass and return them as one apierr.InvalidInput; do NOT short-circuit on the first violation — that is hostile to the agent contract. Field paths anchor on <scope>.variables[<index>].<field> and NEVER echo the submitted value. (3) Customer-input failures (invalid name, duplicate within scope, secret downgrade without opt-in) -> apierr.FieldViolation -> apierr.InvalidInput (HTTP 400). Server-side failures (Open ErrUnknownKey / wrapped ErrInvalidCiphertext / provider id mismatch) -> apierr.Internal with a wrapped cause for server-side logging (HTTP 500). The classification is load-bearing: customer-input means "fix your request"; Internal means "retry or escalate". (4) Three redaction views: (a) Resolved/Rendered are internal-only and carry verbatim plaintext for renderer/worker consumption; (b) LogValue redacts value and ciphertext at the slog boundary as defence-in-depth against stray slog captures; (c) Explained projects every value to output.Sentinel for customer-facing JSON envelopes, audit metadata, and operator diagnostics. Tests prove no error message, JSON marshal, or slog line contains source plaintext or ciphertext. (5) Closed-set Options.AllowSecretDowngrade opt-in: secret -> non-secret at a higher scope is REJECTED by default (apierr.InvalidInput); the opt-in path MUST be backed by a caller-emitted audit event recording the override. The asymmetry between upgrade (always allowed) and downgrade (rejected by default) is the safe direction — upgrading the classification strengthens the posture, downgrading weakens it. Two test-fixture gotchas the pattern documents: (a) whole-error redaction tests must choose fixture values that cannot collide with stable reason phrases (the first BE-0343 iteration used "duplicate" as a fixture value AND as part of the rejection reason — false positive); use distinctive suffixes like "fixture-value-one-zzy" to anchor the redaction invariant. (b) Tests against the Plaintext provider must use different strings for the plaintext-leak assertion and the ciphertext-leak assertion — Plaintext.Seal returns the input verbatim, so using the same string for both would tautology-pass under Plaintext but fail to catch a real leak under AESGCM. NOT applicable to the dokploy renderer's mergeVariables (renderer.go) — that path is intentionally separate because the renderer's Variable input is the deterministic spec, not the at-rest seal tuple, and it ALSO validates tier/role invariants. A future refactor could unify the two but is a distinct story (it changes the renderer's input contract).

- Security-verification two-test pattern, httpapi port (BE-0345 pattern, internal/controlplane/httpapi/{body_size_static_test.go, body_size_test.go, AGENTS.md}; SECOND worked instance of the BE-0344 two-test template — confirms the template ports cleanly across packages and surfaces the httpapi-specific knobs). Four httpapi-flavoured rules the store-flavoured BE-0344 entry does NOT capture: (a) the static analyzer's receiver-name allowlist (`r`, `req`, `request`) is what makes `<*http.Request>.Body` distinguishable from unrelated `<*http.Response>.Body` / `<mail.Message>.Body` selectors in the same package — the convention is uniform (`r` everywhere in httpapi today) so the `req`/`request` aliases are defensive against future rename; document the convention in the analyzer's package doc. (b) the allowed-shape set is a small closed set: validate.DecodeJSON arg, io.LimitReader arg, `BinaryExpr` nil compare (either side), `AssignStmt` LHS, and `CallExpr` with zero args whose method is `.Close()` (the `len(call.Args) == 0` check on Close is what keeps `.Close(someArg)` from accidentally passing — io.Closer.Close takes no args by definition). Each shape lives in its own `markAllowedIn<Kind>` helper so adding a new allowed shape is a single function, not a branching edit on a monolith. (c) the regression self-check covers BOTH known-bad AND known-good synthetic snippets — without the positive cases a future change that over-tightens the analyzer would slip past silently. (d) the runtime test reuses the existing `createOrganizationHandlerFor` / `postOrganizations` / `decodeError` helpers from `organizations_create_test.go`; the entire 4-case end-to-end test is ~120 lines because the handler-wiring helpers already exist for every mutating endpoint. New security-verification runtime tests in httpapi should look for an existing handler-builder in the same package before adding a new one. Acceptance criteria "Unit tests cover success, validation failure, authorization failure, and not-found behavior" maps onto body-size as: success = valid in-cap body decodes (201 yalla.output.v1), validation failure = over-cap body returns 400 E_INVALID_INPUT with "exceeds the maximum allowed size" message, authorization failure = oversized body from an unauthenticated caller is 401 E_AUTH (auth middleware runs before body decode), not-found-style = empty body is 400 E_INVALID_INPUT "must not be empty" (nothing to decode is the symbolic lower edge). All four assertions also pin the no-body-reflection invariant (the error message must NOT echo the submitted body — a 64-byte slice of the padding is the regression probe). Sibling BE-0346..BE-0363 security-verification stories continue to follow the BE-0344+BE-0345 template; the package that owns the invariant determines whether the analyzer scans store SQL or httpapi handlers or worker job inputs etc., but the two-test pair shape, the regression self-check shape, and the AGENTS.md section shape are identical.

- Security-verification two-test pattern (BE-0344 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/{sql_injection_static_test.go, sql_injection_test.go, AGENTS.md}; structural template for BE-0345..BE-0363 sibling security-verification stories and ANY future "this invariant must hold for every call site of a typed surface" verification — request body size, JSON parser hardening, log-redaction fuzzing, environment-variable redaction, audit tamper resistance, etc.). The shape is two complementary tests landing in the package that owns the invariant: (1) a STATIC AST analyzer test that walks every non-test .go file in the package and rejects any source-level shape that re-opens the invariant — runs without a database, fails the build for any regression, and includes a self-check sub-test that parses synthetic bad source snippets and asserts the analyzer reports the expected violations (the self-check satisfies the "tests fail when the control is removed" criterion independently of whether production code happens to be clean today; a future weakening of the analyzer that lets a real regression slip past would itself fail this test). (2) a RUNTIME integration test that runs against an isolated Postgres (testutil.RequireMigratedDB), feeds a canonical attack/probe corpus through every relevant input position, asserts each call returns through the typed error surface (NotFound, InvalidInput, Conflict — never E_UNAVAILABLE, which is the store's mapping for raw driver errors and the load-bearing negative assertion because a control bypass would surface there), AND asserts a post-loop integrity probe (row counts byte-identical to baseline, seeded fixtures readable byte-identical) — plus a verbatim round-trip test that proves the invariant boundary actually IS the pgx parameter binder by inserting each payload as a free-text column value and reading it back byte-identical. Four load-bearing rules: (a) the static analyzer accepts only compile-time-constant expressions (string literals, const-bound identifiers including function-local consts, parenthesised wrappers, +-concatenations of those) — var declarations are rejected because var is mutable and a safe value today could be reassigned to caller input later; the const/var distinction is the language guarantee that makes the rule load-bearing; (b) the analyzer encodes structural exemptions ONLY by receiver type + method name (e.g. *Tx Querier wrappers), never by file path or line number, so the allowlist cannot drift; (c) the runtime payload corpus deliberately omits inputs that fail at a lower protocol layer (NUL bytes for SQL injection — pgx rejects NUL in a text parameter before it reaches the server, surfacing as E_UNAVAILABLE for reasons unrelated to the invariant) so the load-bearing E_UNAVAILABLE negative assertion stays clean; document the exclusion explicitly in the test file's package-doc block; (d) the SQL-keyword scan in the analyzer is case-SENSITIVE and anchors on uppercase keywords — the codebase writes SQL uppercase, so case sensitivity costs nothing and eliminates prose false positives like "transition from %s to %s" or "returning the value"; the regex requires \S (not \w) after UPDATE/FROM so Sprintf templates like "UPDATE %s SET …" still match (% is not a word char). The package's AGENTS.md gets a new section above the existing patterns documenting the threat model, the two-test invariant, the structural exemption, and the deliberate corpus exclusions — so a future developer can find the rule without re-reading the test files. Pre-existing -race failures on the full package run (recordingAuthorizer races, Postgres max_connections saturation at 20×N goroutines) are not regressions; -race -run filtered to the new tests is clean. NOT applicable to verification stories whose invariant is a runtime contract with NO static analog (e.g. log redaction fuzzing, idempotency replay, chaos tests for timeouts) — those follow a single-test runtime-only shape; the two-test pattern applies when the invariant is also a source-code rule.

- Write-endpoint contract-test quadruple (BE-0110 pattern, internal/controlplane/httpapi/variables_put_contract_test.go; WRITE-endpoint variant of the BE-0095/BE-0101/BE-0107 read-endpoint contract-test triple — structural template for every P=2 "Add contract tests for {PUT,PATCH,DELETE,POST} .../{org_id}/X" story whose endpoint mutates state and whose request body MAY carry is_secret=true / API-key / token / cookie values). FOUR named tests close the contract gaps the base *_test.go + *_policy_test.go pair leaves open: (1) "server writes response data only through ResponseWriter" — wraps the served request in captureProcessOutput, asserts os.Stdout AND os.Stderr are empty, AND that the structured logger sink is non-empty, AND that the captured replacer/updater/patcher input carries the {org_id} path parameter (writes don't have a stable "no-data" envelope to spot-check, so the captured-input assertion replaces the read-endpoint's "data == seeded entry" assertion; this is what makes the WRITE quadruple different from the READ triple's first test). (2) "request log redacts the bearer credential" — a single test function with a `tests := []struct{...}` table over (success path, authorization failure path), each subtest builds a separate logger and asserts logBuf.String() and rec.Body.String() are both free of the contract secret. The deny leg uses a replacer/updater whose write-path errors if invoked, so a leaked "store error" cannot be the leak source — the deny must short-circuit at policy. (3) "request log redacts a submitted secret value" — variables-flavoured EXTRA pin the limits sibling (BE-0098) does NOT have. IDENTICAL table shape to (2), but the marker is a customer-submitted is_secret=true value embedded in the request body (yallasubmittedsecretMARKER0123456789FACEFEED). Headers-not-logged / body-not-logged contract applies symmetrically to the request body for write endpoints; a regression that starts dumping the decoded body into the log would silently spill every secret variable through this endpoint, so the contract pin guards against that regression on BOTH legs. The deny-leg leak detection is even more important than the success leg here: a leaked submitted secret in the deny log surface means the operator log holds a value the store layer never wrote — a leak the wire-level redaction CANNOT catch (no row exists to render with output.Sentinel). DROP pin (3) for write endpoints whose body has no submitted-secret to leak (DELETE variables, POST projects unless projects carry secrets in the create body, PATCH limits, etc.); KEEP for every variables/environment-variables/project-variables/service-variables PUT and PATCH. (4) "error envelope doesn't leak dependency cause" — apierr.StoreUnavailable wrapped around stderrors.New("connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432"), asserts 503 / E_UNAVAILABLE / non-empty stable Message / cause string absent / host "10.0.0.5" absent from the body. Probe bytes are intentionally identical across sibling contract tests (read triple AND write quadruple) so the invariant is a single closed regression set, not a per-endpoint variant. The new helper this pattern requires is a "WithLogger" clone of the existing handler-builder that swaps the second-to-last NewHandler nil slot for the caller-supplied *slog.Logger — identical edit across every write endpoint, because the logger seam lives at the same position in NewHandler's parameter list regardless of which writer port the route depends on. Forward-applicable to BE-0113 (PATCH variables — keep all four pins; the PATCH body also carries is_secret=true), BE-0116 (DELETE variables — drop pin (3), DELETE body has no submitted secret), BE-0122 (POST projects — drop pin (3) unless the project create body carries secrets), and every future write-endpoint contract story. The only per-story knobs are the writer port type, the fake writer's field names (`vars`/`err`/`got` for replacers, `limits`/`err`/`got` for limits updaters, etc.), the canonical contract body, and the canonical contract-submitted-secret marker (use a distinct suffix per story so a regression that swaps two surfaces fails loudly — BE-0110 uses CAFEBABE, BE-0098 uses FEEDFACE for the bearer, future stories should pick distinct suffixes for BOTH the bearer credential and the submitted-secret marker).

- Repository CRUD invariants test file for a **TENANT-SCOPED short-lived claim/ledger table whose ONLY repository mutation surface is an InsertReservation (one-shot active-row INSERT) plus a single resolver read (SumActiveReservations), with NO per-row Update/Delete/Get, NO version column, a settled_consistent CHECK pairing status<>'active' with NON-NULL settled_at, a CHECK amount>0, a composite-FK out (organization_id, job_id) -> provisioning_jobs added by a LATER migration than the row's own migration, and a database-managed bump-only set_updated_at trigger fired BEFORE UPDATE** (BE-0455 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/quota_reservation_repository_invariants_test.go). Structurally distinct from BE-0453 (quota_usage -- INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + SELECT FOR UPDATE primitive) and BE-0451 (quota_policies -- INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE upsert) in six load-bearing ways: (a) the row-shape test must anchor BOTH a nullable-pointer JobID (zero on a no-JobID call, *string round-trip on a non-empty-JobID call) AND a nullable-pointer SettledAt (zero on every active-row insert -- there is no public surface that can mint a settled row); (b) the JobID round-trip leg cannot use a synthetic id alone because migration 0008 added a composite FK quota_reservations_job_fk -> provisioning_jobs (organization_id, id), so the test MUST pre-seed a real provisioning_jobs row (`INSERT INTO provisioning_jobs (id, organization_id, job_type, idempotency_key) VALUES (...)`) before InsertReservation -- a regression that dropped the FK or swapped its column order would surface here; (c) the settled_consistent CHECK violation has NO independent client-input surface (settled_at is not in the INSERT column list of InsertReservation), so the test exploits the OTHER direction: passing Status=ReservationStatusCommitted (non-blank, non-'active') sends settled_at=NULL via the default and the CHECK rejects it, proving InsertReservation can ONLY mint ACTIVE rows; (d) the time-filter leg of SumActiveReservations is a SECOND-AXIS exclusion test alongside the status filter -- a row with status='active' AND expires_at<=now must be excluded by the `expires_at > $3` predicate, so the test pre-seeds an active-but-time-expired row and asserts it is excluded WITHOUT mutating its status (a regression that dropped the time predicate would silently sum already-expired rows); (e) the resource-filter leg seeds TWO active reservations under the SAME tenant with DIFFERENT resources and asserts BOTH `SumActiveReservations(org, A, now)` and `SumActiveReservations(org, B, now)` return their own resource's amount (a regression that dropped the resource predicate would return 11 instead of 3 from either call); (f) the duplicate-ID Conflict test uses an explicit caller-supplied ID instead of relying on the qres_ prefix-mint path, because the PK violation is the constraint and a regression that silently re-minted the explicit id would mask the test (the explicit-ID-preservation test PRECEDES the duplicate-ID test and pins the no-remint contract). Forward-applicable to every future short-lived-claim repository whose public surface is a single one-shot active-row INSERT plus a resolver-read (a hypothetical lease-claim table KindResourceLease with active->held|released|expired, or a future job_attempts row whose public surface is a single INSERT per attempt). Test-helper naming caveat at package store_test: every *_test.go file under internal/controlplane/store/ shares the same package, so the type name `quotaReservationTxRollbackSentinel` must be distinct from quotaPolicyTxRollbackSentinel / quotaUsageTxRollbackSentinel / projectTxRollbackSentinel and friends -- grep `TxRollbackSentinel` before adding a new sentinel. Helper REUSE strategy: this file DEFINES its own `runInsertReservationOrFail` / `loadQuotaReservationRowByID` / `countQuotaReservationRowsForOrg` / `rawQuotaReservationRow` (no shared symbols to reuse), and REUSES the existing `insertReservationRow` / `insertSettledReservationRow` helpers defined in quota_repository_test.go for the SumActiveReservations setup legs because those raw-SQL inserts can stamp the schema's required `settled_at = now()` for non-active rows without going through the repository's active-only mint path.
- Repository tenant-isolation test file for a **TENANT-SCOPED CLAIM-PROTOCOL TABLE WHOSE FOUR REPOSITORY SURFACES (Claim upsert with steal-expired branch / Complete state-transitioning UPDATE / Release state-conditioned DELETE / Find composite-tuple read) ALL CARRY organization_id AS THE LEADING COLUMN OF A COMPOSITE PREDICATE TUPLE (organization_id, principal_id, idempotency_key), AND WHOSE ROW BODY CARRIES NULLABLE COMPLETION COLUMNS (response_status / response_body / completed_at) DISTINGUISHED BY NIL-NESS UNDER A COMPLETION-CONSISTENT CHECK, AND WHOSE INVARIANTS FILE ALREADY LANDED IN THE IMMEDIATELY-PRIOR PRD STORY** (BE-0470 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/idempotency_repository_tenant_isolation_test.go for idempotency_keys). Subspecies of the BE-0468 (audit_events) cross-tenant template with seven load-bearing deltas: (a) there is NO ListByOrganization read surface — Find is the only read, scoped to the full (organization_id, principal_id, idempotency_key) tuple — so the "cross-tenant list returns only own rows" probe collapses to "cross-tenant Find returns (zero, false, nil)" with a per-tenant count assertion on both sides, AND the "limit clamping is tenant-scoped" probe drops entirely (no list cap exists). The file's package-doc header MUST document the absence so a future reader does not look for a missing test, mirroring the BE-0426 organizations file's "tenant-root tables have no ListByParent" doc-only delegation; (b) the byte-identity comparator MUST handle three nullable pointer-bearing columns (*int for response_status, []byte for response_body, *time.Time for completed_at) where the pending-vs-completed lifecycle distinction is observable through nil-ness. A simple field-equality loop will silently round-trip a regression that flipped a pending row's NULL completion columns to zero-value scalars (e.g. response_status=0, response_body=[]byte{}, completed_at=epoch). The pattern: switch on (after==nil, baseline==nil) into three branches — both-nil OK, one-nil diff "nil-ness drifted", both-non-nil dereference-compare — and emit a fmt-printer-pair (fmtIntPtr / fmtTimePtr) so the diagnostic reads "before=<nil> after=200" rather than pointer noise. The pattern is forward-applicable to every future tenant-isolation file whose row carries nullable completion columns (e.g. job_attempts with nullable error_summary + finished_at + result, quota_reservations with nullable released_at + job_id); (c) every mutating surface needs its OWN OnOrgADoesNotTouchOrgB pair — Claim, Complete, Release. The Complete probe is structurally distinct from the Claim probe because Complete's WHERE composes `organization_id = $1 AND principal_id = $2 AND idempotency_key = $3 AND status = 'pending'` so the cross-tenant caller falls off the organization_id leg BEFORE the status leg runs, and the typed Conflict ("no longer pending") fires WITHOUT a foreign-row read — a regression that dropped organization_id from the Complete WHERE would either rewrite orgB's row (worst case) OR silently complete orgA's "claim" with a forged response envelope. The Release probe asserts the dual: Release is "safe to call defensively" and returns nil on a zero-row DELETE, so the cross-tenant Release must return nil AND leave orgB's pending row byte-identical AND the per-tenant count unchanged — three separate assertions because a regression that dropped organization_id from the Release WHERE would delete orgB's row, which the bystander byte-identity loader catches as a missing-row error inside loadIdempotencyRowByID's t.Fatalf. The forged Complete envelope MUST carry a recognisable canary string (`"forged":"orgA-tries-to-complete-orgB-claim"`) so a future reader can see immediately what the test was protecting against; (d) the Claim cross-tenant id-collision probe needs a GLOBAL row-count assertion in addition to the per-tenant counts. The PRIMARY KEY on idempotency_keys.id is global, so a rolled-back PK violation under a foreign tenant could in principle land the failing row in some other (third) tenant's slot — the per-tenant probe alone cannot prove the absence because the failing row's organization_id is unknown to the probe. The fix is a tiny totalIdempotencyRows(ctx, t, db) helper that runs `SELECT count(*) FROM idempotency_keys` with no WHERE, snapshotted before and after the failing Claim. The pattern is forward-applicable to every future tenant-isolation file for a table whose PK is global (not parent-scoped); (e) the Claim cross-tenant id-collision probe MUST force the collision through caller-supplied ids on DIFFERENT (principal_id, idempotency_key) tuples so the ON CONFLICT target does NOT match and the PRIMARY KEY violation flows through mapWriteError. A naive collision attempt under the same (principal, key) tuple would be intercepted by ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE and silently rewritten through the expiry-takeover branch — the test would pass on a broken implementation. The id-collision test in this file mints sharedID via mintIdempotencyID and assigns it to a record carrying a DIFFERENT (principal_id, idempotency_key) than the seeded orgA row. The pattern is forward-applicable to every future tenant-isolation file for an UPSERT table whose ON CONFLICT target is a NON-PK unique tuple (idempotency_keys uses (org, principal, key); job_attempts may use (job_id, attempt_number); etc.); (f) the Claim "mirror tuple" probe is the load-bearing per-tenant-uniqueness assertion of the ON CONFLICT target. orgB seeds a row at (orgB, usr_mirror, mirror-key); orgA Claims a row at (orgA, usr_mirror, mirror-key) — same (principal_id, idempotency_key), different organization_id. A regression that dropped organization_id from the ON CONFLICT target would resolve the conflict onto orgB's mirror-tuple row and silently rewrite it through the DO UPDATE branch — the worst-case cross-tenant idempotency data-corruption shape. The assertion: orgA's Claim returns owned=true (fresh INSERT, never DO UPDATE on a foreign row), orgA's new row carries orgA's organization_id and a distinct id, AND orgB's mirror row remains byte-identical (every field including the nullable completion columns and the database-assigned created_at + caller-supplied expires_at). The "mirror tuple" terminology and the explicit comment ("the load-bearing bystander whose presence on orgB exercises the per-tenant uniqueness of the ON CONFLICT target") MUST be carried verbatim in the seed comment because the structural test failure mode (silent peer-row rewrite) is the kind a future reader will rationalise away without it; (g) the cascade-from-organization-delete probe MUST seed orgB rows covering the lifecycle spread — pending, completed-with-envelope, pending-with-future-expiry — because the nullable completion columns are the load-bearing byte-identity surface, not the always-set columns. The single-bystander variant of this cascade is already pinned by the BE-0469 invariants file's TestIdempotencyRepositoryCascadeFromOrganizationDelete (one orgB row, inline column equalities); the tenant-isolation file deepens it with a three-row pool and the assertIdempotencyRowByteIdentical comparator across every row, plus a post-cascade Find for every surviving orgB row to prove the cascade did not silently corrupt the repository read predicate. New helpers introduced: assertIdempotencyRowByteIdentical (nullable-aware comparator), fmtIntPtr / fmtTimePtr / itoaInt (pointer-friendly diagnostic formatters — itoaInt avoids importing strconv solely for the formatter call sites), seedTwoTenantIdempotencyFixture (two-organization shape; idempotency_keys has no project/environment/service parent chain so the fixture is narrower than the dokploy_refs equivalent), totalIdempotencyRows (global PK-collision count probe). Helpers reused: seedOrg (schema_test.go); newIdempotencyStore / idemFixture / claimIdem / completeIdem / findIdem / wantErrCode (idempotency_test.go); rawIdempotencyRow / loadIdempotencyRowByID / countIdempotencyRowsForOrg / mintIdempotencyID (idempotency_repository_invariants_test.go).

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The orphan-reconcile pattern from BE-0466 generalises: at
    iteration start, ALWAYS read `git status --short` BEFORE
    picking a story. If the working tree carries an untracked
    test/source file matching a PRD story ID, the prior turn
    likely completed the work but didn't commit (or didn't
    flip the PRD, or didn't append the progress entry, or some
    combination). The right move is to reconcile that orphan
    in the current iteration (verify, flip PRD if needed,
    append progress, commit) BEFORE picking up the
    higher-priority queue head. Reconciling costs one iteration
    but prevents the orphan from drifting out of sync with the
    codebase (e.g. an interface rename in
    internal/controlplane/httpapi could break the untracked
    test file silently because `go test ./...` would not pick
    it up on `main`).
  - Specifically for BE-0194 vs BE-0468: BE-0468 (priority 1)
    outranks BE-0194 (priority 2), but the orphan file was
    BE-0194 work. The cleanest reconciliation is to commit
    BE-0194 in this iteration (one-story-per-iteration rule
    intact) and let the next iteration pick BE-0468 as a fresh
    queue head.
  - The contract-test pattern for a restore (revive-soft-delete)
    endpoint vs a delete (schedule-soft-delete) endpoint
    differs in three load-bearing axes that the test file's
    structural twin must adapt: (a) success status is 200 OK
    (the row already existed; restore clears
    deletion_scheduled_at and returns the live projection) NOT
    202 Accepted (delete enqueues a worker job and returns a
    deletion plan); (b) no worker provisioning step is required
    because the underlying Dokploy resource was never
    destructively torn down, so the test does not need to
    assert deployment_id / job-id forwarding; (c) the
    DeletionScheduledAt field of the response projection MUST
    be nil -- a future regression that left the stamp on the
    restored row would surface here even though the row was
    successfully revived from the soft-delete state. The
    BE-0193 happy-path test pins the field-is-nil invariant
    directly; the BE-0194 contract-test redaction probe pins
    it indirectly by asserting the response body is
    credential-free which would fail loudly if any future
    change started embedding raw request headers in the
    response.

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:

    to land. audit_events_test.go already covers BE-0104's surface

    PRD stories. BE-0105 should table every built-in role x audit.read,
    revoked/expired Disabled principals, and a wrong-organization
    principal (the same pattern as limits_policy_test.go and
    usage_policy_test.go).

    cursor-based pagination are NOT in scope here — the endpoint serves
    the newest N rows in [1, 200]. A separate "audit events filtering"
    story would add query parameters; the wire envelope is
    forward-compatible (events[] can grow optional sibling fields).
  - The wire projection trusts the persistence-layer redaction contract.
