    Yalla operators, it must NOT go through this customer-facing
    endpoint — it would be a separate /admin/... route with its own

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - For a NewHandler signature change with ~19 call sites in *_test.go,
    a single bulk substitution covers the bulk of the churn IF the
    target substring is regular. The two regular forms in this codebase
    are single-line `fakeUsageReader{}, fakeAPIKeyReader{}` and
    multi-line `fakeUsageReader{},\n\t+fakeAPIKeyReader{}`. The
    exceptions are (a) helpers that pass a named parameter at the new
    port's position (e.g. `, reader,`) and (b) "missing-reader" tests
    that pass nil at the new port's position. Both need targeted follow-up
    edits — a perl/python pass over the common pattern + a manual `grep
    -rn 'fakeOldReader,\n\t+fakeAPIKeyReader{}'` for the residue is the
    reliable workflow.
  - audit_events.go is the third endpoint to use the
    "nullable-nested-object" wire convention (after usage.go and the
    actor/resource pair here). The pattern: when N coupled scalar fields
    are EITHER all-present OR all-absent, project them as a single
    nullable nested object on the wire (`actor: {id, kind}` vs
    `actor: null`), not N coupled-nullable scalars. The agent reads one
    boolean (actor != null) instead of validating N invalid combinations.
    Adding a new field to the nested object later is forward-compatible
    with existing readers.
  - The store contract for audit metadata is "already redacted at
    persistence". A consumer (HTTP handler, future audit-event admin
    surface) must NOT silently un-redact a sentinel value — the wire
    mirrors persistence verbatim. The
    TestAuditEventProjectionDoesNotReintroduceRedaction test pins this
    structurally: feed a fake reader rows whose IP/UA/metadata-value
    are output.Sentinel and assert the wire renders Sentinel, not the
    empty string. A future regression that "cleans up" sentinel values
    in the projection fails this test.
  - audit.read is the load-bearing example of "a read action that is
    NOT CapRead". A viewer (CapRead, CapDeploy in the catalog) cannot
    list the audit log; only CapAdmin (owner, admin) and CapSupport
    (cross-tenant) can. This means the boilerplate "list endpoint" tests
    must NOT assume "every role allowed in the tenant" — the policy
    matrix lands per-action. A viewer-denied contract test (not just a
    matrix test) is good defence-in-depth because it makes a future
    accidental drop to CapRead a contract-test failure, not only a
    matrix-test failure.

  - BE-0098 (contract tests for PATCH /v1/organizations/{org_id}/limits)
    and BE-0099 (policy matrix coverage, the unblocked p1) are now ready.
    limits_patch_test.go covers most of BE-0098's surface, but the two
    remain separate PRD stories.

    in scope here: this endpoint upserts only. A separate "remove
    override" story (or supporting a sentinel value) would land later if
    the customer surface needs it.
  - The audit event currently records updated_resources as
    "projects,services" (closed-set names sorted). It does NOT record the
    submitted limit_value/enforcement_mode pairs — those are sensitive
    business inputs that a future audit-redaction story may decide to
    record under a different policy. The shape is forward-compatible: the
    metadata map can grow without breaking the wire contract.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - ON CONFLICT against a PARTIAL unique index MUST repeat the WHERE
    predicate in the conflict_target clause: Postgres treats the partial
    index as not eligible for ON CONFLICT otherwise. The pattern is `ON
    CONFLICT (cols) WHERE <same predicate> DO UPDATE`.
  - Adding a new dependency to a constructor with ~17 call sites (the
    NewHandler / newRouteTable signature) is genuinely O(N) churn in tests
    — but every test file follows the same wiring pattern, so a single
    consistent substring substitution covers the bulk of it. The two
    files where the substring differed (api_keys_test.go used `reader,
    fakeAPIKeyReader`, limits_test.go used `nil, fakeAPIKeyReader{}` in
    the missing-reader test) needed targeted edits, but the rest fell out
    of one mechanical search/replace.
  - For numeric request fields whose zero is meaningful (a limit of 0
    forbids the resource), use `*int64`. A non-pointer int64 cannot
    distinguish "field omitted" from "set to zero", and the body decoder
    would silently treat the latter as the former — leaking a real client
    intent through a default-zero floor.
  - The handler's "at least one entry / every entry supplies limit_value"
    rejection mirrors the store layer's identical violation. This is
    intentional symmetry — both layers must validate at the boundary —
    not duplication. The field paths match byte-for-byte
    ("limits[i].limit_value"), so a future caller cannot tell whether the
    rejection came from the handler or the store, which keeps the wire
    contract stable across refactors.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0036
- What was implemented: internal/controlplane/validate, the centralized
  request-validation toolkit (validate.go, network.go, resources.go, refs.go,
  json.go).
  - Collector accumulates apierr.FieldViolation entries (stable dotted field
    path + value-free reason) and produces exactly one apierr.InvalidInput via
    Err(); OK()/Violations()/Add()/Addf() round it out.
  - Validators: Name (display name: trimmed, UTF-8, no control chars, rune
    bound), Slug (delegates domain.ValidateSlug), ID (domain.ParseID + kind
    check, value-free reason so a cross-tenant probe is not an oracle), Path
    (repo-relative; rejects absolute, backslash, NUL, ".." traversal),
    URL (http/https only, rejects userinfo so a token cannot leak into stored
    state), Domain (DomainOptions.AllowWildcard gates a single leading "*."
    label — caller resolves feature flag + quota; per-label DNS validation),
    Resources (cpu/memory/replicas: zero=unset, reject negative/over-ceiling,
    per-dimension sub-paths), EnvVars (POSIX names, UTF-8/NUL/length on values,
    duplicate detection; secret vs non-secret split via the ".secret[i]" path
    segment + MaxSecretValueLen ceiling), GitRepoURL (https/ssh/git + scp-like
    git@host:path, rejects embedded credentials), GitBranch (check-ref-format
    subset), GitCommit (7-40 hex), ImageRef (Docker reference subset, rejects
    ".." components + uppercase repo + malformed tag/digest).
  - DecodeJSON: strict, size-capped (custom limitedReader -> errBodyTooLarge),
    DisallowUnknownFields, rejects trailing data; every failure maps to a
    body-free apierr.Invalid / apierr.InvalidInput so a secret in a malformed
    body never leaks through the decode error.
  - Tests: validate_test.go (Collector, every validator success+failure,
    secret/non-secret separation proof, "never echoes the value" proofs for
    Name/Slug/ID/URL/EnvVars/DecodeJSON) + fuzz_test.go (8 fuzz targets:
    FuzzName/Path/Domain/EnvVarName/EnvVarValue/DecodeJSON/ImageRef/GitBranch,
    each seeded with long strings, invalid UTF-8, path traversal, control
    chars; each asserts no panic and re-derives the accept invariants).
  - internal/controlplane/validate/AGENTS.md documents the Collector pattern,
    the no-echo rule, options-not-lookups, field-path conventions, and the
    fuzz-every-validator convention.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/validate/{validate.go,network.go,
  resources.go,refs.go,json.go,validate_test.go,fuzz_test.go,AGENTS.md} (new),
  ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...;
  go test ./...; go test -race ./...; plus a 4s -fuzztime smoke of all 8 fuzz
  targets.
- Results: all passed. goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck not
  installed locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - Acceptance criteria "stable yalla.output.v1/error.v1 envelopes",
    "isolated Postgres migrations", and "authorization failure / not-found
    unit tests" are N/A: validate is a pure, in-memory package with no HTTP
    surface, no Postgres, and no auth — covered success + validation-failure
    + fuzz exhaustively instead (the established pattern for pure packages).
  - validate defines its own EnvVar/ResourceRequest input shapes rather than
    importing dokploy's Variable/ResourceLimits — validate is the request
    layer, dokploy is the provisioning layer, and validate must not depend on
    dokploy. When handlers land they will validate the request DTO, then map
    the validated values into the dokploy/store shapes.
  - The validators are implemented and tested but not yet wired into any
    handler (no customer-facing endpoints exist yet). The first endpoint
    story will call validate.New() + the relevant validators in its handler.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - apierr.InvalidInput already trims + de-dups blank violations and sorts
    deterministically, so a Collector can append freely and rely on it.
  - The Crockford ID alphabet INCLUDES z but EXCLUDES i/l/o/u — to build an
    intentionally-malformed ID suffix for a test, use 'l' (or i/o/u), not 'z'.
  - io.LimitReader reports io.EOF at the cap, indistinguishable from a
    truncated body. For a "body too large" error you need a custom reader
    that returns a distinct sentinel (limitedReader -> errBodyTooLarge).
  - encoding/json reports an unknown field as a plain errors.New whose message
    is `json: unknown field "<name>"` — there is no typed error to errors.As
    against; match on the message prefix.
  - "Separates secret and non-secret fields" was satisfied structurally: the
    EnvVar.Secret flag selects both the length ceiling and the field-path
    segment (".secret[i]" vs "[i]"), so the path alone tells a caller which
    kind failed without inspecting the value.

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0003
- What was implemented: Service lifecycle and graceful shutdown for the API and worker.
  - internal/controlplane/runtime/lifecycle.go (new): Readiness type — concurrency-safe named
    startup gates (NewReadiness/Set/MarkReady/Ready/Snapshot/PendingGates) with the
    ReadinessReporter interface; RunHTTPServer(ctx, srv, shutdownTimeout, logger) — runs
    ListenAndServe in a goroutine, returns early on a pre-shutdown serve error, and on ctx
    cancellation calls Shutdown with a fresh context.WithTimeout so a wedged request cannot
    block exit. http.ErrServerClosed is treated as success.

    bounding, and serve-error propagation (fake httpServer, no real socket).
  - internal/controlplane/worker/loop.go (new): Loop with Claimer/Lease interfaces. Run checks
    ctx before every Claim (stops claiming on shutdown), backs off on empty queue / claim error,
    and on an interrupted in-flight job releases the lease on a context.WithoutCancel context
    bounded by ReleaseTimeout. A job whose Run returns nil is committed, never released.
    NoopClaimer is the placeholder Claimer until the durable Postgres job store lands.
    (replaced worker/doc.go — package doc now lives in loop.go.)

    (local 15s, test 2s, staging/production 25s), Go-duration parsing, and 1s..5m range
    validation as a typed yerr.CodeConfig error. Wired into RedactedConfig/LogValue/String.

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0007
- What was implemented: Structured per-request logging middleware for the control-plane API.
  - internal/controlplane/telemetry/logging.go (new): RequestLogging(logger) middleware emitting
    exactly one JSON record per request after the handler runs — method, route (r.Pattern, the
    ServeMux-matched route, falling back to URL path), target (redacted RequestURI), status,
    latency_ms, bytes, plus request_id/correlation_id from LogAttrs(ctx). statusRecorder wraps the
    ResponseWriter to capture status + byte count (defaults to 200 on an implicit write). Level
    follows the outcome: 5xx error, 4xx warn, else info. Headers and bodies are never logged; the
    target is run through output.NewRedactor() (logRedactor) so a smuggled ?token= is scrubbed.
    requestFields is a request-scoped mutable holder seeded onto the context; SetOrgID/
    SetPrincipalID let the future auth/policy layers enrich org_id/principal_id, which are emitted
    only when non-empty. A nil logger disables logging (io.Discard) without panicking.

    (success/validation-failure/auth-failure/forbidden/not-found/server-error → level + fields +
    request_id matches response header), redaction (Authorization header, Cookie, query token,
    body field — none appear in the log; target shows [REDACTED]), org/principal included when set
    and omitted when unknown, configured-level gating (INFO suppressed under ERROR threshold, 5xx
    still emitted), nil-logger safety, implicit-write status defaults to 200.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler now takes logger *slog.Logger and wraps
    the routed mux in telemetry.RequestLogging(logger) just inside telemetry.Correlate.

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0008
- What was implemented: OpenAPI 3.1 generation + validation for the control-plane API.
  - internal/controlplane/openapi/openapi.go (new): the OpenAPI document builder.
    Build(Info, []Endpoint) -> Document. Endpoint is the neutral per-route metadata
    type (method/path/operationId/summary/description/tags/RequiresAuth/SuccessStatus/
    SuccessDescription/SuccessSchema). Every operation documents a success response and
    a "default" error response, both referencing component schemas. Components always
    define SchemaSuccessEnvelope (yalla.output.v1), SchemaErrorEnvelope (yalla.error.v1),
    SchemaErrorBody, SchemaOpenAPIDocument, and the ApiKeyAuth http/bearer security
    scheme. Public endpoints emit security:[] explicitly; RequiresAuth emits
    [{ApiKeyAuth:[]}]. All map types (Paths/PathItem/Responses/ContentMap/SchemaMap/
    SecuritySchemeMap) marshal with sorted keys via marshalSortedMap so the artifact is
    byte-stable. Examples render secret-shaped values with output.Sentinel; the
    security-scheme description carries a redacted sample bearer token. Document exposes
    HasOperation(method,path) + OperationCount() for the route-coverage test.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go (new): newRouteTable(build, readiness) is
    the single source of truth — []apiRoute pairing a served http.HandlerFunc with its
    openapi.Endpoint. Moved the /healthz, /readyz, /version handlers here from server.go.
    openAPIEndpoint() is the /openapi.json metadata (kept separate because its handler
    is built from the doc itself); openAPIDocument(build, table) folds it back in so the
    published document lists the discovery endpoint. endpointsOf projects metadata out.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler now builds the route table,
    generates the OpenAPI doc once at startup (json.MarshalIndent; panics on a marshal
    error since the input is static), appends the /openapi.json route (serves the raw
    document — deliberately NOT enveloped, since OpenAPI tooling expects the standard
    format — with no auth), and registers every table entry on the mux in a loop.
  - internal/controlplane/openapi/openapi_test.go (new): 3.1 identity, envelope+error
    schemas defined, ApiKeyAuth scheme, every endpoint documents both responses + custom
    success status honoured, public security:[] vs authed ApiKeyAuth, HasOperation
    case-insensitive, deterministic marshal (5x) + valid JSON, examples use output.Sentinel
    and contain no unredacted secret-shaped token.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server_test.go: TestHandlerServesOpenAPIDocument
    (200, application/json, openapi=3.1.0, info.version echoes build, paths include all
    routes, body is the raw doc not an envelope, no auth header sent),
    TestEveryRegisteredRouteIsDocumented (CI guard — every registered route in the doc,
    no extras), TestRegisteredRoutesAreServable (every documented route reachable,
    unknown path still 404), TestOpenAPIDocumentRedactsExampleSecrets.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/openapi/{openapi.go,openapi_test.go} (new),
  internal/controlplane/httpapi/{routes.go (new),server.go,server_test.go},
  internal/controlplane/AGENTS.md, ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...; go test ./...;
  go test -race ./...; go test -race ./internal/controlplane/....
- Results: all passed. goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck not installed locally.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - Endpoint has no request-body modelling yet (no endpoint has a request body). When the
    first mutating endpoint lands, extend openapi.Endpoint with request schema metadata
    and add a RequestBody to operationFor — keep it data-driven from the route table.
  - The route-coverage guard proves newRouteTable -> document parity. It cannot catch a
    raw mux.HandleFunc added outside the table; AGENTS.md forbids that and TestRegisteredRoutesAreServable
    plus the convention are the backstop. If a future story needs a hard guard, expose a
    mux-introspection hook.
  - Acceptance criterion 5 ("all public responses use stable JSON envelopes") does not
    apply to /openapi.json itself: the OpenAPI document is a standardised format and is
    served raw so OpenAPI tooling can consume it. Every API *operation* response still
    uses the envelopes. Validation/authorization-failure unit-test criteria are N/A —
    /openapi.json takes no input and needs no auth; covered success + not-found instead.
  - Postgres integration-test criterion is N/A for a pure API-contract story.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - In a Go composite literal of map[string]*Schema, element values can elide &Schema{}
    (write just {...}); but a *Schema struct *field* (e.g. Items) still needs explicit
    &Schema{...}. Map/slice elements allow elision, struct fields do not.
  - json.RawMessage with `json:",omitempty"` is the clean way to embed deterministic
    example bodies — map[string]any examples would marshal with random key order and
    break a determinism test. MarshalIndent does not re-indent RawMessage, so keep
    embedded examples compact.
  - A custom MarshalJSON on a named map type makes json.Marshal deterministic without
    touching call sites; nest them (Paths -> PathItem -> Operation) and each level sorts
    independently. omitempty still works on a named map type — it is evaluated on the Go
    value (len==0) before MarshalJSON is called.
  - The /openapi.json route is self-referential (its handler needs the doc the routes
    describe). Pattern: keep its metadata in a separate openAPIEndpoint(), have the doc
    builder append it, and register the serving route last in NewHandler.

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0010
- What was implemented: Postgres migration system for the control plane.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrate.go (new): the migration runner.
    Migration/AppliedMigration/Status types; LoadMigrations(fs.FS) parses+validates
    NNNN_name.(up|down).sql files (malformed names, missing up, empty up, conflicting
    names, duplicates -> errors), sha256-checksums each up script, returns them sorted.
    Migrator (New = embedded FS, NewWithFS = arbitrary FS for tests): Up applies pending
    migrations in order, idempotent; Down rolls back newest-first to a target version;
    Status reports applied/pending/current/dirty. Up/Down serialise via a pg session
    advisory lock, bootstrap the schema_migrations ledger (version bigint PK, name,
    checksum, applied_at, dirty), and run each migration in its own transaction (row
    inserted dirty -> SQL -> row finalised clean; a SQL failure rolls the whole tx back
    leaving no row). verify() refuses dirty / unknown-version / checksum-mismatch via
    errors.Is sentinels ErrDirtyDatabase/ErrUnknownVersion/ErrChecksumMismatch;
    ErrIrreversible guards Down across a migration with no down script.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0001_baseline.up.sql + .down.sql (new):
    baseline migration — installs pgcrypto + citext extensions and the set_updated_at()
    BEFORE UPDATE trigger function (the timestamp convention every later table uses).
    Domain tables are deliberately NOT here; they land in BE-0013 (tenant hierarchy),
    BE-0021 (quota), BE-0023 (audit), etc.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrate_test.go (new): pure unit tests via
    fstest.MapFS (embedded parse, 6 validation-failure rows, fixture-FS success, nil
    pool); integration tests against an isolated per-test throwaway database
    (testPool helper: CREATE DATABASE / connect / DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE) on
    cleanup, t.Skip when YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL unset): up-from-empty (ledger row +
    checksum + PK constraint + extensions + function), idempotent up, refuses
    dirty/unknown/checksum-mismatch, down is reversible + re-migratable, failed
    migration rolls back leaving no row, Status pending/applied.
  - internal/controlplane/store/AGENTS.md (new): migration conventions, domain-table
    timestamp/tenant-scoping rules, integration-test approach.
  - docker-compose.yml (new): local Postgres 16 (user/db "yalla", CREATE DATABASE priv).
  - go.mod/go.sum: added github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 v5.9.2 (+ pgxpool).

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - pgx v5 routes Exec/tx.Exec by argument count: a query with ZERO args uses the
    simple query protocol, which allows multiple ;-separated statements in one call —
    so a single .up.sql file with several DDL statements (and dollar-quoted $$ bodies)
    runs fine via one conn.Exec(ctx, mig.UpSQL). A query WITH args uses the extended
    protocol (one statement only).
  - The advisory lock must be held on a single pinned connection: acquire one with
    pool.Acquire(ctx) and run lock + all migration work + unlock on that *pgxpool.Conn,
    not on the pool (the pool hands out different conns).
  - Release the advisory lock on context.WithoutCancel(ctx) so an already-cancelled
    caller context still releases it.
  - Per-test isolation: pgx.Identifier{name}.Sanitize() safely quotes a generated DB
    name; DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE) (PG13+) evicts stragglers. Register cleanups
    so they run LIFO: admin pool close FIRST (runs last), then DROP, then test pool
    close (runs first) — pool closed before drop, admin still open to drop.
  - slog.New(slog.DiscardHandler) (Go 1.24+) is the clean nil-logger fallback.
  - Validation logic that takes an fs.FS (LoadMigrations) is unit-testable with
    fstest.MapFS — no database needed for the "validation failure" acceptance criterion.

  - testing.TB is a sealed interface (private method) — you CANNOT write a fake
    TB to assert "t.Errorf was called". Pattern: keep the decision logic in a
    pure unexported function (lookupAdminDSN, scanLeaks) and white-box unit-test
    THAT; the testing.TB wrapper is then trivial glue. White-box (package

    is closed, then the DB dropped while the admin pool is still open.

    files are package migrate, so they cannot import testutil even though
    they're "just tests". Bootstrap-layer packages keep local helpers.

    seeder should mint real domain.NewID values; the testutil structs are the
    shape that seeder will consume. Aligning testutil's fake prefixes with the
    domain kinds is optional cleanup, not required.
  - Slug uniqueness "within parent scope" (acceptance #2) is half here: domain
    guarantees well-formedness; the per-scope UNIQUE constraint lands with the
    BE-0013 tenant-hierarchy migration.
  - Acceptance #3 ("Dokploy names include deterministic Yalla IDs"): DokployName
    embeds the full ID. The actual Dokploy mapping (org->project->env->service)
    is consumed by the provisioning worker stories, not this one.
  - Acceptance #5-7 (JSON envelopes / authz / not-found / Postgres integration)
    are N/A for a pure domain-primitive package with no HTTP or DB surface;
    covered success + extensive validation-failure + fuzz instead. #8
    (redaction): IDs and slugs are not secrets — N/A, but error messages
    deliberately do not echo untrusted input (TestParseIDErrorDoesNotEchoInput).
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - golang.org/x/text/transform.Chain is STATEFUL and NOT safe for concurrent
    use. A package-level transform.Chain shared across t.Parallel() subtests
    panics in (*link).src. Pool it (sync.Pool) or build per-call. This will
    bite any future package doing Unicode normalisation.
  - cases.Fold() (golang.org/x/text/cases) does full Unicode case folding,
    which is what maps ß -> "ss"; strings.ToLower and NFKC do NOT. Put it first
    in the chain, before NFD/NFKC.
  - 16 random bytes encode to exactly 26 base32 chars with no padding (5 bytes
    -> 8 chars; 16 = 3*5 + 1 -> 24 + 2 = 26). Crockford lowercase alphabet is
    "0123456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz" (i/l/o/u removed).
  - Go fuzz: f.Add seeds live in code; generated "interesting" corpus goes to
    the build cache, NOT testdata/ — testdata/fuzz/ files appear only on a
    failure. A clean fuzz run leaves the working tree untouched.
  - Keep domain primitives free of apierr/apienvelope imports — return plain
    sentinel errors and let the HTTP layer translate. This keeps the dependency
    arrow pointing one way (httpapi -> domain, never the reverse).

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0013
- What was implemented: the tenant hierarchy schema — organizations, users,
  memberships, projects, environments, services, and dokploy_refs — as
  migration 0002, plus schema-level integration tests.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0002_tenant_hierarchy.up.sql
    (new): the seven tables. organizations is the tenant root; users is a
    GLOBAL identity table linked to orgs only through memberships. projects/
    environments/services each carry organization_id (+ parent IDs) and are
    tenant-isolated by COMPOSITE foreign keys — environments reference
    projects(organization_id, id), services reference
    environments(organization_id, project_id, id) — so a child can never cross
    the tenant boundary. Each parent exposes the matching UNIQUE(organization_id,
    [project_id,] id) constraint the composite FK needs. Slugs are citext and
    unique within parent scope (org for projects, project for environments,
    environment for services), never globally. Every table has created_at/
    updated_at + a set_updated_at() BEFORE UPDATE trigger. memberships PK is
    (organization_id, user_id) with a role CHECK (owner/admin/member). services
    has a kind CHECK (application/database/compose). dokploy_refs is the
    polymorphic Yalla-resource -> Dokploy-object map (yalla_kind/yalla_id +
    dokploy_resource/dokploy_id covering organization/project/environment/
    application/compose/database/domain/backup); tenant-scoped via the
    organization_id FK, UNIQUE(dokploy_resource, dokploy_id) so an object is
    claimed once, UNIQUE(organization_id, yalla_id, dokploy_resource, dokploy_id)
    against duplicate rows while still allowing many domains/backups per
    resource. ON DELETE CASCADE everywhere from organizations down.
  - 0002_tenant_hierarchy.down.sql (new): drops the seven tables newest-first;
    DROP TABLE removes each table's indexes + trigger. set_updated_at() itself
    belongs to the baseline migration and is left in place.
  - internal/controlplane/store/schema_test.go (new, package store_test):
    integration tests via testutil.RequireMigratedDB + testutil.NewFactory —

    org, env/service crossing the tenant boundary via the composite FK), slug
    uniqueness within parent (incl. citext case-insensitivity + same slug
    allowed in a different org), cascade delete (descendants gone, global users
    row survives), cross-tenant isolation (org-scoped count), dokploy_refs
    constraints (object claimed once, duplicate rows rejected, bad
    dokploy_resource rejected, org FK), membership constraints (one per org,
    role CHECK, user FK). Constraint violations matched via *pgconn.PgError
    SQLSTATE class 23.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrate_test.go: TestMigrationsUpIs
    Idempotent's Status().Current assertion now derives the expected version
    from m.Migrations() instead of the literal 1, so future migrations don't
    break it.

    boundary, global users table, dokploy_refs polymorphism, the no-ID-prefix-

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Composite foreign keys are the database-level tenant-isolation primitive:
    child FK (organization_id, parent_id) -> parent UNIQUE(organization_id, id)
    makes "child in a different org than its parent" unrepresentable. Every new
    hierarchy table should follow this and expose the UNIQUE its children need.

  - citext columns give case-insensitive UNIQUE for free — 'shared-slug' and
    'SHARED-SLUG' collide within the same parent scope without a lower() index.

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0014
- What was implemented: the repository transaction pattern in
  internal/controlplane/store — the small persistence layer that makes
  transactional policy and quota checks structurally hard to bypass.
  - store.go: the Querier interface (Exec/Query/QueryRow, satisfied by pgx.Tx
    and *Tx); the *Tx handle (wraps pgx.Tx, unexported field); Store with
    New(pool, logger); Store.Write (read/write tx -> *Tx, commit on nil return,
    rollback on any error or panic via a deferred WithoutCancel rollback);
    Store.Read (read-only tx -> Querier); isConstraintViolation (SQLSTATE class
    23) and mapWriteError (constraint -> apierr.Conflict, else
    apierr.StoreUnavailable, raw cause wrapped for logging only).
  - project.go: Project struct + ProjectRepository — the reference repository.
    Insert requires *Tx (mutation), Get/CountByOrganization take Querier
    (reads). Every query is tenant-scoped (organization_id before id) and fully
    parameterized; pgx.ErrNoRows -> apierr.NotFound.
  - projectservice.go: the Authorizer / QuotaReserver / JobEnqueuer port
    interfaces (real engines land in BE-0018/BE-0022/BE-0024), CreateProjectInput,
    validateCreateProjectInput (pure, returns apierr.InvalidInput with field
    paths), and ProjectService.Create — the reference unit of work: validate,
    then inside one Store.Write compose authorize -> reserve quota -> insert ->
    enqueue job. Any step's failure rolls the whole transaction back.
  - doc.go rewritten to document the pattern.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/store/{store,project,projectservice,doc}.go
  (new/rewritten), internal/controlplane/store/{internal_test,store_test,
  project_test,projectservice_test}.go (new), internal/controlplane/store/
  AGENTS.md, ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go build ./...; go vet ./...; go mod tidy;
  go test ./...; go test -race ./... — the last two with
  YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at the docker-compose Postgres 16, so all 18
  new store tests RUN (not skipped) and PASS, including under -race.
- Results: all passed. Unit tests in package store (internal_test.go) run
  without Postgres; the 12 integration tests in package store_test skip cleanly
  when YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset. goimports / golangci-lint /
  staticcheck / govulncheck still not installed locally (documented in earlier
  entries).
- Acceptance criteria mapping:
  - "Repositories accept context and transaction handles explicitly" — every
    method takes ctx + a Querier or *Tx as its first/second parameter.
  - "Mutations combine authorization, quota, and write state in one
    transaction" — ProjectService.Create.
  - "Tests assert rollback on validation, quota, and Dokploy enqueue failures"
    — TestProjectServiceCreate{ValidationFailure,QuotaFailureRollsBack,
    EnqueueFailureRollsBack}, plus TestWriteRollsBackOn{Error,Panic}.
  - "No SQL string concatenation for user input" — all statements
    parameterized; the only `+` in SQL is the compile-time constant column list.
  - Criterion 5 (JSON envelopes) — no-op: this story has no HTTP surface; all
    errors are typed apierr values that already render through apienvelope.
  - "Unit tests cover success, validation failure, authorization failure,
    not-found" — covered across internal_test.go + the two _test.go suites.
  - "Integration tests run against isolated Postgres migrations, no live
    Dokploy" — RequireMigratedDB; the Dokploy dependency is a fake JobEnqueuer.
  - Redaction — no secrets are stored by this layer; TestMapWriteErrorDoesNotLeakCause
    proves a raw driver cause (DSN/credential) never reaches the error message.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - The port interfaces (Authorizer/QuotaReserver/JobEnqueuer) and the
    project.create / project.provision / projects constants are placeholders
    until BE-0018 (RBAC), BE-0022 (quota checker), and BE-0024 (job table)
    land. When they do, wire the real implementations into ProjectService and
    move ownership of the constants to those packages — store must not import
    them.
  - ProjectRepository is intentionally minimal (Insert/Get/CountByOrganization).
    Later hierarchy-CRUD stories extend it and add Environment/Service repos
    following the same *Tx-mutation / Querier-read split.
  - Store is not yet constructed at cmd/yalla-api startup; that wiring (pool +
    Store + migration runner) is still an open seam from BE-0010/BE-0013.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The "hard to bypass" mechanism is a TYPE, not a convention: *Tx has an
    unexported field and is only produced by Store.Write, so a repository
    mutation that takes *Tx literally cannot be called outside a transaction.
    Copy this split (mutations take *Tx, reads take Querier) for every repo.
  - testutil.Factory IDs are deliberately non-canonical (org_<16hex>0001), so
    domain.ParseID rejects them. Any test that feeds a service whose validation
    calls domain.ParseID/ParseSlug must seed rows with real domain.NewID(...)
    values — see seedDomainOrg in projectservice_test.go. Factory fixtures are
    still fine for direct repository/SQL tests that skip domain validation.
  - Store.Write needs no recover(): a deferred rollback runs during panic
    unwinding, and because the deferred func does not call recover() the panic
    keeps propagating. Use a `committed` bool (not the named return error) to
    decide whether the deferred rollback should fire.
  - Rollback uses context.WithoutCancel(ctx): the caller's context is often
    already cancelled (that is *why* we are rolling back), but the rollback
    must still reach the database. Ignore pgx.ErrTxClosed on rollback — it is
    expected after a failed commit.
  - apierr already keeps raw causes out of the user-facing Message
    (yerr.Error.Error() renders only "code: message"), so wrapping a driver
    error via .Wrap() is leak-safe and still errors.Is-traversable.

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0015
- What was implemented: API key hashing, generation, verification, and the
  persistence layer for customer API keys.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0003_api_keys.{up,down}.sql
    (new): the api_keys table. Stores ONLY secret_hash (one-way) + a public,
    globally-UNIQUE prefix — no column ever holds a usable credential.
    Tenant-scoped via organization_id FK (ON DELETE CASCADE). Lifecycle columns
    expires_at / revoked_at / last_used_at; created_by REFERENCES users ON

  - internal/controlplane/auth/apikey.go (new package): the credential
    primitives. Token shape "yk_<prefixRandom>_<secret>" (Crockford base32, no
    padding) is a public contract. Generate() -> GeneratedKey{Token, Prefix,
    SecretHash}; HashSecret = hex SHA-256 (fast unsalted hash is correct for
    192-bit-entropy secrets); VerifySecret uses subtle.ConstantTimeCompare;
    ParseToken validates shape and returns ErrMalformedToken (never echoes
    input). Token is a self-redacting type: String/GoString/LogValue/
    MarshalJSON all yield output.Sentinel; plaintext only via explicit
    Reveal().
  - internal/controlplane/store/apikey.go (new): APIKey row struct +
    lifecycle predicates (IsRevoked/IsExpired/IsUsable) + APIKeyRepository
    following the *Tx-mutation / Querier-read pattern. Insert/TouchLastUsed/
    Revoke take *Tx; FindByPrefix/Get/ListByOrganization take Querier.
    FindByPrefix is the deliberate non-tenant-scoped auth lookup (documented).
    Revoke is idempotent via COALESCE(revoked_at, $3). Zero-row mutations ->
    apierr.NotFound.
  - internal/controlplane/auth/apikey_test.go (new, package auth_test):
    generate->parse->verify round trip, uniqueness, deterministic hashing,
    constant-time verify (correct/wrong/empty/tampered), ParseToken malformed

    APIKeyRepository.FindByPrefix + auth.VerifySecret (subtle.ConstantTimeCompare).

    present as columns + APIKey fields + lifecycle predicates.

    TestAPIKeyPlaintextIsNeverPersisted + TestTokenRedactsItselfInEveryRendering
    + TestGeneratedKeyNeverLeaksTheSecret.

    errors are typed apierr values that already render through apienvelope.

    not-found" — success + validation failure (ParseToken malformed table) +
    not-found (FindByPrefix/Get/TouchLastUsed/Revoke). Authorization-failure is
    N/A at this layer (the policy engine is BE-0018); the *Tx-only mutation
    surface is the structural hook the authorize step will share.

    no plaintext reaches any column.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - No HTTP endpoint or auth middleware yet: the "create API key" endpoint and
    the request-authentication middleware (parse token -> FindByPrefix ->
    VerifySecret -> IsUsable -> TouchLastUsed -> Principal) are later stories.
    auth.VerifySecret + APIKeyRepository are the primitives they compose.

    service account rather than a user; revisit the created_by FK then.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - A self-redacting credential type needs FOUR methods to be leak-proof
    against testutil.AssertRedactedValue: String (covers %v/%+v/%s), GoString
    (covers %#v), LogValue (slog), MarshalJSON (JSON). Missing any one leaks.
  - testutil.Factory.APIKey only reads org.ID and user.ID off its args, so a
    test can pass partial fixtures: f.APIKey(testutil.Organization{ID: orgID},
    testutil.User{ID: uid}, label) just to borrow its globally-unique key ID.
  - For "plaintext never persisted" assertions, concatenate every text-bearing
    column in SQL (id||'|'||...||array_to_string(scopes,',')) and run
    testutil.AssertRedacted on the result — proves absence across the whole row
    in one shot.
  - Idempotent revoke without a Conflict: UPDATE ... SET col = COALESCE(col, $n)
    keeps the first timestamp and still counts the row as affected, so
    RowsAffected()==0 cleanly means "no such row" -> NotFound, never "already
    done".
  - base32.Encoding.EncodedLen() respects the WithPadding setting — compute
    token-part lengths from it rather than hard-coding, so the entropy budget
    and the ParseToken shape check stay in sync.

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0018
- What was implemented: the RBAC and scoped grants engine — internal/controlplane/policy, the
  authoritative authorization decision engine for the control plane.
  - internal/controlplane/policy/policy.go: package doc + core types. Role (six built-in
    constants: owner/admin/developer/viewer/ci/support); Capability (self/read/deploy/write/
    admin/owner/support); Action (dotted string); Scope (Organization->Project->Environment->
    Service, with unexported covers() containment); Grant (Role + Scope); Resource (domain.Kind
    + Scope); Principal (ID/Kind/OrganizationID/Role/Grants/Disabled — the single concrete type
    both API-key and session auth resolve to); Reason (stable allow/deny codes) + Decision.
  - internal/controlplane/policy/catalog.go: builtinRoleCaps (the authoritative role->capability
    matrix, each role listed in full — capabilities are NOT hierarchical); defaultActionCatalog
    (all 61 API-surface requiredActions -> one Capability each); BuiltinRoles()/Actions() stable
    sorted enumerators; CustomRoleResolver hook type; capSet helper.
  - internal/controlplane/policy/engine.go: Engine (immutable, concurrency-safe), NewEngine +
    Option (WithCustomRoles, WithAction). Decide(Principal, Action, Resource) -> Decision is a
    pure, total, panic-free function with a fixed deny-by-default order: no/disabled principal ->
    unknown action -> CapSelf bypass -> unresolvable org role -> cross-tenant (deny unless
    support read/break-glass) -> org-role capability -> covering-grant capability ->
    out_of_scope vs no_capability. Authorize/AuthorizeCtx map denials onto typed apierr
    (Unauthenticated for a missing principal, Forbidden otherwise; message carries only the
    action + reason code, never an ID). WithPrincipal/PrincipalFromContext carry the principal
    on the request context.
  - internal/controlplane/policy/policy_test.go (white-box, package policy): TestPolicyMatrix
    exhaustively covers all 6 built-in roles x all 61 actions (367 subtests) with verdicts
    derived from the matrix+catalog so drift fails CI; plus no-principal, disabled, unknown
    action, unknown role (and CapSelf bypassing the role check), custom roles (as org role and
    as grant role), grant narrowing/widening/out-of-scope/ignored-invalid (unknown role,
    foreign-org scope), cross-tenant deny + support read/break-glass allow, TestScopeCovers
    containment table, Authorize apierr-code mapping with a no-ID-leak assertion, the context
    carrier round trip, and a catalog/roles well-formedness guard.
  - Removed placeholder internal/controlplane/policy/doc.go (package doc now lives in policy.go).
  - internal/controlplane/AGENTS.md: documented the policy engine, the action catalog as the
    requiredAction source of truth, capability-based roles, scoped grants, and the context carrier.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/policy/{policy.go,catalog.go,engine.go,policy_test.go}
  (new), internal/controlplane/policy/doc.go (deleted), internal/controlplane/AGENTS.md,
  ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...; go test ./...;
  go test -race ./....
- Results: all passed (TestPolicyMatrix = 367 passing subtests). goimports, golangci-lint,
  staticcheck, govulncheck not installed locally.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - The store.Authorizer port (Authorize(ctx, q Querier, action, organizationID)) is NOT yet
    wired to this engine — the existing services still use nopAuthorizer test doubles. A later
    story should add a store-port adapter that reads policy.PrincipalFromContext(ctx), builds an
    org-scoped Resource, and calls Engine.Authorize. It was left out here to keep policy from
    taking a build dependency on store and to keep BE-0018 to the engine itself.
  - Grants are in-memory on the Principal. The DB-backed grant rows the store.Authorizer comment
    anticipates ("a policy decision that reads grant rows") land with the grants-persistence
    story; the project.grants.* / environment.grants.* actions are already catalogued.
  - Postgres integration criterion is N/A (pure engine, no persistence). JSON-envelope criterion
    is N/A (no HTTP surface yet) — the engine emits typed apierr the apienvelope renderer maps.
  - "not-found behavior" maps to ReasonDeniedUnknownAction here (an uncatalogued action); there
    is no resource lookup in a pure engine.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Capability indirection keeps the role/action matrix small and TOTAL: roles confer a Capability
    set, actions require one Capability, and the per-action verdict is a set membership check.
    This made an exhaustive 6x61 table test derivable from the two source-of-truth maps rather
    than hand-enumerated, so the test fails the instant either map drifts.
  - CapSelf is checked BEFORE org-role resolution on purpose: auth.me/auth.orgs/organization.create
    must work for any authenticated principal even one with an unknown/empty role.
  - Cross-tenant is enforced structurally (resource.Scope.OrganizationID != principal.OrganizationID
    is the first thing checked after role resolution), and grants are filtered to the principal's
    own org — a foreign-org grant can never widen authority.
  - The 61 distinct requiredAction values come from prd.json apiSurface.endpoints; query them with
    ctx_execute_file rather than reading the 837KB PRD. defaultActionCatalog must stay in sync as
    later endpoint stories land — TestCatalogAndRolesAreWellFormed asserts the count (61).
  - Go 1.25 in this repo: t.Context() is available in tests; no need for context.Background().

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0020 - Implement authorization middleware
- What was implemented: the request authentication + authorization middleware —
  the layer that turns an inbound bearer credential into a policy.Principal,
  attaches it to the request context, and authorizes the route's action.
  - internal/controlplane/auth/authenticator.go (new): Authenticator +
    AuthenticatorConfig + NewAuthenticator. Authenticate(ctx, bearerToken)
    resolves three schemes by shape — API key ("yk_" prefix), human session
    JWT, internal worker shared secret — to one Identity{Principal, Method}.
    Ports: CredentialStore interface (FindAPIKeyByPrefix / FindServiceAccount /
    OrganizationRoleVersion) + auth-local DTOs APIKeyRecord / ServiceAccountRecord
    so auth never imports store. Sentinels ErrNoCredentials / ErrInvalidCredentials;
    every invalid-credential cause (malformed token, unknown prefix, wrong
    secret, revoked/expired key, bad signature, expired/revoked/unknown-subject
    session) collapses to ErrInvalidCredentials — no prefix-existence oracle —
    while a datastore failure is propagated unchanged. AuthMethod constants,
    InternalWorkerPrincipalID, stable SessionIssuer / SessionAudience. API-key
    principals carry no Role/Grants (grant resolution from api_keys.scopes is a
    later story); session principals get their role from the verified claim;
    the internal worker principal is role-less and org-less. constantTimeEqual
    hashes both inputs so the worker-token compare does not leak length.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/middleware.go (new): RequireAuth(authenticator,
    engine, action, ResourceResolver) and RequireInternalWorker(authenticator)
    middleware; bearerToken (RFC 7235 case-insensitive "Bearer " extraction);
    writeAuthError / toAPIError. Missing creds -> 401 E_AUTH ("authentication is
    required"); invalid -> 401 E_AUTH ("the supplied credentials are invalid",
    fixed/generic); unauthorized -> 403 E_FORBIDDEN with the stable policy
    reason; dependency failure keeps its typed 5xx. Attaches the principal via
    policy.WithPrincipal and enriches the log record via telemetry.SetOrgID /
    SetPrincipalID before the authorization decision. Everything renders through
    apienvelope. The middleware is NOT yet wired into newRouteTable — the
    bootstrap routes are all public; endpoint stories wrap their routes.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0005_membership_role_version.
    {up,down}.sql (new): ALTER memberships ADD COLUMN role_version bigint NOT
    NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (>= 1) — the counter behind version-based session
    revocation that BE-0017's session primitive expected to exist.
  - internal/controlplane/store/membership.go (new): Membership struct +
    MembershipRepository.Get (tenant-scoped read, apierr.NotFound for a
    non-member).
  - internal/controlplane/store/credentials.go (new): CredentialReader — the
    production auth.CredentialStore adapter. store imports auth and composes the
    existing tenant-scoped repository methods (no new SQL). OrganizationRoleVersion
    maps a missing membership to (0,false,nil) but propagates a datastore error.
  - Tests: auth/authenticator_test.go (unit, fake CredentialStore — all three
    schemes, the uniform-invalid contract incl. unknown-prefix == wrong-secret,
    dependency-failure-is-not-401, no-credential-echo); httpapi/middleware_test.go

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0021 - Implement quota policy schema
- What was implemented: migration 0006_quota_policy_schema — the four
  source-of-truth quota tables plus two shared domains. Pure schema story,
  same shape as 0002 tenant hierarchy: migration + schema integration tests,
  no Go repository/service/handler yet (those land with BE-0022).
  - quota_resource DOMAIN: the closed set of 14 countable quota dimensions
    (projects, environments, services, applications, compose_stacks,
    databases, domains, preview_environments, cpu_millicores, memory_mb,
    storage_gb, backups, concurrent_deployments, monthly_deployments) — reused
    by all four tables so an unknown dimension is rejected by the database.
  - quota_enforcement_mode DOMAIN: hard | soft | metered | disabled.
  - quota_policies: one limit per (scope, resource). A row is EITHER a
    plan_default (keyed by text `plan`, no FK to a plans table — plans land
    later) OR an organization override (keyed by organization_id), enforced by
    the quota_policies_scope_consistent CHECK + two partial unique indexes. The
    quota checker resolves "org override if present, else plan default".
  - quota_usage: actual allocated amount, one counter row per
    (organization_id, resource) via UNIQUE — the row the checker locks.
  - quota_reservations: in-flight claims (amount > 0), a status lifecycle
    (active -> committed | released | expired), expires_at so a crashed job
    cannot strand quota, and quota_reservations_settled_consistent CHECK tying
    settled_at to non-active status. Nullable job_id (no FK yet —
    provisioning_jobs is BE-0024). Exposes UNIQUE (organization_id, id) as a
    composite-FK target.
  - usage_events: append-only log (no updated_at, no update trigger), signed
    delta, optional reservation link via composite FK
    (organization_id, reservation_id) -> quota_reservations so a cross-tenant
    reservation reference is unrepresentable.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0006_quota_policy_schema.up.sql (new)
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0006_quota_policy_schema.down.sql (new)
  - internal/controlplane/store/quota_schema_test.go (new, package store_test)
  - internal/controlplane/store/AGENTS.md (quota schema section)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0021 passes -> true), ralph/progress.txt
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...;
  go test ./...; go test -race ./internal/controlplane/store/... — and
  go test -race -v -run 'TestQuota|TestUsageEvents' with
  YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL pointed at the docker-compose Postgres 16.
- Results: all green. All 9 quota schema tests RUN (not skipped) and PASS
  under the race detector; the full suite passes. goimports / golangci-lint /
  staticcheck / govulncheck still not installed locally (documented earlier).
- Acceptance criteria mapping:
  - "Quotas cover projects ... monthly deploy count": the quota_resource
    domain names every listed dimension; TestQuotaResourceDomainEnforcesClosedSet
    inserts all 14 and rejects an unknown one.
  - "Inherited from plan defaults and overridden per organization":
    quota_policies scope model; TestQuotaPolicyScopeConsistency /
    TestQuotaPolicyUniquePerScope (a plan default and an org override for the
    same resource coexist; duplicates within a scope are rejected).
  - "Reservation rows expire or release on job completion/failure": status
    lifecycle + expires_at + settled_at CHECK; TestQuotaReservationLifecycleConstraints.
  - "Tests cover concurrent reservations with row locks":
    TestQuotaReservationConcurrentRowLock (two pgx transactions, SELECT ...
    FOR UPDATE / NOWAIT, SQLSTATE 55P03, then success after commit).
  - "Integration tests run against isolated Postgres migrations": all tests use
    testutil.RequireMigratedDB and skip cleanly without YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL.
  - Criteria about JSON envelopes / unit tests for authz / not-found are N/A for
    a pure schema migration with no HTTP surface (same as 0002); covered success
    + extensive constraint-violation + cascade (not-found-style) instead.
  - Redaction: no quota table stores secrets, tokens, or rendered env values.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - quota_reservations.job_id has no FK — provisioning_jobs does not exist
    until BE-0024. A later migration should add the composite
    (organization_id, job_id) FK once that table and its UNIQUE target land.
  - The plan-default scope uses a plain-text `plan` column; when the `plans`
    table is introduced, a later migration can add an FK if desired.
  - BE-0022 (quota checker service) builds the repository + unit-of-work on top
    of this schema, following the ProjectRepository/ProjectService pattern.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - A Postgres DOMAIN over text + CHECK is the clean way to share a closed enum
    across multiple tables; DROP DOMAIN goes in the down migration AFTER the
    tables that use it. Check domain existence in tests via
    information_schema.domains.
  - testutil.DB embeds *pgxpool.Pool, so db.Begin(ctx) yields a real pgx.Tx —
    use two independent transactions for row-lock tests. SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
    NOWAIT raises *pgconn.PgError with SQLSTATE 55P03 (lock_not_available);
    match it with errors.As, not a string compare.
  - "Exactly one of N nullable columns is set" is one table CHECK; pair it with
    partial unique indexes (WHERE scope_kind = '...') so each scope has
    independent uniqueness.
  - A composite FK with ON DELETE SET NULL does NOT work when one FK column is
    NOT NULL (it would null organization_id). For an optional cross-table link
    inside a tenant, use a plain composite FK (MATCH SIMPLE, default NO ACTION) —
    the org-level ON DELETE CASCADE still cleans both sides.
  - Schema-story tests live in package store_test and reuse seedOrg from
    schema_test.go; put story-specific seed helpers in the new test file.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0022
- Implemented the quota checker service: the QuotaReserver unit of work that
  enforces an organization's limits before a resource is created or a
  provisioning job is enqueued.
- Persistence layer (internal/controlplane/store/quota.go): QuotaRepository
  following the ProjectRepository transaction pattern — reads take Querier,
  mutations take *Tx, every query tenant-scoped by organization_id.
  - QuotaResource (closed set mirroring the quota_resource DOMAIN, 14
    dimensions) + EnforcementMode constants + reservation status constants.
  - QuotaLimit / QuotaReservation persistence shapes.
  - EffectiveLimit: one ordered query resolving "organization override else
    plan default" for a (org, plan, resource); returns found=false when no
    policy exists at either scope.
  - LockUsage: upserts the (org, resource) quota_usage counter row
    (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) then SELECT ... FOR UPDATE — the
    serialisation primitive that prevents concurrent over-allocation.
  - SumActiveReservations: COALESCE(SUM(amount)) of active, non-expired
    reservations for a (org, resource).
  - InsertReservation: writes a reservation row, mints a prefixed opaque id
    (newQuotaID) when blank — quota accounting rows are not domain resources
    so they carry their own id, not a domain.Kind id.
- Service layer (internal/controlplane/quota/quota.go): Checker implements
  store.QuotaReserver (compile-time assertion). Reserve validates input,
  resolves the plan via a PlanResolver (StaticPlanResolver placeholder until a
  plans table lands), resolves the effective limit, and for a hard limit locks
  the usage counter, sums active reservations, and rejects when
  current+reserved+requested > limit. Soft/metered limits are recorded but
  never rejected; disabled limits and unconfigured resources are allowed with
  no write. Rejections are apierr.QuotaExceeded with a hint naming
  current/reserved/requested/limit and a recoverable ExceededDetail wrapped as
  the cause (quota.DetailOf).
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/store/quota.go (new)
  - internal/controlplane/store/quota_internal_test.go (new, package store)
  - internal/controlplane/store/quota_repository_test.go (new, package store_test)
  - internal/controlplane/quota/quota.go (new)
  - internal/controlplane/quota/quota_test.go (new)
  - internal/controlplane/quota/doc.go (expanded package doc)
  - internal/controlplane/store/AGENTS.md (quota repository note)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0022 passes: true)
- Verification (YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL set, local Postgres 16 via docker compose):
  - gofmt -l: clean; go mod tidy: no changes; go build ./...: clean.
  - go vet ./...: clean.
  - go test ./...: all pass.
  - go test -race ./...: all pass (incl. TestCheckerReserveConcurrentRespectsLimit,
    9 parallel reservations against a hard limit of 3 — exactly 3 commit).
- Acceptance criteria mapping:
  - "Quota checks run inside the same transaction as desired-state writes":
    Reserve takes the caller's *store.Tx; LockUsage/SumActiveReservations/
    InsertReservation all run on it, so the check and the reservation commit or
    roll back atomically with the resource (proven by the rollback assertion in
    TestCheckerReserveRejectsWhenLimitExhausted).
  - "Checker returns current, reserved, requested, limit, and recoverable hint
    in errors": quota.ExceededDetail wrapped in apierr.QuotaExceeded, recovered
    via quota.DetailOf; hint carries the same four counts.
  - "Concurrent create requests cannot exceed limits" / "Integration tests
    simulate parallel requests": TestCheckerReserveConcurrentRespectsLimit.
  - "Unit tests cover success/validation/authorization/not-found": success +
    validation are covered; "authorization failure" is N/A — quota runs after
    the authz step of the unit of work and has no authz surface of its own;
    "not-found" maps to the no-policy-configured path
    (TestCheckerReserveAllowsWhenNoPolicyConfigured / EffectiveLimitNotFound).
  - "JSON envelopes yalla.output.v1 / yalla.error.v1": N/A for an internal
    service with no HTTP surface; the typed apierr.QuotaExceeded it returns
    renders through apienvelope at the endpoint layer (later HTTP stories).
  - "Integration tests run against isolated Postgres migrations": all use
    testutil.RequireMigratedDB and skip without YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL.
  - "Secrets redacted": no quota table or type stores secrets; ExceededDetail
    carries only resource names and counts.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - quota_usage.used_value is never incremented by Reserve — only active
    reservations count against the limit. Committing a reservation (used_value
    += amount, status -> committed, usage_event row) and releasing/expiring it
    belong to the reservation-lifecycle / metering stories.
  - usage_events is intentionally not written here — it is the metering/audit
    trail and is owned by the metering stories.
  - PlanResolver is a StaticPlanResolver placeholder; when the plans table
    lands, a DB-backed resolver replaces it without touching the Checker.
  - The Checker is not yet wired into a composition root or any endpoint; the
    project/service create endpoints (later stories) pass *quota.Checker as the
    store.QuotaReserver.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The QuotaReserver port signature (Reserve(ctx, *store.Tx, orgID, resource
    string) error) is fixed by store and ProjectService — the checker reserves
    exactly one unit per call; do not change the port.
  - INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING followed by SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in the
    same tx is the safe upsert-then-lock idiom: a concurrent inserter blocks on
    the uncommitted insert, so by the time the SELECT runs the row is always
    visible and lockable — no "0 rows" race.
  - errors.As works with a value-receiver error type as the As target
    (var d ExceededDetail; errors.As(err, &d)) — wrap the value, not a pointer.
  - Quota accounting rows (quota_usage, quota_reservations) have no domain.Kind;
    mint their ids locally with a prefixed crypto/rand helper rather than
    expanding the domain package's public Kind contract.

  - An append-only table that must still participate in ON DELETE CASCADE can
    only block UPDATE — a BEFORE DELETE trigger would also break the cascade.
    Block UPDATE in the DB; keep DELETE out of the application surface instead.
  - pgx.Rows satisfies pgx.Row, so one scan helper (taking pgx.Row) serves both
    a QueryRow RETURNING and a Query/rows.Next loop — no duplicate scanner.
  - A package that needs a *store.Tx in its signature can still be unit-tested
    without a database: depend on a narrow port (here Recorder), and the fake
    ignores the *store.Tx so tests pass a typed nil. The real *Tx path is
    covered by the store package's own integration tests.
  - Redacting audit metadata needs BOTH a key-based rule (a value under a
    secret-shaped key IS the secret — replace it wholesale) and a value-based
    rule (output.Redactor for transport patterns). The structural Redactor
    alone does not catch a bare secret stored under e.g. "api_token".

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0024 - Implement provisioning job table
- What was implemented: the durable provisioning job table — schema, the
  state machine, and the JobRepository persistence layer.
  - store/migrate/migrations/0008_provisioning_jobs.{up,down}.sql: the
    provisioning_jobs table. Carries every field the story requires —
    job_type, resource targets (project_id/environment_id/service_id),
    desired_version, idempotency_key, status, attempts, max_attempts,
    lease_owner, lease_deadline, next_run_at, error_summary — plus payload
    (jsonb), request_id, correlation_id, and the timestamp columns. Tenant
    isolation is database-enforced: organization_id FK to organizations
    (ON DELETE CASCADE) and composite (organization_id, <resource>_id) FKs to
    projects/environments/services, so a job can never target another tenant's
    resource. CHECKs enforce the closed 7-status set, "terminal status iff
    finished_at set", "lease held iff status='running'", and
    attempts<=max_attempts. UNIQUE (organization_id, idempotency_key) is the
    idempotency guarantee; UNIQUE (organization_id, id) is the composite-FK
    target. 0008 also wires the FK that 0006 deferred:
    quota_reservations.job_id -> provisioning_jobs (organization_id, id),
    dropped first in the down migration.
  - store/job.go: JobStatus (the 7 statuses) with Valid/String/Terminal and
    CanTransitionTo backed by the authoritative jobTransitions map. JobRepository
    follows the ProjectRepository pattern — Insert/Transition need *Tx, Get/
    FindByIdempotencyKey/ListByOrganization take Querier, every query tenant-
    scoped, NotFound for cross-tenant ids. Insert mints a domain.NewID(KindJob),
    forces a new job to queued/0-attempts, defaults max_attempts and next_run_at,
    and validates required fields via apierr.InvalidInput. Transition locks the
    row FOR UPDATE, validates the edge with CanTransitionTo before any write
    (illegal edge = apierr.Conflict), then derives lease/attempt/timestamp
    bookkeeping from the target status (claim takes the lease + counts an
    attempt + rejects past the retry budget; retry releases the lease + sets
    backoff; terminals release the lease + stamp finished_at). error_summary is
    run through a package-level output.NewRedactor() on every write.
  - store/job_internal_test.go: white-box unit tests (no DB) — status set, the
    full CanTransitionTo matrix, Terminal, redactJobError, payload (un)marshal,
    nullable helpers, JobTransition.now defaulting, and the nil-tx / invalid-
    status / validation guards on Insert and Transition.
  - store/job_test.go: integration tests — insert+get, idempotency conflict,
    same-key-different-orgs, FindByIdempotencyKey (hit/miss/cross-tenant),
    cross-tenant Get -> NotFound, ListByOrganization tenant isolation, the full
    transition lifecycle (claim/succeed), retry-then-reclaim, dead-letter,
    retry-budget-exhausted, cancellation, invalid transitions (queued->succeeded
    and terminal->running), transition NotFound, claim-without-lease ->
    InvalidInput, cross-tenant resource target rejected by composite FK,
    unknown-org rejected, and the error_summary redaction backstop.

  - JobRepository is not yet wired into a composition root, the worker queue,

    lease-reaper queries on top of provisioning_jobs_claim_idx /
    provisioning_jobs_lease_deadline_idx; the projectservice.go JobEnqueuer port
    will be satisfied by a jobs service that calls JobRepository.Insert.
  - Resource-target FKs are ON DELETE CASCADE: deleting a project/environment/
    service cascade-deletes its jobs (consistent with the hierarchy tables and
    the organizations cascade). If a story later needs job history to survive
    resource deletion, that is a schema change (re-home the rows), not a code
    change here.
  - "Audited" transitions: the hook point is Store.Write composition; the
    Auditor wiring is deferred to the stories that own a composition root.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - A deferred composite FK (0006 left quota_reservations.job_id unconstrained
    because provisioning_jobs did not exist yet) is wired with a plain
    ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT in the later migration, and dropped FIRST in
    that migration's down file — it depends on the table's composite UNIQUE key.
  - The provisioning_jobs lease CHECK ties lease_owner+lease_deadline to
    status='running' (both-set iff running). Transition therefore cannot let a
    caller hand-set the lease; it derives the lease columns from the target
    status, which is also why JobTransition is an options struct, not a full row.
  - mapWriteError already turns a UNIQUE / FK violation into apierr.Conflict,
    so the idempotency-key collision, the cross-tenant resource FK, and the
    unknown-org FK all surface as CodeConflict with one conflictMessage — no
    per-constraint branching needed in the repository.
  - go test -run TestMigrations ./... is the cheap check that a new migration
    loads and applies from an empty DB; the migrate package auto-discovers
    migrations/*.sql via //go:embed, so there is no manifest to update.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0025
- What was implemented: the Postgres-backed worker queue — workers claim durable
  provisioning jobs with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, run them through an
  injected runner, and classify failures into retry / dead-letter / permanent.
  - internal/controlplane/store/job.go: added JobRepository.ClaimNext(ctx, tx,
    owner, leaseDuration, now) — the SKIP LOCKED claim. It selects the single
    most-eligible job (queued|retrying AND next_run_at<=now, OR running AND
    lease_deadline<now) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so concurrent claimers skip a
    locked row instead of blocking, then transitions it to running in the same
    tx. Private reclaimExpiredLease moves a crashed worker's running job back
    through the state machine (running->retrying->running) so attempt/lease
    bookkeeping stays consistent, or dead-letters it when the retry budget is
    already spent (poll then claims nothing rather than handing out a doomed
    job). nil tx / empty owner / non-positive lease are typed apierr.Internal.
  - internal/controlplane/worker/queue.go (new): the store-backed Claimer/Lease
    implementation. loop.go stays pure (interfaces only); queue.go is the only
    worker file importing store. JobRunner/RunnerFunc is the injected work port.
    Terminal(err)/IsTerminal classify a permanent failure. Backoff.Delay is
    bounded exponential (base*2^(attempt-1) capped at Max, optional full
    jitter, overflow-safe by doubling-with-cap). StoreClaimer (built via
    NewStoreClaimer, which validates Store/Runner/Owner -> apierr.InvalidInput)
    leases via ClaimNext; storeLease.Run executes the runner and records the
    outcome — success -> succeeded, Terminal error -> failed, transient with
    budget left -> retrying with backoff, transient with budget spent ->
    dead_letter. complete() writes the outcome on a context.WithoutCancel +
    timeout context so a finished job's result survives shutdown; only an
    interrupted (un-run) job returns non-nil from Run so the loop releases it.
    Release requeues an interrupted job claimable-immediately. NewOwnerID mints
    a process-unique lease owner.
  - internal/controlplane/store/job_test.go: added ClaimNext integration tests
    — leases a due job, empty queue + not-yet-due job, reclaims an expired
    lease (counts an attempt), dead-letters an exhausted expired lease,
    concurrent SKIP LOCKED (6 workers x 24 jobs, each claimed exactly once),
    and validation (nil tx / empty owner / zero lease).
  - internal/controlplane/worker/queue_internal_test.go (new): pure unit tests
    for Backoff.Delay (bounded exponential, defaults, Max<Base, jitter bounds),
    Terminal/IsTerminal classification through wrapping, NewOwnerID uniqueness.
  - internal/controlplane/worker/queue_test.go (new): StoreClaimer integration
    tests — runs a job to succeeded, retries a transient failure with a
    backed-off next_run_at, fails a Terminal error without retrying,
    dead-letters after the retry budget (with a secret redacted in the failure
    summary), Release requeues, and the headline test: two worker.Loop workers
    against the same queue run all 16 jobs exactly once and all reach succeeded.
  - cmd/yalla-worker/main.go: comment updated — StoreClaimer is built and
    tested; the binary stays on NoopClaimer only until the JobRunner (typed
    Dokploy provisioner) lands in a later story.
  - internal/controlplane/worker/AGENTS.md (new): records the loop.go-pure /
    queue.go-store-backed split and the queue conventions.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/store/job.go,
  internal/controlplane/store/job_test.go,
  internal/controlplane/worker/queue.go (new),
  internal/controlplane/worker/queue_internal_test.go (new),
  internal/controlplane/worker/queue_test.go (new),
  internal/controlplane/worker/AGENTS.md (new),
  cmd/yalla-worker/main.go, ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy (no-op, no new deps); go build ./...;
  go vet ./...; go test ./... and go test -race ./... with
  YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL pointed at the docker-compose Postgres.
- Results: all passed (build, vet, full test suite, race detector on store +
  worker). goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck not installed
  locally (documented in earlier entries).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - cmd/yalla-worker still uses NoopClaimer: a StoreClaimer needs a JobRunner,
    which is the typed Dokploy provisioner from a later story (BE-0029+).
    Wiring StoreClaimer into main is a one-liner once that runner exists; it
    also needs a real pgx pool wired into the worker binary at startup.
  - Acceptance criterion "authorization failure" is N/A — the worker queue is
    an internal subsystem with no HTTP surface and no policy action; covered
    success / validation failure / not-found-equivalent (empty queue, expired
    lease) instead. "Stable JSON envelopes" is likewise N/A here (no HTTP).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - SKIP LOCKED + the Store.Write row lock is the whole concurrency story: a
    claimer's open transaction holds the row, a peer's SELECT ... SKIP LOCKED
    skips it, the transition to running commits with the lock held. No queue
    library needed.
  - Reclaiming an expired lease THROUGH the existing state machine
    (running->retrying->running) avoids adding a running->running self-edge to
    jobTransitions and keeps attempt counting honest — a reclaim is just
    another retry.
  - The Lease contract subtlety: storeLease.Run must record outcomes on a
    context detached from cancellation (context.WithoutCancel + timeout). If it
    used the live ctx, a job that finished exactly as shutdown began would fail
    its own success-write, get treated as interrupted, and be released for a
    duplicate run. Only a genuinely un-run (interrupted) job returns non-nil.
  - A concurrent-claim test where workers exit on the first empty result is
    flaky: a job locked by a peer's still-open tx looks empty via SKIP LOCKED.
    Workers must retry-until-drained with a deadline guard.
  - worker_test (package worker_test) cannot reach store/schema_test.go's
    seedOrg helpers — re-seed the org with a local INSERT helper.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0026
- What was implemented: the HTTP idempotency-key middleware that makes mutating
  control-plane endpoints safe for agent and CI retries — a client attaches an
  Idempotency-Key, and the handler runs at most once per key while every retry
  receives the same response.
  - internal/errors/errors.go: added the stable yerr.CodeIdempotencyConflict
    ("E_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT") error code with its codeDescriptions, AllCodes,
    and ExitCode (6, like E_CONFLICT) entries — the code is shared with the CLI
    manifest, so all four sites had to be updated together.
  - internal/controlplane/apienvelope/apienvelope.go: StatusForCode maps
    E_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT -> 409.
  - internal/controlplane/apierr/apierr.go: added the taxonomy entry
    (MessageSpecific, non-retryable) and the apierr.IdempotencyConflict(message)
    constructor, which carries a fixed recovery hint.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0009_idempotency_keys.{up,down}.sql
    (new): the idempotency_keys table — id, organization_id (FK, ON DELETE
    CASCADE), principal_id, idempotency_key, route, request_hash (sha256 hex),
    request_id, status ('pending'|'completed'), response_status, response_body
    (bytea), created_at, completed_at, expires_at. A completion CHECK ties
    status='completed' to a non-null response triple and 'pending' to all-null.
    UNIQUE (organization_id, principal_id, idempotency_key) scopes a key to a
    principal within a tenant; an expires_at index supports a future janitor.
  - internal/controlplane/store/idempotency.go (new): IdempotencyRepository
    with the claim protocol. Claim is a WHERE-guarded upsert (INSERT ... ON
    CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE expires_at <= now()) — fresh claim or
    expired-row takeover both RETURN the row (claimed=true); a live claim makes
    DO UPDATE a no-op so RETURNING yields nothing and a follow-up Find reads the
    row the upsert attempt already locked (claimed=false). Complete updates a
    pending row to completed with the recorded response; Release deletes a
    pending row; Find is the tenant-scoped read. IdempotencyKeyRef bundles
    (org, principal, key); ids are minted locally with an "idk_" prefix like the
    other internal accounting tables.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/idempotency.go (new): RequireIdempotency
    middleware + the narrow IdempotencyStore port + NewIdempotencyStore adapter
    (each repo call in its own Store.Write). Safe methods and keyless unsafe
    requests pass through; a malformed key is 400 E_INVALID_INPUT; a missing
    principal is 500 E_INTERNAL (wiring guard). The request body is buffered to
    compute the sha256 hash, then restored as a fresh r.Body. On claimed=true
    the handler runs against a buffering responseCapture; status < 500 ->
    Complete records the rendered envelope, status >= 500 (or an oversized body)
    -> Release so the failure is retried, not replayed. On claimed=false: hash
    mismatch -> E_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, completed -> replay the recorded
    body+status with Idempotency-Replayed: true, pending -> E_CONFLICT
    "already in progress".
  - internal/controlplane/store/idempotency_test.go (new): integration tests —
    claim+complete, replay after completion, in-flight pending claim,
    same-key/different-request returns the original, expired-claim takeover,
    release-then-reclaim, complete rejects a non-pending claim, tenant + cross-
    principal isolation, validation (nil tx, missing fields, out-of-range
    status), and a missing-key Find.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/idempotency_test.go (new): contract tests with
    a fake IdempotencyStore — safe-method and no-key pass-through, key
    validation (space / control char / too long), missing-principal 500, first
    request runs and records, replay of a completed response, in-flight
    E_CONFLICT, same-key/different-request E_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, 5xx not
    recorded (claim released, retry re-runs), client errors (validation /
    authorization / not-found) recorded and replayed, a concurrent
    before-and-after-completion end-to-end test, claim-store dependency failure,
    request body preserved for the handler, and a redaction check that a secret
    in a handler error never survives into the stored or replayed body.
  - Updated the error-code test tables in internal/errors/errors_test.go,
    apienvelope/apienvelope_test.go, and apierr/apierr_test.go.
- Files changed: internal/errors/errors.go, internal/errors/errors_test.go,

  go build ./...; go vet ./...; go test ./... and go test -race ./... with
  YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL pointed at the docker-compose Postgres.
- Results: all passed (build, vet, full test suite, race detector on httpapi +
  store + the error packages). goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck,
  govulncheck not installed locally (documented in earlier entries).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - RequireIdempotency is implemented and fully tested but not yet wired into
    any route — there are no mutating endpoints in the route table yet. It is
    wired in alongside the first mutating endpoint, the same way RequireAuth is
    built and tested but unused until customer endpoints land.
  - The OpenAPI surface is unchanged: no public endpoint was added, so there is
    nothing to document yet. When the first mutating endpoint lands, its
    OpenAPI operation should document the Idempotency-Key header and the
    E_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT / 409 response.
  - The acceptance criterion "stores ... expiration" is backed by expires_at +
    transparent expired-claim takeover; a background janitor to purge expired
    rows is a natural follow-up (the expires_at index is already in place).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - A WHERE-guarded ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is the clean way to do "claim, or
    take over only if stale": against a live row the DO UPDATE's WHERE makes it
    a no-op so RETURNING yields ErrNoRows, but the conflicting row is still
    LOCKED for the rest of the tx — so the follow-up SELECT inside the same
    Store.Write sees a stable, locked row and concurrent claimers serialise
    there. No xmax trick or advisory lock needed.
  - The idempotency middleware must run a handler against a buffering
    ResponseWriter (responseCapture) rather than streaming, because the
    decision to record vs release depends on the final status — you cannot
    record a response you have already flushed, and you must not record a 5xx.
  - Adding a yerr.Code is a multi-file change: the constant + codeDescriptions
    + AllCodes + ExitCode in internal/errors (it is shared with the CLI
    manifest), the apienvelope.StatusForCode case, the apierr taxonomy entry +
    constructor, and the three test tables (errors_test, apienvelope_test,
    apierr_test). apienvelope_test.TestStatusForCode also iterates AllCodes and
    asserts every code is >= 400, so a new code with no StatusForCode case
    silently passes as 500 — add the case deliberately.
  - readAndRestoreBody buffers r.Body then sets r.Body = io.NopCloser(reader):
    middleware that needs to inspect a request body must restore it or the
    wrapped handler reads nothing.
