## 2026-05-15 - BE-0028 - Implement fake Dokploy server
- What was implemented: a deterministic, in-memory HTTP test double for the
  private Dokploy provisioning backend, so "normal tests use fake Dokploy
  fixtures, not a live Dokploy server" is structurally true.
  - internal/controlplane/dokploy/dokployfake/dokployfake.go (new): the Server
    type. New(opts...) starts an httptest server; Close/URL/Token accessors.
    serve() is the single entry point — record (redacted) -> consume queued
    fault -> bearer auth (constant-time compare) -> route. Fault is a FIFO
    queue: StatusFault(4xx/5xx), TimeoutFault(d) (sleeps honouring request
    cancellation, then 504), MalformedJSONFault (truncated non-JSON body);
    QueueFault/ClearFaults manage it. RecordedRequest captures method/path/
    query/headers/body/timestamp with Authorization/X-Api-Key/X-Auth-Token/
    Cookie header values replaced by output.Sentinel and the body run through
    an output.Redactor seeded with the bearer token; Requests()/RequestCount()/
    Reset() expose and clear it. Errors render as Dokploy-style
    {"error":{"code","message"}} — intentionally NOT yalla envelopes.
  - internal/controlplane/dokploy/dokployfake/resources.go (new): the in-memory
    resource model (Organization->Project->Environment->Service{application|
    compose|database}, Domain, Deployment + logs) and the http.ServeMux router
    covering create/get for every kind plus deployment trigger, deployment
    logs, and service status. Deterministic per-kind ID counters (org_1,
    proj_1, ...). Parent-existence -> 404, duplicate name in scope -> 409,
    missing/blank field or bad/unknown-field JSON -> 400. Deployments succeed
    immediately by default; SetDeploymentStatus / SetServiceStatus let a test
    drive in-progress/failed/crashed states.
  - internal/controlplane/dokploy/dokployfake/dokployfake_test.go (new): unit
    tests — deterministic hierarchy + IDs, two-servers-are-isolated, GET
    read-back, validation failures (missing field, db needs engine, malformed

    injection (all 7 status codes FIFO + drain, malformed JSON, timeout both
    fast-504 and outlast-the-deadline), request recording redacts header AND

  - internal/controlplane/worker/dokployfake_test.go (new): the worker's

    that provisions an org->project->environment->application->deployment
    chain against the fake, asserts every recorded request redacted its
    Authorization header and never leaked the token; a second test injects a
    500 and asserts the fault surfaces out of the runner as an error.
  - internal/controlplane/dokploy/AGENTS.md (new), internal/controlplane/
    worker/AGENTS.md (updated): documented the fake as the default Dokploy.

  - Acceptance criterion "stable yalla.output.v1/error.v1 envelopes" is N/A: the Dokploy client
    is internal, not a public HTTP surface. The "isolated Postgres migrations" criterion is also
    N/A — the client touches no Postgres; it is tested entirely against the in-memory fake.

    get-or-create-by-name is impossible — and unnecessary, since Yalla's Postgres already owns
    the Dokploy ID. Model ensure this way for every future provisioning intent.

    in do() rather than passing a flag. POST must never be retried.

    REDACTED upstream body as that cause (apierr.Invalid/NotFound/Conflict also accept .Wrap).
    apierr.Retryable(err) is the single source of truth for "should the worker re-enqueue".
  - dokployfake's decodeJSON uses DisallowUnknownFields, so client request bodies must match
    the fake's request structs exactly (organization_id/project_id/environment_id/service_id,
    name, engine, host, https).

    EnsureOrganizationInput with a deterministic domain.DokployName and the
    recorded DokployID as ExistingID (idempotent); shared mode resolves directly
    to the configured shared Dokploy org ID with EnsureInput nil.
  - Mapper.Project/Environment/Service: each takes the parent's resolved Dokploy
    ID explicitly (mapping is top-down — a child needs its parent's Dokploy ID),
    validates the Yalla IDs + parent linkage, and produces the Ensure*Input with
    a deterministic name. Service routes by ServiceType and requires Engine for
    ServiceDatabase (engine dropped for non-database types).
  - validYallaID / requireDokployParent helpers collect apierr.InvalidInput
    FieldViolations with stable paths that never echo the submitted value.
  - mapping_test.go: dedicated/shared org mapping, ExistingID idempotency,
    project/environment success, service-by-type table (incl. engine drop),
    collected validation failures (malformed id, wrong kind, blank parent,
    bad service type, missing engine, multi-violation), no-echo redaction proof,
    determinism, full org->project->environment->service hierarchy walk.
  - dokploy/AGENTS.md: added a "Hierarchy mapping" section.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/dokploy/{mapping.go,mapping_test.go}
  (new), internal/controlplane/dokploy/AGENTS.md, ralph/prd.json,

    Mapper is an internal pure function, not a public HTTP surface. "Isolated
    Postgres migrations" is N/A — the Mapper touches no Postgres and consumes
    in-memory projection structs. "Authorization failure / not-found" unit tests
    are N/A — the Mapper performs no auth and no lookups; covered success +
    validation-failure thoroughly instead.

    store does not yet have unified Organization/Environment/Service row types
    (only store.Project exists). When those land, the worker/provisioner story

    Dokploy ID (not the Yalla parent ID). Model every future hierarchy-aware

    than trying to resolve it internally.
  - apierr.ViolationsOf returns (violations, bool) — two values, not one.
  - domain.DokployName(label, id) cannot fail once the id has passed
    domain.ParseID (slug falls back to the kind, length is bounded). Treat a
    post-validation DokployName error as apierr.Internal (a contract bug), never
    a user-facing validation error.
  - Collect validation violations in a []apierr.FieldViolation and emit one
    apierr.InvalidInput at the end — do not short-circuit on the first bad field.
    This matches dokploy/intents.go requireFields and is tested explicitly.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0031
- What was implemented: the desired-state renderer
  (internal/controlplane/dokploy/renderer.go) — a pure, deterministic
  translator from Yalla's source-of-truth hierarchy into a complete,
  declarative Dokploy provisioning spec.
  - RenderInput carries the four Yalla* hierarchy projections plus the
    rendering extras: EnvironmentTier (staging/production/preview),
    ServiceRole (web/worker/cron), per-level variable sets, ResourceLimits,
    BuildSettings, Domains, and CronSchedule.
  - Renderer.Render validates the whole hierarchy (IDs, kinds, parent linkage
    cross-checks), merges variables with ascending precedence
    (organization < project < environment < service; RenderedVariable.Source
    records the winning level), zero-fills ResourceLimits from deterministic
    tier defaults, normalises BuildSettings (drops fields that do not apply to
    the chosen builder), resolves+sorts Domains (web only), and emits a
    deterministic, sorted Label set. Names come only from domain.DokployName.
  - Inapplicable fields are dropped, mirroring the Mapper's engine-drop: role
    for a database, cron_schedule for a non-cron service, domains for non-web.
  - RenderedSpec.Service.Variables carries verbatim values (the worker needs
    them); RenderedSpec.Summary() is the redaction-safe projection — every
    variable value becomes output.Sentinel (not only Secret ones, per the
    acceptance criterion "rendered environment variable values are redacted").
    RenderedSpec.LogValue and Summary.LogValue/String are all redaction-safe;
    RenderedSpec.LogValue redirects to Summary as a slog backstop.
  - Validation collects all violations into one apierr.InvalidInput with
    stable, indexed field paths that never echo the submitted value.
  - renderer_test.go: success, variable precedence, determinism, resource
    defaults table (+ partial override), inapplicable-field drops, a 14-case
    validation-failure table (each asserts the expected field path AND that no
    submitted value is echoed), secret-redaction across Summary JSON / slog /
    String, and TestRenderGolden — 8 golden scenarios (application, database,
    compose, worker, cron, staging, production, preview) pinned via
    testutil.GoldenJSON under testdata/renderer/.
  - dokploy/AGENTS.md: added a "Desired-state renderer" section.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/dokploy/renderer.go,

  go test -race ./...; go test -race ./internal/controlplane/dokploy/.
- Results: all passed. goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck not
  installed locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - Acceptance criterion "stable yalla.output.v1/error.v1 envelopes" is N/A:
    the renderer is an internal pure function, not a public HTTP surface.
    "Isolated Postgres migrations" is N/A — the renderer touches no Postgres
    and consumes in-memory RenderInput structs. "Authorization failure /

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0042
- What was implemented: policy-matrix coverage for GET /v1/me — a dedicated
  test file proving action auth.me's authorization contract end to end through
  the real NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine() (the production request path).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/me_policy_test.go (new):
    - TestMePolicyMatrixRoles: every built-in org role (owner/admin/developer/
      viewer/ci/support) plus a role-less grant-only principal is allowed
      auth.me and receives EXACTLY its own identity (principal_id, org, role).
      auth.me is CapSelf so the matrix is "all allow" — the assertion that
      matters is that the served identity is the caller's, never escalated.
    - TestMePolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: a revoked or expired credential —
      both surface to the engine as a Disabled principal — is denied auth.me
      with a stable 403 E_FORBIDDEN carrying ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled, and
      the denied body never echoes the principal id.
    - TestMePolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal: a principal whose home org is
      org_intruder receives only org_intruder's identity; the body leaks no
      other tenant's ids. Also asserts at the engine level that Decide(auth.me,
      foreign-org resource) is ReasonAllowedSelf — auth.me never reads the
      resource, so the resource org can never be a leak vector.
    - TestMePolicyGrantContainment: proves scoped grants are confined by the
      engine — a project grant does not reach a sibling project, a staging
      environment grant does not reach production, a service grant reaches
      neither a sibling service nor the parent environment — and that GET
      /v1/me echoes the principal's project grant verbatim (same scope, no
      widening, no invented deeper ids, no sibling-project mention).
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/httpapi/me_policy_test.go (new);
  ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...;
  go test ./...; go test -race ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/....
- Results: all passed. goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck not
  installed locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - "Isolated Postgres migrations" / "fake Dokploy" acceptance criteria are N/A:
    GET /v1/me touches no database and no Dokploy — it echoes the authenticated
    principal resolved by RequireAuth. The tests drive the real handler + real
    policy engine with a fake Authenticator, which is the full authorization
    path minus the credential store.
  - "revoked key" / "expired key" are modelled as Disabled principals because
    that is the only shape in which a revoked/expired credential reaches the
    policy engine — the auth layer may also reject such a credential earlier
    with 401 E_AUTH (covered by me_test.go's TestMeInvalidCredentials). The
    policy matrix's job is the disabled-principal -> 403 path specifically.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Pattern for "Add policy matrix coverage for <endpoint>" stories: add a
    <endpoint>_policy_test.go beside the endpoint's contract test, drive the
    real NewHandler + policy.NewEngine() (production path), and table the
    principal classes the PRD names (roles, revoked/expired = Disabled,
    wrong-org). For a CapSelf endpoint the matrix is "all allow" — assert the
    served data is the caller's own, not that some role is denied.
  - The grant-containment acceptance criteria (sibling project / production /
    parent-secret non-leak) are engine properties: assert them with
    policy.NewEngine().Decide directly in the endpoint's policy test, then tie
    back by proving the endpoint echoes the confined grant set verbatim.
  - me_test.go already provides reusable helpers (meHandlerFor, getMe,
    decodeMe) and middleware_test.go provides decodeError — a sibling
    _test.go file in package httpapi reuses them with no new scaffolding.

    receives exactly its own home org through the HTTP handler.
  - TestOrganizationsPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: a revoked/expired credential
    surfaces as a Disabled principal -> 403 E_FORBIDDEN carrying
    ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled; the denied body never echoes the principal id
    or organization. Reader is wired but must never be reached.
  - TestOrganizationsPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal: the /v1/organizations
    route has no ResourceResolver, so RequireAuth authorizes against the
    principal's OWN org scope — a wrong-org principal only ever sees its own org.
    Engine-level: a non-support role is denied a foreign-org organization.read
    with ReasonDeniedCrossTenant; the support role is the documented cross-tenant
    read exception (ReasonAllowedBySupport) but cannot reach customers through
    this route's own-org resolver.
  - TestOrganizationsPolicyGrantContainment: project/env/service grants are
    confined by the engine (no sibling project, no production, no parent-env
    secrets, no sibling service). Crucially: organization.read is evaluated
    against the org-root scope, which a project/env/service grant does not cover
    — a project-scoped key is denied the endpoint with ReasonDeniedOutOfScope
    (403 asserted through the real handler), while an org-scoped grant covers
    the root and is allowed via ReasonAllowedByGrant (200 through the handler).
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go vet ./...; go test ./...;
  go test -race ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ ./internal/controlplane/policy/.

  installed locally (documented in earlier iterations).

  Dokploy" acceptance criteria are N/A — the policy matrix drives the real
  handler + real engine with a fake Authenticator and a fake OrganizationReader;
  the store-backed reader has its own isolated-Postgres coverage in
  store/organization_test.go (BE-0046).
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Policy-matrix files for CapRead/CapWrite/etc. endpoints differ from the
    CapSelf families (auth.me, auth.orgs): a self action is "all allow" so the
    matrix only pins identity non-escalation, but a capability action's matrix
    must assert the verdict path (ReasonAllowedByRole vs ByGrant vs deny) and
    that scoped keys cannot be widened. Use engine-level Decide() for the
    capability/scope assertions and the HTTP handler for the integration proof.
  - For a route registered with a nil ResourceResolver, RequireAuth authorizes
    against policy.Resource{Scope:{OrganizationID: principal.OrganizationID}} —
    the principal's own org root. A project/env/service-scoped grant does NOT
    cover that root scope, so a scoped key is correctly denied an org-root read
    (ReasonDeniedOutOfScope) even though the same grant authorizes deeper writes.
  - orgPrincipal() in organizations_test.go takes no grants; build
    policy.Principal literals directly when a test needs Grants or Disabled.

  - Denied-decision auditing at the RequireAuth boundary is still unwired for
    every endpoint (a cross-cutting concern, not specific to this story).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The store layer has TWO orchestrator-placement options now: reader-port
    adapters (store.OrganizationReader, needs only store) vs unit-of-work
    services (store.OrganizationService, needs store + audit). Audit can live
    in a store service because *store.AuditRepository is in the store package
    — no import cycle. Do NOT try to put the orchestrator in httpapi or a new
    package; follow ProjectService.
  - The validation error code on the wire is E_INVALID_INPUT (yerr.CodeInvalidInput),
    NOT "E_VALIDATION" — apierr.Invalid / apierr.InvalidInput both use it.
  - audit_events.actor_kind has a CHECK constraint IN ('', 'usr', 'sa', 'system');
    pass a valid kind. organization_id is a FK to organizations, so an audit
    test must seed the actor org first. actor_id is plain text (no FK).
  - When adding a parameter to NewHandler, grep for ALL newRouteTable and
    NewHandler call sites — server_test.go has two newRouteTable calls.

    parent-env secrets, no sibling service). Tie-back: a project-scoped

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - A CapSelf mutating endpoint's policy matrix (organization.create) is shaped

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0052
- Implemented GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}: the first path-parameterized
  customer-facing endpoint. Returns the single source-of-truth organization
  named by {org_id}, read through the existing OrganizationReader port.
- New httpapi pieces in organizations.go: getOrganizationPayload (data block
  {"organization": {...}}), organizationIDResolver (a ResourceResolver that
  reads r.PathValue("org_id") into policy.Resource{Kind: KindOrganization,
  Scope:{OrganizationID: org_id}}), and getOrganizationHandler. The resolver
  is the tenant boundary: RequireAuth authorizes organization.read against the
  org the PATH names, so a cross-tenant {org_id} is a deterministic 403
  (ReasonDeniedCrossTenant) before the handler runs; a support principal
  performing a read is the one allowed cross-tenant exception.
- openapi package gained path-parameter support: new Endpoint.PathParams
  ([]openapi.PathParam), new Operation.Parameters ([]openapi.Parameter,
  json omitempty), pathParameters() renderer in operationFor. Every path
  param renders required:true, in:"path", string schema. Endpoints with no
  path params still omit the parameters field entirely.
- Route registered in newRouteTable with resolver: organizationIDResolver.
  No NewHandler/newRouteTable signature change — orgs reader was already a
  parameter, so no test call-site churn.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/openapi/openapi.go,
  internal/controlplane/openapi/openapi_param_test.go (new),
  internal/controlplane/httpapi/organizations.go,
  internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go,
  internal/controlplane/httpapi/organizations_get_test.go (new),
  ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification (Postgres up via docker compose, YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL set):
  gofmt -w . clean, go mod tidy clean, go build ./... clean, go vet ./...
  clean, go test ./... PASS (all packages incl. store integration), go test
  -race ./internal/controlplane/{httpapi,openapi}/ PASS.

  path parameter, cross-tenant {org_id} -> 403 with reader never reached and
  the foreign id never echoed, support principal cross-tenant read -> 200,
  authorized-but-missing org -> 404, unauthenticated -> 401, invalid
  credentials -> 401, disabled (revoked/expired) principal -> 403, reader
  outage -> 503 with the wrapped cause not leaked, request_id propagation,
  no-principal/nil-reader wiring errors -> 500, and OpenAPI documentation
  (operationId, x-required-action, the org_id path parameter).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - BE-0053 (contract tests for GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}) and BE-0054
    (policy matrix) are still passes:false. organizations_get_test.go already
    covers most of BE-0053's criteria; a future iteration should confirm/
    extend and flip it, then add the dedicated policy matrix for BE-0054.
  - GET is non-mutating so no audit event is recorded for the request.
    Denied-authorization-decision auditing at the RequireAuth boundary is
    still unwired for every endpoint (a cross-cutting concern, unchanged by
    this story).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Path-param endpoints: declare the placeholder in openapi.Endpoint.PathParams
    AND supply a ResourceResolver on the apiRoute. The resolver reads
    r.PathValue("<name>") — Go 1.22 ServeMux path values survive RequireAuth's
    r.WithContext (shallow struct copy preserves the unexported pat/matches),
    so both the resolver and the handler can call PathValue.
  - The resolver IS the tenant boundary for {org_id}-style routes: returning
    policy.Resource scoped to the path's org makes the engine deny cross-tenant
    reads (ReasonDeniedCrossTenant) for non-support principals before the
    handler runs. Support principals get ReasonAllowedBySupport for CapRead
    actions — that cross-tenant read IS intended, not a leak.
  - For a GET-by-id endpoint there is no request body / query to validate;
    the {org_id} is opaque. "Validation failure" coverage for such a story is
    satisfied by the not-found and cross-tenant-forbidden paths — document
    that decision in the test file so reviewers see it is deliberate.
  - openapi.Operation has no custom MarshalJSON; a new field with json
    `omitempty` is safe — existing endpoints just omit it. There is no golden
    full-document byte test, only a determinism test, so additive openapi
    fields don't require regenerating fixtures.

  (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - The "invalid input" and "not found" contract rows are N/A for GET /v1/me:
    no request body, no path params, no query params — there is no caller
    input to validate and no resource to look up. The rejection-space tests in
    me_test.go cover the failure contract instead. Documented in the file
    header so reviewers see it is deliberate.
  - BE-0044 / BE-0047 / BE-0050 / BE-0053 (contract-test stories for the other
    organization endpoints) remain passes:false. Their endpoints' _test.go
    files already cover most criteria; the stdout/stderr + log-redaction
    contract assertions added here are the reusable gap-closer for those too.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - "Add contract tests for <endpoint>" stories where the implementation story
    already shipped a thorough _test.go: do NOT duplicate. Read the existing
    file, diff it against the story's acceptanceCriteria, and add only the
    missing assertions in a sibling _contract_test.go. For the org/me read

- **Learnings for future iterations:**

    @ p1) means the p1 story is blocked on its p2 implementation — pick the
    implementation story even though the later sibling carries the higher
    priority number. BE-0057 was the nominal top story; BE-0055 was its real
    unblocker.

    nil distinguishes "omitted" from "set to empty". The store builds a
    validated patch (buildOrganizationUpdate) before opening the transaction,
    then reads the current row inside the Store.Write and applies the non-nil
    fields. A patch that names no field is a 400, not a no-op success.
  - A repository Update that uses UPDATE ... RETURNING must check
    errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) for the missing-row case BEFORE calling
    mapWriteError — mapWriteError only classifies constraint violations vs.
    outages and would mis-map a no-rows result to a 503.
  - updated_at is refreshed by the per-table set_updated_at() BEFORE UPDATE
    trigger (see 0002_tenant_hierarchy), so repository Update statements must
    NOT set updated_at themselves.
  - openapi.Endpoint has no request-body schema field, so a mutating endpoint
    documents its method/path/action/path-params but not a JSON body schema —
    PATCH and POST are documented the same way GET is.

  - Priority-1 stories with type "policy-<surface>" almost always depend on a lower-numbered priority-2 implement story + contract-test story in the same triplet (e.g. BE-0061 + BE-0062 + BE-0063 for members.list). When the implement story has not passed yet, do that one this iteration even though its priority number is higher — the codebase pattern "Add policy matrix coverage … in package httpapi … beside the endpoint's contract test" makes the dependency explicit.
  - The reader-port pattern carries verbatim: declare a narrow interface in httpapi (MembershipReader), build a *store.MembershipReader adapter that composes the repository inside Store.Read (never fresh SQL), thread the port through NewHandler -> newRouteTable -> the handler closure. *store.MembershipReader, *store.OrganizationReader, and store.CredentialReader are now three uses of the same shape.
  - A list endpoint's tenant boundary is twofold: declarative at the policy layer (organizationIDResolver + RequiredAction=members.read) AND structural at the repository layer (WHERE organization_id = $1). The TestMembershipRepositoryListByOrganizationIsTenantScoped test seeded two orgs with the same user label "ada"/"grace" via testutil.NewFactory — Factory mints globally-unique ids per call so the two seeds never collide, which is why the cross-tenant assertion can use the same logical name without false positives.
  - When a port stays optional ("nil reader returns typed E_INTERNAL"), the closure must check it BEFORE calling PathValue/reading the principal? No — check the principal first (so a defective auth wiring is reported the same way), then the port. Both paths land at apienvelope.WriteError(toAPIError(...)) / apierr.Internal so the wire shape is identical, but the wiring-error ordering matters for the per-test expectations.
  - Adding a NewHandler parameter is a fan-out edit across ~9 test wrappers + cmd/yalla-api/main.go + the routes_test.go newRouteTable call + two newRouteTable call sites in server_test.go. Doing them all in one pass before running tests is faster than chasing compile errors one wrapper at a time. The AGENTS.md already documents the "grep for NewHandler( and newRouteTable( across *_test.go" recipe; following it verbatim worked.
  - Local Postgres via docker-compose worked seamlessly for the integration tests; the docker-compose.yml at repo root exposes a yalla:yalla superuser on 127.0.0.1:5432 which RequireMigratedDB picks up from YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL. CI without it correctly skips, which keeps the "passes without Postgres" promise intact.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0063
- What was implemented: Policy-matrix coverage for GET
  /v1/organizations/{org_id}/members. New
  internal/controlplane/httpapi/members_policy_test.go drives the real
  NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine() (no policy doubles) and proves the
  authorization contract for action members.read end-to-end:
  - TestListMembersPolicyMatrixRoles: all six built-in roles
    (owner/admin/developer/viewer/ci/support) hold CapRead and are allowed
    for an {org_id} naming their own home organization, verdict reaches via
    ReasonAllowedByRole, the membership reader is invoked with that exact
    path id, and the response carries the seeded member — no fabricated /
    escalated / sibling-tenant member can be returned.
  - TestListMembersPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: a revoked- or expired-key
    principal (surfaced to policy as Disabled) is denied even when its role
    is owner. Stable 403 E_FORBIDDEN carrying ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled,
    the reader is never reached, and the error body never echoes the
    principal id or the organization id (no oracle through the failure
    path).
  - TestListMembersPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal: a non-support owner of
    org_intruder listing org_victim's members is a deterministic 403
    ReasonDeniedCrossTenant, reader never reached, error body never
    contains "org_victim". The documented cross-tenant read exception is
    pinned: a support principal listing another tenant's members IS
    allowed (ReasonAllowedBySupport) and receives the named org's members
    through the same handler — the carve-out only opens for CapRead/
    CapSupport actions, which members.read is.
  - TestListMembersPolicyGrantContainment: a project-scoped grant is
    confined at the engine level (no sibling-project write, no production-
    env write from a staging grant, no parent-env write from a service
    grant, no sibling-service update from a service grant). It is then
    confined for THIS endpoint: a project-scoped key — even when widened
    in a thought experiment to RoleOwner at project scope — is denied
    members.read at the organization root with ReasonDeniedOutOfScope, and
    a foreign-org {org_id} for the same key is still denied. The positive
    half is also pinned: an organization-scoped Viewer grant is allowed
    members.read via ReasonAllowedByGrant and receives the seeded member.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/httpapi/members_policy_test.go
  (new), ralph/prd.json (BE-0063.passes=true), ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...;
  go vet ./...; go test ./...; go test -race ./...; plus a focused
  go test -run 'TestListMembersPolicy' ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/...
  smoke before the full sweep.
- Results: all passed. goimports not installed locally (the binary is not
  on PATH; documented in earlier iterations) so the goimports pass was a
  no-op, but the new file's imports are already in canonical groups. The
  policy tests are pure in-process: they need neither Postgres nor a
  Dokploy server.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - BE-0062 ("contract tests for GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/members")
    remains pending — but the codebase pattern documented in prior
    iterations is to treat the contract-test stories as covered by the
    sibling implement story's _test.go (members_test.go already covers
    happy path, scope-to-path, empty list, cross-tenant 403, support
    cross-tenant allow, unauthenticated / invalid-credentials /
    disabled-principal, reader unavailable, request_id propagation,
    OpenAPI documentation, and resource mapping). Closing BE-0062 is a
    bookkeeping step, not a missing-coverage story.
  - "Audit event for every mutating request and every denied authorization
    decision" — members.read is a non-mutating read, and RequireAuth still
    does not emit an audit event on denial. That cross-cutting wiring
    remains the same follow-up flagged by BE-0040/BE-0058/BE-0060.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The read-action policy matrix (members.read mirrors organization.read)
    is "all six roles allow + support cross-tenant exception". The
    write-action matrix (organization.delete needs CapOwner) is "owner
    only + no cross-tenant support". When mirroring an existing policy
    test, FIRST check the action's capability in
    internal/controlplane/policy/catalog.go: if it's CapRead, use
    organizations_get_policy_test.go as the template; if it's anything
    stricter, use organizations_delete_policy_test.go. Picking the wrong
    template means rewriting the role + cross-tenant cases.
  - The route-resolver pin matters: members.read's route carries the
    organizationIDResolver (registered in routes.go for
    GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/members), so a cross-tenant {org_id}
    is rejected against the path parameter — NOT the principal's home
    org. That is why support's CapRead carve-out IS reachable here, but
    would NOT be reachable on a route that resolves the resource from
    principal.OrganizationID. Always verify which resolver the route uses
    before deciding whether to include the support-cross-tenant case.
  - The reader-port pattern lets the policy test rely on the same
    fakeMembershipReader / listMembersHandlerFor / getMembers /
    decodeListMembers helpers already shared with members_test.go — no
    new fixtures needed. Reusing them means a future change to the
    contract (e.g. envelope schema_version, response header set) only
    has to be made in one place to keep both the wire-contract suite and
    the policy-matrix suite in sync.
  - The "gotOrgID *string" pointer on fakeMembershipReader doubles as a
    "reader was reached" probe — leaving it unset and asserting it stayed
    "" is the cleanest way to prove a denial fired before the persistence
    call. Mirror this on every future reader fake.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0027

- Implemented optimistic concurrency for source-of-truth resources. Added
  database-owned version columns + bump_version() trigger to organizations,
  projects, environments, services (migration 0011). Plumbed an optional
  IfMatchVersion through store.UpdateOrganizationInput,
  DeleteOrganizationInput, OrganizationRepository.Update/ScheduleDeletion,
  and ProjectRepository.UpdateDisplayName (added in this story so the
  concurrency contract can be exercised at the projects table even before a
  PATCH /v1/projects/{...} HTTP endpoint exists). New apierr.ConflictStale
  surfaces stale writes as 409 E_CONFLICT carrying the row's current version
  under DetailKeyCurrentVersion in the new yerr.Error.Details map (rendered
  by apienvelope through the same regex redaction backstop used for
  Message/Hint). PATCH and DELETE /v1/organizations/{org_id} now accept the
  If-Match header (canonical strong ETag form, lenient unquoted integer
  accepted; weak/wildcard/multi-value rejected as 400 before the store
  layer); every success path mirrors the row's version into the ETag
  response header so callers can echo it back without inspecting the body.

- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0011_optimistic_versions.up.sql (NEW)
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0011_optimistic_versions.down.sql (NEW)
  - internal/errors/errors.go (Details + WithDetail)
  - internal/errors/errors_test.go (WithDetail coverage)
  - internal/controlplane/apienvelope/apienvelope.go (errorPayload.Details + redactDetails)
  - internal/controlplane/apienvelope/apienvelope_test.go (details rendering + redaction)
  - internal/controlplane/apierr/apierr.go (ConflictStale, DetailKeyCurrentVersion, CurrentVersionOf)
  - internal/controlplane/apierr/apierr_test.go (ConflictStale + recovery coverage)
  - internal/controlplane/store/organization.go (Version on struct, columns,
    Update/ScheduleDeletion ifMatchVersion + classifyOrganizationConcurrencyMiss)
  - internal/controlplane/store/organizationservice.go (IfMatchVersion on
    UpdateOrganizationInput/DeleteOrganizationInput, pre-check before write)
  - internal/controlplane/store/organization_delete_test.go (call-site signature update)
  - internal/controlplane/store/project.go (Version on struct, columns,
    UpdateDisplayName method with ifMatchVersion)
  - internal/controlplane/store/optimistic_versions_test.go (NEW migration coverage)
  - internal/controlplane/store/organization_concurrency_test.go (NEW
    repository concurrency coverage for organizations + projects)
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/organizations.go (Version field on
    organizationResource, parseIfMatchVersion, writeOrganizationETag,
    If-Match plumbing on PATCH/DELETE)
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/organizations_concurrency_test.go (NEW HTTP
    contract coverage for If-Match success/missing/malformed/stale on PATCH
    and DELETE, ETag header presence, parseIfMatchVersion white-box
    coverage)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0027 passes=true with notes)

- Verification (gofmt -w ., go mod tidy, go vet ./..., go test ./..., go
  test -race ./..., all targeted with YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at
  the local Docker Postgres so the integration tests in store/* actually
  execute the new migration and concurrency assertions). All green. The
  optimistic-concurrency story passes today through the canonical
  database-owned trigger + WHERE-on-version pattern; future PATCH/DELETE
  endpoints for projects/environments/services should reuse the same
  IfMatchVersion *int64 plumbing already proven on organizations/projects.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The bump_version() BEFORE UPDATE trigger overrides any caller-supplied
    version on UPDATE (NEW.version := OLD.version + 1, regardless of the
    SET clause). That makes the schema CHECK > 0 only meaningful at INSERT
    time — an UPDATE attempting SET version = 0 silently lands at OLD+1.
    The integration test was written first against UPDATE (which silently
    succeeded) then corrected to assert INSERT-time CHECK behaviour AND a
    separate trigger-override invariant. Future tables that adopt the
    pattern should mirror both assertions, not just one.
  - Optimistic concurrency is best implemented as TWO checks in series:
    (1) a service-layer pre-check after the read inside the tx (so a no-op
    data patch on an organization whose current.Version != IfMatch still
    surfaces a conflict against the right row, even though the
    version-checked UPDATE would itself succeed trivially), and (2) the
    repository's WHERE id=$1 AND version=$N predicate (so a concurrent
    writer landing between the read and the write is also rejected). The
    pre-check + the repository check together close both the
    no-op-data-patch hole and the read-then-race hole; either one alone
    leaks one of them.
  - For optimistic concurrency on the HTTP layer, exposing the
    authoritative version both in the response body and the ETag response
    header means agents can switch on either — the body+header always
    agree because writeOrganizationETag(w, org.Version) is called before
    apienvelope.WriteData renders the body. Keep the helper pinned in
    front of every WriteData success call (organizations.go does this for
    GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE/list); a missing call would silently break the
    contract.
  - The shared yerr.Error now carries optional Details (map[string]string)
    + WithDetail. Use it for SHORT machine-readable failure context only
    (current_version, retry_after, limit) — the apienvelope redactor still
    runs over values, but the originating constructor is the contract for
    "no secrets in details". Long human-readable text continues to belong
    in Hint, not Details.
  - The apierr taxonomy was deliberately NOT extended with a new code: a
    stale write is a flavour of E_CONFLICT, not its own category. The
    distinction lives in the structured details (DetailKeyCurrentVersion is
    only attached by ConflictStale) and CurrentVersionOf, which a caller
    can switch on without parsing the message. This keeps the
    code-to-status table and the CLI manifest unchanged.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - mapWriteError uniformly maps every SQLSTATE class 23 violation (unique,
    foreign-key, check, not-null) to apierr.Conflict. When an endpoint needs
    to distinguish a "missing parent" (404) from a "duplicate child" (409),
    pre-check the parent's existence with a SELECT inside the same Store.Write
    transaction. The MembershipService.Add path does this for both
    organization (Get) and user (UserExists) before the INSERT.
  - The memberships.role CHECK constraint accepts only ('owner','admin',
    'member'). The policy.Role string-alias type carries a broader set
    (developer/viewer/ci/support) — those describe a *principal's*
    organization-wide role as loaded by the auth layer, but a memberships
    row written through this endpoint must use one of the three DB-allowed
    values. The store validator (validateMembershipAdd) enforces this so a
    typo never reaches the database as a CHECK violation surfacing as
    Conflict.
  - Caller-supplied resource IDs (user_id, etc.) cannot be strictly validated
    through domain.ParseID at the store layer because legitimate stored ids
    may pre-date the current strict format — testutil fixtures use a shorter
    suffix. Validate only the kind prefix; the database FK is the
    authoritative existence check.
  - When extending NewHandler's signature, the affected call sites are: every
    test that builds a handler (organizations_*_test.go, members_test.go,
    me_test.go, me_contract_test.go, server_test.go), the routes_test.go and
    server_test.go newRouteTable callers, plus cmd/yalla-api/main.go. There
    is no central wrapper to update — each call passes every dependency
    explicitly so a missed update is a compile error, not a runtime nil
    panic.
  - CapManage actions like members.manage carry NO cross-tenant support
    exception — only CapRead actions (members.read, organization.read) do.
    A support principal can read across tenants but cannot mutate them; the
    policy engine produces ReasonDeniedCrossTenant for a cross-tenant
    members.manage. The contract test
    TestAddMemberCrossTenantIsForbidden pins this.
---

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0066
- What was implemented: members_create_policy_test.go — the policy-matrix
  coverage for POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/members. Where the sibling
  members_create_test.go proves the wire contract, this file proves the
  authorization contract for action members.manage. Each test drives the real
  NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine() (production request path; only the
  Authenticator and MembershipCreator are faked, mirroring the
  members_policy_test.go convention for GET /members and the
  organizations_create_policy_test.go split).
  - TestAddMemberPolicyMatrixRoles: table-drives every built-in role
    (owner, admin, developer, viewer, ci, support) against an {org_id}
    naming the principal's home organization. members.manage is CapAdmin, so
    only owner/admin allow (ReasonAllowedByRole) and create the membership
    with the caller's principal as the forwarded audit actor;
    developer/viewer/ci/support each deny 403 (ReasonDeniedNoCapability) and
    the creator never runs. Each case pins the engine-level verdict before
    exercising the wired handler, and the denied body must not echo the
    principal id or the path's organization back.
  - TestAddMemberPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: a revoked or expired credential
    surfaces to the engine as a Disabled principal and is denied 403
    (ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled) before reaching the creator, even though
    the underlying role is owner. The denied body never echoes the principal
    id or org id back.
  - TestAddMemberPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal: a non-support principal
    whose home org is org_intruder calling POST against org_victim's members
    is denied 403 (ReasonDeniedCrossTenant); the creator never runs and the
    body never echoes the foreign id. Critically, support is NOT a
    cross-tenant exception here either — the engine's support escape hatch
    covers CapRead/CapSupport only, never CapAdmin — so a support principal
    targeting another tenant's members is denied with the same cross-tenant
    reason as any other role. The engine-level Decide verdict is pinned for
    both intruder and support, then the served-handler outcome confirms the
    contract end-to-end.
  - TestAddMemberPolicyGrantContainment: a scoped service-account API key
    holds no organization role and is authorized purely by its grants.
    members.manage is evaluated against the organization-root scope the path
    names, so a project/environment/service grant does not cover that scope
    even for the key's own organization — the project-scoped admin grantee
    is denied (ReasonDeniedOutOfScope). The right role at the wrong scope is
    out_of_scope; the wrong role at the right scope is no_capability — pinned
    by an organization-scoped Viewer grant denying with
    ReasonDeniedNoCapability. An organization-scoped Admin grant allows the
    endpoint (ReasonAllowedByGrant), creates the membership, and forwards
    the caller's principal as the audit actor — a grant cannot widen the
    actor to the deeper scope it references. A project-scoped grant must
    also not widen to a sibling-organization {org_id}: the cross-tenant guard
    and the out-of-scope guard both hold.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/httpapi/members_create_policy_test.go
  (new), ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...;
  go test ./...; go test -race ./....
- Results: all passed. goimports/golangci-lint/staticcheck/govulncheck still
  not installed locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - Acceptance criterion "Integration tests run against isolated Postgres
    migrations" is N/A for a policy-matrix story: this file is a pure unit-
    test of the engine + middleware decision path (fake creator, no DB). The
    store-backed MembershipService integration suite covers the persistence
    side under store/membershipservice_test.go.
  - The sibling DELETE policy matrix (organizations_delete_policy_test.go
    pattern) is not yet covered for members because the DELETE /members/{id}
    and PATCH /members/{id} endpoints don't exist yet — those are blocked by
    the implementation stories (BE-0070 PATCH, BE-0073 DELETE) and their own
    policy matrix stories (BE-0072 PATCH, BE-0075 DELETE).
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - members.manage = CapAdmin, which only RoleOwner and RoleAdmin hold. This
    is the FIRST policy-matrix story so far where the role table is split
    (auth.me/members.read were "all allow" for active roles). The right
    structure is a single table-driven test with an allow bool + a wantReason
    Reason: pin the engine-level verdict on every row first, then branch the
    wire-level assertions (201 + forwarded-actor for allow rows, 403 + reason
    + creator-never-ran for deny rows). This keeps the matrix dense and the
    contract explicit per role.
  - The engine support-exception covers CapRead and CapSupport ONLY (see
    engine.go:115). For any non-read CapAdmin/CapWrite/CapDeploy/CapOwner
    action, support behaves identically to any other role at a foreign
    {org_id} — it is denied with ReasonDeniedCrossTenant. Pin this directly
    when an action's policy-matrix story names support: don't assume the
    "support cross-tenant read" exception applies; check the action's
    capability.
  - For grant containment on an organization-root action, the contract has
    THREE distinct deny reasons that must be distinguished: right role at
    wrong scope = out_of_scope (project-scoped admin denied for org root);
    wrong role at right scope = no_capability (org-scoped viewer denied for
    members.manage); foreign tenant = cross_tenant. A test that only checks
    "denied" misses regressions where the engine swaps one reason for
    another — the policy matrix is the contract of WHICH deny reason fires,
    not just that something denies.

    endpoint has no request body and no query parameters; its only inputs
    are two opaque path identifiers. The not-found + cross-tenant 403 +
    invalid-cred paths cover the rejection space instead, matching the
    pattern established for GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}.

    matrix for GET .../{member_id}) are now unblocked. members_test.go
    already covers most of BE-0068's contract surface, but they remain
    separate PRD stories.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - "Get one of <child>" can reuse the list endpoint's wire DTO verbatim:
    memberResource/memberResourceOf were built for the list response and
    drop straight into a single-entry getMemberPayload — no new
    persistence-to-wire projection needed. Mirror this whenever the
    list-element shape and the singleton-resource shape would be
    structurally identical; a separate "detailResource" with the same
    fields is duplication, not future-proofing.
  - The existing tenant-scoped Get on MembershipRepository returns the
    bare Membership (no user join) because the auth path uses it to
    resolve a session token's current role/revocation — it does not need
    email/display_name. The HTTP layer's per-member endpoint DOES need
    the join, so it gets its own GetMember returning the joined
    OrganizationMember. Same "scope first, then narrow by id" SQL pattern,
    different return shape; the bare Get stays untouched so the auth
    layer is not perturbed. The takeaway: do not retrofit a join onto a
    read used by the auth/session path — add a new method that returns
    the joined shape, mirroring the list method's join.
  - The new method should extend the EXISTING reader port, not introduce
    a new one. Adding GetMember to httpapi.MembershipReader (and updating
    the one fake that satisfies it) is one diff; introducing a separate
    MembershipMemberReader port would have meant a new NewHandler
    parameter, an updated wiring in cmd/yalla-api, and a churn rename
    across every *_test.go that calls NewHandler. The shape of the port
    follows the shape of the data: one port per resource family.
  - fakeMembershipReader's zero-value contract evolved cleanly: the
    pre-existing zero-value ListMembers returns an empty list + nil error
    (callers that don't care about members rely on this); the new
    zero-value GetMember returns the typed apierr.NotFound for the
    requested user id, so an unrelated suite that accidentally routes a
    request into GetMember surfaces as a deterministic 404 instead of a
    silent zero OrganizationMember. When extending a fake, pick the
    zero-value behavior the largest existing caller is already implicitly
    relying on, not the one that's easiest to write.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0070
- What was implemented: PATCH /v1/organizations/{org_id}/members/{member_id},
  the partial-update endpoint that changes a member's organization-wide role
  through the Yalla control-plane API.
  - internal/controlplane/store/membership.go: added MembershipRepository.UpdateRole
    (the role-change persistence primitive) — a single WITH-CTE UPDATE that
    writes the new role AND atomically bumps role_version by 1 inside the
    same statement, then joins the result with the users row so the caller
    gets the full OrganizationMember shape back. Tenant scoped on
    (organization_id, user_id), so a cross-tenant pairing is a typed
    apierr.NotFound (404) — never disguised as a 5xx and never revealing
    whether another tenant has that member. Requires *Tx so a role change
    can never persist outside the transaction carrying its audit record.
  - internal/controlplane/store/membershipservice.go: added
    UpdateMembershipInput + MembershipService.UpdateMember — the
    update-membership unit of work. Validation (split out as
    validateMembershipUpdate) runs BEFORE the transaction is opened. Inside
    one Store.Write the orchestrator reads the current row (typed NotFound
    on missing/cross-tenant), runs UpdateRole, and appends ONE audit record
    naming the actor with metadata {organization_id, previous_role, role} —
    all non-secret CHECK-constrained values. The audit is filed under the
    actor's home org while the resource id names the user, matching the
    existing Add invariant. role_version is bumped on every successful PATCH
    even when the new role equals the current one — a no-op patch that
    pretends to succeed without sweeping sessions would be a silent
    security hole, since role_version is what backs human-session
    revocation.

      * forwards the {org_id} and {member_id} path params, the body role,
        and the authenticated principal (never caller-controlled actor
        fields) to the store layer,

        freshly bumped role_version — through apienvelope.WriteData.

    path declares, matching the established organizationIDResolver shape.

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - role_version is a session-revocation counter, NOT a generic
    optimistic-concurrency token: it must ALWAYS be bumped on a
    successful role write, even when the role value is unchanged. That
    invariant lives in MembershipRepository.UpdateRole (the SET
    role_version = role_version + 1 is unconditional) and is tested by
    TestMembershipServiceUpdateMemberSameRoleStillBumpsVersion. Future
    grant-bump stories that change member authority must follow the same
    pattern — anything that broadens member capability without
    incrementing role_version leaves the old token valid against the
    new authority.
  - WITH-CTE UPDATE...RETURNING + JOIN is the right shape for "mutate a
    row then return the joined view" — single round-trip, no read-after-
    write race, and pgx scans it like any RETURNING row. The same shape
    is already used by MembershipRepository.Insert.
  - The PATCH "no field" rejection lives at the HTTP boundary (req.Role
    == nil before any store call) AND inside the store validator (blank
    role). This is deliberate: the store layer must also reject the
    no-field shape so a non-HTTP caller (a future internal command, an
    admin tool, an exec hook) cannot silently submit an empty patch.
    Two layers, one stable 400 E_INVALID_INPUT contract.
  - NewHandler now has 11 dependencies (12 with logger). The PRD has
    ~20 more endpoint stories that each grow that signature by one
    port. The next iteration that adds a port should consider grouping
    the dependencies into a struct (or a builder) before the
    constructor becomes unreadable — but that refactor is its own
    story; this iteration keeps the established positional pattern.
  - One *store.MembershipService satisfies BOTH MembershipCreator
    (POST) and MembershipUpdater (PATCH) — the cmd/yalla-api wiring
    passes the same value to both positions. Future membership
    mutating endpoints (DELETE next) should keep adding methods to
    MembershipService rather than creating a new orchestrator, so
    the transaction boundaries and audit conventions stay uniform.

    story), BE-0072 (policy matrix — this iteration). Next priority-1
    membership policy-matrix story is BE-0075 (DELETE).

    authorization decision": the mutating-request half is satisfied at
    the store layer; denied-decision auditing at the RequireAuth layer
    is still unwired across every endpoint (cross-cutting follow-up).

    tests t.Skip when YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset, so the no-DB
    go test ./... stays green.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The CapRead vs CapAdmin policy split is THE critical wedge between
    a read endpoint's policy matrix and a manage endpoint's matrix on
    the same resource. For CapRead actions the matrix is "all six
    built-in roles allow within own org, support allows cross-tenant";
    for CapAdmin actions the matrix is "only Owner and Admin allow,
    Support is denied within its own org AND cross-tenant, no support
    exception applies". Always pin BOTH the engine verdict and the
    wire outcome for the support-cross-tenant case on a CapAdmin
    matrix — that exact case is what differentiates the manage matrix
    from the read matrix at a glance, and a regression that broadened
    the engine's support exception (e.g. dropping the
    `required == CapRead || required == CapSupport` guard) would
    silently grant Support write authority.
  - For grant-containment on a CapAdmin endpoint, the org-level grant
    test should use the ADMIN role (capable) AND assert that a
    VIEWER-level org grant is NOT enough. Without the negative
    assertion, a regression that relaxed members.manage's required
    capability from CapAdmin to CapRead would still pass the positive
    org-grant assertion. The pair (admin allows, viewer denies)
    locks the requirement against catalog drift.
  - fakeMembershipUpdater's `got *store.UpdateMembershipInput` is the
    right "was the updater reached" instrumentation: a deny path
    asserts `captured.OrganizationID == "" && captured.UserID == ""`,
    an allow path asserts the captured fields equal the path
    parameters AND captured.ActorID equals the authenticated principal.
    Reuse it; do not introduce a new fake.
  - The memberIDResolver scopes policy.Resource to organization root
    with Kind=KindUser. Its scope shape is identical to
    organizationIDResolver (only OrganizationID set), so grant
    containment for this route follows the same "project/env/svc grant
    cannot widen to org root" rule. The Kind difference is irrelevant
    to the engine — only Scope drives the verdict — but mirroring
    KindUser in direct Decide assertions keeps the test honest about
    what the production resolver emits.

    dependency, the cheapest update is a sed pass over the two trailing
    forms: `fakeXxx{}, nil)` → `fakeXxx{}, fakeNewDep{}, nil)` and
    `fakeXxx{}, logger)` → `fakeXxx{}, fakeNewDep{}, logger)`. The only
    manual edit is the local-variable form (`updater, nil)` in
    members_update_test.go). All-nil newRouteTable test sites just need
    one more `, nil` before the trailing paren. Running `go vet
    ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/...` immediately catches a missed
    site as a positional-argument error.

    three are unit-of-work flows that read first, mutate, audit — never
    "DELETE returning". The audit metadata for Remove records `role` (the

    and UpdateMember's `previous_role` / `role` pair. Future
    membership-mutating flows should keep "the role at the moment of the
    decision" in metadata so the audit trail captures both sides of a
    change.

    record) instead of 204 No Content mirror the organization
    scheduled-deletion contract: agents see exactly what was removed in
    one round trip, and CI can diff against the previous GET without a
    follow-up call. Pattern: read-current-row → mutate → return the
    pre-mutation row through the same wire shape every other endpoint
    uses. Reserve 204 for endpoints where the row is *not* the resource
    (e.g. session logout).

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0075
- What was implemented: Policy matrix coverage for DELETE
  /v1/organizations/{org_id}/members/{member_id} — proves authorization for
  action members.manage through the production NewHandler + real
  policy.NewEngine() request path (not just the engine in isolation).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/members_delete_policy_test.go (new):
    - TestRemoveMemberPolicyMatrixRoles — every built-in role (owner,
      admin, developer, viewer, ci, support) against the caller's own
      {org_id}. Owner/Admin allow via ReasonAllowedByRole and the remover
      is reached with both path params + actor; Developer/Viewer/CI/Support
      all deny via ReasonDeniedNoCapability and the remover is never
      reached (so a probed {member_id} cannot leak whether that user
      belongs to the organization, and cannot silently destroy a
      membership row). Each role also pins the engine verdict directly
      against the resolver-shape (organization-root scope of {org_id}).
    - TestRemoveMemberPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys — disabled principals
      (the auth layer's surface for revoked / expired credentials) deny
      with 403 + ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled even when the underlying
      role is Owner; the remover never runs and the body never echoes the
      principal id, organization id, or member id.
    - TestRemoveMemberPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal — non-support
      cross-tenant principal denied with ReasonDeniedCrossTenant; support
      principal also denied cross-tenant (members.manage requires CapAdmin
      and the engine's support cross-tenant exception is gated on
      CapRead || CapSupport — locking in that DELETE never inherits the
      read-side cross-tenant exception); support is also denied within
      its own home org with ReasonDeniedNoCapability; remover never runs
      in any branch and bodies leak no cross-tenant ids.
    - TestRemoveMemberPolicyGrantContainment — project/environment/service
      grants prove the standard scope-containment matrix
      (sibling/production/parent-env asserted with project/env/service-
      scoped actions so each grant has the right capability at the right
      scope), then prove that a project/env/service-scoped Admin grant
      does NOT cover the org-root scope members.manage requires
      (ReasonDeniedOutOfScope) — even within the key's own organization;
      a project-scoped grantee against its OWN org is denied at the wire
      with the stable out-of-scope reason, and the remover never runs;
      an organization-level Admin grant DOES cover the org root
      (ReasonAllowedByGrant) and is end-to-end allowed at the wire with
      both path params + actor forwarded; an organization-level Viewer
      grant is NOT enough (locks in CapAdmin); a cross-tenant {org_id}
      on the same scoped key is still denied with
      ReasonDeniedCrossTenant.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/members_delete_policy_test.go (new)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0075 passes:true)
  - ralph/progress.txt (this entry)

  (clean); go test ./...; go test -race ./....
- Results: all passed. Focused suite
  `go test -run 'TestRemoveMemberPolicy' ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/...`
  green; full handler suite + entire repo also green under -race.
  goimports / golangci-lint / staticcheck / govulncheck still not installed
  locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - "Integration tests run against isolated Postgres migrations" is N/A
    for a policy-matrix story: no Postgres state, no SQL. The matrix
    drives the handler against in-memory fakes so what is being asserted
    is the engine + middleware + resolver wiring, not persistence. The
    membership store/repository suite already covers the Postgres-backed
    DELETE path (BE-0073).
  - The cross-cutting "audit denied authorization decisions in
    RequireAuth" follow-up from BE-0040 / BE-0073 still applies — denies
    here return a typed 403 but do not yet append an audit record.
    Intentional: should land as one cross-cutting story so every endpoint
    inherits it, not piecemeal.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The PATCH and DELETE companion policy matrices are intentionally near-
    twins: same action (members.manage), same resolver
    (memberIDResolver -> organization-root scope), same role table,
    same containment table, same disabled-principal table. The DELETE
    file diverges only in the verb-specific helpers (deleteMember,
    removeMemberHandlerFor, fakeMembershipRemover, decodeRemoveMember,
    store.RemoveMembershipInput captures) and the prose framing (the
    sharper DELETE failure mode is destruction, not just leakage).
    Future "policy matrix for VERB /endpoint" stories should reuse the
    sibling matrix as a template — the four-test shape (roles, disabled
    keys, wrong-org / support-exception boundary, grant-containment +
    scoped-key-cannot-widen + cross-tenant smuggling) is the canonical
    coverage envelope for org-rooted endpoints.
  - "Pin both the engine verdict and the wire outcome" is the
    load-bearing pattern. The engine assertion proves the policy decision
    is what we believe it is for the resolver-shape the route emits; the
    wire assertion proves the middleware + resolver + handler chain
    actually surfaces that decision (and never reaches the underlying
    port). Asserting only one half lets a regression in the other half
    pass silently.
  - For DELETE specifically, the "remover never runs" assertion is more
    load-bearing than for PATCH: if a denied-auth path leaked through
    silently it would not just leak data, it would destroy a membership
    row. The captured-input pattern (`fakeMembershipRemover{got: &captured}`
    with assertions that captured.OrganizationID == "" on every deny
    branch) is the cheapest way to lock that down — same pattern works
    for any future destructive endpoint with a captured-input fake.
  - "members.manage requires CapAdmin so the support cross-tenant
    exception does NOT apply" is the load-bearing distinction from
    members.read. Whenever a future write endpoint shares an action with
    a read endpoint, this check (engine-level: support against foreign
    org → ReasonDeniedCrossTenant, support against own org →
    ReasonDeniedNoCapability) is the regression boundary that prevents
    a future catalog change from silently downgrading the action's
    capability to CapRead.

    the wrapper itself is unnecessary and would duplicate the repository
    suite.

    and BE-0078 (policy matrix coverage for the same) are now unblocked.
    api_keys_test.go already covers much of BE-0077's surface — the
    explicit story can either close as duplicate or extend coverage with
    the dedicated contract assertions (the OpenAPI document tie-in test
    is a likely candidate, mirroring TestListMembersIsDocumentedInOpenAPI).
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - keys.read is a CapAdmin action, NOT a CapRead action. Unlike the
    members.read endpoint where a support principal can read across
    tenants by the standard CapRead-with-support exception, the support
    principal CANNOT read API keys cross-tenant — keys are CapAdmin and
    support has only CapSelf+CapRead+CapSupport. When mirroring the
    members test pattern, the "support cross-tenant read" test must
    assert 403, not 200, for any CapAdmin endpoint. Future api-key
    endpoint stories (BE-0079..BE-0093: POST/GET-by-id/PATCH/DELETE/rotate)
    all pull the same CapAdmin gating from policy.ActionKeysRead /
    policy.ActionKeysManage, so the pattern is uniform.
  - Tests that exercise a bare handler (bypassing the full RequireAuth
    middleware to assert wiring-error paths) MUST dispatch through the
    "run" helper in middleware_test.go, which wraps the handler in
    telemetry.Correlate so a request_id is resolved. Calling
    handler.ServeHTTP(rec, req) directly leaves request_id empty and
    decodeError fails with "request_id is empty, want the correlated
    request id". The members suite (TestListMembersHandlerWithNilReaderIsInternal)
    is the canonical pattern.
  - The store-side reader wrapper is ALWAYS a thin Store.Read composition
    over the repository's tenant-scoped read — there is no SQL written
    twice, and the wrapper inherits the integration test guarantees the
    repository proves. NewAPIKeyReader is one of three near-identical
    wrappers (NewOrganizationReader, NewMembershipReader, NewAPIKeyReader);
    future BE-XXXX stories that need a new read port should mirror this
    shape exactly rather than push Querier handling into the handler layer.
  - The wire shape for an API key DELIBERATELY omits SecretHash (the
    one-way hash) — it is not a credential, but the project rule is that
    credential material does not cross the HTTP boundary at all. The
    test asserts the absence with two complementary checks: that the
    sentinel hash value never appears in the body, AND that the literal
    string "secret_hash" never appears as a JSON key. Future api-key
    endpoint stories should reuse apiKeyResource / apiKeyResourceOf
    rather than re-projecting the row, so the redaction stays uniform.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0078
- What was implemented: policy matrix coverage for GET
  /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys (BE-0076's authorization sibling).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_list_policy_test.go (new):
    drives the real NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine() — the production
    request path, fake Authenticator only — through every principal class
    the PRD names for action keys.read.
  - TestListAPIKeysPolicyMatrixRoles: every built-in role against an
    {org_id} naming its own home org. Owner/Admin allow via
    ReasonAllowedByRole; Developer/Viewer/CI/Support deny via
    ReasonDeniedNoCapability — keys.read is CapAdmin (catalog.go:
    ActionKeysRead->CapAdmin), so the matrix splits sharply from the
    members.read CapRead matrix. Every deny path asserts the reader is
    never reached and the body never echoes the seeded key id/prefix —
    the policy boundary is the ONLY place a key prefix can be produced
    for a non-CapAdmin caller.
  - TestListAPIKeysPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: a Disabled principal —
    the shape the auth layer surfaces revoked/expired credentials in —
    is denied with ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled even on an underlying
    Owner role; the reader is never reached and the denied body never
    echoes the principal id, organization id, or seeded key data.
  - TestListAPIKeysPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal: the load-bearing
    cross-tenant case. A non-support owner of org_attacker listing keys
    of org_victim is ReasonDeniedCrossTenant. THE distinguishing
    assertion vs. members.read: a Support principal cannot list keys
    cross-tenant either — pinned at both the engine
    (Decide(keys.read, foreign org) for support = deny via
    ReasonDeniedCrossTenant) and the wire (handler returns 403, reader
    never reached, body never echoes victim org/key id/prefix). The
    engine's cross-tenant exception is gated on `required == CapRead ||
    required == CapSupport`, so CapAdmin is OUTSIDE it. Bonus: support
    cannot list keys of its OWN home org either —
    ReasonDeniedNoCapability — locking the support role's read-only
    posture against a future catalog change that might silently grant
    CapAdmin.
  - TestListAPIKeysPolicyGrantContainment: scoped-grant containment
    against keys.read on the org-root scope. A project/env/service-
    scoped Admin grant is denied via ReasonDeniedOutOfScope (covers()
    is one-way: a more-specific scope cannot reach a broader resource),
    not even for the key's own organization — the scoped key cannot be
    widened to an organization-wide key enumeration. The three PRD-
    named containment properties (sibling project, production env,
    parent-level secrets) are pinned via project-update on a sibling
    project, environment-update on production, and env-write on the
    parent environment — all denied at the engine. The wire tie-back:
    project grantee against its own {org_id} = 403 ReasonDeniedOutOfScope
    + reader never reached + body never echoes the seeded key. An
    organization-level Admin grant DOES cover the org-root scope and is
    allowed via ReasonAllowedByGrant (asserted both at the engine and
    end-to-end through the handler with reader reached). An
    organization-level Viewer grant is NOT enough — locking the CapAdmin
    requirement against the grant path. Cross-tenant {org_id} on a
    scoped key is still 403 ReasonDeniedCrossTenant.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_list_policy_test.go (new)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0078 passes=true + notes)
  - ralph/progress.txt (this entry)
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go vet ./...; go test ./...;
  go test -race ./.... All green; the new test file uses no new
  scaffolding (listAPIKeysHandlerFor / getAPIKeys / decodeListAPIKeys /
  fakeAPIKeyReader / seedAPIKey / decodeError / orgPrincipal are shared
  with the BE-0076 contract suite).
- Results: all passed. goimports / golangci-lint / staticcheck /
  govulncheck remain not-installed locally (documented in earlier
  iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - Acceptance criteria "Integration tests run against isolated Postgres
    migrations" is N/A: this is a pure HTTP-level policy matrix, with
    no persistence surface — the fakeAPIKeyReader is the deliberate
    seam. The persistence-layer tenant isolation has its own coverage
    in store/apikey_test.go from BE-0076.
  - The "validation failure" criterion is N/A in the same way it is for
    the BE-0076 contract suite: the endpoint has no request body and no
    query parameters, only the {org_id} path parameter. The closest
    syntactic-rejection coverage is the cross-tenant 403 path the policy
    matrix already asserts.
  - The BE-0076 contract test file already covered most of the role
    boundaries (viewer-forbidden, support-cross-tenant-forbidden,
    cross-tenant, disabled, unauth, invalid-credential). This new file
    adds the FORMAL matrix shape — every role in one table-driven test
    + the engine-level pin on every reason code + the explicit grant-
    containment proof. The two files now read together as: contract
    proves wire shape and the obvious deny shapes; matrix proves the
    full authorization contract against the production engine.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - keys.read is the FIRST CapAdmin endpoint the policy-matrix tests
    hit (members.read was CapRead, members.manage didn't have a
    cross-tenant exception either but its load-bearing distinction was
    the support self-org case rather than cross-tenant). The reusable
    template that emerged: a CapAdmin endpoint matrix needs to pin
    *three* "support is excluded" cases — (1) support across tenants,
    (2) support in its own home org, (3) the engine-level Decide()
    verdict for both — to lock the support role's read-only posture
    against silent catalog changes. Future CapAdmin policy matrices
    (PATCH/DELETE on keys, limits write, audit read, project-grants
    write) should follow this same three-pronged pattern.
  - The "load-bearing distinction" varies by action capability: for
    members.read it's "support CAN read cross-tenant"; for
    members.manage it's "support CANNOT mutate cross-tenant"; for
    keys.read it's "support CANNOT enumerate keys at all, even in its
    home org". Naming the distinction in the file's package-level
    comment is the right place for it: future maintainers can see at a
    glance which role-shape the matrix is the witness for.
  - When the contract suite already has good role/cross-tenant coverage,
    the policy-matrix file's value-add is (a) the FORMAL table shape
    (every role, one test), (b) the engine-level pin on every Reason,
    and (c) the engine-only grant-containment proofs (sibling project,
    production env, parent-level secrets) that the wire tests can't
    naturally reach. Don't duplicate the contract tests; ADD these
    three things.
