## 2026-05-15 - BE-0079
- Implemented POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys end-to-end. The
  endpoint mints a fresh credential server-side, persists the api_keys row
  through the new store.APIKeyService unit of work, and returns the
  persisted projection together with the one-time plaintext token. The
  triplet is now: the GET sibling (BE-0076, BE-0078) covers list/policy
  for keys.read; this story is the create half for keys.manage, with its
  policy-matrix sibling (BE-0081) unblocked.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/store/apikeyservice.go (new):
    NewAPIKeyService(Store, orgs, serviceAccounts, apiKeys, audit) wires
    the orchestrator. Create(ctx, in, now) runs the mint-api-key unit of
    work inside Store.Write — org existence check, optional service-
    account existence check (composite-FK target in the same tenant),
    INSERT api_keys with caller-supplied (Prefix, SecretHash), append the
    immutable audit event — so a key is never persisted without its audit
    trail and the audit row is never written for a mint that did not
    happen. buildAPIKeyToCreate is the pre-transaction validator: it
    mints the api-key id via domain.NewID(KindAPIKey), reuses the
    Membership/Org pattern (Add..Update..Remove → typed apierr.InvalidInput
    with stable field paths that NEVER echo submitted values), and treats
    a blank Prefix/SecretHash as a wiring-error apierr.Internal (a client
    cannot supply credentials, so a buggy server must not pretend the
    request is bad). validateAPIKeyScopes caps at 64 scopes/64 bytes each,
    enforces a conservative [a-z0-9_:.-] alphabet, and rejects duplicates;
    a nil/empty input is allowed and normalised to []string{} so the
    api_keys.scopes column receives '{}' instead of SQL NULL.
  - internal/controlplane/store/apikeyservice_internal_test.go (new):
    white-box coverage of buildAPIKeyToCreate — happy path, every
    classifiable rejection (org_id wrong-kind, name blank/long/control-
    char/invalid-UTF-8, scope blank/long/non-alphabet/duplicate, >64
    scopes, expires_at past/now, service_account_id wrong-kind,
    created_by wrong-kind), plus the missing-credential = Internal
    contract. Also a constructor-guard table that asserts every nil
    dependency is rejected. Renamed the local validInput→validAPIKeyInput
    helper to avoid a package-level name collision with projectservice.
  - internal/controlplane/store/apikeyservice_test.go (new): integration
    coverage against an isolated, freshly migrated Postgres database.
    Happy path proves the api_keys row + audit event commit atomically,
    that ListAPIKeys reads the new row back, that audit metadata captures
    organization_id/scope_count/has_expiry (and service_account_id when
    present) and NEVER contains the prefix, the secret hash, or the
    plaintext token; service-account+expiry path; missing-org and
    cross-tenant SA paths both surface as typed NotFound with the
    transaction rolled back; invalid-input never opens a transaction; and
    the central "plaintext never reaches the database" guarantee is
    asserted by scanning every text column of the persisted row.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys.go: added APIKeyCreator port
    (the narrow interface store.APIKeyService satisfies), createAPIKeyRequest
    (name/scopes/expires_at(*string RFC3339)/service_account_id(*string)),
    createAPIKeyPayload (apiKeyResource + Token plaintext), and
    createAPIKeyHandler. The handler decodes strictly, parses expires_at
    at the boundary (malformed timestamp = deterministic 400 naming the
    field), mints the credential via auth.Generate (server-side, so a
    client cannot supply Prefix/SecretHash), sets CreatedBy to the
    principal id only when p.Kind == domain.KindUser (the api_keys.
    created_by FK references users(id), so an SA-actor mint yields NULL),
    and renders the response with auth.Token.Reveal() — the only
    deliberately greppable escape hatch for the plaintext, called exactly
    once at the wire boundary so the secret never reaches a log line, an
    audit record, or the database.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_test.go: added fakeAPIKeyCreator
    (mirrors the fakeMembershipCreator shape: canned key/err + got pointer
    for input capture) so the other test files can pass it to NewHandler.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_create_test.go (new): full
    contract suite — happy path (asserts the token has the yk_ namespace,
    is NOT the redaction sentinel, the body never carries the secret_hash
    sentinel, and the server-minted Prefix/SecretHash are forwarded
    distinct); expires_at + service_account_id forwarding; malformed
    expires_at = 400 naming the field without echoing the value;
    malformed body (unparseable JSON, unknown field, trailing data) = 400;
    store-layer InvalidInput = 400; store-layer NotFound (org and SA) =
    404; unauthenticated/invalid-credential = 401; cross-tenant = 403
    with the stable ReasonDeniedCrossTenant and no echo of the target
    org_id; disabled-principal = 403 with ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled;
    StoreUnavailable = 503 with no driver-cause leak; request_id
    propagation; defensive "no principal on context" = 500 E_INTERNAL;
    "nil creator wired" = 500 E_INTERNAL; OpenAPI document carries the
    POST operation with security, x-required-action=keys.manage, and
    documented 201; token-not-persisted guard (token appears exactly
    once in the body, not in any header); two consecutive mints produce
    distinct (Prefix, SecretHash) — a guard on the auth-layer wiring;
    SA-actor mint leaves CreatedBy empty (NULL for the FK).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go: registered POST
    /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys (operationId createOrganizationAPIKey,
    RequiredAction=policy.ActionKeysManage, SuccessStatus=201, tagged
    api-keys, resolver=organizationIDResolver). Threaded the new
    apiKeyCreator argument through newRouteTable and refreshed the
    doc-comment naming every wired port.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: extended NewHandler with the
    apiKeyCreator parameter and updated the doc-comment for the new
    backing port.
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go: constructed serviceAccountRepo + apiKeyRepo
    once at startup, wired store.NewAPIKeyService(dataStore, orgRepo,
    serviceAccountRepo, apiKeyRepo, auditRepo), and passed it as the new
    NewHandler argument.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/{me,me_contract,members,members_create,
    members_delete,members_update,organizations,organizations_create,
    organizations_delete,organizations_patch,server,routes}_test.go: every
    NewHandler / newRouteTable call site updated with the new
    fakeAPIKeyCreator{} / extra nil argument.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; goimports -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...;
  go vet ./...; go test ./...; go test -race ./...
- Results: all passed. golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck still not
  installed locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - BE-0080 (contract tests for POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys)
    is almost fully satisfied by the new api_keys_create_test.go suite —
    that ticket can be marked passing the next iteration once the new
    suite is reviewed against the AC.
  - BE-0081 (policy matrix coverage for POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/
    api-keys) is now unblocked and is the highest-priority pending story.
  - The policy matrix proves cross-tenant + disabled + role coverage at
    the engine level (siblings of api_keys_list_policy_test.go); the
    contract suite already exercises owner/cross-tenant/disabled, so
    BE-0081 adds the engine-only role-table + grant-containment proofs.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Mutating-endpoint pattern reuse: the writer-port + store-unit-of-work
    pattern transfers verbatim from Membership/Organization to API keys.
    For each new mutating endpoint, declare a narrow Creator/Updater/
    Remover interface in httpapi (the handler depends only on it; tests
    supply a fake), and have store.<Service>{Create,Update,...} run the
    validator BEFORE Store.Write, then compose existence checks + INSERT
    + audit inside one tx so audit is impossible to bypass.
  - Credential primitives stay at the boundary: the handler calls
    auth.Generate(), passes only (Prefix, SecretHash) to the store layer,
    and surfaces the plaintext exactly once via Token.Reveal() at the
    wire boundary. Store never imports auth and never sees the plaintext;
    the redaction-by-default behaviour of auth.Token guards every other
    code path (slog, fmt, JSON), so the explicit Reveal() is the only
    greppable escape hatch.
  - CreatedBy must be empty for SA actors: api_keys.created_by REFERENCES
    users(id), so the column stores SQL NULL when an SA mints a key. The
    handler explicitly gates the assignment with p.Kind ==
    domain.KindUser; any other shape (writing the SA id into a users-FK
    column) would fail at the database with a confusing FK violation.
  - Service-account composite FK: the api_keys.service_account_id FK is
    composite on (organization_id, service_account_id), so the database
    rejects a cross-tenant SA reference even without the existence check.
    The service-layer Get is still required to surface the rejection as a
    typed NotFound (the FK would surface as a Conflict otherwise).
  - Scope vocabulary is conservative-by-default: a scope is bounded to
    [a-z0-9_:.-] up to 64 bytes with no duplicates and a 64-entry cap.
    The PRD has no enumerated catalog yet, so the validator enforces the
    SHAPE of a scope (printable, log-safe, machine-readable) without
    pinning specific verbs — leaving the action catalog to the policy
    package. When the catalog lands, this validator stays the boundary
    against control-character injection in audit metadata.
  - Test name collision: a top-level validInput() helper in the store
    package's _internal_test files collides with projectservice's existing
    fixture. Future store-layer service tests should namespace the helper
    (e.g. validAPIKeyInput()) — the gofmt-clean replace_all was a foot-
    gun and accidentally rewrote CodeInvalidInput → CodeInvalidAPIKeyInput
    before I caught it.
  - When the store.APIKeyService.Create signature took a `now time.Time`
    third argument for testable expires_at, both the http handler and the
    integration tests had to pass `time.Now()` (or a fixed time) — keep
    the orchestrator pure of time.Now() so a unit test can pin the wall
    clock.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0081
- What was implemented: policy matrix coverage for POST
  /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys (BE-0079's authorization sibling).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_create_policy_test.go (new):
    drives the real NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine() — the production
    request path, fake Authenticator only — through every principal class
    the PRD names for action keys.manage. The structural twin of
    api_keys_list_policy_test.go (BE-0078), adapted GET -> POST,
    reader -> creator, keys.read -> keys.manage; reuses the shared
    scaffolding from api_keys_test.go / api_keys_create_test.go
    (createAPIKeyHandlerFor, postAPIKey, decodeCreateAPIKey, orgPrincipal,
    fakeAPIKeyCreator, seedAPIKey, decodeError) so this file adds no
    helpers.
  - TestCreateAPIKeyPolicyMatrixRoles: every built-in role against an
    {org_id} naming its own home org. Owner/Admin allow via
    ReasonAllowedByRole (201, persisted projection + one-time token in
    the success envelope); Developer/Viewer/CI/Support deny via
    ReasonDeniedNoCapability (403 E_FORBIDDEN). keys.manage is CapAdmin
    (catalog.go: ActionKeysManage->CapAdmin), so the role matrix matches
    its keys.read sibling exactly — and the role matrix is independently
    locked here, so a regression that downgraded keys.manage to a
    non-Admin capability (a credential-minting escalation) would fire
    here, not only in the read sibling. Every deny path proves the
    creator was never reached via a captured store.CreateAPIKeyInput
    (got.OrganizationID stays ""), and the denied body never echoes the
    principal id, the supplied request name ("matrix"), the seeded key
    id, or its prefix. The happy-path branch also asserts the seedAPIKey
    secret_hash sentinel never reaches the wire.
  - TestCreateAPIKeyPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: a Disabled principal —
    the shape the auth layer surfaces revoked/expired credentials in —
    is denied with ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled even on an underlying
    Owner role; the creator is never reached and the denied body never
    echoes the principal id, the organization id, or the request name.
    A revoked or expired credential must never be able to mint a fresh
    credential, otherwise revocation is meaningless.
  - TestCreateAPIKeyPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal: the load-bearing
    cross-tenant case. A non-support owner of org_attacker minting in
    org_victim is ReasonDeniedCrossTenant. THE distinguishing assertion
    vs. members.read / org.read: a Support principal cannot mint a key
    cross-tenant either — pinned at both the engine
    (Decide(keys.manage, foreign org) for support = deny via
    ReasonDeniedCrossTenant) and the wire (handler returns 403, creator
    never reached, body never echoes victim org or request name). The
    engine's cross-tenant exception is gated on `required == CapRead ||
    required == CapSupport`, so CapAdmin is OUTSIDE it. Bonus: support
    cannot mint in its OWN home org either — ReasonDeniedNoCapability —
    locking the support role's read-only posture against a future catalog
    change that might silently grant CapAdmin minting authority.
  - TestCreateAPIKeyPolicyGrantContainment: scoped-grant containment
    against keys.manage on the org-root scope. A project/env/service-
    scoped Admin grant is denied via ReasonDeniedOutOfScope (covers()
    is one-way: a more-specific scope cannot reach a broader resource),
    not even for the key's own organization — the scoped key cannot be
    widened to mint an organization-wide credential. The three PRD-named
    containment properties (sibling project, production env, parent-
    level secrets) are pinned via project-update on a sibling project,
    environment-update on production, and env-write on the parent
    environment — all denied at the engine. The wire tie-back: project
    grantee POSTing against its own {org_id} = 403 ReasonDeniedOutOfScope
    + creator never reached + body never leaks the request name or
    fabricated key data. An org-level Admin grant is allowed via
    ReasonAllowedByGrant and end-to-end at the wire (201 + token + creator
    saw the path org_id). An org-level Viewer grant is denied — keys.manage
    requires CapAdmin, not CapRead, locking the CapAdmin requirement
    against the grant path. The same project-scoped grantee against a
    foreign {org_id} is denied via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant (the cross-
    tenant guard fires first since the scope's organization id no longer
    matches the principal's own), proving a scoped key cannot be smuggled
    across tenants by fabricating a path parameter.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_create_policy_test.go
  (new), ralph/prd.json (BE-0081 passes -> true), ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go vet ./...;
  go test -count=1 ./...; go test -race -count=1 ./....
- Results: all green. goimports/golangci-lint/staticcheck/govulncheck
  still not installed locally (documented in earlier entries).
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: none specific to BE-0081. The remaining
  api-keys triplets (BE-0083/BE-0084 GET-by-id, BE-0086/BE-0087 PATCH,
  BE-0089/BE-0090 DELETE, BE-0092/BE-0093 rotate) still need their
  implementation + matrix pairs — each will reuse the same shared
  scaffolding and follow the same four-test structure (role matrix,
  disabled, cross-tenant w/ support pin, grant containment).
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Both keys.read AND keys.manage are CapAdmin in catalog.go, so their
    policy matrices are STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL — same role allowances,
    same denials, same cross-tenant behavior (no support exception),
    same grant containment. Pinning both matrices independently isn't
    redundant: it locks the catalog so a future change that downgraded
    one but not the other would fire here.
  - The "creator never reached" guarantee for a POST policy test is
    structurally stronger via fakeAPIKeyCreator's captured got pointer
    (`got *store.CreateAPIKeyInput`) than via a sentinel error: a 403
    alone doesn't prove the creator wasn't called, but
    got.OrganizationID == "" after the request does. The shared
    fakeAPIKeyCreator already accepts a got pointer, so this is free —
    future POST/mutation policy tests across the codebase should adopt
    this pattern.
  - The validCreateAPIKeyBody constant (`{"name":"matrix"}`) is the
    minimal valid body the endpoint accepts. Keeping the request name a
    short non-secret token like "matrix" lets the body-redaction
    assertions check for a specific JSON value (`"matrix"`) and trust
    that absence proves no field of the request reached the response —
    a stronger guarantee than asserting any single secret is absent.
  - This file landed BE-0081 (p1, policy matrix) directly atop BE-0079
    (p2, implementation) following the BE-0076 -> BE-0078 pattern: the
    p1 matrix story is always blocked on its p2 implementation, and the
    matrix file is a near-mechanical adaptation of its sibling once the
    p2 wire contract + shared scaffolding land. For the remaining api-key
    triplets, the implementation story remains the real unblocker; the
    matrix file is a tight clone.

  still not installed locally (documented in earlier entries).
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: BE-0083 (contract tests) and BE-0084
  (policy matrix coverage) are the natural sibling stories — the contract
  coverage already in api_keys_get_test.go addresses much of BE-0083's
  scope (success envelope, error envelope, request_id propagation, OpenAPI
  operation registration, unauthenticated/unauthorized/invalid/not-found/
  happy paths) but BE-0084's role-by-role matrix against NewHandler +
  policy.NewEngine() is its own dedicated file, to land in the next
  iteration. The remaining api-keys triplets (BE-0085/BE-0086/BE-0087
  PATCH, BE-0088/BE-0089/BE-0090 DELETE, BE-0091/BE-0092/BE-0093 rotate)
  still need their implementation + matrix pairs.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The "fakeXReader carries the union of list + get fields" pattern is
    established by fakeMembershipReader and is the right shape when a
    single port interface backs both a LIST and a GET-by-id endpoint:
    keys/err/gotOrgID for the list, key/getErr/gotKeyOrgID/gotKeyID for
    the get. The zero value must keep its existing meaning for every
    callsite that only exercises the OTHER route — so GetAPIKey returns
    apierr.NotFound on the zero-value key (not an empty struct success),
    mirroring fakeMembershipReader.GetMember.
  - The store-side *APIKeyReader is the adapter, NOT a SQL-issuing
    duplicate: GetAPIKey opens its own Store.Read transaction and
    delegates to APIKeyRepository.Get. Tenant scoping is inherited from
    the repository — TestAPIKeyRepositoryGetIsTenantScoped already proves
    it. The new TestAPIKeyReaderGetAPIKey pins the adapter wiring
    (Store.Read + repo call + error mapping) end to end without
    re-proving the repository's tenant filter.
  - keys.read is CapAdmin, NOT CapRead: a viewer/developer cannot read a
    single key (just as they cannot list them), and the support
    cross-tenant exception (CapRead-only) does NOT apply. The
    GetAPIKey-by-id route therefore uses organizationIDResolver and the
    same denial semantics as the LIST route — the matrix is "owner +
    admin allow; viewer + developer + ci + support deny; cross-tenant
    deny for everyone, including support". The new contract tests pin
    each of those, but the dedicated BE-0084 policy matrix file should
    independently exercise every role against the real policy.NewEngine().
  - Documentation comment maintenance: when a port grows from one
    endpoint to two (LIST -> LIST + GET), update both the port's own
    doc comment AND the newRouteTable doc comment that names which
    dependency backs which route. A drift here is invisible to vet but
    misleads future contributors.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0084
- What was implemented: Policy-matrix coverage for GET
  /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys/{key_id} — the BE-0082
  implementation sibling. Same authorization contract as BE-0078
  (list policy matrix) since both LIST and GET-by-id carry the same
  keys.read action (CapAdmin) and the same organizationIDResolver. The
  matrix file is a near-mechanical adaptation of api_keys_list_policy_test.go
  to the GET-by-id wire shape (the {key_id} path parameter, the
  fakeAPIKeyReader.key/gotKeyOrgID/gotKeyID/getErr fields, the
  decodeGetAPIKey envelope), reusing every helper already in
  api_keys_test.go and api_keys_get_test.go — no new scaffolding.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_get_policy_test.go (new):
    four tests against the real NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine().
    - TestGetAPIKeyPolicyMatrixRoles: all six built-in roles
      (owner/admin/developer/viewer/ci/support) against an ({org_id},
      {key_id}) naming a key inside the principal's own home
      organization. Owner and Admin hold CapAdmin and allow keys.read
      via ReasonAllowedByRole — the reader is reached on BOTH the
      {org_id} and {key_id} path parameters and the response carries
      the named key. Developer, Viewer, CI, and Support all lack
      CapAdmin and are denied with 403 E_FORBIDDEN carrying
      ReasonDeniedNoCapability — the reader's gotKeyOrgID + gotKeyID
      both stay empty, and the denied body never echoes the seeded
      keyID or prefix. The {key_id} path is NOT consulted by the
      engine: the engine assertion uses orgRoot only, and the wire
      assertion proves the denied path's reader-never-reached property.
    - TestGetAPIKeyPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: a revoked- or
      expired-key principal (surfaced to policy as Disabled, with the
      underlying role kept as Owner so the disabled flag is the only
      thing in the way) is denied even when the underlying role would
      have allowed. Stable 403 E_FORBIDDEN carrying
      ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled, the reader is never reached
      (gotKeyOrgID + gotKeyID both stay empty), and the error body
      never echoes the principal id, the organization id, the key id,
      or the prefix — no oracle through the failure path.
    - TestGetAPIKeyPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal: a non-support
      owner of org_attacker reading a key of org_victim is a
      deterministic 403 ReasonDeniedCrossTenant, the reader is never
      reached, and the body carries no cross-tenant id. A support
      principal of org_yalla — the one that COULD have read a member
      or organization cross-tenant — is ALSO denied cross-tenant for
      keys.read with the same ReasonDeniedCrossTenant: the engine
      verdict and the handler outcome are BOTH pinned, since support
      IS the cross-tenant exception for members.read. The engine-level
      cross-tenant boundary is asserted directly via policy.Decide. A
      bonus assertion proves support cannot read keys of its OWN home
      tenant either: RoleSupport lacks CapAdmin entirely, so within
      the home tenant the verdict is ReasonDeniedNoCapability — not
      the cross-tenant denial — locking the support role's
      read-only-for-non-key-data posture at the engine level so a
      future catalog change cannot silently grant it key-read authority.
    - TestGetAPIKeyPolicyGrantContainment: a scoped key (no role,
      grants only) holding an Admin grant at the project, environment,
      or service scope is denied at the organization-root resource the
      resolver emits, with ReasonDeniedOutOfScope. The three
      containment properties — sibling-project, production
      environment, parent-level secrets — are pinned against the
      engine via the project/env/service grants (ActionProjectUpdate
      for sibling-project; ActionEnvironmentUpdate for production;
      ActionEnvWrite on the parent env for parent-level secrets), then
      tied back at the wire by proving the project grantee is denied
      its OWN ({org_id},{key_id}) with the stable out-of-scope reason,
      the reader never reached, the body never echoing the seeded
      keyID or prefix. An organization-level Admin grant DOES cover
      the org-root scope and is allowed via ReasonAllowedByGrant, with
      the reader reached on BOTH the {org_id} AND {key_id} path
      parameters — and a Viewer grant at the same scope is denied
      (CapAdmin not CapRead), locking the CapAdmin requirement against
      the grant path so a future catalog change cannot silently
      downgrade keys.read to a read-level capability. The cross-tenant
      smuggling guard fires for the same project-scoped grantee
      against a foreign {org_id} — the scoped key cannot be widened
      across tenants by fabricating a path parameter.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_get_policy_test.go
  (new), ralph/prd.json (BE-0084 passes -> true), ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go vet ./...;
  go build ./...; go test -count=1 ./...; go test -race -count=1 ./....
- Results: all green. goimports/golangci-lint/staticcheck/govulncheck
  still not installed locally (documented in earlier entries).
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: none specific to BE-0084. The
  remaining api-keys triplets (BE-0085/BE-0086/BE-0087 PATCH,
  BE-0088/BE-0089/BE-0090 DELETE, BE-0091/BE-0092/BE-0093 rotate)
  still need their implementation + matrix pairs — each will reuse
  the same shared scaffolding and follow the same four-test structure
  (role matrix, disabled, cross-tenant w/ support pin, grant
  containment). The natural next iteration is BE-0085 (PATCH
  implementation), which unblocks BE-0086 contract tests + BE-0087
  policy matrix.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The pattern "GET-by-id policy matrix clones LIST policy matrix"
    holds when (a) both endpoints share the same action constant in
    the catalog and (b) both routes use the same Resolver (here:
    organizationIDResolver -> organization-root scope). The only
    delta is wire-shape: LIST uses (orgID) + ListAPIKeys + Data.APIKeys
    + gotOrgID; GET-by-id uses (orgID, keyID) + GetAPIKey + Data.APIKey
    + gotKeyOrgID/gotKeyID/getErr. The structural authorization
    assertions — role allow/deny set, ReasonDeniedNoCapability vs
    ReasonAllowedByRole, ReasonDeniedCrossTenant for non-support AND
    support, ReasonDeniedOutOfScope for scoped grants — are identical.
    This is by design: organizationIDResolver projects the resource to
    organization-root regardless of how many path parameters the
    endpoint exposes, so the engine sees the same input and the matrix
    must therefore be the same.
  - When a GET-by-id endpoint's authorization decision is independent
    of its second path parameter (as here: keys.read is decided on
    {org_id} only — {key_id} only selects the row once authorized),
    the matrix tests should still assert BOTH path parameters propagate
    to the reader on the allowed path (gotOrgID == org AND gotKeyID ==
    keyID). The reader's "never reached" property on the denied path
    then has the strongest possible meaning: not just "no row
    returned" but "the {key_id} we sent was never used to look up
    anything", which structurally prevents a cross-tenant {key_id}
    from acting as an oracle through any read side-effect.
  - The fakeAPIKeyReader.key / gotKeyOrgID / gotKeyID / getErr fields
    already exist for the GET-by-id contract suite (api_keys_get_test.go,
    BE-0082) — the matrix file reuses them without extending the fake.
    Note the zero-value getErr path: when fakeAPIKeyReader.key is the
    zero value, GetAPIKey returns apierr.NotFound (see api_keys_test.go
    line 80). The policy-matrix tests always set f.key to a fully
    populated seedAPIKey on the ALLOWED path so the allowed assertions
    can prove field-level projection; on the DENIED path, the engine
    short-circuits before GetAPIKey runs, so the f.key value doesn't
    matter — but we still set it to non-zero so a regression that
    accidentally lets the reader run would surface as a 200 with the
    seeded data, not as a confusing 404.

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - PRE-EXISTING (not introduced by this story): TestAPIKeyServiceCreate*
    integration tests fail when run against a live Postgres because
    buildAPIKeyToCreate calls domain.ParseID and the testutil Factory
    produces ids with a 20-character suffix while ParseID requires 26
    (Crockford base32 over idEntropyBytes=16). Every Create integration
    test has always rejected the seeded fixture ids with E_INVALID_INPUT.
    This is a long-standing test-infrastructure mismatch — either the
    factory should mint canonical ids through domain.NewID, or
    buildAPIKeyToCreate's ParseID guard should be relaxed to a HasPrefix
    check the way validateMembershipUpdate already does. I sidestepped
    the issue for BE-0085 by (a) using HasPrefix in the new Update
    validation path, and (b) seeding api_keys rows directly through the
    repository in seedAPIKeyForUpdate instead of going through Create.
    This is worth its own dedicated story; fixing it here would expand
    BE-0085 well past its scope.
  - PATCH is a partial-update of name and scopes only. Lifecycle
    mutations (extend expiry, revoke, rotate) are explicitly NOT in
    scope — they belong to BE-0088 (DELETE) and BE-0091 (POST rotate).
    If a future story adds expires_at to the patch surface, it must use
    the **time double-pointer / sentinel idiom so a JSON `null` reaches
    the store as "clear the column" rather than "leave unchanged".
  - The api_keys schema (migration 0003) carries no `version` column, so
    PATCH has no optimistic-concurrency precondition today — concurrent
    re-writes are last-writer-wins. If the api-key surface ever needs
    If-Match semantics, the migration must land first (parallel to the
    organizations version+trigger from 0009).
  - BE-0086 (contract tests for PATCH) and BE-0087 (policy matrix for
    PATCH, priority 1) are now unblocked. The current handler tests
    cover most of BE-0086 already, but the policy matrix tests will
    need a sibling api_keys_update_policy_test.go that exercises every
    role × scope combination, the same way api_keys_get_policy_test.go
    does for GET.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The endpoint triplet (implement @ p2, contract tests @ p2, policy
    matrix @ p1) means the p1 story is always blocked on its p2
    implementation. When the next pending story is a policy matrix for
    an endpoint that does not yet exist, pick the lower-priority
    implementation first; do not block on the priority number alone.
  - Adding a new dependency to NewHandler / newRouteTable touches
    ~15 test files. The mechanical part is a one-pass regex rewrite over
    `fakeAPIKeyCreator{}, nil)` → `fakeAPIKeyCreator{}, fakeAPIKeyUpdater{}, nil)`
    (and the `, logger)` variant); the only non-mechanical site is the
    file that uses a function variable instead of the canned fake
    (api_keys_create_test.go's `, creator, nil)`). Plan for ~13 edits
    when adding a port; the next port should consider whether the
    newTestHandler helper can absorb it (server_test.go).
  - The "partial update" pattern in this codebase is consistent across
    organizations, memberships, and now api-keys: pointer fields on the
    input DTO, validation produces a {fields, *value, ...} change record,
    the in-tx read materialises the current row, the non-nil fields
    overwrite, and the audit metadata carries `updated_fields` as a
    stable wire-name list — never the submitted values. Following this
    template keeps the patch surface uniform.
  - The factory id ↔ ParseID mismatch is a real, long-standing
    integration-test breakage in store/apikeyservice_test.go that I had
    to navigate around. Worth a dedicated story to either fix the
    factory or relax buildAPIKeyToCreate the same way validateMembership*
    already does for member_id.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0087

    BOTH the {org_id} AND {key_id} path params and the response carries

    return 403 E_FORBIDDEN, the updater never runs, and the denied body
    never echoes the seeded key_id or prefix. Support is the
    load-bearing case shared with BE-0084: CapAdmin is excluded from
    the support cross-tenant exception, so support cannot mutate keys
    of its own home tenant either.

    (revoked or expired credential) whose underlying role would have

    id, the organization id, nor the seeded key data.

    cross-tenant owner is denied with ReasonDeniedCrossTenant; a
    Yalla-internal support principal is ALSO denied cross-tenant
    (CapAdmin excludes the support exception); engine verdicts are
    pinned directly against an api-key Resource so the resolver-shape
    is exactly what the engine sees. Bonus assertion: a support
    principal cannot mutate keys of its OWN home org either — the
    home-tenant verdict is ReasonDeniedNoCapability, not the
    cross-tenant denial. This locks the support role's posture so a

    invariants the PRD names are pinned engine-level against
    project/env/service-scoped admin grants (sibling project, staging
    vs production, service vs parent-env-write), then tied back to the

    own ({org_id},{key_id}) with ReasonDeniedOutOfScope, body free of
    key_id/prefix. An organization-level Admin grant DOES allow
    (ReasonAllowedByGrant) and the same patch end-to-end succeeds with
    the updater reached on both path params; an organization-level
    Viewer grant does NOT allow (locks CapAdmin against a downgrade to
    CapRead). A foreign {org_id} on a scoped grantee still surfaces
    ReasonDeniedCrossTenant — a scoped key cannot be smuggled across
    tenants by fabricating a path parameter.

    no secret material crosses the boundary. The contract sibling
    (BE-0086) already pins envelope shape and the secret_hash sentinel
    is asserted out of the wire; here the structural guard is "denied
    response never echoes the seeded key_id or prefix", which it does.

    already passes=true, so this story has no further blocker. Next
    open p1 in the queue is BE-0090 (policy matrix for DELETE
    /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys/{key_id}), still gated on its
    p2 implementation story BE-0088.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The keys.read (BE-0084) and keys.manage (BE-0087) matrices are
    structurally identical because the catalog maps BOTH to CapAdmin
    (catalog.go:120-121). The wire-contract differences are: GET reads
    via APIKeyReader.GetAPIKey and asserts gotKeyOrgID/gotKeyID;
    PATCH writes via APIKeyUpdater.Update and asserts
    gotInput.OrganizationID/gotInput.KeyID. Use seedAPIKey for the
    happy-path response value either way — it is the credential
    helper, not the reader-vs-updater distinction.
  - apiKeyIDResolver emits Kind=domain.KindAPIKey, NOT
    KindOrganization like organizationIDResolver. The engine's
    cross-tenant clause cares about Scope.OrganizationID, not Kind,
    so the verdict shape is the same — but engine-level assertions in
    policy_test files must use the matching Kind to pin the exact
    resolver shape on the wire path.
  - The handler-comment claim in api_keys.go that "keys.manage is a
    CapManage action" is misleading commentary — there is no
    CapManage in capabilities.go. catalog.go is authoritative:
    ActionKeysManage requires CapAdmin. Trust catalog.go over
    handler-comment when they disagree.
  - For a denied-policy case driven through the wire, the request
    body must still be at least a structurally-valid PATCH ({"name":
    "renamed"}) so that the policy boundary is provably the only
    thing rejecting it — an empty {} body would hit the handler's
    "patch with no field" 400 if the policy ever let it through. The
    minimal-valid-body convention makes a future regression where
    the policy allows a denied caller surface as a 200, not a 400.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0088
- What was implemented: DELETE /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys/{key_id},
  the revoke-api-key customer-facing endpoint. Revocation is the customer-
  facing soft delete for an API key: the api_keys row stays in the database
  so the audit trail of who minted it remains linked to a live row, but the
  credential is permanently unusable from that moment on. Every subsequent
  authentication attempt fails through the uniform invalid-credentials path
  (the existing prefix-lookup -> IsUsable check rejects a revoked row).
  - internal/controlplane/store/apikey.go: changed APIKeyRepository.Revoke
    to return (APIKey, error) using UPDATE ... RETURNING so a caller can
    see the row Postgres just stamped (revoked_at + trigger-refreshed
    updated_at) without a follow-up Get. SQL-level idempotency preserved
    via COALESCE(revoked_at, $now); the no-row case maps to apierr.NotFound
    via errors.Is(pgx.ErrNoRows). The single existing test of the
    repository was updated; one other caller (credentials_test.go) was
    updated to discard the new row return value.
  - internal/controlplane/store/apikeyservice.go: added RevokeAPIKeyInput
    (OrganizationID, KeyID, plus the Actor*/RequestID/CorrelationID
    correlation set that the handler fills in from policy.PrincipalFromContext
    + telemetry.FromContext, same pattern as the create/update inputs).
    Added APIKeyService.Revoke(ctx, in, now): id-shape pre-check (kind-
    prefix guard mirroring Update); in tx — Get current row (tenant-
    scoped, so cross-tenant key_id is the same typed NotFound as a missing
    row), conflict early if current.IsRevoked() (apierr.Conflict, so a
    re-revoke is never a silent success that would write a misleading
    audit record), call repo.Revoke, append audit event with metadata
    {organization_id, revoked_at=RFC3339Nano} — no credential material,
    just non-secret structural values. now is plumbed in so tests pin
    time without monkey-patching time.Now.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys.go: added the APIKeyRevoker port
    (interface depends on store.RevokeAPIKeyInput so the handler stays
    unit-testable with a fake), revokeAPIKeyPayload wire DTO (single
    apiKeyResource — same stable wire shape as every other api-key
    endpoint, the secret hash is never projected), errNoAPIKeyRevoker
    typed-internal sentinel for the wiring-error path, and
    revokeAPIKeyHandler — a thin handler that reads
    policy.PrincipalFromContext + telemetry.FromContext, forwards to the
    revoker with the actor + correlation set, and renders 200 OK carrying
    the revoked row (mirrors members.Remove's terminal-view convention).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go: registered the DELETE route
    in the data-driven route table — RequiresAuth=true,
    RequiredAction=keys.manage (CapManage — no cross-tenant support
    exception, mirror of PATCH semantics), resolver=apiKeyIDResolver (the
    same resolver PATCH uses, scopes the policy decision to the {org_id}
    path parameter), Method=DELETE, OperationID=revokeOrganizationAPIKey,
    tags=[api-keys], 200 default success status. newRouteTable signature
    gained apiKeyRevoker APIKeyRevoker.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler signature gained
    apiKeyRevoker APIKeyRevoker (16th positional arg, last before logger),
    forwarded into newRouteTable. The "registering an authenticated route
    without authenticator/engine panics at startup" fail-fast posture

    now unblocked; api_keys_delete_test.go already covers a good chunk of
    BE-0089's surface but those remain separate PRD stories.
  - Pre-existing TestAPIKeyServiceCreate* failures should be filed and
    fixed — they break the integration suite for everyone touching the
    api-key store.
  - "Record an audit event for every ... denied authorization decision"
    is still N/A at the per-endpoint level: RequireAuth does not yet
    emit audit events for denied decisions for any endpoint. The
    cross-cutting follow-up that lands denied-decision auditing in
    RequireAuth will pick up DELETE /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-
    keys/{key_id} along with every other authenticated route.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When changing a repository method's signature (here Revoke's `error`
    return became `(APIKey, error)`), greppping ALL callers is mandatory
    — even test-only ones, because go test compiles them. The
    apikey_test.go + credentials_test.go updates were needed before
    `go build` would pass.
  - The "soft delete" surface for an API key is a one-way revocation,
    NOT the scheduled-deletion-with-deletion_scheduled_at pattern used by
    organization.delete. An API key's revoked_at column already exists
    and the auth path already enforces "revoked => unauthenticated", so
    revocation is the natural and immediate customer-facing soft delete.
    Return 200 OK with the revoked snapshot (mirror members.Remove), not
    202 Accepted (which is for asynchronous teardown like
    organization.delete schedules).
  - SQL idempotency is fine for the repository, but the customer
    endpoint should NOT silently succeed on a re-revoke — the caller's
    view of the lifecycle is stale, and a silent success would write a
    misleading audit record. Pre-check the current state in the service
    layer (Get -> isRevoked() -> Conflict) and let the repository remain
    silently idempotent for non-customer callers (workers, admin jobs).
    This mirrors organization.delete's scheduling pre-check exactly.
  - "Add policy matrix coverage" and "Add contract tests" stories
    skipped on the PRD don't necessarily mean the endpoint is
    under-tested. The BE-008x cycle pattern in this repo has been
    "implement + happy/edge tests in one commit, policy matrix in a
    follow-up". BE-0083/BE-0086/BE-0089 in particular cover OpenAPI/
    contract assertions that overlap heavily with the implementation
    commit's own tests.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0090
- What was implemented: api_keys_delete_policy_test.go — policy-matrix
  coverage for DELETE /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys/{key_id}.
  Mirrors the BE-0087 sibling (PATCH api_keys_update_policy_test.go) since
  both endpoints share action keys.manage + apiKeyIDResolver, only
  swapping the handler/helper/fake/input triplet:
    revokeAPIKeyHandlerFor / deleteAPIKey / decodeRevokeAPIKey /
    fakeAPIKeyRevoker / store.RevokeAPIKeyInput.
  Three Test functions, no new scaffolding:
    1. TestRevokeAPIKeyPolicyMatrixRoles — every built-in role
       (owner/admin/developer/viewer/ci/support) drives both the engine
       Decide call and the wired handler against ({org_id},{key_id})
       inside the principal's home org. CapAdmin holders allow via
       ReasonAllowedByRole; the rest deny via ReasonDeniedNoCapability,
       the revoker is never reached on a deny, and the denied body
       cannot echo the seeded key id or prefix.
    2. TestRevokeAPIKeyPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys — a Disabled principal
       (the auth-layer surface for both revoked and expired credentials)
       whose underlying role is Owner is denied via
       ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled; the revoker is never reached and
       the body never echoes principal id, organization, key id, or
       prefix. The "stale credential scorched-earths the tenant's CI
       keys" abuse is the load-bearing motivation.
    3. TestRevokeAPIKeyPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal — a non-support
       cross-tenant owner AND a Yalla support principal both deny against
       a foreign org with ReasonDeniedCrossTenant; engine verdict pinned
       directly. Bonus: support cannot revoke its OWN home-tenant keys
       either (ReasonDeniedNoCapability — RoleSupport lacks CapAdmin),
       which locks the support role's read-only-for-key-data posture
       against silent catalog drift.
    4. TestRevokeAPIKeyPolicyGrantContainment — sibling project,
       production environment, and parent-level secrets pinned via the
       project/env/service grant Decide calls; then the load-bearing
       extension: a project/env/service-scoped Admin grant does NOT
       cover the api-key scope of its OWN org (ReasonDeniedOutOfScope),
       so a leaked scoped CI key cannot be weaponised to revoke
       organization-wide owner keys. Tied back at the wire: project
       grantee gets 403 OutOfScope at its own ({org_id},{key_id}); an
       org-level Admin grant gets 200 with the revoker reached on both
       parameters; an org-level Viewer grant is denied (CapAdmin not
       CapRead); the same project grantee against a foreign {org_id} is
       still denied via the cross-tenant guard.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_delete_policy_test.go
  (new), ralph/prd.json (passes: true), ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...;
  go test -run 'TestRevokeAPIKeyPolicy' ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/;
  go test ./...; go test -race ./....
- Results: all passed. goimports not installed locally (PATH); gofmt is
  the source of truth and ran clean. golangci-lint, staticcheck, and
  govulncheck still not installed locally (documented in earlier
  iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups: none for BE-0090. The same load-bearing
  property (a scoped key cannot widen to org-wide key.* operations)
  applies identically to keys.manage on POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/
  api-keys/{key_id}/rotate (BE-0093, the next p1 in the queue), and the
  matrix structure here transplants cleanly with no new helpers.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The "Add policy matrix coverage" stories for the api-keys endpoints
    that share action keys.manage (PATCH/DELETE/rotate) are pure mirrors
    of one another — only the handler/helper/fake/input quadruple
    differs. Once BE-0087's structure existed, BE-0090 was a sub-200
    line edit-with-substitutions; rotate (BE-0093) will be the same.
  - DELETE has no body, so the "minimal valid body keeps the deny path
    indistinguishable from a would-have-succeeded request" caveat the
    PATCH file's preamble carries does NOT apply here. Replaced with a
    one-sentence note that the policy boundary fires purely off the
    {org_id} path parameter — keep this distinction when mirroring to
    other body-less mutating endpoints (POST .../rotate also has no
    body, so the same simplification applies there).
  - The "revoker received the path's key_id verbatim" assertion only
    holds for ALLOW cases — gotInput must be tested for empty fields on
    DENY cases (proves the policy boundary stopped the request before
    it reached the persistence layer). Mirror this everywhere:
    `gotInput.OrganizationID != "" || gotInput.KeyID != ""` is the
    structural anti-bypass invariant.
  - seedAPIKey returns a store.APIKey whose RevokedAt is nil by default;
    for the success-path assertions in a DELETE test the seeded row has
    to mimic the post-revoke snapshot, so the test stamps a deterministic
    revokedAt and assigns persisted.RevokedAt = &revokedAt before handing
    it to the fake. The PATCH equivalent did not need this because the
    success snapshot it returns is just the renamed row.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0032
- What was implemented: internal/controlplane/reconcile, the pure
  reconciliation engine that classifies drift between Yalla's source-of-truth
  hierarchy and Dokploy's actual state into safe, dangerous, or unmanaged
  buckets and routes each through the matching port (Repairer / ReviewRecorder
  / UnmanagedRecorder).
  - doc.go: package overview that names the three drift kinds, the stable
    DriftReason vocabulary, and the Plan/Apply lifecycle the worker drives.
  - types.go: the DriftKind / ActionType / DriftReason / ResourceLevel
    enums; the Desired*/Actual* in-memory snapshot shapes (Organization ->
    Project -> Environment -> Service, with EnvVars and Domains on services);
    ServiceRef and DomainRef (resolved Yalla+Dokploy locators); UnmanagedResource
    and ReviewEvent payload structs. Closed-set Valid() guards on DriftKind
    so a future bug can't smuggle in a new kind silently. Value-free design:
    Reason/Level/Kind never carry env-var values or hostnames a customer
    submitted.
  - diff.go: the pure Diff(desired, actual) Plan function. Walks every level
    top-down with Dokploy-ID-keyed lookup tables, classifies divergence, and
    emits a stable sorted Plan. Safe drift (env_var_changed, env_var_missing,
    env_var_extra, domain_missing) -> Repairer; dangerous drift
    (service_missing / database_missing on a recorded Dokploy ID,
    domain_renamed, service_type_changed) -> Reviewer; everything in actual
    without a desired counterpart (project / environment / service / domain
    level) -> Unmanaged. The DesiredValue field is the only path an env-var
    value reaches an Action, and only ActionUpdateEnvVar consumes it.
  - reconcile.go: the Reconciler engine and its ports
    (DesiredStateReader, ActualStateReader, Repairer, ReviewRecorder,
    UnmanagedRecorder). New() fails fast with apierr.Internal on any missing
    port. Plan() validates the org ID (apierr.InvalidInput on blank /
    malformed / wrong-kind), preserves typed apierr from adapters, and
    upgrades untyped errors to apierr.StoreUnavailable (desired reader) or
    apierr.DokployUnavailable (actual reader). An organization whose
    DokployID is empty short-circuits to an empty plan — pre-provisioned
    state is not drift. Apply() is best-effort: every per-action failure is
    captured in Result.Failures with the error string scrubbed through
    output.Redactor; the loop only stops when ctx is cancelled. Reconcile()
    is the Plan+Apply convenience wrapper that emits one structured tick log.
  - AGENTS.md: documents the "value-free classification", safe-vs-dangerous
    boundary, deterministic-order, best-effort Apply, and "quarantine never
    delete" conventions for future adapters and follow-up reviewers.
  - Tests: 21 unit tests across diff_test.go and reconcile_test.go covering
    every acceptance test case explicitly — TestDiff_DeletedApp (dangerous,
    service_missing), TestDiff_RenamedDomain (dangerous, domain_renamed),
    TestDiff_ChangedEnvVar (safe, env_var_changed, with a "no value leaks
    into the classification fields" assertion), TestDiff_MissingDatabase
    (dangerous, database_missing — separate code from missing application),
    TestDiff_UnmanagedResource (unmanaged at service level). Plus
    no-drift baseline, missing-env-var safe ensure, extra-env-var safe
    removal, service-type change, unprovisioned-desired ignored, and
    deterministic ordering. Engine-level: TestNew_RequiresPorts (each missing
    port yields apierr.Internal), TestPlan_ValidationFailure (blank,
    malformed, wrong-kind org IDs return apierr.InvalidInput with typed
    FieldViolations, no port is called), TestPlan_NotFoundFromDesired
    (typed apierr.NotFound preserved, actual reader not called),
    TestPlan_AuthorizationFailureFromDesired (apierr.Forbidden preserved),
    TestPlan_UntypedDesiredErrorBecomesStoreUnavailable +
    TestPlan_UntypedActualErrorBecomesDokployUnavailable (untyped errors
    upgraded, token strings scrubbed), TestPlan_UnprovisionedOrganizationReturnsEmptyPlan,
    TestApply_RepairsSafeDrift (env-var Repairer call carries Secret=true,
    Reviewer not called, secret never reaches captured log buffer),
    TestApply_RecordsDangerousDrift (deleted app -> Reviewer, Repairer
    untouched), TestApply_MarksUnmanagedResource (rogue service -> Unmanaged
    only, locates parent without exposing it), TestApply_BestEffortContinuesPastFailure
    (one Repairer error doesn't stop the rest of the plan, Failure.Err is
    scrubbed through Redactor with no upstream token leak),
    TestApply_CancelledContextStopsLoop (ctx.Err() returned mid-loop),
    TestApply_UnmanagedActionWithoutPayloadIsCaptured (malformed-internal
    plan captured as Failure, not panic), TestApply_RedactsSensitiveErrorsInResult
    (Reviewer's upstream "Authorization: Bearer ..." string scrubbed in
    Failure.Err and in the captured log).
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/reconcile/{doc.go,types.go,diff.go,
  reconcile.go,diff_test.go,reconcile_test.go,AGENTS.md} (all new),
  ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...;
  go test ./...; go test -race ./....
- Results: all passed. goimports binary not installed locally (documented in
  earlier iterations); golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck still not
  installed locally.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - The acceptance criterion "stable yalla.output.v1 / yalla.error.v1
    envelopes" is N/A: reconcile is a pure service package with no HTTP
    surface. The taxonomy is enforced at the apierr boundary instead —
    every error the engine returns is either a typed apierr.* preserved
    from an adapter or a typed apierr.* produced by the engine
    (Invalid / Internal / StoreUnavailable / DokployUnavailable).
  - "Integration tests run against isolated Postgres migrations" is N/A
    here for the same reason: reconcile depends on no database. The
    store-backed DesiredStateReader and the store-backed Review/Unmanaged
    recorders will land as their own follow-up adapter stories once the
    service/application/domain persistence schema (currently
    not on disk past migration 0011) ships.
  - The Dokploy-backed ActualStateReader adapter is also a follow-up: the
    typed dokploy.Client today only exposes Ensure*/Get*/Remove operations,
    not bulk List operations needed to enumerate actual state. When that
    adapter lands it will add the List intents (or paginated reads) to
    dokploy/intents.go alongside the engine adapter.
  - The five "test cases" enumerated in the PRD acceptance criteria are all
    covered by named tests (deleted app, renamed domain, changed env var,
    missing database, unmanaged resource). Each test asserts both the
    classification (Kind/Reason) and the no-value-leak property, so a
    regression that started routing values into Reason or EnvVarKey would
    fail loudly.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Crockford Base32 (lowercase) excludes i / l / o / u — hand-rolled test
    IDs that contain "kvl" / "demo" / "old" / "ufo" fail domain.ParseID().
    Use domain.MustNewID(domain.KindX) in tests (the existing convention in
    internal/controlplane/dokploy/mapping_test.go and others) rather than
    string-literal IDs; this also future-proofs tests against ID-format
    changes. A test failure like
    "error code = E_INVALID_INPUT; want E_NOT_FOUND" where every port-side
    test fails with the same code is almost always the org ID validator
    rejecting the fixture before the port is reached.
  - apierr.Internal(cause).Error() returns the fixed Message string
    "an internal error occurred" only — the wrapped cause is reachable via
    errors.Unwrap, not via Error(). When a test wants to assert a redacted
    upstream string is captured, walk the chain with errors.Unwrap (see
    errChainString in reconcile_test.go) instead of inspecting
    err.Error() directly.
  - apierr.Forbidden/NotFound from an adapter must be PRESERVED, not
    re-wrapped — the engine's wrapDesiredErr / wrapActualErr only upgrade
    untyped errors and short-circuit on a *yerr.Error via errors.As.
    Otherwise the typed taxonomy collapses to "E_UNAVAILABLE" everywhere
    and callers lose the ability to act on the real reason.
  - For a Reviewer port, the action's Reason carries the classification
    code but the engine still needs to choose a Level for the ReviewEvent:
    LevelDomain for ActionReviewRenamedDomain, LevelService for everything
    else dangerous. Hard-code that mapping inside reviewEventFor; if it
    drifts, the review queue UX (not yet built) will route to the wrong
    triage view.
  - When the planner inserts a "service type changed" review action it
    still scans the service's env-var and domain children. Suppressing the
    children would lose drift signal the operator may want to see before
    deciding whether to adopt or destroy the type-changed service; emitting
    review-only actions for the service body keeps the deeper diff
    available without auto-repairing through a wrong-typed service.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0091
- Implemented POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys/{key_id}/rotate
  (Rotate API key) end to end through the same vertical the rest of the
  api-key endpoints follow: store-layer unit of work, narrow handler port,
  thin handler, route + OpenAPI metadata folded into newRouteTable, full
  test surface (contract/wire + policy matrix at handler, integration at
  store).
- Store layer:
  - apikey.go: APIKeyRepository.RotateCredential — `UPDATE api_keys SET
    prefix=$3, secret_hash=$4 WHERE organization_id=$1 AND id=$2 RETURNING ...`,
    tenant-scoped (a cross-tenant key_id matches no rows → typed NotFound,
    never a 5xx and never disguised as another tenant's key), nil-tx
    guarded, mapWriteError funnels a prefix-collision into the same typed
    Conflict the other writes produce.
  - apikeyservice.go: RotateAPIKeyInput + APIKeyService.Rotate. Validates
    id shape first (so an invalid id never opens a transaction), demands
    server-minted Prefix and SecretHash as a wiring-error Internal (the
    handler is responsible for minting through auth.Generate before
    delegating), then runs read-current-row → reject revoked/expired as
    typed Conflict → repository.RotateCredential → audit.Append, all in
    one transaction. The audit metadata carries the new public prefix
    (non-secret) as rotated_prefix; the secret hash is never recorded.
- HTTP layer:
  - api_keys.go: APIKeyRotator interface + rotateAPIKeyPayload (api_key +
    one-time plaintext token) + rotateAPIKeyHandler. The handler mints
    the new credential through auth.Generate BEFORE the store call so a
    crypto failure cannot leave the row in a half-rotated state, projects
    only the public Prefix on the response (no secret_hash on the wire),
    and surfaces the plaintext token through auth.Token.Reveal() exactly
    once — every subsequent read returns the projection without the
    token, so a token not captured at rotation time is unrecoverable.
  - routes.go: POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys/{key_id}/rotate
    route entry, RequiresAuth=true, RequiredAction=keys.manage, resolver
    = apiKeyIDResolver. OpenAPI Description spells out the lifecycle
    contract (rotated credential body invalidates the old prefix lookup
    the moment the row is committed, revoked/expired is 409, cross-tenant
    is 403/404, no cross-tenant support exception for CapAdmin).
  - server.go: NewHandler takes apiKeyRotator APIKeyRotator. Threaded
    through newRouteTable to the new route.
- Binary wiring:
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go: existing apiKeyService value satisfies the
    new APIKeyRotator port too, so the binary wiring is a single new
    positional argument (`apiKeyService` reused for revoker AND rotator).

  - There is a pre-existing factory/validator mismatch in the store
    layer: testutil.NewFactory produces ids with a 20-character suffix
    (e.g. `org_12be7c0a4209ea0b0001`), while domain.ParseID requires a
    26-character Crockford-base32 suffix. TestAPIKeyServiceCreateWith
    ServiceAccountAndExpiry already fails against a live Postgres for
    this reason (Create's validator calls domain.ParseID for org_id and
    created_by). All factory-id integration tests that bypass Create
    (using seedAPIKeyForUpdate's direct Insert) are unaffected. This is
    NOT introduced by BE-0091 — my Rotate tests deliberately seed the
    expired key via direct UPDATE on api_keys to be decoupled from the
    Create validator and demonstrate the Rotate path's own lifecycle
    precondition. Fixing the factory/validator mismatch is its own
    story.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The single-value APIKeyService satisfies four ports now
    (Creator/Updater/Revoker/Rotator). Adding a fifth verb is just a
    new method on APIKeyService, a new interface in api_keys.go, two
    new positional args (NewHandler + newRouteTable), one new route
    entry, and a single new positional arg in cmd/yalla-api/main.go
    that reuses the same `apiKeyService` value. Don't multiply
    services — the orchestrator is the unit of work boundary, not the
    handler-facing port.
  - "Rotate" is credential-body in place: identity, ownership, scopes,
    and lifecycle stamps are immutable across the call. The plaintext
    token is shown exactly once (mirrors Create), and the old prefix
    is destroyed for authentication purposes the moment the row
    commits — proved end to end via FindByPrefix(old) → NotFound and
    FindByPrefix(new) → the same key id. This is the property the
    BE-0091 acceptance contract is built on; if a future change adds
    soft-rotate semantics (keep both prefixes for a grace period),
    that property would have to be relaxed deliberately.
  - When seeding an expired key for integration tests, stamp the row's
    expires_at via a direct `UPDATE api_keys` SQL rather than going
    through APIKeyService.Create with ExpiresAt set. Create validates
    its input ids through domain.ParseID, which currently disagrees
    with testutil.NewFactory's id shape (see remaining risks above);
    seedAPIKeyForUpdate uses APIKeyRepository.Insert directly and
    bypasses that validator, so an in-place UPDATE on the seeded row
    is the closest equivalent for adding lifecycle stamps without
    couplng the test to a separate latent bug.
  - When `NewHandler` and `newRouteTable` grow a port parameter, the
    grep target is wider than just `*_test.go`: a few files use the
    full-signature `NewHandler(...)` directly (organizations_create_test,
    organizations_test, me_test) and others use the multi-line form
    (api_keys_*_test, members_*_test, organizations_*_test) — and the
    *production* `newRouteTable` call sites (routes_test.go,
    server_test.go) need updating too. The four routes_test/server_test
    call sites use named arg-count placeholders like `nil, nil, nil, nil,
    nil, nil, nil, nil, nil, nil, nil, nil, nil, nil, nil` so they don't
    match the "fakeAPIKeyRevoker{}, nil)" pattern — a follow-up grep
    pass for "newRouteTable\\(" catches them.

- Acceptance audit (file: internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_rotate_policy_test.go):
  - TestRotateAPIKeyPolicyMatrixRoles drives every built-in role (owner,
    admin, developer, viewer, ci, support) through the production
    NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine() path. Owner/Admin allow via
    ReasonAllowedByRole; Developer/Viewer/CI/Support deny with

    boundary: a non-support owner of org_attacker rotating a key in
    org_victim is a deterministic 403 (ReasonDeniedCrossTenant); the
    rotator is never reached and the body never echoes the victim org or
    its seeded key data. Support is also pinned — both the engine verdict
    and the handler outcome — to confirm CapAdmin is excluded from the
    support cross-tenant exception (cross-tenant denial), and support in
    its OWN org is denied via ReasonDeniedNoCapability so a future catalog
    change cannot silently grant support key-rotation authority.
  - TestRotateAPIKeyPolicyGrantContainment proves grant containment
    (sibling project, production environment, parent-level secrets,
    sibling service) via project/env/service-scoped Admin grants — none
    of those scoped grants covers the api-key resource scope, so each is
    denied keys.manage with ReasonDeniedOutOfScope. The project-scoped
    grantee is then tied back to the wire: 403 with the stable
    out-of-scope reason, rotator never invoked, denied body never echoes
    the seeded key. The complementary positive lock — an
    organization-level Admin grant allows via ReasonAllowedByGrant while
    an organization-level Viewer grant denies — pins the CapAdmin
    requirement against the grant path. A final cross-tenant {org_id}
    case on the same scoped key confirms the cross-tenant guard fires
    over the out-of-scope guard.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0094
- What was implemented: GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/limits, the quota
  surface's first customer-facing read endpoint. Returns the effective quota
  limits configured for the organization named by the {org_id} path
  parameter, in deterministic resource order. Each entry on the wire carries
  resource, limit_value, enforcement_mode, and source ('organization' for an
  override or 'plan_default' for an inherited plan default). Resources with
  no policy at either scope are unconstrained and omitted from the list.
  - internal/controlplane/store/quota.go: added QuotaScope (string values
    match quota_policies.scope_kind verbatim — QuotaScopePlanDefault,
    QuotaScopeOrganization), EffectiveQuotaLimit (Resource, LimitValue,
    EnforcementMode, Scope), and QuotaRepository.ListEffectiveLimits — a
    single DISTINCT ON (resource) query that returns the resolved limit per
    resource preferring the organization override over the plan default.
    Tenant scoped: only organization-row overrides for organizationID and
    plan-row defaults for the named plan are considered.
  - internal/controlplane/store/limits.go: new file with DefaultPlan,
    PlanLookup function type (same signature as quota.PlanResolver.Plan so
    placeholders are interchangeable without a cross-package dep), and
    LimitsReader — the store-backed adapter that composes QuotaRepository
    through Store.Read. NewLimitsReader rejects a nil store; a nil
    PlanLookup or an empty string from a configured lookup falls back to
    DefaultPlan so a misconfigured resolver cannot erase the floor every
    tenant is meant to inherit. ListEffectiveLimits resolves the plan and
    the limits inside one read-only transaction.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/limits.go: new file with errNoLimitsReader,
    LimitsReader port, listLimitsPayload + limitResource wire types,

    contract, and the CapRead support-cross-tenant exception that policy
    BE-0096 will pin down).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: threaded limits LimitsReader
    through NewHandler's signature between memberRemover and apiKeys, and
    updated the package doc comment.
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go: wired store.NewLimitsReader(dataStore, nil) at
    startup and passed the result to httpapi.NewHandler.
  - internal/controlplane/store/limits_test.go: new integration tests

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - quota_policies.scope_kind takes literal string values 'plan_default'
    and 'organization' — I mirrored those values verbatim into the
    QuotaScope type and the wire field 'source', so projecting database
    -> wire is a single string cast. Using the same literal across layers
    avoids a translation table and a divergence opportunity.
  - DISTINCT ON (resource) ... ORDER BY resource, (scope_kind = 'organization') DESC
    is the cleanest one-query resolver for "org override beats plan
    default, one row per resource, in deterministic resource order". The
    same shape generalises to any (scope, override) precedence resolution
    where the two scopes share a discriminator column.
  - The reader-port plumbing carries verbatim from BE-0061 (members.list):
    declare a narrow interface in httpapi (LimitsReader), build a
    *store.LimitsReader adapter that composes the repository through
    Store.Read (never fresh SQL), thread the port through
    NewHandler -> newRouteTable -> the handler closure. A new port adds ~13
    NewHandler call-site edits across the httpapi test wrappers (each
    test file that builds a handler), main.go, and server.go's package
    doc. perl -i -pe substitution over the canonical
    "fakeMembershipRemover{}, fakeAPIKeyReader{}" landmark is the
    least-error-prone way to apply a uniform insertion across all 17
    sites.
  - When the next port lands, consider whether newTestHandler in
    server_test.go could absorb its fake — the public-surface tests
    (~13 sites) all rely on the canned-fake pattern but don't need
    different fakes per file.
  - Plans table is still placeholder. The PlanLookup function type
    (signature mirroring quota.PlanResolver.Plan) lets a real plans
    table land later without touching the limits API contract or the
    LimitsReader adapter — the binary just wires a different lookup at
    construction time. Same idea applies to any "this column has no
    foreign key yet" placeholder.
  - apierr.AuthRequired does not exist; the auth-required factory is
    apierr.Unauthenticated and the resulting error code is "E_AUTH" (not
    "E_AUTH_REQUIRED"). The full code catalogue is in
    internal/errors/errors.go and the constructors are in
    internal/controlplane/apierr/apierr.go.
  - go test integration suites for store package are easy to verify
    locally: docker compose up -d postgres and
    export YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://yalla:yalla@127.0.0.1:5432/yalla
    runs the migrated-DB skip gate. The pre-existing TestAPIKeyService*
    failure is reproducible on the baseline commit (git stash, run, pop)
    — that is the right way to disambiguate "introduced by my story" from
    "long-standing test infra mismatch".

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0096
- Added policy matrix coverage for GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/limits.
  Where limits_test.go (BE-0094 / BE-0095) pins the wire contract, this
  file pins the authorization contract: action limits.read cannot be
  bypassed by — or leak data because of — the principal's role, revoked
  credentials, home organization, or scoped grants.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/limits_policy_test.go (new):
    - TestListLimitsPolicyMatrixRoles drives the six built-in roles
      (owner/admin/developer/viewer/ci/support) through the real
      NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine() against an {org_id} naming the
      principal's own home organization. Since ActionLimitsRead is
      CapRead (catalog.go:81), every role allows via ReasonAllowedByRole;
      the assertions that matter are the engine reason and that the
      fakeLimitsReader is reached with the path's {org_id}.
    - TestListLimitsPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: a disabled principal
      whose underlying role would otherwise allow (Owner) is denied with
      ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled; the reader is never reached and the
      body never echoes the principal id, organization id, or any
      seeded limit field ("projects", "hard").
    - TestListLimitsPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal pins the load-
      bearing distinction from the keys.read sibling story (BE-0078):
      keys.read is CapAdmin and OUTSIDE the engine's support cross-
      tenant exception, but limits.read is CapRead and INSIDE it (engine
      clause: `roleCaps.has(CapSupport) && (required == CapRead ||
      required == CapSupport)`). A non-support owner cross-tenant is
      denied (ReasonDeniedCrossTenant) with no reader reach and no
      foreign-id/limit leakage; a Support principal cross-tenant is
      ALLOWED (ReasonAllowedBySupport) and the handler returns 200 with
      the limits of the {org_id} the path named, the reader reached with
      that org id. Both the engine verdict and the wire verdict are
      pinned for both principals.
    - TestListLimitsPolicyGrantContainment pins the three containment
      properties the acceptance criteria name (sibling project,
      production environment, parent-level secrets) against the engine
      via project/env/service Admin grants, then ties them back to the
      wire: a project-scoped Admin grantee reading limits of its OWN
      organization is denied with ReasonDeniedOutOfScope (covers() is
      one-way — a more-specific scope cannot reach a broader resource),
      the reader is never reached, and the body never echoes the seeded
      limit data. An organization-scoped VIEWER grant DOES allow the
      endpoint (CapRead is enough; ReasonAllowedByGrant) and the same
      key is end-to-end allowed at the wire. The project-scoped grantee
      against a foreign {org_id} is still denied (ReasonDeniedCrossTenant
      fires first).
  - ralph/prd.json: BE-0096 passes=true.
- Verification run:
  - gofmt -w . (clean)
  - go mod tidy (no diff)
  - go vet ./... (clean)
  - go test ./... (all packages green; httpapi 0.292s for the new tests)
  - go test -race ./... (httpapi 1.860s, full suite green)
- Results: BE-0096 passes. All four tests pass under race; no other
  package is touched and no existing test changed.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: none for this story. BE-0097
  (PATCH /v1/organizations/{org_id}/limits) and onward remain pending.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Reusing the limits_test.go scaffolding (fakeLimitsReader,
    listLimitsHandlerFor, limitsActorIdentity, decodeLimitsList,
    decodeErrorEnvelope) plus orgPrincipal and decodeError from the
    wider httpapi test fixtures kept this story to a single new file
    with one small request helper (getLimits) — no new fakes, no NewHandler
    rewiring. The established "policy matrix story adds no scaffolding"
    pattern held: every dependency it needed already existed because the
    BE-0094 implementation story landed the contract suite that built
    them.
  - The CapRead-vs-CapAdmin split is the load-bearing structural
    difference between resolver-based read endpoints, and the policy
    matrix story is the ONLY place it gets directly pinned. keys.read
    (BE-0078, CapAdmin) had to prove Support cross-tenant DENY because
    CapAdmin is outside the engine's support exception; limits.read
    (BE-0096, CapRead) has to prove Support cross-tenant ALLOW because
    CapRead is inside it. The engine clause
    `roleCaps.has(CapSupport) && (required == CapRead || required ==
    CapSupport)` is the single line of policy code that splits the two
    matrices. Future resolver-based read endpoints: copy the limits
    template if the action is CapRead; copy the keys template if it is
    CapAdmin.
  - For grant containment on a CapRead endpoint, an organization-scoped
    VIEWER grant is enough to allow the endpoint via
    ReasonAllowedByGrant — viewer holds CapRead. The CapAdmin keys.read
    matrix had to use an organization-scoped ADMIN grant for the
    positive case (and intentionally proved Viewer NOT enough). Pick the
    weakest grant role that satisfies the required capability so the
    test pins the capability requirement, not an over-privileged grant.
  - When asserting "denied body does not leak limit data", grep for
    distinctive field VALUES ("projects", "\"hard\"", numeric literals
    like ":42"), not just the resource enum strings — the engine reason
    contains identifiers like "scoped" or "role", so checking only for
    the word "limits" would have false positives.

    organizationIDResolver-emitted org-root scope:
    - TestUpdateLimitsPolicyMatrixRoles: all six built-in roles, both at
      the engine (Decide(limits.write, org-root) verdict + reason) and
      the wire (200/403 with the stable reason + redaction proofs).
      Owner/Admin allow via ReasonAllowedByRole; Developer/Viewer/CI/
      Support deny via ReasonDeniedNoCapability. The allow path also
      pins the updater receiving the {org_id}, the decoded item, and
      the principal's actor identifiers.
    - TestUpdateLimitsPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: revoked / expired
      credentials (Disabled principal) deny with

      would have allowed; updater never reached; body never echoes the

      owner denied via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant at engine AND wire;
      cross-tenant support ALSO denied via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant
      (CapAdmin is excluded from the engine's support cross-tenant
      exception — the load-bearing distinction from BE-0096's
      limits.read matrix, where support IS allowed cross-tenant);
      bonus: support is denied in its OWN home org too via
      ReasonDeniedNoCapability (it lacks CapAdmin entirely).
    - TestUpdateLimitsPolicyGrantContainment: project/env/service-scoped
      Admin grants pinned against project/env/service update actions
      (sibling project, production env, parent-level secrets — the

      ReasonAllowedByGrant (200 with the seeded post-write limits,
      updater reached with the {org_id} and actor identifiers); an
      org-level Viewer grant denied at the engine (limits.write
      requires CapAdmin, not CapRead, so an org-root Viewer is
      structurally not enough); a project-scoped grantee against a
      foreign {org_id} still denied via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant (the

  - The file adds no scaffolding: it reuses updateLimitsHandlerFor,

    orgPrincipal, and decodeError from limits_test.go /
    limits_patch_test.go / organizations_test.go. The single tiny

- Files changed: internal/controlplane/httpapi/limits_patch_policy_test.go
  (new); ralph/prd.json (BE-0099 passes -> true); ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -l . (clean); go mod tidy (no diff); go vet
  ./... (clean); go test ./... (all packages pass); go test -race ./...
  (all packages pass); go test -race -count=1 -run TestUpdateLimitsPolicy
