The audit Metadata records ONLY closed-taxonomy enums (status_before/status_after) and structural identifiers (service_id) — caller-controlled free text (display_name, schedule) is NOT recorded because the action does not mutate it and including it would expose a future redaction footgun. The httpapi handler is the canonical verb-handler shape — empty body, principal home org + path {service_id} + path {child_id} forwarded to the runner, RequireAuth gates on the action's catalog mapping (backup.run -> CapDeploy), nil-runner guard runs after RequireAuth admits, 202 Accepted on success. Route entry's resolver is the bare-id resolver of the PARENT (serviceIDResolver), not the child — the resource scope pins to the parent's path identifier so scoped grants on parent siblings still get the engine's one-way covers() rule applied. The catalog mapping (CapDeploy vs CapWrite vs CapRead) is THE single load-bearing distinction in the policy matrix: CapDeploy widens the allow set to include CI (which holds CapRead+CapDeploy), so backup.run is allowed for CI keys even though backup.create (CapWrite) is denied — the policy matrix test pins this distinction at every grant scope.
  - **Bulk test-fixture sweep for a new positional port at the route-table call seam:** A new port inserted into newRouteTable / NewHandler at slot N expands ~70 existing test files that pass literal fakes positionally. The mechanical sweep is `perl -i -pe 's/fakePREVIOUS\{\},/fakePREVIOUS{}, fakeNEW{},/g' $(grep -rl 'fakePREVIOUS{}' internal/controlplane/httpapi/)` keyed on the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING port's bare struct literal. For BE-0253 this updated 71 files cleanly. The two ALWAYS-MANUAL call sites to follow up after the bulk pass are: (a) the resource's OWN create-test helper that uses a local variable `creator` (or analogous local) for the previous slot — `..., creator, fakeServiceVariableReader{}, ...` must become `..., creator, fakeServiceBackupRunner{}, fakeServiceVariableReader{}, ...`; (b) any wiring test that explicitly passes `nil` for the previous slot to reach the typed-internal guard (e.g. TestCreateServiceBackupNilCreator) — `..., fakeServiceBackupReader{}, nil, fakeServiceVariableReader{}` must become `..., fakeServiceBackupReader{}, nil, fakeServiceBackupRunner{}, fakeServiceVariableReader{}`. Then `go build ./...` confirms arity end-to-end; the new fake type itself is declared once in the new test file (here: fakeServiceBackupRunner in service_backups_run_test.go) and is visible to every test file in the same package.
  - **Why CapDeploy widens the allow set vs CapWrite:** builtinRoleCaps[RoleCI] = CapSelf+CapRead+CapDeploy and builtinRoleCaps[RoleSupport] = CapSelf+CapRead+CapSupport. backup.run -> CapDeploy (catalog.go) admits Owner/Admin/Developer/CI and denies Viewer/Support; backup.create -> CapWrite admits Owner/Admin/Developer and denies CI/Viewer/Support. The "automation keys can trigger backups but cannot author them" distinction is a single catalog-line constant — keep it pinned in the policy matrix test under a comment that names the load-bearing CI allow/deny so a future catalog change that downgrades backup.run to CapWrite (which would silently lock out every CI deployment script) fails here before it could regress a real customer.
  - **POST /restart pattern doesn't change desired state; POST /run does (flip to pending):** services_restart is a fire-and-forget signal whose worker enqueue happens via the jobs table — no row update. backup.run cannot use that shape yet because backups have no jobs queue (BE-0497 is the worker story). Instead, the customer-facing "run now" semantic is encoded by flipping the row's status column from {succeeded, failed, pending, disabled-but-enabled=true} -> 'pending' so the worker's regular scheduling pass picks it up on its next tick. The disabled-policy 409 is essential — without it a customer who PATCH-disabled a row could trigger a "run now" that immediately raced the worker's "ignore disabled" check; rejecting at the boundary surfaces the customer error deterministically rather than as a silent no-op the customer would only notice from absent worker logs.

The matching verification test would be internal/controlplane/build/worker_dockerfile_test.go, structurally parallel to api_dockerfile_test.go but with EXPOSE 8080 replaced by an absent-EXPOSE check and the binary path swapped.
  - BE-0411 (docker-compose local stack) extends the existing docker-compose.yml (already has postgres) with the API service (built from the new Dockerfile) and the worker service. The verification surface is YAML-shaped — a parallel test that loads the compose file via gopkg.in/yaml.v3 and asserts service names, image references, port mappings, and env-var passthroughs.
  - BE-0412 (k8s manifests / Helm chart) and BE-0413 (systemd) sit further along the same axis. Each one gets its own *_test.go in this package.
  - The Dockerfile pins GO_VERSION=1.23 — this needs to be bumped in lockstep with go.mod when the toolchain version moves. A future test could read both go.mod's `go` directive and the Dockerfile's GO_VERSION ARG and assert they match within minor-version compatibility; today the assertion is "GO_VERSION default exists and is not :latest", which catches the unpinned-tag regression but not a drift between Dockerfile and go.mod.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The repo had no operations artefact directory before this story — `internal/controlplane/build/` is now the canonical verification leaf for any future operations artefact (worker Dockerfile, docker-compose stack, k8s manifests, systemd units, deploy scripts). The convention is: artefact lives at the repo root or under a top-level operations directory; its verification test lives in this package with one *_test.go per artefact. Tests use the `_test` external package so the verification surface has no production-code dependency.
  - `repoRoot(t)` (walks up from os.Getwd() until it finds go.mod) is the stable way to locate repo-root artefacts from a test that lives several packages deep. Hard-coded `../../Dockerfile` would break if the test ever moved; the go.mod walk is portable to any future verification test.
  - The verification surface for operations artefacts is necessarily structural (regex over the Dockerfile text, set membership over .dockerignore lines, YAML parse + key lookup for compose / k8s). A real `docker build` would catch syntax errors but not the audit properties this test pins — non-root user, pinned tags, no baked secrets — which is what operations review actually cares about.
  - The forbidden-secret list in TestAPIDockerfileIsProductionGrade should track config.Config's secret fields (DatabaseURL, SigningKeys, DokployToken) and the most common database-side secret (POSTGRES_PASSWORD). When future config stories add new secret fields (Stripe keys, Slack webhook URLs, etc.), extend the forbidden list in lockstep so a developer who accidentally types `ENV YALLA_STRIPE_KEY=...` into a Dockerfile fails this test in CI.
  - Distroless static-debian12:nonroot is the canonical runtime for a CGO_ENABLED=0 Go binary in this repo — no shell, no package manager, UID/GID 65532. HEALTHCHECK is intentionally omitted because the image has no curl/wget/sh; orchestrators (Kubernetes, Nomad, ECS, Docker Compose's healthcheck stanza) probe /healthz and /readyz over HTTP directly. This decision is documented in the Dockerfile header comment so a future ops engineer doesn't add a HEALTHCHECK that depends on a non-existent shell.
  - The BuildKit `--mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod` and `--mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build` lines speed up rebuilds dramatically but require BuildKit (`DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1` or modern docker engines that default to it). The `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7` directive at the top of the file is what unlocks `--mount=type=cache`. Without that syntax line the build silently falls back to legacy syntax and the cache mounts become no-ops.

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - The store-layer integration test for ServiceBackupService.Delete (verifying the tenant-scoped DELETE predicate, the If-Match precondition + classifyServiceBackupConcurrencyMiss disambiguation, and the audit metadata composition end-to-end against real Postgres) is not added in this iteration — a future Postgres-integration story should clone the BE-0252 pattern at store/service_backup_test.go. The BE-0252 progress note documents the pre-existing skip behavior with no DB.
  - Deleting a backup whose status is currently 'running' is intentionally NOT rejected at the application layer here (the row is removed outright on the destructive verb, mirroring service_domains DELETE which has no analogous in-flight precondition). The worker side that may already be processing the row will see the row vanish on its next poll and abort its transition — but if the customer needs a soft "stop running" toggle, that is the existing PATCH ... enabled=false path, not this destructive endpoint. If a worker-aware "delete only when not running" precondition becomes desired, it would land as a separate story.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **DELETE-on-child-resource vertical with optional If-Match (BE-0259+0260+0261, DELETE /v1/services/{service_id}/backups/{backup_id}, exact structural twin of BE-0244+0245+0246 for service_domains DELETE):** the repo's canonical shape for a hard-DELETE of a bare-{id}-resolver child resource has stabilised — store-side `<Resource>Repository.DeleteByID(ctx, tx, parents..., childID, ifMatchVersion *int64) (<Resource>, error)` returning the deleted snapshot, reusing the SAME `classify<Resource>ConcurrencyMiss` helper that the PATCH path declared (so the staleness disambiguation is a single chokepoint per resource), no soft-delete column (a backup policy is desired-state configuration, never a continuing audit-trail tie that must outlive the row — the audit row itself outlives it); store-side `<Resource>Service.Delete(ctx, Delete<Resource>Input)` validates path identifiers BEFORE opening Tx, then Write -> DeleteByID -> audit append with the closed-set / structural-identifier metadata only (never caller-controlled free text); httpapi-side narrow Deleter port, errNo<Resource>Deleter sentinel, payload type that re-uses the SAME wire shape every other endpoint for that resource returns (no DELETE-specific projection), handler order: RequireAuth -> nil-principal Internal -> nil-deleter Internal -> parseIfMatchVersion -> deleter.Delete -> 200 yalla.output.v1; route registration with serviceIDResolver, RequiredAction=<action>.delete, two PathParams, multi-paragraph Description that explicitly states the no-soft-delete invariant + the If-Match contract + the cross-tenant 404 + the CapWrite Support suppression. **The reason this is one vertical and not three:** BE-0261 (priority=1, the policy-matrix story) is logically blocked on BE-0259 (priority=2, the endpoint) — the policy tests have no fakeServiceBackupDeleter wiring to call into until the deleter port exists — so the picker rule "land the highest-priority STORY GROUP that is doable, not the highest-priority story considered in isolation" applies, and the trio ships in one commit per the bundling convention.
  - **Audit metadata for delete: closed-set + structural identifiers only, NEVER caller-controlled free text.** For service_backups DELETE the metadata records service_id (structural), status (closed enum), enabled (bool), retention_count (schema-bounded int), and version (int — useful for forensics and idempotency analysis). It deliberately omits display_name and schedule because both are caller-controlled free text — the application layer cannot prove redaction-safe by construction, and the audit row's value should not depend on values the customer chose. This matches the PATCH metadata convention from BE-0256 (which records updated_fields stable wire names, never the submitted values) and is the same invariant service_domains DELETE applies (records hostname, path, certificate_type — all routing metadata + closed enums, never caller-typed free text the application cannot prove safe). When the BE-0497+ worker stories land that may emit a status_after='deleted' transition event, they should follow the same rule.
  - **The "no destructive op on deny" invariant is the load-bearing assertion that distinguishes DELETE policy tests from CREATE/UPDATE/RUN policy tests.** For backup.delete the policy suite asserts callCount == 0 on every deny path — the role-deny path, the disabled-principal path, the project/env/service-scoped grant path. A scoped principal denied on the wire MUST NOT have committed a destructive row removal in the background. This is structurally MORE load-bearing for DELETE than for any other mutation because the row's removal is irreversible at the application layer (the audit trail outlives it, but the desired-state row does not — there is no soft-delete column to clear, no version flip to undo). The body-leak guard (deleteServiceBackupDenyBodyLeak) needles for the canonical backup_id / display_name / schedule / project / environment so an accidental on-deny render of the "deleted" snapshot fails the test even before the deleter-not-reached assertion fires. The malformed-If-Match contract test ALSO asserts the no-run invariant: a malformed precondition that silently degraded into "no precondition" would be a particularly load-bearing footgun for a destructive op, so the assertion is doubly structural.
  - **CI cap-class distinction in the policy matrix for CapWrite verbs:** the BE-0261 matrix pins CI as DENIED on backup.delete via ReasonDeniedNoCapability — CI is CapSelf+CapRead+CapDeploy, no CapWrite. This is the same split BE-0246 (domain.delete), BE-0258 (backup.update), and BE-0243 (domain.update) make: automation keys CAN trigger deployments (CapDeploy) but CANNOT mutate or destroy desired-state rows (CapWrite). The matrix asserts this distinction at BOTH the engine level (e.Decide returns deny via ReasonDeniedNoCapability) AND the wire level (the HTTP response is 403 E_FORBIDDEN carrying the stable reason in error.message). When the worker-tier stories land that introduce backup.run-related transitions, they will follow the deploy-tier matrix (BE-0255 RUN matrix) where CI IS allowed because the action class flips from CapWrite to CapDeploy.
- Repository for an **APPEND-ONLY EVENT LOG table whose row body has NO updated_at column, NO version column, and is guarded by a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that rejects every UPDATE at the SQL level, AND whose tenant scope is enforced through a composite FK back to a DEEPER parent (deployments, not directly organizations)** (BE-0459 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/deployment_event.go + 0035_deployment_events migration + deployment_event_repository_invariants_test.go). Structurally distinct from BE-0455 (quota_reservations — append-only-from-the-customer-perspective but still has updated_at + settled_at lifecycle UPDATE surface from the worker; tenant-scoped directly to organizations) and from AuditRepository (also append-only with BEFORE UPDATE trigger but tenant-scoped DIRECTLY to organizations with NO composite FK to a deeper parent) in three load-bearing ways: (a) the table has only TWO timestamp columns (occurred_at + created_at), both stamped by now() at INSERT; occurred_at is caller-overridable to support a worker reconciling after a restart that persists the original wallclock the event was observed at, while created_at is always database-stamped. The repository's Append uses `COALESCE($N, now())` so a zero time.Time defaults to now() but a non-zero caller-supplied time round-trips verbatim. (b) The composite FK leg (organization_id, deployment_id) references deployments(organization_id, id), not organizations(id) directly — this means a cross-tenant Append surfaces as apierr.Conflict via mapWriteError (FK violation) BEFORE the row gets near the organizations table, and ON DELETE CASCADE chains through deployments rather than directly from organizations. The cascade-delete test must therefore DELETE the parent deployment (not the parent organization) to exercise the chain, and the FK rejection test seeds two orgs but only ONE deployment so the cross-tenant probe references alpha's deployment id with bravo's organization_id — the (bravo.ID, alphaDep.ID) tuple matches no row in deployments and the FK trips. (c) The repository surface is intentionally narrower than QuotaRepository's: Append + GetByID + ListByDeployment, no Update, no Cancel, no aggregation method. GetByID exists despite the table being internal-accounting (audit_events has no GetByID for the same reason) because the timeline endpoint's future read paths benefit from a tenant-scoped point lookup and the cost is a single short method. ListByDeployment orders occurred_at ASC + id ASC (chronological — the timeline endpoint renders the deployment unfolding forward in time, opposite to deployments' reverse-chronological list path).

The 20-test shape pins: Append-mints-id-and-row-shape (depev_ prefix), Append-blank-fields-default (Message='' RequestID='' CorrelationID='' Metadata=nil), Append-respects-caller-supplied-id, Append-respects-caller-supplied-occurred-at (worker-reconciliation contract), Append-unknown-event-type-rejected (CHECK via mapWriteError -> Conflict), Append-blank-event-type-rejected (apierr.Internal at application boundary, NOT a database-CHECK pass-through — the empty string is a programming error caught before SQL, since a blank value would also pass the CHECK if the CHECK accepted '' which it does not but the application boundary catches it first), Append-unknown-deployment-rejected (composite FK -> Conflict), Append-cross-tenant-deployment-rejected (composite FK -> Conflict + countDeploymentEventRowsForDeployment proves no row persisted), Append-duplicate-id-Conflict (PRIMARY KEY collision via mapWriteError), Append-nil-Tx-Internal, Append-rolls-back-on-tx-rollback, Append-peer-row-byte-identity (NO updated_at column to drift, so the test asserts byte-identity on id+EventType+Message+OccurredAt+CreatedAt — the absence of bump_version + set_updated_at triggers MEANS the peer can never drift on a successful sibling Append), Update-rejected-by-trigger (raw `db.Exec UPDATE` bypasses the repository surface entirely so the trigger is the only thing that can stop the write), cascade-delete-on-deployment (raw `DELETE FROM deployments WHERE id = $1` cascades through the composite FK ON DELETE CASCADE), GetByID-returns-persisted-row / unknown-NotFound / cross-tenant-NotFound-with-no-leak-on-foreign-deployment-id, ListByDeployment-chronological-order (seed three rows OUT OF chronological order so the ASC ordering must reorder them on read), ListByDeployment-unknown-deployment-empty (returns empty slice not error — distinguishes "no events" from "no parent" is the caller's responsibility, mirrors deployment ListByService), ListByDeployment-cross-tenant-empty. The peer-row test gets simpler than quota_reservations or deployments because there is NO updated_at column to drift and NO version column to bump — append-only is structural in the column list, not just the trigger. Forward-applicable to every future append-only event-log surface (e.g. provisioning_job_events when that lands).

GOTCHA on apierr.Internal for blank-event-type at the application boundary (NOT mapWriteError -> Conflict): a blank EventType `""` would pass the `event_type IN (...)` CHECK only if `''` were in the closed set, which it is not — but the test must still encode that the application boundary catches it FIRST and surfaces yerr.CodeInternal, not the database CHECK surfacing yerr.CodeConflict. The repository explicitly does `if e.EventType == "" { return apierr.Internal(...) }` before any SQL — same reason AuditRepository.Append explicitly checks `if !e.Decision.Valid()` rather than letting the database CHECK reject it. The constraint surface and the application-boundary surface have DIFFERENT typed errors, and the test must pin both.

GOTCHA on the apierr import being unused in the test file: yerr.From().Code is how the test reaches typed codes; the test never directly constructs an apierr. Don't add a placeholder `var _ = apierr.Internal` to keep the import — just omit the apierr import entirely. The auto-import-cleanup pass (when goimports runs) catches this anyway, but writing the file correctly the first time avoids a wasted edit cycle.

GOTCHA on the linter reformatting: when the editor's gofmt-on-save normalises tabs/indentation in heredoc-style multi-line SQL strings within test helpers (loadDeploymentEventRowByID's QueryRow), the linter may reflow whitespace inside the raw SQL literal — the SQL is still valid because PostgreSQL ignores whitespace, but a future diff against the unformatted original would be noisy. Accept the linter's pass and never revert it.

This is the load-bearing structural pin that lets a single resource builder fixture both authorize "list previews under THIS project" (CapRead) and "create a preview under THIS project" (CapDeploy) — and lets future endpoint regressions that resolved into a deeper scope (e.g., {home_org, path_project_id, preview_id} for the list endpoint, which would be wrong because the path has no preview id) fail one of the grant-containment cases.
  - The foreign-home-org grant filter is identical across CapRead and CapDeploy actions: a scoped grant minted for orgA, carried by a principal whose home org is orgB, against a resource in orgB → the cross-tenant guard does NOT fire (resource org == home org), then the engine's `g.Scope.OrganizationID != principal.OrganizationID` filter skips the grant entirely, and the verdict is ReasonDeniedNoCapability (not ReasonDeniedOutOfScope, not ReasonDeniedCrossTenant). This is the engine-level twin of the wire-level "stolen scoped key" property: CapRead being inside the support cross-tenant exception does NOT save a stolen key, because the exception is gated on the principal's home-org role (which a stolen scoped key does not carry).

The constants are package-internal, so future engine-level policy files for the same subsystem (preview_delete_policy_test.go for BE-0270 once the wire endpoint lands) should follow the same naming convention: canonicalPreview<Verb>ProjectID / canonicalPreview<Verb>SiblingID. This keeps a future shared-helper refactor (e.g., a generic previewProjectResource(org, projectID) function) from accidentally cross-contaminating fixture state across matrices.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **The "contract test for an existing endpoint" template (BE-0047 pattern, organizations_contract_test.go, structural twin of me_organizations_contract_test.go BE-0044 and me_contract_test.go):** when a contract-test story lands on an endpoint whose base *_test.go file already pins the success/error envelopes, request_id, OpenAPI registration, and the unauth/invalid/disabled/notfound/dependency-failure rejection space, the new *_contract_test.go file is small (~200 LOC) and closes only the three remaining contract criteria the base file cannot reach: (1) "HTTP server writes response data only to http.ResponseWriter" (verified by captureProcessOutput from me_contract_test.go — swaps global os.Stdout/os.Stderr, asserts both stay empty across a served request); (2) "per-request structured log redacts the bearer credential on success AND on auth-failure paths" (verified by injecting a slog.Logger into a caller-supplied *bytes.Buffer via a new <endpoint>HandlerForWithLogger ctor — same NewHandler call but with the second-to-last positional argument set to the caller-supplied logger instead of nil); (3) "error envelope built from a wrapped dependency cause never leaks that cause onto the wire" (verified by apierr.StoreUnavailable wrapping a recognisable string with host:port — asserts 503 + the wrapped string AND the address are both absent from the response body).
  - **captureProcessOutput is the load-bearing helper for the stdout/stderr-isolation row** — defined once in me_contract_test.go at line 56 and reusable from every contract test in the same package because they're all package httpapi. It uses os.Pipe + io.Copy in two goroutines and swaps the package-global os.Stdout/os.Stderr in/out around fn(), then restores them. The test that uses it MUST NOT call t.Parallel() because the swap is global; document this in the test's top comment so a future contributor doesn't add t.Parallel() and turn it into a flake.
  - **The authorization-failure-path redaction row uses a poisoned reader, not a happy reader** — the disabled-principal identity must trigger the policy deny BEFORE the reader is consulted; a reader that returns stderrors.New("reader must not be called") proves the deny short-circuits at policy, so any string in logBuf can only come from the request line / principal claims / policy reason / response envelope — never from a reader error message — and a future logging change that DID start invoking the reader on a deny path would fail this test with "reader must not be called" appearing in the log. This is a structural integrity check, not just a redaction check.
  - **The dependency-cause leak test uses a recognisable cause string with a host:port** — "connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432" gives the test TWO independent absence assertions (the verbatim cause string AND the address substring). Either one failing means the apierr layer started passing wrapped cause text onto the wire, which is the regression mode the test pins. The cause string is intentionally NOT a real datastore address — 10.0.0.5 is RFC 1918 space that no production system uses.
  - **organizationsHandlerForWithLogger is a parallel ctor to the existing organizationsHandlerFor** — it adds a *slog.Logger parameter and threads it as the second-to-last positional argument of NewHandler. The existing organizationsHandlerFor still passes nil for that argument; the new ctor lets the contract test inject a logger without disturbing the dozens of existing organizations_*_test.go call sites. The same shape will apply to every future *_contract_test.go in this directory: add an <endpoint>HandlerForWithLogger ctor in the new file, leave the base ctor alone.
  - **A contract-test bundling rule:** the new *_contract_test.go file should never re-test what the base *_test.go file already pins. Doing so creates two sources of truth for the same invariant and a future schema change requires updating both files. The contract-test file is a closure for the three rows the base file can't reach (process-stream isolation, log-credential redaction, envelope-cause redaction) — nothing more. The base file remains the single source of truth for envelope shape, status codes, request_id propagation, OpenAPI registration, and rejection-space coverage.

  - Mutating-endpoint contract test (BE-0050 pattern, internal/controlplane/httpapi/organizations_create_contract_test.go; structural template for BE-0053/0056/0059/0062/0065/0068/0071/0074/0077 and every future mutating-endpoint contract story — PATCH/DELETE/POST). The structural twin of the GET-endpoint contract pattern (BE-0047, organizations_contract_test.go) and the no-input contract pattern (BE-0044, me_organizations_contract_test.go), adapted to a POST request shape. Three tests close the contract checklist beyond what the per-endpoint *_create_test.go (or *_patch_test.go / *_delete_test.go) already pins: `Test<Action><Resource>ServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter` (not parallel — captureProcessOutput swaps global os.Stdout/os.Stderr — and asserts both rec.Code == 2xx-for-the-mutation AND that the payload identifier is carried only by the response body), `Test<Action><Resource>RequestLogRedactsBearerToken` (parallel, table-driven over the success-path-owner-principal AND the disabled-principal-403 authorization-failure path; the auth-failure leg uses a fake port (here fakeOrganizationCreator with stderrors.New("creator must not be called")) so any logged "port error" can't be the leak source), `Test<Action><Resource>ErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause` (parallel; the existing per-endpoint dep-failure test pins the typed status — this test pins the absent-from-wire half: the wrapped driver cause string "connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432" AND the bare datastore address "10.0.0.5" must both be absent from rec.Body.String()). One per-test helper is required: `<action><Resource>HandlerForWithLogger(id, authErr, <port>, logger)` — the structural twin of the GET-version `<resource>HandlerForWithLogger`, identical NewHandler-signature body, only the named-port parameter changes shape and position. The per-endpoint bearer-credential constant is `<action><Resource>ContractSecret = "yk_live_supersecret_<endpoint>_DEADBEEF0123456789"` — distinct per file so a false positive in one test can't quietly satisfy the redaction assertion in another, and recognisable enough that a future regression that does leak shows up in logs immediately.
  - The "authorization-failure path" leg of the bearer-redaction test is what distinguishes a mutating-endpoint contract test from the no-input GET version structurally: the auth-failure path on POST is reached via a disabled-but-otherwise-authorized principal (orgPrincipal(..., policy.RoleOwner); principal.Disabled = true → 403 E_FORBIDDEN through policy.ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled), NOT via a principal-without-the-cap (which the request-body-validation layer would short-circuit first on a real-policy handler). The deny-port assertion (`fakeXCreator{err: stderrors.New("port must not be called")}`) proves the policy short-circuit fires BEFORE the validation+port dispatch path, which is the structural anti-leak the test protects.
  - For mutating endpoints the success status in the no-stdout/stderr test is the endpoint's actual mutation status (201 for POST, 200 for PATCH, 200/204 for DELETE — match the real handler), NOT 200 from the GET template. The dependency-cause-leak test status stays 503 regardless of the success-leg status, because apierr.StoreUnavailable always maps to 503 E_UNAVAILABLE via toAPIError; this is invariant across every mutating endpoint that depends on a store port.

When this iteration's pin is the template, the next iterations should clone job_read_policy_test.go's structure but flip the capability class (job.cancel + job.retry are CapDeploy — viewer + support denied at role matrix, denied at org-grant matrix, denied at cross-tenant; CI is the canary row that flips from deny to allow vs job.read because CI holds CapDeploy).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Engine-only policy pin for an org-level list endpoint (BE-0273 pattern, internal/controlplane/policy/job_read_policy_test.go; structural template for any future P=1 policy story whose wire endpoint is at the bare /v1/<resource> path with no path param — most notably BE-0276/0279/0282 for jobs and BE-0285/0288/0291 for admin/dokploy, though the admin family also depends on the admin-role gating which is its own concern).** The pattern is the structural twin of the project-scoped engine pin (BE-0267 preview_read_policy_test.go) but adapted to the org-level list shape: the canonical resource has Kind=K<Resource> and Scope={OrganizationID:home_org} only (no project/env/service narrowing), and the project/env/service grant-containment cases prove BOTH directions explicitly — (1) deeper grant CANNOT reach the org-level list resource (covers() one-way deny, ReasonDeniedOutOfScope), and (2) deeper grant CAN authorize a deeper resource shape that mimics the future query-filter case (?project_id= / ?environment_id= / ?service_id= filters that BE-0271 will likely add). The project-scoped preview pattern only pins direction (1) because its canonical resource is already at the project level — the org-level list pattern adds direction (2) because it must prove the deeper-filtered case is reachable from the deeper grant.
  - **Resource Kind constants are decorative, not load-bearing in the engine.** The engine.Decide() flow at internal/controlplane/policy/engine.go:88+ does NOT branch on resource.Kind at any point — only Scope.OrganizationID (cross-tenant guard) and Scope.covers() (grant containment) participate in the verdict. Kind is for downstream consumers (audit metadata, error rendering, defense-in-depth invariants in handler tests). This means: (a) Engine-level policy pins for a list endpoint CAN pick any reasonable Kind for the canonical resource shape — Kind=KindJob is the natural choice for job.read but Kind=KindOrganization would yield the same engine verdict. (b) A future endpoint that changes its resolver's Kind choice will NOT break the engine pin — the wire-level policy file would need to update its Kind assertions but the engine verdicts pinned in this file would survive intact. (c) Wire-level policy tests should assert Kind separately (the audit-event resource kind and the policy-resource Kind are both observable wire properties); engine-level tests do not need to.
  - **The "stolen scoped key" property has two engine-level facets that must BOTH be pinned in the engine policy test for read actions on cross-tenant resources.** Facet 1 (the cross-tenant role guard): when home_org == resource_org but the principal's home role is Support, the engine's CapRead+CapSupport exception fires — that's TestJobReadPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal, support row, allow. Facet 2 (the cross-tenant grant guard): when home_org == resource_org but the grant scope is in a different org, the engine's grant-filter clause `g.Scope.OrganizationID != principal.OrganizationID` skips the grant — that's TestJobReadPolicyForeignHomeOrgGrant, deny with ReasonDeniedNoCapability. The two facets are distinct because (1) the cross-tenant role guard is gated on the principal's HOME role (a service account with grants only has no home role and so cannot inherit the Support exception even if the grant role is Support), and (2) the cross-tenant grant guard is independent of the role at all — the grant is filtered out before the role is even consulted. Both must be pinned, because a future engine refactor that consolidated the two guards into a single check could pass facet 1 while breaking facet 2 (or vice versa) and the test would catch it.
  - **The picker rule for engine-only pins, expanded: when the wire endpoint does not exist AND the AC are all engine properties, prefer the engine-only pin over bundling the endpoint+contract+policy into a single iteration.** This iteration's BE-0273 acceptance criteria are entirely engine properties (the principal-role matrix, the disabled-principal short-circuit, the cross-tenant guard, the three grant-containment cases). The bundling rule (BE-0244+0245+0246 / BE-0256+0257+0258 / BE-0259+0260+0261) applies when the P=1 policy story's coverage REQUIRES a wire endpoint to exist (so wire-level test assertions about resolver scope construction can be made). When the AC are pure engine properties, the engine pin is sufficient AND the bundling cost (a 5+ layer greenfield drop: store port + service + handler + route + contract + policy-wire + policy-engine) is unjustified for a single P=1 story. The trade-off: the wire-level twin of this file (httpapi/jobs_list_policy_test.go) MUST be added when BE-0271+0272 land, otherwise the resolver-scope-construction and 404-vs-403-ordering properties remain unpinned at the wire level. The engine pin alone is sufficient for BE-0273 because the AC do not reference resolver scope construction or 404-vs-403 ordering; those are properties of the endpoint, not the action.
  - **Project/env/service grant containment for an org-level list must pin allow-equal-scope alongside deny-shallower-resource.** The project-scoped preview pattern in preview_read_policy_test.go pins only the deny direction (deeper grant denied against project-level resource is impossible because the canonical resource IS project-level). For an org-level list, the same containment matrix has TWO sides: (1) deeper grant denied against the shallower org-level resource (ReasonDeniedOutOfScope), and (2) the SAME deeper grant ALLOWED against a deeper resource shape that mimics the future query-filter case (ReasonAllowedByGrant). Pinning only (1) would let a future regression that broke covers() at the deeper-scope-equals-resource-scope case slip through silently — a project-scoped automation key that should be able to list its own project's jobs would be denied with no signal. Pinning (2) alongside (1) is what makes the matrix proof complete.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0053
- Added contract test suite for GET /v1/organizations/{org_id} closing the
  contract-test gaps left by organizations_get_test.go: server writes response

  (organizations_contract_test.go) contract suites, adapted to the GET
  single-organization shape ({org_id} path parameter, 200 success status,
  OrganizationReader port). All three contract suites now share the same
  three-test shape (stdout/stderr capture, bearer-redaction matrix, dependency-
  cause-leak) so future per-endpoint contract suites can clone from any of the
  three with mechanical substitutions.

  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0053 passes=true)

  and BE-0059 (DELETE /v1/organizations/{org_id}) are the next contract suites
  in the same family; they will follow the same three-test shape and can clone
  this file with substitutions for HTTP method, request body shape, success
  status (200 for PATCH, 200 with snapshot or 202 for DELETE), and port
  (OrganizationUpdater / OrganizationDeleter respectively).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The contract-test suite family for a single endpoint is now a stable
    three-test shape: (a) ServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter using
    captureProcessOutput (must be non-parallel because it swaps the global
    os.Stdout/os.Stderr), (b) RequestLogRedactsBearerToken as a table test
    with a success row and an authorization-failure row (the deny row uses a
    fake port that errors if invoked, which proves the deny path short-circuits
    at policy before reaching the persistence layer), (c) ErrorEnvelopeDoesNot
    LeakDependencyCause asserting both the wrapped driver text and the
    datastore host are absent from the response body. The three tests together
    close the "stdout/stderr / log redaction / response redaction" rows of the
    public-API contract checklist that the main endpoint test file
    (organizations_get_test.go, organizations_create_test.go,
    organizations_test.go) does not assert directly.
  - The per-endpoint *HandlerForWithLogger helper takes the same NewHandler
    argument list as the non-logger variant plus a *slog.Logger as the
    second-to-last argument (logger, nil): the final nil is the metrics
    parameter. Keep them in lockstep — the non-logger variant ends with
    (nil, nil) and the logger variant ends with (logger, nil).
  - For an endpoint with no request body and no query parameters (GET single
    resource), the "invalid input" row of the contract checklist is satisfied
    structurally — there is no syntactic request to reject. A malformed or
    unknown {org_id} surfaces as the typed NotFound the reader produces, and
    an id outside the principal's tenant surfaces as a deterministic 403; both
    paths live in the main endpoint test file, not the contract suite. Document
    this in the file header so a future reader does not look for a missing
    "invalid input" test.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0056
- Added contract-test coverage for PATCH /v1/organizations/{org_id} pinning the three "no-leak" invariants that organizations_patch_test.go does not assert directly: (1) the HTTP server writes response data only through http.ResponseWriter — never to process stdout/stderr; (2) the per-request structured log redacts the bearer credential on the success path AND the authorization-failure path; (3) an error envelope built from a wrapped dependency cause never leaks that cause onto the wire.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/organizations_patch_contract_test.go (NEW, 211 lines): structural twin of organizations_get_contract_test.go (BE-0053) and organizations_create_contract_test.go (BE-0050) adapted to the PATCH single-organization request shape. Three tests:
    - TestUpdateOrganizationServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter (uses captureProcessOutput to swap os.Stdout/os.Stderr, asserts both are empty after a 200 PATCH, and asserts the organization payload is carried by the response body via decodeUpdateOrganization).
    - TestUpdateOrganizationRequestLogRedactsBearerToken (table-driven over success path RoleOwner + authorization-failure path Disabled-owner; deny path uses fakeOrganizationUpdater{err: "must not be called"} so a logged updater-error cannot be the leak source; asserts the contract secret never appears in slog output or response body).
    - TestUpdateOrganizationErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause (wraps apierr.StoreUnavailable around a synthetic "connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432" cause and proves the 503 E_UNAVAILABLE envelope contains a stable generic message with neither the wrapped cause string nor the datastore host:port leaking on the wire).
  - New helper updateOrganizationHandlerForWithLogger mirrors the existing getOrganizationHandlerForWithLogger / createOrganizationHandlerForWithLogger pattern: real policy engine, fake Authenticator, caller-supplied updater + slog.Logger, with the OrganizationUpdater port positioned at slot 9 of NewHandler (after creator) and fakeBreakGlassController, logger, nil tail.

  - gofmt -l internal/controlplane/httpapi/organizations_patch_contract_test.go (clean)
  - go vet ./... (clean; no warnings beyond the sandbox TMPDIR cosmetic)
  - go mod tidy (no changes)

  - go test -race ./... -count=1 -> ALL 37 packages PASS
- Results: PRD story BE-0056 set to passes:true. 396 stories remain pending.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: none specific to this story. The structural twin pattern continues to scale linearly across {GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE} of every endpoint family — DELETE /v1/organizations/{org_id} contract (BE-0059) is the next obvious clone of this file (s/Update/Delete/, s/updater/deleter/, s/OrganizationUpdater/OrganizationDeleter/, body argument dropped, 200 status retained per the convention pinned by BE-0244-style delete verbs).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **THE no-leak contract triad is now a canonical pattern for every public endpoint** with a body, path parameter, or both. The triad is: (1) ResponseWriter-only output, (2) bearer-token redaction on success AND authorization-failure paths, (3) wrapped-dependency-cause redaction. Three tests per endpoint, structurally identical to BE-0050 (POST) and BE-0053 (GET). The deny path of test #2 should ALWAYS use a fake port that errors if invoked — this proves the policy short-circuit, so a leaked "port error" log entry cannot be confused with the bearer redaction failure mode.
  - The contract test file is the SHORTER half of the contract surface. The handler-level unit test (organizations_<verb>_test.go) carries the wire-shape + validation + status-code + OpenAPI + actor-forwarding contract; the contract test file (organizations_<verb>_contract_test.go) carries only the three no-leak invariants. Splitting them across two files keeps each <250 lines and lets the picker treat each acceptance-criteria triad as independently verifiable.
  - The bearer secret constant is per-endpoint (createOrganizationContractSecret, getOrganizationContractSecret, updateOrganizationContractSecret, ...) NOT shared package-wide. Sharing would let an accidental t.Log of one endpoint's secret falsely-fail another endpoint's redaction test; the per-endpoint naming makes the contract failure mode obvious in test output.
  - The PATCH contract test body must be a single column patch ({"display_name":"Acme, Inc."}) — NOT a multi-column patch and NOT an empty object. The empty-object body is a valid PATCH (no-op) but it exercises a different validation path; the multi-column body adds noise to the wire payload assertion. One mutable column is the simplest valid PATCH and lets every test in the file share the same body constant.
  - updateOrganizationHandlerForWithLogger is the THIRD instance of the *HandlerForWithLogger pattern in the organizations endpoint family (after organizationsHandlerForWithLogger for GET-list and getOrganizationHandlerForWithLogger for GET-single and createOrganizationHandlerForWithLogger for POST). Each helper hardcodes the FULL NewHandler signature with one port slot replaced by the caller's value and one trailing logger slot — when NewHandler's arity grows by one port (the recurring "port-arity sweep" pattern from BE-0244), every *HandlerForWithLogger helper grows by exactly one fakeX{} literal at the same slot the production-code arity grew. The perl sweep pattern from BE-0244 applies here unchanged.
  - go vet's "ignoring go.mod in system temp root" warning is a sandbox cosmetic: the context-mode ctx_execute sandbox sets TMPDIR=/Users/juribadev/projects/poc/yalla in some configurations, and Go's module loader refuses to load a go.mod that lives under the configured TMPDIR. Running via Bash (which inherits the user shell's TMPDIR=/tmp) sidesteps the issue completely. Future iterations should not chase the warning as a real bug; the workaround is to run go commands via Bash rather than ctx_execute.

    row), jobReadByIDProjectResource (project-owned), jobReadByIDEnvResource
    (env-owned), jobReadByIDServiceResource (service-owned) — model every
    owning-scope shape the bare-id resolver will construct when it looks
    up the row's owner before deciding. The {job_id} segment is treated as
    a routing artefact, not a policy boundary; the load-bearing pin is
    that a service-scoped key cannot escalate to a parent- or sibling-
    owned job row by id, and a staging-env-scoped key cannot fetch a
    production-owned job row by id.
  - ralph/prd.json: BE-0276 passes:true.
  - ralph/progress.txt: this entry.
- Verification: gofmt clean; go vet ./... clean; go test ./... PASS; go
  test -race ./... PASS; focused TestJobReadByIDPolicy* — 7 tests + 28
  subtests PASS.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups: BE-0274 (Implement GET /v1/jobs/{job_id})
  and BE-0275 (contract tests) still pending — the engine pin here is the
  authoritative contract until they land. The wire 404-vs-403 distinction
  (treat foreign-tenant or unknown-row {job_id} as not-found for non-
  Support roles, allow Support to surface it for cross-tenant incident
  response) lives in the contract test for BE-0275 and is intentionally
  not pinned at the engine layer.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Bare-{id} fetch policy matrices for org-rooted resources (job, future
    deployment-by-id at /v1/deployments/{deployment_id}, audit-event-by-
    id, etc.) follow the same containment shape as the list variant they
    sit alongside, with one structural difference: the resource the
    resolver constructs reflects the ROW'S OWNING SCOPE (the depth at
    which the row was created), not the path. So instead of a single
    org-only or project-narrowed Resource builder, the file ships ONE
    builder per layer (org/project/env/svc) and the containment matrix
    pins every (grant-depth × resource-owner-depth) cell rather than just
    the (grant-depth × filter-narrowing) cells the list variant pins.
    The (grant-deeper-than-resource) cells are denies; the
    (grant-equal-or-shallower-than-resource) cells are allows. A
    sibling-row-at-same-depth deny cell (e.g. service-scoped grant on
    svc_a evaluating against an svc_b-owned job row) is the destructive-
    by-omission case that catches a future resolver regression
    collapsing every row's owning scope to the org root.
  - The list-variant policy file (job_read_policy_test.go) and the byid-
    variant policy file (job_read_byid_policy_test.go) deliberately use
    DISTINCT canonical project ids so a future shared helper cannot
    leak fixture state between the two matrices. Same convention as the
    three preview matrices (canonicalPreviewProjectID /
    canonicalPreviewReadProjectID / canonicalPreviewDeleteProjectID).
  - Engine-only pin precedent: when an action's wire endpoint hasn't
    landed yet but a sibling endpoint of the same action HAS landed
    (here: GET /v1/jobs at BE-0271 pending, with BE-0273's engine pin
    covering the list shape), the bare-id-variant engine pin lands
    BEFORE the wire endpoint and is the authoritative contract until
    the route appears. This is the same posture preview_read /
    preview_create / preview_delete adopted before their respective
    wire endpoints landed.

  - Bare-{id} CapDeploy verb engine pins (job.retry BE-0279, future job.cancel BE-0282, future deployment-by-id mutate verbs like deployment.cancel-by-id / deployment.rollback-by-id at /v1/deployments/{deployment_id}/cancel / .../rollback) follow the EXACT SAME containment shape as the bare-{id} CapRead pin (job_read_byid BE-0276) with three mechanical differences. (1) The role matrix flips from six-row allow (CapRead) to four-row allow / two-row deny (CapDeploy) — Viewer and Support deny ReasonDeniedNoCapability in the role matrix and in the org-grant capability matrix. (2) The cross-tenant matrix flips Support from allow (ReasonAllowedBySupport via the CapRead+CapSupport exception) to deny (ReasonDeniedCrossTenant — CapDeploy is OUTSIDE the exception). (3) Project/env/service grant fixtures use RoleAdmin (or RoleCI for the explicit CI pin) instead of RoleViewer because Viewer doesn't hold CapDeploy and would deny on capability rather than scope — RoleAdmin keeps the test ANCHORED on scope containment, with one explicit "viewer on target project denies no capability" subtest in the project-grant suite to anchor on capability instead. Pattern locks in for BE-0282 (job.cancel) which is the IDENTICAL CapDeploy + bare-{id} story for the cancel verb — mechanical clone of this file by s/Retry/Cancel/ + s/retry/cancel/ + s/ActionJobRetry/ActionJobCancel/.
  - The "wire endpoint pending" pattern reaches 5 stories now: preview_create (BE-0264), preview_read (BE-0267), preview_delete (BE-0270), job_read (BE-0273), job_read_byid (BE-0276), job_retry (BE-0279). The next obvious clone in the bare-{id} CapDeploy family is BE-0282 (job.cancel — POST /v1/jobs/{job_id}/cancel) which mechanically clones this file; after that, the BE-0285/0288/0291 admin-dokploy P=1 trio (drift/reconcile/import) which need a DIFFERENT structural template because admin endpoints use ActionAdminRead/ActionAdminReconcile/ActionAdminImport (CapSupport — Support-only, every other role denied) and a Yalla-internal-admin-org scope shape, not a customer-organization scope shape. The admin variant is a fresh structural template, not a clone of any existing file in the package.
  - The "stolen scoped key" pin (TestJobRetryPolicyForeignHomeOrgGrant) for CapDeploy verbs resolves to ReasonDeniedNoCapability (same as the CapRead by-id variant) because the engine's grant filter `g.Scope.OrganizationID != principal.OrganizationID` skips the foreign-org grant entirely BEFORE any capability check. The verdict is identical to BE-0276's foreign-home-org pin — the only thing that changes between CapRead and CapDeploy at this guard is the docstring framing (mutating-side-effect-at-Dokploy vs. cross-tenant-read-of-provisioning-history). The mechanical lesson: the foreign-home-org grant test is verbatim-clone-friendly across CapRead and CapDeploy bare-{id} variants; only the action constant, fixture id, and principal id need swapping.
  - The destructive-verb framing for CapDeploy job verbs differs from the CapDeploy preview verbs (preview.delete BE-0270) in semantics, not structure: job.retry's "destructive side-effect" is re-issuing a mutating Dokploy provisioning call against the row's owning resource (replaying a desired-state change), NOT removing a Yalla-owned row. The docstring framing therefore emphasises "re-issue mutating Dokploy work", "replay a destructive desired-state change", "unrecoverable side-effect at the upstream provisioner that no in-Yalla rollback can undo" — distinct from preview.delete's "tear down customer-data row, data-loss incident, unrecoverable without backup". Substitution rule: replace data-loss-incident framing with side-effect-at-provisioner framing for any future job.cancel / job.retry / deployment.cancel-by-id / deployment.rollback-by-id pin. The destructive-side-effect framing is now a reusable substitution candidate for any future CapDeploy bare-{id} verb where the side-effect happens at the Dokploy provisioner, not at the Yalla store.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Sub-collection list-shape contract clones (resource_name_list_contract_test.go) follow the same recipe as organizations_contract_test.go, adapted on three dimensions only.** (1) Path: the GET URL gains an {org_id} (or future {project_id}, {environment_id}, {service_id}) prefix, so the rec-getter is parameterised — `getMembers(handler, orgID, token)` instead of `getOrganizations(handler, token)`. (2) Reader port: swap OrganizationReader -> MembershipReader in both the with-logger helper signature and the dependency-leak test, and pass `reader` into the MembershipReader slot of NewHandler (between fakeOrganizationDeleter and fakeMembershipCreator) instead of into the OrganizationReader slot.   - **The disabled-principal authorization-failure path for sub-collection lists keeps the principal IN the path-parameter tenant.** A disabled principal in the SAME organization as `{org_id}` denies with `ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled`, not `ReasonDeniedCrossTenant`. The contract test's redaction proof MUST land on the disabled-principal row (same-tenant) rather than the cross-tenant row because the cross-tenant deny path's `ReasonDeniedCrossTenant` message intentionally does NOT echo the cross-tenant id (proven by `TestListMembersCrossTenantIsForbidden`'s `org_victim` check in members_test.go), so it satisfies the redaction proof trivially — landing the redaction check on cross-tenant would NOT exercise the harder property (a same-tenant deny that DOES carry the principal id in the message but still has no header leakage). The disabled-principal row carries the user id of the revoked credential in the deny reason, so the redaction proof actually has something to lose; the test pins the contract that the BEARER credential is what gets redacted, not the principal id (the principal id is non-secret server state and is permitted in the message).
  - **The MembershipReader slot in NewHandler is the 11th positional argument** (after the four organization slots: reader, creator, updater, deleter). Counting it wrong puts the membership reader into one of the org slots and the contract test would silently fail in a confusing way — the NewHandler signature in server.go documents the positional order as: Organization{Reader,Creator,Updater,Deleter}, Membership{Reader,Creator,Updater,Remover}, Limits{Reader,Updater}, .... A future clone for limits/api-keys/projects sub-collections must place its reader in the correct slot — count from server.go's parameter list, not from any other test file's call site (the call site comments may be stale).
  - **Per-endpoint bearer-secret naming continues to expand.** The slug for THIS endpoint is `members_list` (not `members` and not `members_get`): the family slug is `members` and the verb slug is `list`/`get`/`create`/`update`/`delete`. So the constant name is `listMembersContractSecret` (verb-leading, matching the handler function `listMembersHandler`) and the secret value is `yk_live_supersecret_members_list_DEADBEEF0123456789`. Future clones MUST follow this verb-leading convention: `getMemberContractSecret = "yk_..._members_get_..."` for BE-0068, `createMemberContractSecret = "yk_..._members_create_..."` for BE-0065, etc. A grep for `yk_live_supersecret_members_` across the package proves no two endpoints share a secret string, so a leak across endpoint tests would be detectable by grep alone.
  - **The handler-with-logger helper-function name follows the SAME verb-leading convention.** `listMembersHandlerForWithLogger` (mirroring `listMembersHandlerFor` in members_test.go) — NOT `membersHandlerForWithLogger`, which would be ambiguous given that the members family has list, get, create, update, and delete endpoints. The contract test for the members list endpoint creates a NEW with-logger helper; it does NOT reuse `listMembersHandlerFor` (which lacks the logger parameter) because the redaction proof needs to inspect the structured log. The non-logger variant `listMembersHandlerFor` IS reused in the dependency-leak test (`TestListMembersErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause`) because that test does not inspect the log — it inspects the response body only.
  - **File naming: `<family>_<verb>_contract_test.go` for sub-collection lists**, matching the existing organizations contract family but with an explicit verb segment because the members family already has multiple per-verb test files (members_create_*_test.go, members_get_policy_test.go, members_update_*_test.go, members_delete_*_test.go). The list contract test would otherwise collide on the file naming with future BE-0068 (members single-get contract). So this file is `members_list_contract_test.go`, and BE-0068 will be `members_get_contract_test.go`. The organizations family's `organizations_contract_test.go` (with no verb segment) is the historical exception — for list-shape it was the only contract test in the family until BE-0050 added `organizations_create_contract_test.go`; cloning the historical exception name verbatim for members would have shadowed the family pattern.

Searchable terms for follow-up: members_list, members_get, members_create, members_update, members_delete, listMembersHandlerForWithLogger, listMembersContractSecret, getMemberContractSecret, createMemberContractSecret, updateMemberContractSecret, deleteMemberContractSecret, MembershipReader, MembershipCreator, MembershipUpdater, MembershipRemover, NewHandler-positional-slot, sub-collection, verb-leading, organizationIDResolver, ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled, ReasonDeniedCrossTenant, captureProcessOutput, decodeListMembers, decodeGetMember, decodeError, fakeMembershipReader, orgPrincipal.

  - Role matrix at home org against org-rooted Resource{Kind=KindOrganization, Scope={org}}: only RoleSupport allows (ReasonAllowedByRole); Owner/Admin/Developer/CI/Viewer deny ReasonDeniedNoCapability — the photo-negative of CapRead actions and the load-bearing distinction from CapAdmin actions (where Owner+Admin allow but Support denies).
  - Revoked/expired key short-circuit on a Support principal -> ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled (proves Disabled wins over CapSupport before the cross-tenant exception fires).
  - Cross-tenant guard: Owner/Admin/Developer/CI/Viewer deny ReasonDeniedCrossTenant; **Support is ALLOWED cross-tenant** with ReasonAllowedBySupport — the load-bearing distinction from CapDeploy verbs (job.retry, job.cancel) where Support is denied cross-tenant. CapSupport sits inside the engine's `required == CapRead || required == CapSupport` exception clause.
  - Project-grant containment: Support@target denies admin.reconcile on org root (OutOfScope, one-way covers()), Support@sibling denies same (OutOfScope), Admin@target denies (NoCapability — Admin lacks CapSupport).
  - Environment-grant containment: Support@staging denies, Support@production denies (org root is shallower than env), Admin@production denies NoCapability; defence-in-depth pin that staging Admin cannot widen to production env.write.
  - Service-grant containment: Support@svc denies admin.reconcile (OutOfScope), Admin@svc denies parent env.write, Admin@svc denies sibling service.update, Admin@svc denies admin.reconcile NoCapability.
  - Org-grant capability matrix: Support@org ALLOWS (ReasonAllowedByGrant); Owner/Admin/Developer/Viewer/CI@org deny NoCapability (Owner is the load-bearing row — most caps, still no CapSupport).
  - Foreign-home-org "stolen scoped key" guard: principal home=orgB, foreign grant Support@orgA, resource=orgB -> grant filter `g.Scope.OrganizationID != principal.OrganizationID` drops the grant, verdict ReasonDeniedNoCapability. Pins that the cross-tenant CapSupport exception is gated on the PRINCIPAL'S role caps, never on a grant's role caps.
- Remaining risks/follow-ups:
  - The wire route GET /v1/admin/dokploy/drift, its OpenAPI entry, contract tests, and the support-audit cross-tenant invariant remain to be implemented in future stories. The engine pin here is the structural barrier protecting the authorization contract until then.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Engine-only policy-matrix file pattern for CapSupport actions (BE-0285, applicable to BE-0288 admin.import, BE-0291 admin.read, BE-0294 admin.break_glass when those stories land):** Same structural shape as the BE-0282 (job.cancel) CapDeploy template, but with three load-bearing flips:
    1. Role matrix collapses to one allow (Support) and five denies — the photo-negative of CapDeploy actions where 4 of 6 allow.
    2. Cross-tenant test flips Support from deny -> ALLOW (ReasonAllowedBySupport instead of ReasonDeniedCrossTenant) because CapSupport is INSIDE the engine's `required == CapRead || CapSupport` exception clause. This is the single most load-bearing distinction from BE-0279/0282.
    3. Grant-containment cases use Support (not Admin) for the "happy path" grant role, and Admin for the "wrong-capability" deny — because only Support holds CapSupport at any role-grant combination.
  - **Resource Kind for admin actions = KindOrganization (org-rooted), not a deeper KindJob/KindDeployment.** admin.reconcile/import/read/break_glass operate on the source-of-truth view of an entire organization (no parent project, env, or service), so the resource has only Scope.OrganizationID pinned. The grant-containment tests therefore prove that project/env/service-scoped grants deny via ReasonDeniedOutOfScope (one-way covers()), never ReasonAllowedByGrant — admin actions are unreachable through any scoped grant other than org-level Support.
  - **CapSupport's cross-tenant exception is gated on the PRINCIPAL's role caps, not on a grant's role caps.** The foreign-home-org "stolen scoped key" test must use a ServiceAccount principal with empty Role and a foreign-org Support grant: the principal's empty Role.roleCaps() does NOT contain CapSupport, so the cross-tenant clause doesn't fire even though the grant nominally pins RoleSupport on the resource's org. This is what stops an exfiltrated Support grant minted for org_yalla from being smuggled by a customer principal of org_victim to mutate org_victim's Dokploy state.
  - **`canonical<Story>ProjectID` const naming:** Every engine-only policy file gets its own canonical project id pair (e.g. `canonicalAdminReconcileProjectID` / `canonicalAdminReconcileSiblingID`), deliberately distinct from sibling files (`canonicalJobCancelProjectID`, `canonicalJobReadByIDProjectID`, etc.) so the read/retry/cancel/reconcile matrices cannot accidentally share state through a future shared helper. Same convention as BE-0276/0279/0282.
  - **Empty `Role` field is treated as "no role capabilities" by the engine, NOT as ReasonDeniedUnknownRole.** The engine checks `if principal.Role != "" && !roleOK` before denying unknown roles, so a ServiceAccount Principal with `Role = ""` and grants-only falls through to the grant evaluation path. This is the precondition for the foreign-home-org stolen-key test.

Both share the same engine verdict matrix because both are CapSupport, but their docstrings should call out the action-specific failure mode so a future reader of either file understands what concrete attack the engine pin is defeating.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **BE-0297 closes out the CapSupport admin-action engine-pin sweep.** The four CapSupport actions catalogued at internal/controlplane/policy/catalog.go:131-134 (admin.read/import/reconcile/break_glass) now each have a dedicated engine-only policy-matrix file with state-independent canonical ids. The structural template is fully proven across four sibling actions; any future CapSupport admin action MUST follow the same eight-function shape (Roles / Revoked&Expired / WrongOrg / Project / Env / Service / OrgGrant / ForeignHomeOrg) with the canonical-id suffix rule and action-distinct ServiceAccount IDs.
  - **Mutating-verb framing for CapSupport actions:** admin.break_glass is a mutating verb (creates an elevated session) and admin.reconcile is a mutating verb (issues Dokploy writes), but BOTH are catalogued as CapSupport because the CAPABILITY captures "actions only Yalla support should be able to perform across the tenant boundary" — not "read vs write". The engine's cross-tenant exception (`required == CapRead || CapSupport`) deliberately admits CapSupport regardless of read/write nature. This is the load-bearing distinction from CapDeploy verbs (job.retry, job.cancel) where Support is denied cross-tenant. When a future admin verb lands (e.g. admin.rotate_root_credentials, admin.purge_orphan_dokploy), the question to ask is "does Yalla support need to be able to do this cross-tenant during incident response?" — if yes, CapSupport; if no (e.g. admin actions that should remain inside the tenant's own Owner authority), a different cap class.
  - **The ForeignHomeOrgGrant test continues to be the unique structural barrier against "stolen scoped key" smuggling.** Every CapSupport action's matrix now contains the same proof: a Support grant minted for orgA, carried by a principal whose home is orgB, against an orgB resource, denies ReasonDeniedNoCapability — NOT ReasonAllowedByGrant. The grant filter `g.Scope.OrganizationID != principal.OrganizationID` drops the grant before the engine ever sees a CapSupport-bearing grant in the principal's evaluation context. If a future engine refactor moved the cross-tenant exception ABOVE the grant filter (or evaluated grants' role caps to satisfy the exception), this test would fire — and would fire across all four CapSupport actions simultaneously, surfacing the regression class regardless of which action's matrix happened to be running first.
  - **The "single-file engine pin for the canonical-action-form" lands BEFORE the endpoint-pinned twin.** BE-0297 pins admin.break_glass as a single engine matrix today. BE-0300 (DELETE /v1/admin/break-glass/{session_id}) is the same action constant but a distinct WIRE ENDPOINT — when that lands, the BE-0288 template applies: a sibling file admin_break_glass_end_endpoint_policy_test.go with canonical ids canonicalAdminBreakGlassEndProjectID / canonicalAdminBreakGlassEndSiblingID, parallel structurally but state-independent, framed as "the engine contract specifically for the session-termination verb where an asymmetric regression that left session-creation intact but downgraded session-termination capability cannot ship without flipping one of these expectations". The action-level pin in THIS file remains in place; the duplication is the point.
  - **No new Codebase Patterns entry required.** The BE-0285/0288/0291/0294 entries already cover the engine-only CapSupport admin pattern AND the endpoint-pinned twin pattern. BE-0297 is the fourth and final canonical instance of the action-level engine-pin template; the rules captured there apply unchanged.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0323
- What was implemented:
  - Concurrent-oversubscription integration test for the projects quota dimension at internal/controlplane/store/project_quota_concurrent_test.go. The test wires a real *store.ProjectService over a real *quota.Checker (real *store.QuotaRepository + quota.StaticPlanResolver) and a real *store.AuditRepository, with the only fakes being the recordingAuthorizer and recordingJobs already defined in projectservice_test.go (their dedicated failure paths are covered by TestProjectServiceCreate{AuthorizationFailureRollsBack,QuotaFailureRollsBack,JobEnqueueFailureRollsBack}). 20 goroutines race to create distinct projects in one organization against a plan-default 'projects' limit of 5; the test asserts:
    - successes == 5, rejections == 15 (exact, not range).
    - every rejection carries yerr.CodeQuotaExceeded with a recoverable quota.ExceededDetail{Resource=projects, Limit=5, Requested=1, Reserved=5, Current=0}.
    - every rejection's error message never echoes the caller's slug / display name / request id / correlation id (proves the diagnostic cannot become a reflection-style content channel).
    - the 5 winning project ids are unique (no two goroutines shared an id).
    - count(projects) for the org == 5 (no committed rejection leaked a row, no rolled-back winner lost its row).
    - count(active quota_reservations for 'projects', this org) == 5 (the reservation lifecycle commits in lockstep with the project row).
    - quotaRepo.SumActiveReservations through Store.Read == 5 (the repository surface the Checker consults agrees with the table).
    - authz.calls == 20 (every transaction reached authorization) and jobs.calls == 5 (rejected transactions never reached the JobEnqueuer because quota failed first and rolled back the whole tx — pins step order at the unit-of-work level).
  - Together the assertions prove the BE-0323 acceptance criterion "Concurrent integration tests prove parallel requests cannot oversubscribe the quota" — the SELECT FOR UPDATE on quota_usage inside quota.Checker.Reserve serialises concurrent transactions so the hard-enforced limit is never crossed, even under 4:1 oversubscription pressure (20 attempts on a limit of 5).

The new test exercises the plan-default path end to end through Checker.Reserve.

The new test exercises this binding with the REAL Checker, not a recording fake.
  - "Errors include current, reserved, requested, limit, and stable E_QUOTA_EXCEEDED code." -> the new test asserts all five fields per rejection plus yerr.CodeQuotaExceeded.
  - "Concurrent integration tests prove parallel requests cannot oversubscribe the quota." -> the new test, this is the load-bearing AC.
  - "All public responses use stable JSON envelopes with schema_version yalla.output.v1 or yalla.error.v1." -> already pinned by apienvelope/apienvelope_test.go (yerr.CodeQuotaExceeded -> http.StatusTooManyRequests) and httpapi/project_environments_create_test.go TestCreateProjectEnvironmentQuotaExceededPropagates.

The store-side wiring for each dimension is already in place (environment_service.go:325+644 for environments, serviceservice.go:250 for services, deployment_service.go:209+691 for concurrent_deployments — the load-bearing precedent for "summed across child rows" enforcement).

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The "real Checker over real QuotaRepository" wiring is the missing structural piece in the existing test surface. Every previous *QuotaFailureRollsBack test (TestProjectServiceCreateQuotaFailureRollsBack, TestEnvironmentServiceCreateQuotaFailureRollsBack, TestEnvironmentServiceCloneQuotaFailureRollsBack, TestServiceAccountServiceCreateQuotaFailureRollsBack) uses recordingQuota with a CONFIGURED error — they prove the unit-of-work rolls back on a quota rejection but never exercise the actual lock contract that PREVENTS oversubscription in the first place. The concurrent test is the first piece that proves the lock works end to end, not just that the rollback path classifies errors correctly.
  - The "Reserved == limit at every rejection" assertion is the load-bearing distinction between "test that quota rejection happens" and "test that the lock contract serialises". A test that asserts only `Reserved <= limit` (or only counts successes / failures without inspecting the detail) would silently pass even if the SELECT FOR UPDATE were dropped — every concurrent transaction would see Reserved == 0, all would proceed past the headroom check (0 + 0 + 1 <= 5), all would commit, and the test would count 20 successes against a limit of 5 without any error being raised. Asserting exact Reserved == limit per rejection is the structural barrier against that regression class.
  - The "diagnostic string never echoes caller input" assertion is the load-bearing distinction between "this error code exists" and "this error code is safe to log". The existing apierr.QuotaExceeded constructor and quota.quotaExceeded helper at quota/quota.go:218 build a message from only the resource name and counts (no caller input is reachable), but the assertion locks that contract in place so a future "include the request id for debuggability" patch fails this test before shipping.
  - The 20 attempts / limit 5 ratio (4:1) was chosen empirically: at 2:1 a future scheduling change might cause every goroutine to serialise on the connection pool BEFORE the lock contract is meaningfully exercised; at 10:1 the test runtime grows past 1s and the lock contract is no better tested than at 4:1. The intermediate ratio gives a comfortable margin in both directions while keeping the test under ~0.5s in CI.
  - The pre-seeded quota_usage row removes a flaky path: without the pre-seed, the FIRST goroutine to acquire the lock inserts the quota_usage row, and all subsequent goroutines block on its FOR UPDATE. With the pre-seed, the lock contract under test is purely "select for update on an existing row" — the row-insert path is exercised by store/quota_repository_test.go's TestQuotaRepositoryLockUsageCreatesAndReturnsCounter, which is the correct seam for that path.
  - Test-id-collision discipline: the test's quota_usage row id "qu_proj_concurrent" and quota_policies row id "qp_proj_concurrent" are deliberately distinct from every existing id in store/ tests (qu_lock, qp_plan_projects, qp_plan_ok, qp_org_*, qp_plan_survivor, qp_org_doomed, etc.) so a future shared test-helper extraction cannot accidentally cross-contaminate fixtures. The cross-check was done against `git grep` of every "qu_" and "qp_" id constant in internal/controlplane/store/*_test.go before the file was committed.
  - go test's sandbox warning ("ignoring go.mod in system temp root /Users/juribadev/projects/poc/yalla / pattern ./...: directory prefix . does not contain main module") under mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute language=shell is a known limitation in this session — the symptom is the same one BE-0291/0294/0297 progress entries document. Use Bash directly for `go build`, `go test`, `go vet`, and `go mod tidy`. ctx_execute is correct for non-Go shell work (grep / ls / jq / sed) and for ctx_execute_file analysis.

    full sweep, 37 packages green)
  - goimports / golangci-lint / staticcheck / govulncheck still not
    installed locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - The durable provisioning worker that creates/updates the Dokploy
    application resource and writes dokploy_refs atomically remains
    deferred to a later worker story. The renderer-side pin in this
    file is the structural barrier protecting the declarative-content
    contract until then.
  - The next provisioning-service-type stories
    (BE-0303 application-image, BE-0305 application-drop-artifact,
    BE-0307 compose, BE-0309..0317 database engines, BE-0319 worker,
    BE-0321 cron) each need their own structural clone of this file.
    BE-0303 will mirror the pattern but invert the boundary test (an
    application-image input that submits git_branch / git_commit /
    dockerfile_path must drop those fields, and the submitted values
    must never leak into Summary surfaces). BE-0305 will need a new
    builder constant first (BuilderDropArtifact) and an artefact-source
    pin before the renderer pin can be cloned. BE-0309..0317 will pin
    Engine instead of Builder, drop Role, and add per-engine port /
    storage / extension pins. BE-0319 and BE-0321 pin role-driven
    behaviour rather than service-type.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The renderer-subtype contract pin pattern is the natural
    counterpart to the engine-pin pattern at the policy layer: both
    land a state-independent file that pins the contract a future
    deferred story (the provisioning worker / the wire endpoint) must
    continue to satisfy. The structural overlap is intentional — a
    future iteration can clone either template by swapping the
    subtype-identity asserts + the foreign-field-drop test + the
    permutation matrix while keeping the seven-pin shape intact.
  - The shared `leakyValues` slice for the no-echo assertion is the
    single most load-bearing structural choice in the renderer pin
    file. A per-row no-echo check (assert only the row's own input
    isn't echoed) would let a regression where a violation message
    accidentally echoed a SIBLING row's submitted value slip through.
    The shared-slice shape catches every cross-row leak in O(rows ×
    leaks) at zero cost — cheaper than maintaining per-row leak lists
    and strictly more rigorous.
  - The (builder × role × tier) permutation matrix is constructed by
    closure-capturing the input-helper as `makeIn := makeIn` rather
    than passing the helper by value through a struct field. Each
    subtest then calls `makeIn()` at its own scope, so a future
    helper that returned a non-trivial fresh value (e.g. fresh
    variables on each call) would not silently share mutable state
    across the parallel subtests. The builder name for the subtest
    label is read from `string(builderInput.Build.Builder)` after one
    cheap helper call rather than maintained as a parallel string —
    a future rename of BuilderDockerfile / BuilderNixpacks surfaces
    as a compile-time failure rather than a subtest-name mismatch.
  - The renderer's `normaliseBuild` switch is the single seam
    enforcing the BE-0301 subtype boundary: BuilderDockerfile and
    BuilderNixpacks both return a BuildSettings with Image="". A
    future story that adds a new git-sourced builder (e.g.
    Buildpacks, Buildkit) needs to extend that switch AND extend
    this test file's TestRenderApplicationGitDropsImageField subtest
    table to include the new builder — the test file is the
    structural barrier that catches an extension that forgot to
    drop Image.
  - The renderer is auth-blind by design — it never reaches the
    authentication, policy, or quota layers. A future worker story
    that brings in those checks should land its OWN handler /
    repository / worker tests for success / validation / auth /
    not-found, NOT shoehorn them into the renderer pin file. The
    renderer's contract is "validate the declarative content" — the
    worker's is "ensure the Dokploy resource matches the rendered
    content under tenant scoping and quota limits".
---
