## 2026-05-16 - BE-0349 (Security verification: SSRF protection for webhooks and Git URLs)
- What was implemented:
  Added the `disallowedSSRFHost` helper (internal/controlplane/validate/ssrf.go)
  that rejects customer-supplied URLs whose host targets a non-routable
  address: any IP literal in the unspecified / loopback / link-local /
  multicast / private (RFC1918) / unique-local-v6 / CGNAT / benchmark /
  limited-broadcast ranges (covers 127.0.0.1, ::1, 169.254.169.254 cloud
  metadata, 169.254.170.2 ECS task metadata, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16,
  fc00::/7, 100.64/10, 198.18/15, 255.255.255.255), the closed hostname set
  {localhost, ip6-localhost, ip6-loopback, metadata, metadata.google.internal,
  metadata.aws.internal, 169.254.169.254}, and the leading-dot suffix set
  {.localhost, .internal, .local, .localdomain}. The helper is pure (no DNS),
  emits one of nine canonical value-free classification reasons, and is
  wired into BOTH `validate.URL` (webhook / notification URLs) and
  `validate.GitRepoURL` — the scp-like `git@host:path` form is checked via
  the extracted host, and the https/ssh/git URL form is checked via
  `urlHost(u)`. Added a static analyzer (`ssrf_static_test.go`) that walks
  each function body with ast.Inspect and asserts a call to the exact
  identifier `disallowedSSRFHost`; self-checks against known-good,
  known-missing, and look-alike-but-wrong fixtures keep both directions
  honest. A sealing-trap (`TestSSRFHostnameListsAreCanonical`) pins required
  hostname / suffix entries and the leading-dot invariant. Runtime tests
  (`ssrf_test.go`) drive every documented IP range, every hostname, and
  every suffix through both validators, prove every rejection is a member
  of the closed `canonicalSSRFReasons` set, prove public hosts are
  accepted, and prove a planted secret-shaped query-string canary never
  appears in the reason. Added a `FuzzURL` target seeded with one URL per
  forbidden range so a corpus replay surfaces a dropped category. Added an
  "SSRF protection for webhooks and Git URLs" section to
  internal/controlplane/validate/AGENTS.md documenting the threat model,
  the closed reason set, the layered-defence requirement (runtime
  resolved-IP re-check is a separate worker-side wall — not in this
  package), and the maintenance contract for adding a new classification.
- Files changed:
  internal/controlplane/validate/ssrf.go (new),
  internal/controlplane/validate/ssrf_static_test.go (new),
  internal/controlplane/validate/ssrf_test.go (new),
  internal/controlplane/validate/network.go (URL now calls disallowedSSRFHost),
  internal/controlplane/validate/refs.go (GitRepoURL now calls
  disallowedSSRFHost on the scp host and the parsed URL host),
  internal/controlplane/validate/fuzz_test.go (added FuzzURL with SSRF seeds),
  internal/controlplane/validate/AGENTS.md (added "SSRF protection for
  webhooks and Git URLs" section above the BE-0346 section),
  ralph/prd.json (BE-0349 passes=true),
  ralph/progress.txt (this entry + a new Codebase Patterns entry).
- Verification run:
  - gofmt -l internal/controlplane/validate (clean)
  - go vet ./... (clean — full module)
  - go test -count=1 ./internal/controlplane/validate/... (green — all 4
    new SSRF runtime test functions + 4 static-analyzer subtests + 1
    hostname-sealing-trap test pass alongside the existing suite)
  - go test -race ./internal/controlplane/validate/... (green)
- Results: all required quality checks pass on the validate package; the
  rest of the module continues to build and vet clean.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - The validator cannot catch DNS-rebinding: a public hostname that
    resolves to a private IP at fetch time will pass this layer. The
    runtime HTTP client / git client used by the worker MUST re-validate
    the resolved address before connecting. That second wall is a
    separate worker-side story and is called out explicitly in
    AGENTS.md so the next iteration doesn't assume the validator-layer
    check is sufficient.
  - The hostname blocklist is intentionally tight: it covers the
    canonical names {localhost, ip6-localhost, ip6-loopback, metadata,
    metadata.google.{aws.}internal} plus the .internal/.local/.localhost/
    .localdomain suffixes. Other site-specific internal suffixes (e.g.
    a cluster's mDNS namespace) are NOT in the set and would need a
    deployment-time configuration seam — out of scope for this pure
    validator story.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The two-test security-verification template (BE-0344..BE-0348)
    extends cleanly to the validate package. The package's existing
    helpers (`findFuncDecl`, `mustParseValidateFile`, `equalStringSlices`
    from `json_static_test.go`) are reused by the new static analyzer —
    every new security-verification static analyzer in this package
    should look for those helpers first before adding new ones.
  - Reason text in a redaction-sensitive validator is most robustly
    pinned as set-membership against a closed list of canonical
    strings, not as a substring-doesn't-contain-host check. The
    BE-0343 fixture-collision pattern flagged the failure mode in
    advance: stable classification phrases legitimately contain words
    like "localhost" / "metadata" / "loopback" that an unwary
    redaction test would treat as a host echo. The closed-set
    assertion (`isCanonicalSSRFReason`) makes the invariant strictly
    stronger AND makes a future "add a new classification" PR
    immediately visible because the new string must be added to the
    test's whitelist alongside the production code.
  - Go's `net.IP.IsPrivate()` covers RFC1918 (10/8, 172.16/12,
    192.168/16) AND ULA (fc00::/7) but does NOT cover CGNAT
    (100.64/10) or the RFC2544 benchmark range (198.18/15); a
    hand-rolled v4-only branch on top of `IsPrivate` is required to
    cover those. 169.254.169.254 cloud metadata is link-local, not
    private — `IsLinkLocalUnicast()` is the correct branch for that
    range, and the entry in `forbiddenSSRFHostnames` is belt-and-braces.
  - IPv6 literals in URL form MUST be bracketed (`[fd00::1]`); without
    brackets, `url.Parse` treats the colons as port separators and the
    extracted host is wrong. Runtime fixtures must use the bracketed
    form. The validator's `disallowedSSRFHost` helper strips one set of
    surrounding brackets so it works on both `u.Hostname()` output
    (already unbracketed) and direct-from-caller bracketed input.
  - GitRepoURL has three syntactic shapes (https:// / ssh:// /
    scp-like `git@host:path`); presence-of-call static analysis pins
    that the helper is called somewhere in the body, but per-shape
    runtime coverage is required to prove the SSRF guard fires on
    every shape. The runtime table includes one row per shape per
    representative blocked host.
  - Sealing-trap tests on package-private name/suffix lists belong in
    the same package as the production code (not the `_test` package)
    so they can read the unexported variables directly. The two test
    files in this story are split intentionally: `ssrf_static_test.go`
    is in `package validate` (it inspects unexported state and AST), and
    `ssrf_test.go` is in `package validate_test` (it drives the public
    API surface, matching the existing `validate_test.go` shape).

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0350 (Security verification: domain takeover prevention)
- What was implemented:
  Added the `disallowedTakeoverHost` helper (internal/controlplane/validate/
  domain_takeover.go) that rejects customer-supplied service-domain
  hostnames whose shape is structurally illegitimate as a public-facing
  domain: any IPv4 dotted literal (`net.ParseIP` parses the host), any
  exact-match RFC 6761 / RFC 2606 special-use label or shared-hosting eTLD
  bare form (`localhost`/`local`/`internal`/`lan`/`home.arpa`/...,
  `appspot.com`/`azurewebsites.net`/`cloudfront.net`/`elasticbeanstalk.com`/
  `firebaseapp.com`/`github.io`/`gitlab.io`/`herokuapp.com`/`netlify.app`/
  `pages.dev`/`vercel.app`/`web.app`), and any hostname ending in the
  closed set of reserved internal suffixes
  {.localhost, .localdomain, .local, .internal, .intranet, .private,
  .corp, .home, .home.arpa, .lan}. The helper is pure (no DNS), emits one
  of three canonical value-free classification reasons ("must not be an IP
  address literal — register a hostname instead", "must not be a reserved
  or shared-hosting domain", "must not target a reserved or internal-use
  namespace"), and is wired into `validate.Domain` at the end of the
  function (after the FQDN/label-shape checks already in place). RFC 2606
  documentation-only suffixes (`.test`, `.example`, `.invalid`) are
  DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the suffix walk while staying in the
  exact-match map: those names cannot intercept real customer traffic
  (only squat, which the `service_domains` UNIQUE constraint already
  bounds) and the omission keeps every existing httpapi test fixture
  using `.example` valid.

  Added a static analyzer (`domain_takeover_static_test.go`) that walks
  `Domain` in network.go with ast.Inspect and asserts a call to the exact
  identifier `disallowedTakeoverHost`; self-checks against known-good,
  known-missing, and look-alike-but-wrong fixtures keep both directions
  honest. A sealing-trap (`TestDomainTakeoverListsAreCanonical`) pins
  the required exact-match and suffix entries and the leading-dot
  invariant on every suffix entry.

  Runtime tests (`domain_takeover_test.go`) drive every blocked IPv4
  literal, the `home.arpa` exact-match, every reserved suffix host, every
  shared-hosting eTLD bare form, and every public-host accept case
  through `Domain`, prove every rejection is a member of the closed
  `canonicalTakeoverReasons` set, and prove every legitimate registrable
  hostname (`example.com`, `myapp.appspot.com`, `acme.github.io`,
  `flocal.example.com`) keeps validating. Additional tests cover the
  wildcard interaction (a wildcard form like `*.appspot.com` strips to
  the bare eTLD and rejects with the same canonical reason — a wildcard
  makes takeover STRICTLY WORSE), the redaction backstop (a planted
  secret canary as a sub-label of a reserved-suffix host never appears
  in the reason or the wrapped error), and the order-of-precedence
  (`Domain("")` keeps the existing "must not be blank" diagnostic).

  Seeded `FuzzDomain` with one input per documented forbidden category
  and added an accept-branch re-derivation (`net.ParseIP(v) != nil` and
  reserved-suffix HasSuffix) that fires on any future regression that
  drops the takeover guard from Domain. Added a "Domain-takeover
  prevention (BE-0350)" section to internal/controlplane/validate/
  AGENTS.md documenting the threat model, the closed reason set, the
  layered-defence requirement (ownership PROOF lives in the
  certificate-issuance / routing-attach worker, NOT in this package),
  the deliberate `.test`/`.example`/`.invalid` exclusion, the
  distinction from `disallowedSSRFHost` (inbound vs outbound), and the
  maintenance contract for adding a new classification.

- Files changed:
  internal/controlplane/validate/domain_takeover.go (new),
  internal/controlplane/validate/domain_takeover_static_test.go (new),

- Remaining risks or follow-ups: none for BE-0350. The ownership-PROOF
  runtime wall (HTTP-01 / DNS-01 / ALPN-01 challenge against the
  resolved hostname) is the layered-defence story for the
  certificate-issuance and routing-attach worker — explicitly out of
  scope here, AGENTS.md flags the boundary. Sibling security-
  verification stories BE-0351..BE-0363 follow the BE-0344/0345/0346/0349/
  0350 two-test pattern (helper + static-analysis test + runtime test +
  AGENTS.md section + fuzz seeds where applicable); each picks the
  package that owns the invariant.

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Two-test template ports cleanly across SSRF (outbound URLs) and
    domain-takeover (inbound hostnames), but the threat models are
    structurally distinct and MUST live in separate helpers / analysers
    — `disallowedSSRFHost` and `disallowedTakeoverHost` share a shape
    but check disjoint sets. A host legitimate to attach
    (`myapp.example.com`) may still be illegitimate to fetch (resolves
    to a private IP), and vice versa. Reusing the SSRF helper would
    collapse the threat models and hide which class applies to which
    surface.
  - The takeover guard's call site in `Domain` goes AT THE END (after
    the FQDN/label checks), not at the start. Single-label reserved
    names (`localhost`, `local`, `internal`, `lan`, `test`, `example`,
    `invalid`) and IPv6 literals (single label after `.` split) are
    rejected by the existing FQDN check BEFORE reaching the guard, so
    the runtime test table MUST restrict itself to inputs that pass
    through the helper today (IPv4 dotted literals, multi-label reserved
    exact-matches like `home.arpa`, suffix-match cases, shared-hosting
    eTLD bare forms). The unreachable single-label entries stay in the
    map as defence-in-depth — a future FQDN-check loosening must still
    trip the takeover guard — but the runtime regression table only
    asserts on what's actually reachable so a missing call site is
    caught by a FAILING subtest rather than a silently-skipped one.
  - The reserved-name lists MUST exclude `.test`/`.example`/`.invalid`
    from the SUFFIX walk while keeping them in the EXACT-MATCH map.
    Those names are not publicly routable (they cannot intercept real
    customer traffic) so they are a squatting threat — already bounded
    by the `service_domains` UNIQUE constraint — rather than a takeover
    threat. The httpapi test fixtures across ~7 files use `.example` per
    RFC convention; adding `.example` to the suffix walk would break
    every one of them with no real takeover-defence benefit. Document
    the omission AND the asymmetry in the helper's package-doc, the
    AGENTS.md section, and the test file's blocked-hosts table comment.
  - The wildcard interaction is load-bearing: with wildcards enabled,
    `*.appspot.com` strips to `appspot.com` which the takeover guard
    rejects — a wildcard makes takeover STRICTLY WORSE (the bare suffix
    locks one routing entry, the wildcard locks every sub-tenant of
    that suffix) so the wildcard rejection gets its own dedicated test.
    The helper ALSO defensively strips a leading `*.` itself so it
    remains correct for any future caller that passes the raw value.
  - The redaction backstop MUST plant the canary as a sub-label of a
    reserved-SUFFIX host (e.g. `canary + ".lan"`), not a reserved-
    exact-match host (where the canary would not appear in the matched
    host at all). The suffix walk's `strings.HasSuffix(h, suffix)`
    reduces the entire host to the suffix-class reason without
    inspecting the canary, so a reason containing the canary proves
    the validator interpolated the value. The canary string must be
    picked to NOT collide with any word in the canonical reason set
    (no "domain", "namespace", "address", "literal", "hostname") —
    BE-0343 already flagged that substring redaction checks false-
    positive on stable classification phrases.
  - The FuzzDomain accept-branch re-derivation (`net.ParseIP(v) != nil`
    and reserved-suffix HasSuffix) is what makes the fuzz target
    actually catch a regression of the takeover guard. Without it,
    dropping the helper would let IPv4-literal seeds pass through to
    the accept branch without firing any assertion (the existing
    FQDN+label re-derivation accepts `8.8.8.8` because each `8` is a
    valid DNS label). The reservedSuffixes slice in the fuzz target is
    a deliberate DUPLICATE of the package-private one — that is the
    cost of the `_test` package split: a future helper change must
    update BOTH lists or `TestDomainTakeoverListsAreCanonical` fires
    for the package list and the fuzz target silently accepts the
    dropped category. Document the duplication in the seed-loop
    comment.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0083
- Added public-API contract test file at internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_get_contract_test.go closing the BE-0083 acceptance criteria not asserted by api_keys_get_test.go (BE-0082): (1) HTTP server writes response data only through http.ResponseWriter — never the process stdout/stderr (captureProcessOutput swap); (2) per-request structured log is redacted on both the success path and the disabled-principal authorization-failure path so a recognisable bearer credential never appears in logBuf or the response body; (3) error envelope built from a wrapped reader-store cause carries a stable generic message and never leaks the wrapped cause string or the datastore address (10.0.0.5:5432).

The third structural twin (after list BE-0077 and create BE-0080) of the api-keys contract test pattern lands cleanly with zero churn to existing files — the new test file is purely additive and reuses listAPIKeysHandlerForWithLogger / listAPIKeysHandlerFor / getAPIKey / decodeGetAPIKey / seedAPIKey / fakeAPIKeyReader.getErr / captureProcessOutput / orgPrincipal / decodeError without touching any of them.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Patterns discovered:
    - Per-endpoint public-API contract test (api_keys_get_contract_test.go) is the third worked instance after api_keys_list_contract_test.go (BE-0077) and api_keys_create_contract_test.go (BE-0080) of the api-keys family pattern. The three tests are mechanically the same shape for every api-keys endpoint:
      1. TestXxxAPIKeyServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter (not parallel — captureProcessOutput swaps os.Stdout/os.Stderr globals) that proves the served response carries data only through the http.ResponseWriter and the structured logger is the only sanctioned out-of-band writer (asserted via a non-empty logBuf).
      2. TestXxxAPIKeyRequestLogRedactsBearerToken (parallel, table-driven with two cases: success path with the production-shape success-fake and authorization failure path with a disabled-principal + a deny-fake whose method errors if invoked, so a logged "fake error" cannot be the leak source) that proves a recognisable bearer credential never appears in the per-request structured log OR the response body.
      3. TestXxxAPIKeyErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause (parallel) that wires the reader/creator/updater/revoker/rotator fake with apierr.StoreUnavailable(stderrors.New("connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432")) and asserts both the 503 typed-status and that the wrapped cause string AND the bare datastore address never appear in the response body — the bare address is the kind of internal-network detail an error envelope must never leak even when the cause string carries it. api_keys_xxx_test.go pins the typed-status half of this contract (TestXxxAPIKeyReaderUnavailable / equivalent); the contract test pins the wire-leak half.
    - Helper reuse for GET-by-id contract test: api_keys_get_test.go (BE-0082) already defined getAPIKey(handler, orgID, keyID, token) request helper, getAPIKeySuccessEnvelope decode struct, and decodeGetAPIKey(t, rec) decoder. The contract test file imports none of those — they are package-level, already visible to every _test.go file in package httpapi — and reuses them directly. The contract test ALSO reuses listAPIKeysHandlerForWithLogger (from api_keys_list_contract_test.go) and listAPIKeysHandlerFor (from api_keys_test.go) without any wiring churn: both helpers build the FULL NewHandler surface so the same wiring serves GET /api-keys, GET /api-keys/{key_id}, POST /api-keys, PATCH /api-keys/{key_id}, DELETE /api-keys/{key_id}, and POST /api-keys/{key_id}/rotate from one shared APIKeyReader port. The future contract test stories for PATCH (BE-0086), DELETE (BE-0089), POST rotate (BE-0092) can reuse the SAME helpers — the only per-story moves are: declare a new ${endpoint}APIKeyContractSecret constant (so a leak in one test cannot mask a leak in another), pick the correct request-helper (patchAPIKey, deleteAPIKey, rotateAPIKey) and decoder, and pick the correct fake port (APIKeyUpdater, APIKeyRevoker, APIKeyRotator) — the success/disabled/deny fake-call-stub triple is structurally identical.
    - fakeAPIKeyReader has TWO error fields: `err` (gates ListAPIKeys) and `getErr` (gates GetAPIKey). GET-by-id contract tests MUST use `getErr` for both the deny-leg "must not be called" sentinel and the StoreUnavailable cause. A typo (`err` instead of `getErr`) silently passes because GetAPIKey only consults `getErr` and the zero `key` then triggers the typed not-found branch (apierr.NotFound("api_key", keyID)) — the deny-leg test would still pass (the wrong path still returns the wanted forbidden via policy) but the StoreUnavailable test would FAIL because the 200 success / 404 not-found branch would replace the expected 503. The contract-test file uses `getErr` consistently.
  - Gotchas encountered:
    - The sandbox shell exports TMPDIR=/Users/juribadev/projects/poc/yalla (the project root itself). Go's `cmd/go` refuses to load a module from a path it considers a "system temp root" and errors out with `go: warning: ignoring go.mod in system temp root` + `cannot find main module`. Workaround: every ctx_execute shell session that runs a `go` command must FIRST `export TMPDIR=/tmp` (the sandbox's TMPDIR setting persists into subprocess env). Plain `cd` is not enough — the module loader honours TMPDIR for the "temp root" check independent of CWD. Document for every future iteration that uses ctx_execute with go.
    - The contract test file's import block must drop the `internal/controlplane/store` import that the list/create contract tests carry. The list-contract-test needs `store.APIKey` literal in the table-driven test seed; the create-contract-test needs it for the same reason. The GET-by-id contract test only uses seedAPIKey() (which returns store.APIKey) — the variable is captured into `fakeAPIKeyReader{key: ...}` without ever naming the type at the contract-test source. A leftover `_ "store"` import (or a `var _ = store.APIKey{}` sentinel kept "for future use") trips `go vet`'s unused-import rule and is also flagged by the project's "no backwards-compat hacks" guidance — drop unused imports, let a future story that needs the type add it back.
  - Useful context:
    - All contract tests in this family use `captureProcessOutput` from me_contract_test.go (FIRST place it was defined). The helper swaps the global os.Stdout/os.Stderr via os.Pipe(), runs fn, restores the originals, and returns the captured strings. The test that uses it MUST NOT be t.Parallel() — concurrent tests would race on the os.Stdout/os.Stderr swap. The other two tests in each contract-test file ARE t.Parallel() — only the captureProcessOutput-using test opts out.
    - decodeError(t, rec, "E_UNAVAILABLE") is the canonical "decode an error envelope and assert the code constant" helper. It is package-visible from api_keys_test.go and used across every contract test. The code constants are: E_VALIDATION, E_FORBIDDEN, E_UNAUTHENTICATED, E_NOT_FOUND, E_CONFLICT, E_UNAVAILABLE, E_INTERNAL — every contract-test file should anchor on these constants, never on a substring of the message field (the message text is brittle prose, the code is the stable contract).

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0351 - Security verification: secret encryption key rotation
- Documented the secret-encryption key rotation threat model and operator runbook in `internal/controlplane/secrets/AGENTS.md` (Key rotation section: threat model, four-method provider surface, routing index, runbook steps, verification tests pinning the rotation contract).
- Added `internal/controlplane/secrets/key_rotation_static_test.go` — sealing-trap that parses `aesgcm.go` and pins (NewAESGCM takes `[][]byte`, ActiveKeyID exists, KeyIDs exists, Open iterates the receiver's `keys` slice AND returns `ErrUnknownKey`) with a self-check that drives synthetic regression sources.
- Added `internal/controlplane/secrets/key_rotation_test.go` — runtime test that drives the full three-phase rotation lifecycle (pre-rotation Seal under k_old, mid-rotation provider [k_new, k_old] Opens retired ciphertext and Seals under k_new, re-seal step produces a fresh ciphertext under k_new, post-rotation provider [k_new] surfaces ErrUnknownKey for a row missed by the re-seal worker) plus a separate `TestAESGCMRotationDoesNotLeak` that captures the slog JSON and `fmt.Sprintf("%s", provider)` projections across every rotation phase and asserts none of (k_old, k_new, plaintext, pre/mid ciphertext) leaks into either redaction projection.
- Added `internal/controlplane/store/migrate/secret_routing_idx_static_test.go` — sealing-trap that reads each `*_variables_encrypted_secrets.up.sql` from the embedded migration FS (no database required) and asserts the partial routing index `CREATE INDEX <table>_secret_routing_idx ON <table> (secret_provider, secret_key_id) WHERE is_secret = true` exists with the documented shape. Self-check feeds eight synthetic SQL snippets (canonical, single-line, IF NOT EXISTS, missing, wrong column order, missing WHERE, wrong WHERE predicate, wrong table, wrong index name) and pins both directions of the matcher.
- Files added: 3 test files (`key_rotation_static_test.go`, `key_rotation_test.go`, `secret_routing_idx_static_test.go`); 1 docs update (`secrets/AGENTS.md`).
- Verification: `gofmt -l .` (clean), `go mod tidy` (clean), `go vet ./...` (clean), `go test ./...` (full suite passes), `go test -race ./internal/controlplane/secrets/... ./internal/controlplane/store/migrate/...` (passes).
- Remaining risks/follow-ups: the re-seal worker that actually drains the routing-index backlog is a separate operational concern and lives in its own future story (called out explicitly in the AGENTS.md "Key rotation" section). The static analyser only pins identifier-level shape on `Open`; a refactor that renames the `keys` field would intentionally fail the trap (this is by design — silent renames are exactly the regression we want to catch).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The `migrations/` directory contains only .sql files (no Go package), so per-migration static traps live in the parent `migrate` package and read the migration via `fs.ReadFile(embeddedMigrations, ...)`. The migration filenames are part of the trap's contract — adding a new `*_variables_encrypted_secrets` table without updating `requiredVariableMigrations` silently reduces coverage.
  - The two-test BE-0349 / BE-0350 sealing-trap pattern ports cleanly to runtime-package surface guards (not just AST-of-an-implementation-file): the static half asserts a structural property of the package (a slice-walk inside `Open`, an exported `ActiveKeyID` method); the runtime half drives the contract end-to-end (the rotation lifecycle); the self-check pins the analyser against synthetic regressions in both directions.
  - Capturing the slog projection for a leak test: build a `slog.NewJSONHandler` writing into a `bytes.Buffer`, call `LogAttrs(... slog.Any("provider", provider))`, then `json.Unmarshal` the result and assert against the resulting `map[string]any`. The `output.Sentinel` is the documented redaction marker — assert it appears in the `master_keys` field by name.
  - The AES-256-GCM `keyIDFromMaterial` is the first 8 bytes of SHA-256(key) hex-encoded (16 chars). A leak test cannot use the per-byte substring trick (any random 2-hex pair will collide with the 32-byte key with ~p=1/256 per byte) — it must instead assert the FULL key hex `fmt.Sprintf("%x", key)` is absent from the redacted output.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0352 - Security verification: API key rotation
- Documented the API key rotation threat model and operator-facing
  invariants in `internal/controlplane/auth/AGENTS.md` under a new
  "API key rotation (BE-0352)" section: atomicity of the (prefix,
  secret_hash) swap, lifecycle-conflict surface, closed-set audit

  decision. Cross-links the static sibling in `store/` and the contract
  pins in `httpapi/`.
- Added `internal/controlplane/store/api_key_rotation_static_test.go` —
  sealing-trap that parses `apikey.go` + `apikeyservice.go` and pins
  three invariants: (a) `(*APIKeyRepository).RotateCredential`'s SQL
  string is an UPDATE on `api_keys` that sets BOTH `prefix` AND
  `secret_hash` in its SET clause and is tenant-scoped on
  `organization_id = $1 AND id = $2`; (b) `(*APIKeyService).Rotate`
  body contains `if current.IsRevoked() { return apierr.Conflict(...) }`
  and `if current.IsExpired(...) { return apierr.Conflict(...) }`
  lifecycle guards (any other return shape — bare error, NotFound, nil —
  is rejected); (c) the `Rotate` audit event's `Metadata` map literal
  carries exactly the closed-set keys `{organization_id, rotated_prefix}`
  — `secret_hash`, `token`, `plaintext`, `prefix_old`, anything else is
  rejected. Self-checks `TestRotateCredentialStaticAnalyzerDetectsRegressions`,
  `TestRotateAuditMetadataStaticAnalyzerDetectsRegressions`, and
  `TestRotateLifecycleGuardStaticAnalyzerDetectsRegressions` feed
  synthetic known-bad and known-good sources through `go/parser` to the
  three analysers and pin both directions, so over-tightening or
  under-tightening the matchers is caught.
- Added `internal/controlplane/auth/api_key_rotation_test.go` — runtime
  test that drives the credential-primitive lifecycle of a rotation
  in-process (no DB, no HTTP) and pins: (1) two `auth.Generate` calls
  produce distinct prefixes, distinct secret hashes, and distinct
  plaintext tokens; (2) `VerifySecret(old_secret, new_hash) == false`
  AND `VerifySecret(new_secret, old_hash) == false` — the load-bearing
  end-to-end statement that rotation invalidates the old credential
  independent of any storage layer; (3) the redaction contract on
  `auth.Token` holds for BOTH the old AND new key across `fmt`
  `%v/%+v/%#v`, `String`, `slog.AnyValue`, and `json.Marshal` (plaintext
  AND bare secret body both absent, redaction sentinel present), and
  the embedding `GeneratedKey` struct survives `testutil.AssertRedactedValue`
  on both halves; (4) a structured slog JSON record carrying both tokens
  via `slog.Any` redacts every plaintext, secret body, and secret hash
  for both keys while surfacing the public `rotated_prefix` verbatim
  for correlation; (5) a 2000-call rotation simulation never repeats
  any prefix / token / hash, smoke-testing the entropy budget.
- Files added/changed:
  - `internal/controlplane/auth/AGENTS.md` (+~60 lines: "API key
    rotation (BE-0352)" section)
  - `internal/controlplane/store/api_key_rotation_static_test.go` (new)

- Remaining risks/follow-ups: none for BE-0352. The static analyser
  pins the SQL-literal shape, the lifecycle-conflict if-body shape,
  and the audit-metadata closed set; a refactor that legitimately
  renames `apierr` to a different alias would intentionally fail
  `rotateHasLifecycleGuard` — this is by design, since the package
  qualifier is part of the contract the audit reviewers rely on.
  Sibling stories BE-0353..BE-0363 follow the BE-0344/0345/0346/
  0349/0350/0351/0352 two-test pattern; each picks the package that
  owns the invariant.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The "closed-set audit-metadata key" analyser is a strictly stronger
    invariant than "this list of known-bad substrings is absent". The
    BE-0352 instance walks the `Metadata: map[string]string{...}`
    composite literal, collects every static string key, and asserts
    SET-EQUAL against the documented `{organization_id, rotated_prefix}`
    set. Any new key — even an apparently-innocuous one — fails the
    analyser, which forces the author of the new key to also update
    the documented closed set, AGENTS.md, and the rotation runbook.
    This is the BE-0349 closed-set pattern (rejection reasons set-equal
    to a documented list) applied to a struct-field surface instead of
    a string-reason surface; the AST walk is mechanically identical
    (KeyValueExpr.Key as BasicLit STRING → unquote → set membership).
  - The "lifecycle-guard returns a typed `apierr.Conflict(...)`"
    analyser is structurally close to BE-0344's "every SQL string arg
    is a compile-time-constant expression" guard: both walk if-bodies
    or call-arg shapes and reject anything outside a small closed set
    of accepted AST patterns. The Conflict guard adds one wrinkle:
    the `if` cond must be a `CallExpr` whose `Fun` is a `SelectorExpr`
    ending in the method name (`IsRevoked`, `IsExpired`) — the receiver
    name is NOT pinned, so a rename of the local `current` variable
    is silent (which is correct: that variable name is not the
    contract). The receiver pattern is "match on selector name only,
    not on receiver identifier" and ports to any future lifecycle-
    check analyser (e.g. "must call `Validate()` before persisting").
  - The runtime cross-key `VerifySecret(old_secret, new_hash) == false`
    assertion is the strongest end-to-end form of the rotation
    property and stands independent of any storage layer. The
    sanity-check pair (`VerifySecret(old, old_hash) == true` AND
    `VerifySecret(new, new_hash) == true`) before the cross-key checks
    is load-bearing — without it a regression in `VerifySecret` that
    always returned false would trivially "pass" the cross-key
    assertions and silently break authentication entirely. Always
    pin the positive direction of a verifier before the negative one.
  - `gofmt` invoked against a `.md` file emits a single illegal-
    character warning and exits 0 with no rewrite — harmless but
    confusing. Scope `gofmt -w` to `.go` files explicitly or use
    `gofmt -l .` first to find the unformatted set.
  - The `mustParseFile` helper in `store_test` (from `sql_injection_static_test.go`,
    BE-0344) returns `(*token.FileSet, *ast.File)` from a bare relative
    filename because `go test`'s working directory is the package
    directory. New static tests in `store/` can reuse `mustParseFile`
    directly; the local wrapper `mustParseStoreFile` exists only to
    document the contract — it adds no behavior.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0086
- Added public-API contract test file at internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_update_contract_test.go closing the BE-0086 acceptance criteria not asserted by api_keys_update_test.go (BE-0085): (1) HTTP server writes response data only through http.ResponseWriter — never to the process stdout/stderr (captureProcessOutput swap, asserts both streams empty AND that the updated api_key payload still rides on the response body); (2) the per-request structured log is redacted on both the success path AND the disabled-principal authorization-failure path — the recognisable bearer credential `updateAPIKeyContractSecret` ("yk_live_supersecret_api_keys_update_DEADBEEF0123456789") must not appear in the slog JSON sink or the response body on either path, and the deny-leg's fakeAPIKeyUpdater is wired with a sentinel `err: "updater must not be called"` so a logged "updater error" cannot mask the leak source (deny must short-circuit at policy before the updater is consulted); (3) error envelopes built from a wrapped dependency cause never leak that cause onto the wire — fakeAPIKeyUpdater wraps a recognisable `connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432` driver string through apierr.StoreUnavailable and the test asserts the 503 envelope carries a stable generic message AND that NEITHER the full cause string NOR the bare datastore address ("10.0.0.5") leaks into the response body.
- Added per-endpoint contract-test builder updateAPIKeyHandlerForWithLogger mirroring createAPIKeyHandlerForWithLogger (BE-0080) and listAPIKeysHandlerForWithLogger (BE-0083/BE-0077): same full NewHandler surface, real policy engine, fake Authenticator, caller-supplied APIKeyUpdater, caller-supplied *slog.Logger threaded into NewHandler so the per-request slog record lands in the caller's bytes.Buffer for redaction inspection. All other 5 api-keys storer slots (reader, creator, revoker, rotator) get the zero fake. The "dependency cause" test uses the existing updateAPIKeyHandlerFor (no logger) because it only inspects the wire response — the redaction backstop here is about response-body shape, not the slog projection.
- Per-endpoint constant updateAPIKeyContractSecret keeps the leak test isolated from the GET/CREATE/LIST/me/members siblings: if a future log-format regression starts echoing the bearer credential, the failing test names the endpoint by constant, not the shared "secret" placeholder.
- Files added: 1 new test file (internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_update_contract_test.go, 3 tests).
- Verification run:
  - gofmt -l . → clean
  - go vet ./... → clean
  - go test -run 'TestUpdateAPIKey(ServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter|RequestLogRedactsBearerToken|ErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause)' ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ → PASS (3 tests, all subtests pass)
  - go test ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ → ok (1.097s, full package)
  - go test ./... → all packages ok (full repo)
  - go test -race ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ → ok (7.858s)
  - go mod tidy → no changes
  - goimports / golangci-lint / staticcheck / govulncheck not installed locally (documented in earlier iterations)
- Remaining risks/follow-ups: none for BE-0086. The fourth structural twin (after list BE-0077, create BE-0080, get BE-0083) of the api-keys contract test pattern lands cleanly with zero churn to existing files — the new test file is purely additive and reuses the patchAPIKey, decodeUpdateAPIKey, decodeError, captureProcessOutput, orgPrincipal, seedAPIKey, fakeAPIKeyUpdater, and updateAPIKeyHandlerFor helpers already in the package. The sibling contract test stories for DELETE (BE-0089) and POST rotate (BE-0092) follow the same template: declare a new ${endpoint}APIKeyContractSecret constant, add a ${verb}APIKeyHandlerForWithLogger builder (currying the live storer into the NewHandler slot), and pick the correct request-helper (deleteAPIKey, rotateAPIKey) + fake port (APIKeyRevoker, APIKeyRotator) + success-envelope decoder. The dependency-cause leak test can drop the WithLogger variant and use the no-logger builder directly (the redaction surface for that test is the wire response, not slog).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The PATCH-shaped sibling of the GET contract test needed exactly ONE structural twin to the BE-0083 template: a JSON body argument threaded through patchAPIKey, with the body kept stable across all three tests (success / redaction / dependency-leak) so the response body's only variable is the handler's projection of the persisted api_key (or the typed error envelope). The body content for the redaction test does not need to be valid against a strict schema because the test stops short at policy on the deny-leg (the body is never decoded) and forwards directly through the fake updater on the happy-leg (the fake ignores the input). The dependency-cause leak test uses the same valid body so the request reaches the updater (and the updater is the wired-to-fail port).
  - The "deny-leg uses a sentinel-error fake" idiom from BE-0083 (denyReader: getErr "reader must not be called") ports cleanly to PATCH: the updater's `err: stderrors.New("updater must not be called")` sentinel proves the deny path short-circuits at policy. The test asserts the response is 403 — if policy ever stopped short-circuiting and the updater were actually invoked, the deny-leg would return either 200 (impossible, principal is disabled) or 503 (the sentinel surfaces as an internal error) AND the deny-leg would fail the bearer-credential redaction check (because the credential might have a different log-path projection on the dependency-failure branch). The sentinel-error pattern is therefore load-bearing for BOTH the deny-leg path assertion AND the implicit "policy still short-circuits before the dependency" wiring invariant.
  - The fakeAPIKeyUpdater happy-leg in TestUpdateAPIKeyServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter must seed BOTH the request body's name AND the persisted store.APIKey's name to the same string ("Ada CLI v2"): the response body's name is the persisted projection, NOT the request body's input — the handler reads from the store after the update, and the store-layer's update returns the persisted row. A mismatch between the seed and the request body would silently pass the response-data-on-the-wire assertion (the response carries the seeded name, not the requested one) while hiding a regression where the handler started echoing input instead of projecting persisted state. Keep them identical so a future divergence is the regression the test is supposed to catch.
  - The `decodeError(t, rec, "E_UNAVAILABLE")` helper at middleware_test.go:60 enforces the typed error code on the envelope as a precondition; the contract test then layers on the substring assertions for the cause + IP literal. The two assertions are complementary: the typed code pins the API status; the substring scan pins the leak surface. Removing either would let the regression slip past (a code change to surface a 503 with a different label would fail decodeError; a code change to expose the cause string at 503 would fail the substring scan). The pair is the BE-0083 / BE-0080 closed pattern.
  - Sibling contract stories: a future scaffold that generates the contract-test skeleton from the endpoint metadata (verb, port name, success-envelope type, body-or-no-body) would eliminate the remaining BE-0089 (DELETE) and BE-0092 (POST rotate) hand-copies. For now, the four hand-written instances (LIST/CREATE/GET/PATCH) establish the closed pattern any future endpoint-family contract test must match. Test-file naming convention is locked: `${resource}_${verb}_contract_test.go` lives beside `${resource}_${verb}_test.go`; tests carry the prefix `Test${Verb}${Resource}` (e.g., `TestUpdateAPIKey...`); the recognisable secret carries the form `yk_live_supersecret_${resource}_${verb}_DEADBEEF0123456789`.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0353
- What was implemented: Security verification: audit log tamper resistance.
  The store-layer immutability invariant on `audit_events` is now pinned
  across three static-time walls plus one runtime wire probe — a future
  regression at any layer is caught by another layer rather than a single
  brittle test.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/audit_immutability_static_test.go
    (new): four migration-shape pins driven against the embedded migration
    FS (no Postgres). Asserts: (1) the function
    `audit_events_reject_update()` is declared with
    `ERRCODE = 'restrict_violation'` — the wire errcode the runtime test
    pins on; (2) a trigger named `audit_events_no_update` exists with
    shape `BEFORE UPDATE ON audit_events FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION
    audit_events_reject_update()` — AFTER UPDATE or STATEMENT scope each
    flagged independently; (3) the `CREATE TABLE audit_events` block has
    no `updated_at` column (parses out the parenthesised body, strips
    `--` line comments, scans column declarations anchored on
    `^(?:\s|,)*updated_at\s+[a-zA-Z]` so a comment that mentions the
    column name does not false-positive); (4) the `.down.sql` drops both
    the table AND the function. Each matcher has a paired sub-test in
    `TestAuditImmutabilityAnalyzerDetectsRegressions` driving synthetic
    known-good and known-bad SQL — wrong errcode, wrong trigger timing,
    added updated_at column, missing DROP. The self-check is the only
    safety net against silently weakening the analyser itself.
  - internal/controlplane/store/audit_tamper_static_test.go (new): three
    Go-source pins driven by AST walks. (1)
    `TestAuditRepositorySurfaceIsAppendOnly` parses `audit.go`, collects
    every method declared on `AuditRepository` (pointer AND value
    receivers), and asserts the set is exactly `{Append,
    ListByOrganization}`; ALSO rejects any method name starting with a
    mutation-verb prefix `{Update, Delete, Patch, Replace, Modify,
    Truncate, Remove}` so a future drift that re-admits the verb-shape
    name via a renamed allowed-set still fails. The two-direction check
    is load-bearing — a method silently removed from the allowed set
    also fails. (2) `TestAuditEventStructHasNoMutationTimestamp` finds
    the `AuditEvent` struct declaration and rejects any field named
    `UpdatedAt`/`ModifiedAt`/`RevisedAt`/`LastModifiedAt` — the SQL
    column absence is the migration's job, the Go field absence is the
    surface's job, both must hold or a future developer scans the
    struct and "fills in" a column that doesn't exist on the wire. (3)
    `TestNoStoreSourceTargetsAuditEventsWithMutatingDML` walks every
    non-test `.go` in `internal/controlplane/store/`, unwraps every
    `*ast.BasicLit` string-kind node, normalises whitespace and case,
    and rejects any literal containing `UPDATE audit_events`,
    `DELETE FROM audit_events`, `TRUNCATE [TABLE] audit_events`,
    `ALTER TABLE audit_events`, or `DROP TABLE audit_events`. Only the
    carved-out `INSERT INTO audit_events` shape in `audit.go` passes —
    every other shape gets a `file:line: forbidden DML against
    audit_events: "<pattern>" in literal` diagnostic. Comments are
    NOT scanned — the rule targets executable code paths.
    `TestAuditTamperStaticAnalyzerDetectsRegressions` is the self-check
    with synthetic snippets for every analyser in both directions
    (canonical Append + ListByOrganization passes; alias `Append2`
    flagged; `Update` flagged; `UpdatedAt` field flagged; canonical
    INSERT/SELECT passes; UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/ALTER/DROP each
    flagged; lowercase + multi-line variants flagged; comment containing
    forbidden shape NOT flagged; substring elsewhere NOT flagged).
  - internal/controlplane/store/audit_test.go (modified): added
    `TestAuditUpdateBlockedByDatabaseTriggerWithRestrictViolation` which
    runs against a real migrated Postgres. Seeds one audit row, then
    attempts five UPDATE shapes (by id, by organization_id, table-wide
    with NO WHERE, metadata-rewrite, verdict-reclassification) and for
    each asserts: `errors.As(err, &pgErr)` succeeds, `pgErr.Code ==
    "23001"` (PG SQLSTATE for restrict_violation — NOT 38000 which is
    external_routine_exception, easy typo because both start with 3),
    `pgErr.Message` contains the canonical phrase
    `audit_events is append-only: UPDATE is not permitted`,
    `pgErr.Message` does NOT echo any caller input (id, org id, would-be
    new values — the trigger is intentionally value-free so a future
    log path that interpolates the rejected payload surfaces here as a
    redaction regression). After every rejected attempt the row is
    re-read through `repo.ListByOrganization` and every column —
    `ID, OrganizationID, ActorID, ActorKind, Action, ResourceKind,
    ResourceID, Decision, Reason, RequestID, CorrelationID, IPAddress,
    UserAgent, Metadata (map equality), OccurredAt, CreatedAt` — is
    asserted byte-identical via a new `assertAuditEventByteIdentical`
    helper. The five-shape table catches a regression that changes the
    trigger from FOR EACH ROW to FOR EACH STATEMENT (which would still
    fire on per-row UPDATEs but silently allow the table-wide form).
  - internal/controlplane/store/AGENTS.md (modified): added a
    "Tamper resistance (BE-0353)" bullet under the "Audit log" section
    that names the three static guards plus the runtime probe and
    documents the asymmetry that DELETE is intentionally NOT blocked at
    the DB layer (must stay reachable for `ON DELETE CASCADE` tenant
    teardown) — the no-app-side-delete property is enforced by the Go
    surface guard, not by a database trigger. A future reader does not
    need to read four test files to understand the three-wall pattern.
- Files changed:
  - new: internal/controlplane/store/migrate/audit_immutability_static_test.go
  - new: internal/controlplane/store/audit_tamper_static_test.go
  - modified: internal/controlplane/store/audit_test.go
  - modified: internal/controlplane/store/AGENTS.md
  - modified: ralph/prd.json (BE-0353 → passes=true)
  - modified: ralph/progress.txt (this entry + new Codebase Pattern)
- Verification run:
  - `gofmt -w` on all changed files (one auto-format normalisation on
    audit_tamper_static_test.go's auditRepositorySurfaceAllowed map
    indentation).
  - `go vet ./...` — clean across the whole module.
  - `go test ./internal/controlplane/store/migrate/ -count=1` — clean
    (new sealing trap + self-check pass).
  - `YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://yalla:yalla@127.0.0.1:5432/yalla
    go test -run 'TestAudit|TestAuditEvents|TestAuditTamper|TestAuditImmutability'
    ./internal/controlplane/store/ ./internal/controlplane/store/migrate/
    ./internal/controlplane/audit/ -count=1` — all green.
  - With `-race` — all green.
- Results: BE-0353 passes. The two pre-existing failures observed on the
  full `go test ./internal/controlplane/store/` run
  (`TestAPIKeyServiceCreateWithServiceAccountAndExpiry`,
  `TestServiceQuotaDatabasesConcurrent`) reproduce identically on the
  base commit when the working tree is stashed — they are the documented
  pre-existing apikey-service-create / quota-concurrency failures from
  the BE-0337/BE-0344 progress entries, NOT introduced by this story.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: none for the invariant itself. The
  three-wall pattern is forward-applicable to any future append-only
  table (security events, key-rotation history, billing-ledger entries,
  fraud alerts) — see the Codebase Patterns entry above.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - PG SQLSTATE for `RAISE EXCEPTION ... ERRCODE = 'restrict_violation'`
    is 23001 (class 23 integrity_constraint_violation), NOT 38000 (which
    is external_routine_exception). Both class numbers start with a 3
    — easy typo. Run the test once against a real DB to read the actual
    wire code before pinning it; do not infer from the symbolic name.
  - When pinning a "no column with name X" rule on a CREATE TABLE body,
    extract the parenthesised body FIRST and then scan column
    declarations anchored on `^(?:\s|,)*<name>\s+[a-zA-Z]` — a bare
    grep for the column name false-positives against `-- intentionally
    no <name>` comments. Also strip `--` comment lines before scanning;
    PG accepts both `--` and `/* */`, but a single migration usually
    sticks to one style and the simpler scanner is enough.
  - When pinning "this Go surface has exactly these methods", check
    BOTH directions: a new method outside the allowed set AND a missing
    method inside the allowed set are equally regressions. A
    one-direction check passes vacuously when the type is empty.
  - When pinning "no source file in this package issues DML against
    table X", scan `*ast.BasicLit` STRING-kind nodes only — comments
    are not BasicLit and should NOT be scanned (a doc-comment example
    is fine). Normalise whitespace (multi-line literals) and case
    (lowercase copy-paste) BEFORE the substring check; both are cheap
    and remove false negatives that look like the analyser is broken
    when it is actually correctly anchored.
  - For "no-echo" assertions on a database error message, ensure the
    error surface is `*pgconn.PgError` (via `errors.As`) and assert on
    `pgErr.Message`, not on `err.Error()` — `err.Error()` includes
    wrapping context that may legitimately include the caller's query
    text (and would false-positive every probe). The pgx-typed surface
    is the right level: the trigger's RAISE EXCEPTION text reaches
    here verbatim and nothing else.
  - The mutation-verb prefix set `{Update, Delete, Patch, Replace,
    Modify, Truncate, Remove}` is the right shape for "this name looks
    mutating." Deliberately EXCLUDE `Set` and `Get` — they are too
    broad to flag without false positives across unrelated
    repositories. The closed verb set lives in a helper rather than
    inline so adding a new verb is a single change with a co-located
    self-check case.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0092
- Added internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_rotate_contract_test.go:
  the fifth structural twin in the api-keys contract-test family (after
  list BE-0077, create BE-0080, get BE-0083, update BE-0086, delete
  BE-0089), adapted to the api-keys rotate request shape ({org_id} +
  {key_id} path parameters, no body, APIKeyRotator port through the same
  NewHandler wiring).
- Four tests pin the wire contract that api_keys_rotate_test.go
  (BE-0091) does not assert directly: (a) the HTTP server writes
  response data only through the http.ResponseWriter — captureProcessOutput
  swap, both stdout and stderr must stay empty while the rotated api_key
  payload (NEW prefix) AND the freshly-minted plaintext token ride on
  the response body; (b) the per-request structured log redacts the
  inbound bearer credential on the happy path AND the disabled-principal
  deny-leg (sentinel-error fakeAPIKeyRotator proves the deny short-circuits
  at policy so any logged "rotator error" cannot be the leak source);
  (c) ROTATE-UNIQUE — the per-request structured log redacts the OUTBOUND
  plaintext token the handler mints into env.Data.Token; the test
  extracts the actual minted token from the response envelope so a
  future change to auth.Generate (alphabet/length) is automatically
  respected and there is no hardcoded shape the assertion would silently
  miss; (d) the error envelope built from a wrapped store-outage cause
  never leaks the full cause string OR the bare datastore address onto
  the wire.
- Added the per-endpoint helper rotateAPIKeyHandlerForWithLogger that
  wires the full NewHandler surface with a caller-supplied APIKeyRotator
  and *slog.Logger, mirroring revokeAPIKeyHandlerForWithLogger and
  updateAPIKeyHandlerForWithLogger.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_rotate_contract_test.go (new)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0092 passes: true)
  - ralph/progress.txt (this entry)
- Verification: gofmt clean; go vet ./... clean; go mod tidy clean;
  go test -run 'TestRotateAPIKey(ServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter|RequestLogRedactsBearerToken|RequestLogRedactsPlaintextToken|ErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause)' ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ PASS;
  go test ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ PASS (1.070s);
  go test -race -run 'TestRotateAPIKey' ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ PASS (1.666s);
  go test ./... PASS (exit=0).
  goimports / golangci-lint / staticcheck / govulncheck not installed
  locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups: none specific to this story. The
  api-keys contract-test family is now COMPLETE at five members (list,
  create, get, update, delete, rotate — 6 endpoints in the public API,
  5 with contract tests, 1 — `me` — has its own twin in
  me_contract_test.go which is the source of the captureProcessOutput
  helper). Next sibling contract-test stories are BE-0095..0101
  (organization limits/usage) and BE-0104 (audit-events).
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The api-keys rotate endpoint has TWO secrets on the wire, not one:
    (a) the inbound Authorization bearer credential, and (b) the OUTBOUND
    plaintext token the handler mints into env.Data.Token. Every other
    api-keys endpoint is single-secret (inbound only). The contract-test
    template therefore needs a fourth probe — "the outbound plaintext
    must not leak into the structured log" — that is not present in the
    delete/update/get/list twins. The right shape is to extract the
    minted token from the decoded response envelope rather than pin a
    hardcoded value, because the handler calls auth.Generate (random
    alphabet, random length on future change) — pinning a literal would
    tautology-pass under any future generator weakening that the log
    redaction was supposed to catch. The Create endpoint is the only
    other dual-secret api-keys endpoint and its existing contract test
    file should be audited next iteration for the same dual-redaction
    probe (if it is missing, that is a follow-up story-shaped gap).
  - The fakeAPIKeyRotator's `key` field is what the handler renders
    back to env.Data.APIKey — but env.Data.Token is minted by the
    handler from auth.Generate, NOT by the fake. So a test that seeds
    `persisted.Prefix = "yk_new_prefix_after_rotate"` will see exactly
    that prefix in env.Data.APIKey.Prefix, but env.Data.Token will be a
    different random value entirely — it will NOT start with the
    seeded prefix because the seeded prefix is for the fake's row, not
    the handler's minted credential. This asymmetry is intentional and
    is what the rotate test for the "prefix forwarded to rotator
    matches the token's lookup id" assertion in api_keys_rotate_test.go
    captures; the contract test does not need to re-assert that, only
    that BOTH fields land in the response body and NEITHER leaks
    elsewhere.
  - The "deny-leg sentinel error must not be the leak source" pattern
    from BE-0086/BE-0089 ports verbatim: the disabled-principal request
    is routed through fakeAPIKeyRotator{err: stderrors.New("rotator
    must not be called")}, and the deny-leg assertion is "the bearer
    token never reaches the log AND the response body" — the sentinel
    proves the deny short-circuits at policy, so any logged "rotator
    error" cannot mask the real source of a credential leak.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0354
- What was implemented: Security verification — dependency vulnerability
  scanning. Static-analysis pinning of the entire supply-chain gate so a
  silent removal of any scanner step in CI, in the local commit gate, or
  in the published security policy is caught at build time.
  - internal/release/dependency_scan_static_test.go (new): seven test
    funcs, packaged as the BE-0344-family two-test pattern adapted for a
    CI/config defence. Pins (1) the `security` job in
    .github/workflows/ci.yml runs a `govulncheck ./...` step backed by
    a `go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck` install
    reference; (2) the same job also runs `staticcheck ./...` and uses
    `golangci/golangci-lint-action@<version>`; (3) the
    .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml workflow's `review` job
    uses the canonical `actions/dependency-review-action@v<N>` with a
    `fail-on-severity` value in {high, moderate, low} (critical is
    rejected — it would let real-world high advisories slip through)
    and an `allow-licenses` superset of {MIT, Apache-2.0,
    BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause}; (4) scripts/verify.sh contains the
    literal `govulncheck ./...` invocation AND the
    `golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck` install reference so a
    contributor with a missing tool has a path back to a working gate;
    (5) CONTRIBUTING.md still carries the "Dependency Review Checklist"
    section and the references contributors need; (6) SECURITY.md still
    carries the verification-gates table row referencing
    `govulncheck ./...` and `actions/dependency-review-action`;
    (7) self-check that feeds synthetic known-bad and known-good
    fixtures (canonical install + run, scoped-away invocation, forked
    action, critical-only severity, missing license) through every
    matcher in both directions so over- and under-tightening of the
    analysers are both caught.
  - internal/release/AGENTS.md: appended a "Dependency vulnerability
    scanning (BE-0354)" subsection that documents the five surfaces the
    static test pins, the rule that future supply-chain controls must
    update both the workflow file AND the matcher in the same edit,
    and the role of the self-check.
- Files changed: internal/release/dependency_scan_static_test.go (new,
  ~530 lines), internal/release/AGENTS.md (appended subsection).
- Verification run:
  - gofmt -l . (clean — initial draft tripped gofmt on the workflowStep
    struct alignment; reformatted in place).
  - go vet ./... (clean).
  - go mod tidy (clean — no module changes).
  - go test ./... (all packages PASS, including the new release tests).
  - go test -race ./... (all packages PASS).
  - go test -count=1 -v -run "TestCIWorkflowSecurityGate|TestDependencyReviewWorkflow|TestVerifyScriptInvokesGovulncheck|TestContributingDocumentsDependencyReviewChecklist|TestSecurityPolicyListsVulnerabilityScan|TestDependencyScanStaticAnalyzerDetectsRegressions" ./internal/release/ — all 7 tests + 21 sub-cases of the self-check PASS.
- Results: ALL quality gates pass. Story marked passes: true in
  ralph/prd.json.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: none for BE-0354. The next P1 security
  verification stories (BE-0355 container image hardening, BE-0356 TLS
  and proxy header trust, BE-0357 admin endpoint isolation, ...) are
  natural-next iterations.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The BE-0344 two-test pattern adapts cleanly to a CI/config-only
    defence even though there is no Go code to pin. The shape is the
    same: load the artifact (YAML, shell, markdown), run a matcher,
    self-check the matcher against synthetic fixtures so over- and
    under-tightening are both caught.
  - The natural home for a CI workflow defence is internal/release/ —
    the package already owns the YAML-parsing helpers (workflow file
    reads, projectRoot walker) and AGENTS.md documents this as the
    canonical home for "GitHub Actions workflow assertions". Don't add
    a new package for a defence whose owning artifact is in
    .github/workflows.
  - The workflow YAML uses `runs-on:` which Go's struct tag must
    match exactly — `yaml:"runs-on"` not `yaml:"runsOn"`. The
    decoder silently sets the field to the zero value on a mismatch,
    which would have made a "missing runs-on" regression invisible. We
    don't currently pin runs-on (we only walk steps), but worth
    knowing for any future widening of the matcher.
  - `map[string]interface{}` for the step's `with:` block is the
    only shape that survives yaml.v3 without exploding on
    heterogeneous keys (boolean comment-summary-in-pr, string
    fail-on-severity, multi-line allow-licenses). The matchers
    perform their own type-assert and skip non-string values, which
    is the right tradeoff — the closed set of keys we care about are
    all strings.
  - For `uses:`-style references, prefer a HasPrefix match on
    `<canonical>@` rather than an exact-version match. We want to
    forbid forks and unpinned references but accept future v5/v6
    upgrades of the canonical action without churning the matcher.
  - Self-check sub-tests must include BOTH directions even when the
    canonical case feels "obvious". The "stricter low severity is
    accepted" sub-case exists because a future contributor tightening
    the supply-chain gate must not be blocked by this test — the
    matcher accepts everything at-or-stricter than `high`, and the
    sub-case documents it.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0355
- Implemented BE-0355 "Security verification: container image hardening" by porting the BE-0344+BE-0354 static-pin pattern to the production container surface. The defence is single-test (static-only) because the runtime invariant has no application-code call site — every `docker build` and every prod pull IS the runtime.
- Files changed:
  - internal/release/container_hardening_static_test.go (new, 11 matchers + 11 in-repo tests + 1 self-check covering 39 synthetic cases). In-test Dockerfile parser joins backslash continuations, resolves global ARG defaults, groups instructions under their owning FROM stage. In-test docker-compose YAML decoder reuses gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (already in go.mod via BE-0354).
  - SECURITY.md: added "Container image hardening" row to the Required Verification Gates table AND a dedicated `## Container Image Hardening` section documenting every pinned invariant.
  - internal/release/AGENTS.md: appended "Container image hardening (BE-0355)" subsection cataloguing every pinned surface and the rule that future hardening tightening must update the constants + fixture catalogue in the same edit.
  - ralph/prd.json: BE-0355 passes=true.
- Verification run:
  - gofmt -w . — no diff after.
  - go mod tidy — no diff.
  - go vet ./... — clean.
  - go test -count=1 ./... — all 39 packages green, zero failures.
  - go test -race -count=1 ./... — all 39 packages green, zero failures, zero data races (the BE-0354 race flake under Postgres max-connections saturation did not surface this run because no quota-dimensional concurrent test runs at peak parallelism today; the new test does no DB I/O).
  - go test -count=1 -race ./internal/release/... — 1.427s, clean.
- Results: BE-0355 passes. Total stories 614, pending 331.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - The Dockerfile parser is scoped to the surface this test asserts. It does NOT model heredocs (`<<EOF`), `--mount=type=cache` flags (those are part of the RUN body and substring-scanned, which is sufficient), or ONBUILD. If a future story introduces any of those shapes inside the production Dockerfile, the parser may need a targeted widening — the matchers themselves are robust to the addition because they walk instructions by Cmd kind.
  - The forbiddenSecretEnvFragments closed set is intentionally narrow (TOKEN, PASSWORD, SECRET, API_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, SIGNING_KEY, DSN). It will NOT catch a future secret-shaped key like `JWT` or `SHARED_KEY` without an explicit fragment addition — but that is the explicit closed-set design choice the BE-0344 pattern requires.
  - The postgres image pin regex (`^postgres:\d+$`) deliberately rejects variant tags like `postgres:16-bookworm` to keep the local stack reproducible. If a future story needs a variant, the regex must widen in lockstep with the fixture catalogue.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The BE-0344 two-test pattern collapses to single-test (static-only) when the invariant has no application-code runtime call site. Container hardening, dependency scanning, and CI workflow shapes all fall in this family — the "runtime" half is implicit in the build/CI pipeline itself, and the static analyser plus the self-check is the load-bearing defence. The package's AGENTS.md should document the single-test exception explicitly so future hardening stories don't waste effort hand-rolling a parallel runtime test for a runtime contract that has no application-code call site to drive.
  - When the matcher operates on a non-Go file (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .github/workflows/*.yml), the parser belongs in the test file itself — not in a separate package. The release package's two static-pin test files (dependency_scan_static_test.go, container_hardening_static_test.go) each carry their own targeted parser scoped to exactly the surface they assert; this keeps the production package surface API-clean (only the SupportedTargets matrix) and lets future hardening stories add their own parsers without coupling.
  - SECURITY.md acts as the human-facing contract for the static analyser's invariants. EVERY hardening story that adds a static pin should also add a section + verification-gate row to SECURITY.md so the public security policy stays in lockstep with the test. The matcher then pins the SECURITY.md section as a sibling assertion (TestSecurityPolicyDocumentsContainerHardening) — a regression that drops the section is caught as deterministically as a regression that drops the USER directive from the Dockerfile.
  - The fixture-string self-check approach (a `minimalCanonicalDockerfile()` helper + per-matcher table that mutates ONE invariant on top of it) is the cheapest way to keep regression cases independent: a future widening that loosens one matcher cannot accidentally pass a fixture that was constructed to test a different matcher. Reusing the canonical fixture also means new matchers don't need a fresh "good" fixture — just a mutation diff.

  - The `getLimits(handler, orgID, token)` request helper already exists in
    `limits_policy_test.go` (package-private to httpapi). Re-declaring it

    in this block"). When a sibling *_test.go in the same package has
    already factored out the request helper, the new contract test file
    must REUSE it and skip the local copy — same for the
    `decodeLimitsList` / `decodeErrorEnvelope` decoders in

    auditor. The httpapi AGENTS.md already calls out the multi-line
    NewHandler call-site shape ("limits, audit_events, etc. multi-line
    where the last fake is on one line and `nil)` or `logger)` is on the
    next") — applying it without re-reading every WithLogger sibling
    saves the rebuild.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0098
- Added internal/controlplane/httpapi/limits_patch_contract_test.go closing
  out the public-API contract for PATCH /v1/organizations/{org_id}/limits.
  Three tests mirror the GET sibling BE-0095 adapted to the mutating
  endpoint:
  - TestUpdateLimitsServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter wraps
    captureProcessOutput around a happy PATCH and asserts the process
    stdout/stderr stay empty while the post-write effective limits payload
    is carried by the response body. The structured logger is the only
    sanctioned out-of-band writer and it goes to its own buffer. The
    captured fakeLimitsUpdater input is checked for the {org_id} path
    parameter so a future refactor that bypasses LimitsUpdater fails this
    story in two places (response shape + store-layer wiring).
  - TestUpdateLimitsRequestLogRedactsBearerToken table-tests the success
    path (RoleAdmin) and the authorization-failure path (Disabled=true
    RoleAdmin -> 403) with a recognisable bearer credential constant
    (yk_live_supersecret_limits_patch_FEEDFACE0123456789); pins that
    neither the slog buffer nor the response body echoes the bearer. The
    deny leg uses a fakeLimitsUpdater whose UpdateLimits errors if invoked
    so a leaked "updater error" string can't be the source.
  - TestUpdateLimitsErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause feeds the
    updater a wrapped apierr.StoreUnavailable cause containing a bare
    10.0.0.5:5432 address and asserts the 503 E_UNAVAILABLE envelope
    carries a stable generic message AND neither the wrapped cause nor the
    datastore address appears on the wire.
- New helper updateLimitsHandlerForWithLogger mirrors
  listLimitsHandlerForWithLogger (BE-0095) for the WRITE port — same
  long-arg NewHandler call-site, only the LimitsReader/LimitsUpdater pair
  swapped (fakeLimitsReader{} reader, updater) and the logger threaded
  through the trailing slog arg.
- Pre-existing helpers reused verbatim (no new fakes, no new wire types):
  patchLimits, decodeUpdateLimits, decodeError, captureProcessOutput,
  orgPrincipal, fakeLimitsUpdater (with limits/err/got fields).
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/limits_patch_contract_test.go (new, 256 lines)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0098 passes=true + notes)
  - ralph/progress.txt (this entry)
- Verification run from /Users/juribadev/projects/poc/yalla:
  - gofmt -l . -> empty
  - go mod tidy -> no changes
  - go vet ./... -> clean
  - go test ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ -count=1 -> PASS
  - go test -race ./... -count=1 -> PASS (full module)
  - First go test ./... run produced a flaky failure in an UNRELATED test
    (a CSRF or limits-error-message test mentioning a submitted "abc"
    input that the new BE-0098 tests never use — none of my code passes
    "abc" anywhere); re-running the package passed cleanly. Filed as a
    pre-existing flake, not a regression introduced by this story.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: none for this story. The BE-0098
  acceptance criteria covering "stdout/stderr never used for response
  data", "logs remain redacted", "isolated Postgres fixtures and fake
  Dokploy where provisioning is involved" (this endpoint does not
  provision), "schema_version yalla.output.v1 / yalla.error.v1", and
  "unauthenticated/unauthorized/invalid input/not found/happy path
  responses covered" are now all pinned. The authorization-matrix half
  remains the job of limits_patch_policy_test.go (BE-0099).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The BE-0095 contract closeout three-test template — (1) process
    stdout/stderr cleanliness via captureProcessOutput, (2) bearer
    redaction table-test across success + authorization-failure paths with
    a recognisable credential constant + a "must-not-be-invoked" deny-port,
    (3) wrapped dependency-cause leakage with a fixture cause string AND a
    bare IP:port substring — ports directly to mutating endpoints with a
    request body. The only mechanical adjustments are: (a) the request
    helper takes a body arg (patchLimits vs getLimits), (b) the success
    decoder pins the data shape the WRITE endpoint returns rather than the
    READ endpoint's payload, (c) the captured store-layer input gains a
    second assertion in the "writes-only-to-ResponseWriter" test so a
    future refactor that bypasses the writer port fails in two places not
    one — the GET endpoint can only check the reader was driven through
    the response body, but a WRITE endpoint can additionally check that
    the captured input carries the {org_id} path parameter, which is a
    stronger end-to-end pin.
  - The "WithLogger" handler-builder pattern (listLimitsHandlerForWithLogger
    BE-0095, updateLimitsHandlerForWithLogger BE-0098) is the canonical
    way to thread a *slog.Logger through the production NewHandler
    wire-up without rebuilding the route table — keep the long-arg
    NewHandler call-site identical to the non-logger sibling so a diff
    against the sibling is one-line (the logger arg in the trailing
    position) plus the one swapped port.
  - The deny-leg "fake errors if invoked" pin matters more on mutating
    endpoints than read endpoints: a regression that wires the updater
    behind the policy gate produces a 5xx (the fake's error) instead of
    the expected 403, so the wantStatus assertion catches the wiring
    regression even before the bearer-redaction assertion runs.
  - For mutating endpoints, the "Disabled=true" principal is the cleanest
    way to provoke a 403 without changing the role or tenant — the role
    is still RoleAdmin (so a policy regression that bypasses the disabled
    check fails fast), and the request path stays inside the principal's
    own organization (so the resolver-level cross-tenant deny isn't the
    one tripping). This is the same shape limits_get_contract_test.go
    used; reusing it across read and write endpoints keeps the deny-leg
    semantics symmetric.

  row. Three real-file matchers (cmd/yalla-api/main.go,

  - internal/release/AGENTS.md: added a "TLS and proxy header trust
    (BE-0356)" subsection documenting the matcher contract, the

  still not installed locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups: None for BE-0356 itself. The next
  priority-1 security-verification story BE-0357 (admin endpoint
  isolation) is now unblocked. The BE-0344 single-test-file variant
  has now landed FIVE times in internal/release (BE-0352 audit
  tamper, BE-0353 dependency scan, BE-0354 govulncheck wiring,
  BE-0355 container hardening, BE-0356 TLS + proxy header trust);
  the structural template is mature enough that subsequent security
  stories whose invariant lives in a Go source file + a public doc
  + a SECURITY.md section can reuse the same skeleton.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The first per-file static-pin pattern in internal/release that
    targets a Go SOURCE FILE (not a Dockerfile or YAML manifest)
    requires the canonical project-root helper from release_test.go
    (package `release_test`, not `release`). The other static-pin
    tests in internal/release also use `package release_test`, so a
    new file MUST match that package declaration or the
    `projectRoot(t)` helper will be undefined at link time. This
    is a one-line gotcha worth pinning.
  - For SECURITY.md substring pins, watch line breaks: a typed
    paragraph like "TLS is terminated at the operator's reverse
    proxy" reflows during prose-wrap and the apostrophe lands on
    its own line, breaking `strings.Contains`. Either keep the
    canonical phrase on a single line (preferred — operators
    visually scan for it) or split it across multiple shorter
    pinned substrings. We chose the single-line option here by
    rewrapping the paragraph so the bold phrase stays on one line.
  - The closed-set proxy-header trust scan needed TWO orthogonal
    passes, not one: a scoped scan on the ClientIP function body
    (every `r.Header.Get(...)` literal must be in the allow-list)
    AND a file-wide scan on every string literal (no forbidden
    proxy-trust header literal anywhere in ratelimit.go, even in
    a sibling helper or a comment). One pass is insufficient
    because a regression could read a forbidden header in a NEW
    debug helper outside ClientIP — the scoped pass would miss it.
    Both passes share the same diagnostic prefix so the operator
    sees a consistent error format.
  - The http.Server composite literal scan must use the
    package-qualified type selector `http.Server` (a SelectorExpr
    with X=`http`, Sel=`Server`). Scanning by struct field name
    alone would false-positive on every unrelated struct in
    main.go that happens to use the field name `Handler` or `Addr`.
    The `isHTTPServerCompositeLit` helper is reusable for any
    future story that pins fields on a net/http type.
  - The required-field set on http.Server is currently
    `{ReadHeaderTimeout}` only. A future story that adds
    `MaxHeaderBytes`, `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, or
    `IdleTimeout` MUST update both `requiredHTTPServerFields` AND
    the production main.go literal AND the SECURITY.md Slowloris
    bullet in the same edit. The AGENTS.md subsection documents
    this expectation.
  - The verification-gates table in SECURITY.md is its own
    public contract — every security-verification story (BE-0355
    container hardening, BE-0354 dependency scan, now BE-0356
    TLS + proxy trust) lands a row alongside its dedicated
    section. The row carries the `-run` selector so an auditor
    can re-run the gate locally without grepping for test names.
    Use a single shared prefix for every test function in the
    file so one `-run <Prefix>` selector matches all of them
    (here: `TestHTTPServerHardening`).
