  now BE-0357 admin endpoint isolation) — the structural template
  is mature.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The BE-0356 Go-source-file variant of the BE-0355 single-test
    template scales naturally to "directory of source files"
    rather than a single named file. The trick is a small helper
    (`adminProductionFiles(t, root) -> []string`) that enumerates
    every non-`_test.go` `.go` under the in-scope directory plus
    any pinned entry binaries, sorted for determinism. Test files
    are deliberately skipped so a future runtime-shape regression
    test (e.g. a `httptest` probe of `/debug/pprof` asserting the
    `notFoundRecorder` envelope) can simulate the threat without
    tripping the gate. Future "no production source under D may
    do X" stories should adopt the same helper shape.
  - When parsing Go source for a static-pin matcher, choose the
    parser mode by what the matcher reads. Import-only matchers
    should use `parser.SkipObjectResolution|parser.ImportsOnly` —
    it's ~10x faster and avoids surprises from synthetic
    fixtures whose function bodies are deliberately ill-formed
    (the `findForbiddenAdminImports` self-check uses
    `_ = pprof.Handler` against a `package main` body that would
    otherwise need a real `pprof` declaration). Literal/selector
    matchers need the full parse and should use
    `parser.SkipObjectResolution|parser.ParseComments`. Mixing
    modes by matcher is the right call.
  - The `http.Server.Handler` regression has TWO equivalent
    shapes that the matcher must both reject: the field omitted
    entirely (zero value = nil interface) AND an explicit
    `Handler: nil` literal. The standard library documents both
    as falling back to `http.DefaultServeMux`. A static analyser
    that flags only the omission gives the gate a false sense of
    security — a contributor who knows the gate would write
    `Handler: nil` and slip past. Both shapes get the same
    diagnostic so the gate is honest.
  - For the private-mux contract on a single file
    (`internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go`), two orthogonal
    passes are required: a PRESENCE assertion (the function MUST
    call `http.NewServeMux()` somewhere in the file) AND an
    ABSENCE assertion (no SelectorExpr anywhere in the file may
    have `Sel.Name == "DefaultServeMux"`). A regression that
    builds a private mux for the customer surface AND ALSO hands
    a route to the default mux as a "debug aid" would slip past
    either pass in isolation — only the two together close the
    door. This is the SAME shape as BE-0356's "scoped pass on the
    ClientIP body + file-wide pass on every BasicLit" rule, and
    it generalises: when a security-verification story says
    "include X and exclude Y", encode each half as its own pass.
  - The synthetic self-check sub-test
    `TestAdminEndpointIsolationStaticAnalyzerDetectsRegressions`
    treats over-tightening and under-tightening as equally
    important to catch. Every required-presence rule, every
    forbidden-form rule, and every multi-regression composition
    gets its own fixture — including a known-GOOD fixture per
    matcher that MUST produce zero hits. Without the known-good
    fixtures, a too-aggressive matcher would silently fail on
    every PR. The BE-0356 pattern of one good fixture + one bad
    fixture per matcher dimension is the right granularity.
  - SECURITY.md "## Admin Endpoint Isolation" deliberately names
    every forbidden import path BY NAME (`net/http/pprof`,
    `expvar`, `golang.org/x/net/trace`) so a reader scanning the
    public security policy learns the closed set without needing
    to open the test file. Future security-verification stories
    whose contract has a closed-set component should do the same
    — the dual representation (test file as authority, doc as
    explanation) is the BE-0356 contract and it scales.

  BE-0355 container hardening, BE-0356 TLS + proxy header
  trust, BE-0357 admin endpoint isolation, now BE-0358 support
  access review). BE-0358 is the FIRST instance to pin
  invariants spanning three production packages in a single
  static file (store + policy + httpapi), confirming the
  template scales to multi-package contracts.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Multi-package static gates: when an invariant spans three
    production packages whose drift is meaningful in different
    ways (audit shape in store, capability binding in policy,
    wire-shape projection in httpapi), it is still cleanest to
    house the gate as ONE static-pin file in internal/release.
    The per-package AGENTS.md update points back to a single
    test file and a single SECURITY.md section, so a future
    contributor changing any of the three files learns where
    to look without grepping across release/{*/static_test.go}.
    The parseSupportFile helper takes the relative path so the
    same helper serves all three target files; the matchers
    take (*token.FileSet, *ast.File) so position diagnostics
    line up with the file under review.
  - Position-table correctness pitfall: an early draft of this
    test had separate `parseSupportFile` and `supportFileSet`
    helpers that each parsed the file into a DIFFERENT
    token.FileSet. The AST nodes carry token.Pos values that
    are only meaningful against the fset that parsed them;
    calling `fset.Position(node.Pos())` against a different
    fset returns "-" or a wildly wrong position. Future
    multi-file static gates should return (fset, file)
    together from one helper, OR thread a single fset through
    every parse call, OR re-parse the file each matcher
    invokes (slower but isolated). The "two helpers" shape is
    the trap.
  - Matcher self-check fixture-counting precision: when the
    matcher walks every *ast.Ident in the file (as
    findSupportCredMintRegressions does), an identifier
    appearing at BOTH a type declaration AND a value-position
    reference (e.g. `type APIKeyService struct{}` plus
    `*APIKeyService` field type) counts TWICE. The synthetic
    self-check wantHits MUST mirror this; otherwise the
    self-check passes accidentally because it under-counts.
    The fix is to either explicitly call out the dual-counting
    in the fixture's comment (the convention used here) or to
    fold both decl- and ref-position hits into a single
    diagnostic via a per-identifier "seen" set (rejected here
    because it would mask a genuine "declared but unused"
    regression).
  - Closed-set forbidden-identifier scans for "access-only"
    invariants: the credential-mint forbidden set is curated
    to the credential-bearing types in the local store
    package. A naive design would forbid imports of an
    "apikey" sub-package, but that breaks down inside a
    single-package store layer where APIKeyService is just
    another type in the same package. File-wide
    identifier-name scanning is the right shape for "this
    package must not reach for these named types"; the closed
    set documents the threat model and the AGENTS.md
    "extending this set" rule keeps it honest.
  - AGENTS.md subsection ordering: append every new
    security-verification subsection at the BOTTOM of the
    sequence (after the previous story's update-bottom
    rules). The chronological ordering means a contributor
    looking up the most recent template instance finds it at
    the bottom of the file without scrolling past unrelated
    older subsections.
  - SECURITY.md substring choice: the test pins
    output.NewRedactor (the actual constructor) rather than
    output.Redactor (a bare type name) in the
    requiredSupportSecuritySubstrings list because the
    constructor is what the store-layer service actually
    calls. Pinning the constructor catches a regression that
    swaps to a different constructor (a hypothetical
    output.NewNoopRedactor would be a quiet downgrade); the
    bare type name would match a passing reference and miss
    the swap.
  - The runtime evidence story for a static gate: where the
    invariant is "this method ALWAYS does X", the static gate
    is necessary (a runtime test cannot prove the property
    for every future call site) and SUFFICIENT (the runtime
    test confirms X works once). The pre-existing
    break_glass_test.go family already covers the "X works"
    runtime evidence, so BE-0358 is a static-only delivery.
    The threat-model comment block in the test file
    explicitly cross-references the runtime tests by name so
    a future reviewer learns where the runtime evidence
    lives without having to discover it.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0359 — Security verification: log redaction fuzzing
- What was implemented:
  - Added internal/output/redact_fuzz_test.go with four Go
    `Fuzz*` targets and one regression test pinning the
    documented scope exclusions:
      * FuzzRedactor_NoPanic — `*Redactor.Redact` never
        panics for any (secret, haystack) pair.
      * FuzzRedactor_ExplicitSecretNeverLeaks — a literal
        secret registered with `NewRedactor` never appears
        in `Redact`'s output for any haystack in scope.
      * FuzzRedactor_AuthorizationHeaderNeverLeaks — the
        bearer regex scrubs the value of Authorization /
        X-API-Key / X-Auth-Token lines for every casing.
      * FuzzRedactor_QueryTokenNeverLeaks — the queryToken
        regex scrubs the value of `?token=`, `?api_key=`,
        `?access_token=`, `?x-auth-token=` (and `_`/`-`
        variants) for every casing.
      * FuzzRedactor_Idempotent — `Redact(Redact(s)) ==
        Redact(s)` for every input within the contract
        scope.
      * TestRedactor_FuzzScopeExclusionsAreReal — pins the
        three documented scope exclusions so a future
        redactor change that closes a gap deliberately
        breaks this test.
    The seed corpus (`redactFuzzSeeds`) covers the hostile
    shapes log-redaction must survive: long inputs, invalid
    UTF-8, embedded control characters, regex metacharacters,
    mixed-case header / query keys, the sentinel literal,
    and the registered secret shape itself.
  - Threaded the contract scope into the package's
    AGENTS.md (`## Log redaction fuzzing (BE-0359)`) and a
    new top-level SECURITY.md section
    (`## Log Redaction Fuzzing`) that documents the threat
    model, the runtime evidence, the scope exclusions, and
    the no-live-secrets rule.
- Files changed:
  - internal/output/redact_fuzz_test.go (new — five tests).
  - internal/output/AGENTS.md (appended a `Log redaction
    fuzzing (BE-0359)` subsection at the bottom — five
    pinned invariants plus the rule for extending the
    seam).
  - SECURITY.md (new section between Support Access Review
    and Disclosure Timeline — threat model, runtime
    evidence, scope exclusions, no-live-secrets rule).
  - ralph/prd.json: BE-0359.passes = true.
  - ralph/progress.txt: this entry.

  The next priority-1 security-verification stories
  BE-0360 (environment variable redaction), BE-0361
  (Dokploy token isolation), BE-0362 (backup encryption),
  and BE-0363 (rate-limit bypass resistance) are
  unblocked. The seed-corpus regression net catches every
  scope-internal regression; the operator-opt-in `-fuzz`
  flag is the deeper net.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - **Fuzz harness vs. structural rules: pair markers
    with rules, not values.** The first revision of the
    Authorization / query fuzz targets asserted that the
    fuzz-supplied value did not appear in the redacted
    output. That is fragile: if the fuzz value happens
    to equal `"example"` (the static suffix the test
    constructs) the assertion fires a false positive.
    The robust shape is to bracket the value with a
    unique, fixed marker (e.g. `"FUZZAUTHMARKERXYZ"`)
    and assert that the marker never appears in the
    redacted output. The marker is the leak detector,
    independent of the value's bytes. Apply this
    pattern to every future fuzz target that proves
    "structural rule X scrubs the value half of
    transport Y".
  - **Regex value classes have surprising boundary
    characters.** Go's `regexp` `\s` is exactly
    `[\t\n\f\r ]` — vertical-tab (`\v`) is NOT in `\s`,
    but form-feed (`\f`) IS. The first revision of the
    query-token fuzz stripped only `\t \n \r ` from the
    fuzz-supplied value and left form-feed alone; a
    seed containing `\f` ended the regex match
    mid-value and the marker bracket survived,
    producing a false-positive leak. When constructing
    a fuzz-generated value that must traverse a regex
    value class without being cut short, strip every
    character in the regex's exclusion set including
    every member of Go's `\s` (`\t \n \f \r ` plus the
    explicit literals from the character class).
  - **Defence-in-depth rules interact under fuzz.**
    A fuzz value containing `AUTHORIZATION:`
    (substring shape) triggers the bearer regex when
    embedded in a URL, which consumes the rest of the
    URL up to the next CR/LF. The downstream
    query-param survival assertion (`&page=2` still
    present) fails — but the marker leak assertion
    still passes, because both rules contribute to
    scrubbing the value. The lesson: assert only the
    safety property (marker absent) in fuzz targets,
    not the cosmetic property (non-secret params
    survive). Document the interaction in the test
    file so a future reader understands why the
    survival assertion is absent.
  - **Sentinel-overlap is a redactor footgun.**
    `Redactor.Redact` uses `strings.ReplaceAll(s,
    secret, Sentinel)`. If `secret` is a substring of
    `Sentinel` (e.g. `"REDA"`), the second pass
    rewrites the freshly-inserted sentinel substring
    and the function is NOT idempotent
    (`"[REDACTED] token"` → `"[[REDACTED]CTED] token"`).
    This is unreachable in practice — `[REDACTED]` is
    not a plausible real secret — but the fuzz harness
    must scope it out explicitly. The
    `TestRedactor_FuzzScopeExclusionsAreReal` test
    pins this as the current behaviour, so a future
    fix to the redactor (e.g. switching to a regex
    substitution that does not re-scan substituted
    text) deliberately breaks the test and forces a
    coordinated update to the fuzz scope, the
    `SECURITY.md` section, and the AGENTS.md note.
  - **Per-target seed corpus is the CI gate; `-fuzz`
    is the operator-opt-in net.** `go test ./...`
    runs every seed in `f.Add` once, so the seed
    corpus is the regression net every commit
    exercises. `-fuzz` exercises the random-mutation
    stage and is operator-opt-in. When a new
    redaction rule is added (cookies, refresh
    tokens), the worked pattern is: (1) add a seed
    input to `redactFuzzSeeds` that triggers the new
    rule, (2) add a fuzz target if the new rule has
    a structural shape distinct from the existing
    four, (3) update both the AGENTS.md `Log
    redaction fuzzing (BE-0359)` section and the
    `SECURITY.md` `Log Redaction Fuzzing` section to
    cover the new transport pattern.
  - **`-fuzztime` shutdown timing with many
    workers.** `go test -fuzz=… -fuzztime=5s` with
    the default 16 workers sometimes reports
    `context deadline exceeded` at shutdown — this
    is a harness-internal timing quirk, not a real
    fuzz failure (no `testdata/fuzz/…` corpus file
    is written). Re-running with `-parallel=2`
    makes the shutdown cleaner. Document this in
    the progress entry so a future iteration does
    not chase a phantom failure.
  - **Single-test runtime-only verification pattern.**
    Earlier security-verification stories (BE-0344
    through BE-0358) follow the two-test pattern
    (static AST analyzer + runtime integration
    test) when the invariant has a source-code rule
    AND a runtime contract. BE-0359 is the FIRST
    worked instance of the single-test runtime-only
    shape called out in the BE-0344 pattern's
    closing line: "verification stories whose
    invariant is a runtime contract with NO static
    analog (e.g. log redaction fuzzing, idempotency
    replay, chaos tests for timeouts) — those
    follow a single-test runtime-only shape". The
    fuzz harness IS the runtime contract; there is
    no source-code shape an analyzer could pin (the
    redactor's structural rules are regex patterns,
    and a regression that weakened them would still
    look like a regex). Future stories of this
    shape (BE-0360 environment-variable redaction
    where the rule is "the variables service MUST
    pass every rendered value through the redactor
    before logging" is also runtime-only if there
    is no AST shape to gate; BE-0363 rate-limit
    bypass resistance is similarly runtime-only)
    can mirror BE-0359's single-fuzz-file +
    SECURITY.md section + AGENTS.md subsection
    layout.

  BE-0102 (policy matrix) were already passing; BE-0101 closes the
  contract-test row of that endpoint trilogy. The next pending
  contract-test story in this family is BE-0104 (GET
  /v1/organizations/{org_id}/audit-events).
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The BE-0095 limits_get_contract_test.go template ports
    one-for-one to GET /usage with only three substitutions:
    (a) helper name listLimits -> listUsage, (b) reader port type
    LimitsReader -> UsageReader and reader fake fakeLimitsReader
    -> fakeUsageReader (whose fields are usage []store.OrganizationResourceUsage,
    err error, got *string — identical shape to fakeLimitsReader),
    (c) envelope decoder decodeLimitsList(t, body) -> decodeUsageList
    (t, body) which projects under .Data.Usage (the limits decoder
    projects under .Limits at the top level because the existing
    limits envelope shape predates the data-block convention).
    The handler-builder NewHandler arg position the reader takes is
    different (UsageReader is the third arg after LimitsReader and
    LimitsUpdater in NewHandler's parameter list) but the second-
    to-last "logger seam" nil slot is in the SAME place — this is
    the load-bearing invariant that lets the contract-test pattern
    generalise across every read endpoint sharing the NewHandler
    wiring contract.
  - The "datastore address must not leak" assertion bytes (cause
    string "connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432" + host probe
    "10.0.0.5") are the same bytes the limits contract test uses
    on purpose: the goal is to pin the structural invariant ("a
    bare host:port in a wrapped cause never reaches the wire"),
    not to vary the byte pattern per endpoint. Future sibling
    contract tests (BE-0104 audit-events, BE-0107 variables list,
    every GET .../{org_id}/* read endpoint that surfaces
    apierr.StoreUnavailable) should reuse the same probe bytes
    so the invariant is a single closed set of regression probes
    across the read surface.
  - Sandbox TMPDIR quirk: the ctx_execute shell sandbox sets
    TMPDIR to a path that contains the project root. Go's module
    resolver then reports `ignoring go.mod in system temp root
    /Users/juribadev/projects/poc/yalla` and refuses to honor the
    module. Workaround: `export TMPDIR=/tmp; export GOTMPDIR=/tmp`
    at the top of every ctx_execute shell block that runs `go
    test|vet|mod`. Forward-applicable to every future Ralph
    iteration on this machine.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0360 - Security verification: environment variable redaction

- What was implemented: BE-0360 — the third clone of the BE-0344
  security-verification two-test pattern (after BE-0345 httpapi body size
  and BE-0356/BE-0357/BE-0358 release-package static pins), this time
  applied to the variables package's redaction surface. The static half
  (internal/controlplane/variables/env_var_redaction_static_test.go) walks
  every non-test .go file and enforces three structural rules: (1) each
  of (ScopedVariable).LogValue / (Rendered).LogValue / (Resolved).LogValue
  MUST reference output.Sentinel AND MUST NOT emit a <receiver>.Value /
  <receiver>.SecretCiphertext selector inside the method body; (2) every
  ExplainedVariable{...} composite literal MUST set the Value field to
  output.Sentinel exactly (omitted Value is also rejected); (3) no
  fmt.Sprint*/Errorf, errors.New, apierr.Internal/InvalidInput/NotFound/
  Conflict call, and no apierr.FieldViolation{Reason: …, Field: …}
  composite literal, may carry a `.Value` / `.SecretCiphertext` selector
  or a local identifier named `plaintext` (the resolver's conventional
  name for bytes recovered through secrets.Provider.Open). A
  TestRedactionStaticAnalyzerDetectsRegressions self-check parses
  synthetic bad and good source snippets and asserts each rule fires (or
  stays silent). The runtime half
  (internal/controlplane/variables/env_var_redaction_test.go) lands five
  table-driven runtime tests and two Go fuzz targets that pin the no-leak
  invariant across a hostile-value seed corpus (long values, invalid
  UTF-8, control characters, NEL line terminator, regex metacharacters,
  JSON-escape sequences, the output.Sentinel literal, a marker-prefixed
  literal). The marker-bracket pattern (`FUZZENVMARKERLMN`) borrowed from
  the BE-0359 log-redaction fuzz suite is the leak detector — every
  fuzz-supplied value is wrapped with the marker so a leak surfaces
  independently of the bytes the value happens to carry. The variables
  package's AGENTS.md gets a new "Env-var redaction verification
  (BE-0360)" section documenting the two-test contract. The top-level
  SECURITY.md gets a new "Environment Variable Redaction" section above
  the existing "Log Redaction Fuzzing" section plus a new row in the
  Required Verification Gates table pointing at
  `go test ./internal/controlplane/variables/... -run TestRedaction`.

- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/variables/env_var_redaction_static_test.go (new)
  - internal/controlplane/variables/env_var_redaction_test.go (new)
  - internal/controlplane/variables/AGENTS.md (Env-var redaction section)
  - SECURITY.md (Environment Variable Redaction section + table row)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0360 passes=true)
  - ralph/progress.txt (this entry)

- Verification run:
  - `gofmt -w internal/controlplane/variables/` → no output (formatter
    rewrote the static test once to canonical alignment; behaviour
    unchanged).
  - `go vet ./...` → no output.
  - `go test ./...` → all packages OK (the variables package now runs
    TestRedactionLogValueMethodsReferenceSentinel,
    TestRedactionExplainedVariableLiteralsRedactValue,
    TestRedactionNoPlaintextInErrorSurface,
    TestRedactionStaticAnalyzerDetectsRegressions plus the five runtime
    redaction tests and the two fuzz targets' seed corpora).
  - `go test -race ./...` → all packages OK.
  - Control-removal sanity check: temporarily mutating the first
    `slog.String("value", output.Sentinel)` in resolver.go (the one in
    ScopedVariable.LogValue) to `slog.String("value", v.Value)` makes
    both the static analyzer (`(ScopedVariable).LogValue does not
    reference output.Sentinel — the slog redaction seam has been
    removed` AND `emits forbidden selector v.Value`) and the runtime
    test (`plaintext or ciphertext leaked through
    ScopedVariable.LogValue marker: "FUZZENVMARKERLMN"`) fail. The two
    layers are independently load-bearing.

- Results: all tests pass; the two-test pair fails when the control is
  removed; the threat-model documentation in SECURITY.md and AGENTS.md
  stays in sync with the runtime evidence.

- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - The Dokploy renderer at internal/controlplane/dokploy/renderer.go
    consumes the merged Resolved view. The current renderer emits
    variables into a Dokploy provisioning payload — that is a separate
    audit/observability surface from the customer-facing API, so a
    renderer regression that surfaced plaintext into the Dokploy wire
    is NOT caught by this BE-0360 pair. The defence is the
    dokploy/renderer's own redaction tests (BE-0301 family) which pin
    the per-builder/per-type drop-and-redact contract for Dokploy
    payloads. A future "all environment variables on the Dokploy wire
    are also redacted in slog/audit captures" verification would be
    its own sibling story; BE-0361 (Dokploy token isolation) is the
    closest neighbour and may carry that scope.
  - The store-package per-scope Reader integration tests already pin
    tenant-scoping but do not pin redaction at the read boundary. The
    Reader returns ScopedVariable values, so the redaction contract
    holds transitively through LogValue, but a future Reader that
    returned a different shape would need a sibling static rule. The
    pattern's "Adding a new redaction-bearing type extends
    redactingTypes" extension point is the right hook.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The BE-0344 security-verification two-test pattern keeps cloning
    cleanly. Three structural rules in the static half plus a hostile-
    value runtime fuzz seed corpus is the right size for a single
    P=1 verification story. Past clones (BE-0345 body size, BE-0356
    TLS, BE-0357 admin endpoints, BE-0358 support access, BE-0359 log
    redaction) all converged on the same shape; this one extends it.
  - The receiver-name tie in bodyForbiddenSelectors is what keeps the
    LogValue forbidden-selector rule from generating false positives.
    Without the tie, an unrelated `<other>.Value` inside the method
    body (a literal map key, a constant lookup) would fire. The
    receiverIdentNames helper extracts the name from fd.Recv.List;
    anonymous receivers (`func (T) M() {}`) deliberately produce an
    empty set so the rule degrades to "no forbidden selector ever",
    which is also the safe default for a future anonymous LogValue.
  - The errorFormingFuncs map is a closed set, not an allowlist of
    safe calls. A future helper added without a corresponding entry
    here passes the static check unconditionally, so the entry edit
    is the load-bearing one when adding a new helper. The runtime
    test is the second wall: even when the static analyser misses, a
    helper that produces a string carrying the fuzz marker still
    fails the captureSlog assertion.
  - The Write tool occasionally corrupts string literals that mix
    Go-escape sequences and non-ASCII characters in the same source
    file (the NEL character U+0085 round-tripped as a literal 0xc2
    0x85 byte sequence in one line and dropped the literal `" -null-
    end",` line entirely, producing an unterminated string literal).
    Workaround: prefer explicit `\xNN` escapes for non-ASCII bytes in
    test seed corpora; never embed raw bytes in a Write call. The
    runtime test's seed corpus uses `"\xc2\x85nextline-after-NEL"`
    rather than the literal NEL character, and the file round-trips
    cleanly through both gofmt and the build.
  - The TMPDIR=/tmp prefix discovered in the BE-0101 entry still
    applies to every shell sandbox `go` invocation; without it, Go
    refuses to honour go.mod and reports `ignoring go.mod in system
    temp root`. Forward-applicable to every future Ralph iteration.
  - For env-var redaction specifically, the Plaintext provider
    (secrets.NewPlaintext) is the right test seam — its ciphertext is
    byte-equal to the plaintext, so the runtime tests can assert both
    plaintext and ciphertext are redacted with a single marker check
    on the slog output. A future test against the AES-GCM provider
    would need a separate `Open()` step before the marker check.

    BE-0101 usage -> BE-0104 audit-events) now has a THIRD worked instance, and
    the audit-events instance confirms the template scales unchanged to endpoints
    that ALSO accept an optional query parameter (?limit= in [1,200]). The
    invalid-input path the template glosses over for parameterless endpoints
    ("there is therefore no syntactic request to reject as invalid input beyond
    the rejection paths already covered") is already pinned for audit-events by
    the existing TestListAuditEventsRejectsMalformedLimit /
    TestListAuditEventsRejectsOutOfRangeLimit tests in audit_events_test.go, so
    the contract-test file deliberately does NOT duplicate them — the file
    closes only the three criteria (ResponseWriter-only, log-redaction,
    dependency-cause-non-leak) that the base test pair leaves open. The opening
    block-comment makes this scope explicit so a future maintainer doesn't add
    a fourth redundant test.

    is the SAME deny shape across endpoints regardless of whether the action is
    CapRead (usage.read) or CapAdmin (audit.read) — the policy engine short-circuits

    transfers verbatim. NOT applicable to endpoints where the deny path is itself
    an interesting policy-matrix coordinate (e.g. CapAdmin with a viewer role) —
    that belongs in the *_policy_test.go file, not the contract-test file.

    SECOND-to-last positional argument (`fakeBreakGlassController{}, logger, nil)`),
    NOT a leading slot. The audit-events instance places the AuditEventReader
    parameter `reader` in the slot that the usage instance fills with
    fakeAuditEventReader{} — the rest of the 81-arg call stays identical. This
    keeps the helper signature stable across endpoint stories and makes the
    diff between usage_get_contract_test.go and audit_events_get_contract_test.go
    a clean three-line swap.
  - decodeAuditEventList lives in audit_events_test.go and returns an envelope
    with Data.Events as a []struct with explicit JSON tags — the contract-test
    file can reuse it directly without redeclaring the type. Same convention
    used by usage_get_contract_test.go (decodeUsageList) and
    limits_get_contract_test.go (decodeLimitsList).

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0362 - Security verification: backup encryption
- What was implemented:
  - BE-0362 follows the BE-0344 two-test pattern (eighth worked
    instance, FIRST whole-package-confinement application — prior
    instances pinned single functions, directory-import rules, or
    cross-package secret seams; this one pins that the backup leaf
    package MUST NOT carry a data plane in the first place).
  - Static half (internal/release/backup_encryption_static_test.go):
    six tests pin the structural invariants:
    (a) TestBackupEncryptionNoForbiddenImports — every non-test .go
        file directly under internal/controlplane/backup is parsed
        with parser.ImportsOnly and every import path is checked
        against a closed forbidden set covering symmetric/asymmetric
        ciphers (crypto/aes, crypto/cipher, crypto/des, crypto/rc4,
        crypto/rsa, crypto/ecdsa, crypto/ed25519), crypto/tls,
        archives (archive/zip, archive/tar), compression
        (compress/gzip|zlib|flate|bzip2), database drivers
        (database/sql, github.com/jackc/pgx/v5, pgxpool), os/exec,
        and net/http. The package's only legitimate I/O is
        os.ReadFile on the operator-supplied status path.
    (b) TestBackupEncryptionReporterInterfaceIsReadOnly — the
        Reporter interface declaration in health.go is located by
        AST name, then validated to have exactly one named method
        whose name is "Status". Embedded interfaces are rejected
        as a separate regression (embed io.Writer would silently
        expand the surface).
    (c) TestBackupEncryptionNoWriteSeams — every CallExpr whose
        Fun is a SelectorExpr is checked against a forbidden write/
        exec set (os.Create, os.CreateTemp, os.WriteFile,

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The BE-0344 two-test template now has EIGHT worked instances
    spanning four distinct invariant shapes:
    (i) single-function-rule (BE-0346 environment-variable redaction
        in variables service),
    (ii) directory-import-rule (BE-0357 admin endpoints, BE-0349
         SSRF),
    (iii) cross-package secret-confinement (BE-0361 Dokploy token —
          single secret flows through one seam, projection methods
          must consult the redactor first),
    (iv) NEW: whole-package data-plane confinement (BE-0362 backup
         encryption — a leaf package MUST NOT carry an entire
         data plane: cipher, archive, database, exec, HTTP). The
         template's flexibility is in the matcher's targeting
         (single Sel.Name vs InterfaceType.Methods vs package-
         qualified CallExpr selector) and in the closed-set
         tightness; the doc pinning + self-check + marker-pattern
         halves are constant across all four shapes.
  - WRAP-ROBUST DOC SUBSTRINGS — when pinning content from a
    wrapped Markdown document, choose substrings short enough to
    survive line wraps and **bold** runs. The first iteration of
    this story used "Plaintext WAL must never" and "no read
    access"; both spanned a wrap or a markdown-bold run in the
    source files ("Plaintext WAL must\n   never" in the runbook,
    "**no** read access" — actually just "**read access**" in the
    new SECURITY section) and the test fired false-positive
    diagnostics. Fix is structural: use "Plaintext WAL" + "read
    access" — same semantic, robust to Markdown wrap and to
    in-line **bold** markers. Forward-applicable to every future
    doc-pinning gate: the matcher reads RAW Markdown bytes, so
    substrings that contain ASCII spaces, line wraps, or bold
    runs need a wrap-robust form. The lesson is: doc-pinning
    substrings should be at most one short phrase, never multi-
    word sentences that the formatter might re-wrap.
  - INTERFACE-METHOD-COUNT-AND-NAMES is a new matcher shape worth
    documenting. The matcher locates an InterfaceType by name,
    then walks iface.Methods.List and rejects (a) embedded
    interfaces (len(field.Names) == 0 — embed io.Writer would
    silently expand the surface), (b) named methods whose Name
    is not in the allowed set, and (c) the interface being
    missing entirely. The third case is the easy regression — a
    renamed interface (Reporter -> BackupSurface) would silently
    disable the gate without it. The self-check pair must
    include a "renamed-interface" synthetic for the gate to be
    load-bearing.
  - DUAL-DOC PIN is genuinely new — most prior security-
    verification stories pinned one document (SECURITY.md). BE-
    0362 pins SECURITY.md AND docs/operations/backup-restore.md
    because the runbook is part of the operator contract (KMS
    rotation cadence, restore audit-event semantics). Each gets
    its own test function with its own constant-list. Forward-
    applicable to any story whose threat model relies on
    operator-facing runbooks (replica-lag oncall guide, KMS
    rotation playbook, certificate-renewal runbook).
  - IMPORT-WHITELIST-AS-FORBIDDEN-LIST design — when the
    invariant is "this leaf package MUST NOT carry a data plane",
    list every package the data plane would require as forbidden
    rather than listing the small read-only seam as the only
    allowed set. The forbidden list is closed and the boundary is
    explicit; an extension (e.g. needing crypto/sha256 for an
    integrity check) must surface in review, not slip in via a
    "this isn't really an encryption library" argument. The
    AGENTS.md note in the package documents the rule alongside
    its rationale so a contributor learns the rule by reading the
    package, not by reading the failing test output.
  - The "ignoring go.mod in system temp root" pattern when running
    go via context-mode's ctx_execute(shell): the sandbox prefixes
    cd but does not preserve cwd for subsequent go commands, so go
    treats /Users/juribadev/projects/poc/yalla as a temp root and
    fails with "directory prefix X does not contain main module".
    Workaround: use Bash for go invocations (cwd is preserved by
    the shell tool's working-directory contract) and reserve
    ctx_execute(shell) for short scripted multi-step pipelines
    that don't need cwd inheritance, OR rely on Python sandbox
    scripts that read absolute paths. Documented here so the next
    iteration does not waste a round on the same false alarm.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0110
- Added internal/controlplane/httpapi/variables_put_contract_test.go (~340 lines): three contract tests + one variables-specific log-redaction pin for PUT /v1/organizations/{org_id}/variables, structurally cloned from limits_patch_contract_test.go (BE-0098).
- New helper: replaceOrgVariablesHandlerForWithLogger (logger-seam variant of replaceOrgVariablesHandlerFor — the only per-story knob beyond constants).
- Tests: TestReplaceOrgVariablesServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter (captureProcessOutput proves the HTTP server uses only ResponseWriter, replacer received {org_id}, structured log non-empty); TestReplaceOrgVariablesRequestLogRedactsBearerToken (success-path owner + auth-failure-path disabled-owner subtests, both prove the bearer credential never reaches logBuf or response body; deny leg uses an erroring replacer to prove policy short-circuits before reaching the store); TestReplaceOrgVariablesRequestLogRedactsSubmittedSecretValue (the variables-specific extra pin — a submitted is_secret=true value never reaches the per-request structured log, on success AND deny legs; deny-leg leak would be operator-visible even though the value never reached the store); TestReplaceOrgVariablesErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause (StoreUnavailable cause string + bare datastore address 10.0.0.5 never reach the wire).
- Verification: gofmt -l (clean), go vet ./... (clean), go test ./... (all packages pass, no failures), go test -race ./... (no race failures), go test -race -run TestReplaceOrgVariables ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... (ok).
- Remaining risks/follow-ups: none for this story. The same template (write-endpoint contract triple + body-secret-redaction quadruple for endpoints that accept is_secret=true) ports to BE-0113 (PATCH variables) and BE-0116 (DELETE variables) — the DELETE one drops the submitted-secret quadruple since the body has no secret to leak.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Write-endpoint contract-test quadruple (BE-0110 pattern, internal/controlplane/httpapi/variables_put_contract_test.go; structural template for every P=2 "Add contract tests for {PUT,PATCH,DELETE,POST} .../{org_id}/X" story whose endpoint carries a request body that MAY include is_secret=true / API-key / token / cookie values). Four named tests close the contract gaps the base *_test.go + *_policy_test.go pair leaves open: (1) "server writes response data only through ResponseWriter" — wraps the served request in captureProcessOutput, asserts os.Stdout AND os.Stderr are empty, AND that the structured logger sink is non-empty, AND that the captured replacer/updater/patcher input carries the {org_id} path parameter (writes don't have a "no-data" envelope to spot-check, so the captured-input assertion replaces the read-endpoint's "data == seeded entry" assertion); (2) "request log redacts the bearer credential" — a single test function with a `tests := []struct{...}` table over (success path, authorization failure path), each subtest builds a separate logger and asserts logBuf.String() and rec.Body.String() are both free of the contract secret. The deny leg uses a replacer/updater whose Replace/Update path errors if invoked, so a leaked "store error" cannot be the leak source — the deny must short-circuit at policy; (3) "request log redacts a submitted secret value" — IDENTICAL shape to (2), but the marker is a customer-submitted is_secret=true value inside the request body (yallasubmittedsecretMARKER0123456789FACEFEED). This is the variables-specific extra pin the limits sibling does NOT have — limits' PATCH body carries numeric limit_value plus enforcement_mode and is_secret=true is not a concept; variables, environment-variables, project-variables, and service-variables all carry is_secret=true in the request body and need this extra pin. The deny-leg leak detection is even more important than the success leg here, because a leaked submitted secret in the deny log surface means the operator log holds a value the store layer never wrote — a leak the wire-level redaction cannot catch; (4) "error envelope doesn't leak dependency cause" — apierr.StoreUnavailable wrapped around stderrors.New("connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432"), asserts 503 / E_UNAVAILABLE / non-empty stable Message / cause string absent / host "10.0.0.5" absent from the body. Probe bytes are intentionally identical across sibling contract tests so the invariant is a single closed regression set, not a per-endpoint variant. The new helper this pattern requires is a "WithLogger" clone of the existing handler-builder that swaps the second-to-last NewHandler nil slot for the caller-supplied *slog.Logger — identical edit across every write endpoint, because the logger seam lives at the same position in NewHandler's parameter list regardless of which writer port the route depends on. Forward-applicable to BE-0113 (PATCH variables — keep all four pins; the PATCH body also carries is_secret=true), BE-0116 (DELETE variables — drop pin (3), the DELETE body has no submitted-secret to leak), BE-0122 (POST projects — drop pin (3) unless projects carry secrets in the create body), and any future write endpoint whose body carries customer-submitted secrets. The only per-story knobs are the writer port type, the fake writer's field name (`vars`/`err`/`got`), the canonical contract body, and the canonical contract-submitted-secret marker (use a distinct suffix per story so a regression that swaps two surfaces fails loudly — e.g. PUT_CAFEBABE, PATCH_FACEFEED, DELETE_DEADBEEF).

  - go vet ./internal/release/... ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... ./internal/controlplane/ratelimit/... → clean
  - go test -run TestRateLimitBypassResistance ./internal/release/... ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... → PASS (12 test functions, all subtests green)
  - go test ./... → PASS (full module, no FAIL lines)

- Remaining risks / follow-ups: none.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - **Shared test helpers race under -race**: the existing `rateLimitOK{ran bool}` helper in ratelimit_test.go writes its `ran` field on every ServeHTTP call. When N goroutines hit the SAME helper instance (BE-0363's concurrent-burst test originally did this), the -race detector flags the write-write race even though the field is logically irrelevant to the assertion. **Pattern**: any test that fans out N goroutines through one http.Handler MUST use a stateless handler (an inline `http.HandlerFunc` that writes only to its per-call ResponseWriter), NOT a shared helper struct with mutable fields. The non-race tests in this file can keep using the shared helper because httptest single-request flow is sequential.
  - **AST `ast.Inspect` does not expose parent**: BE-0363's `findRateLimitWrapSeams` matcher needed to know "the local variable `rateLimit` was bound to `RateLimit(...)`" before it could look for `h = rateLimit(h)` wrap sites. Solution: TWO passes — first walk records binders (`<name> = RateLimit(...)`) into a `map[string]struct{}`; second pass looks for assignments whose RHS is `<binder>(<lhs>)`. Same shape applies to any "find downstream uses of a CallExpr-bound name" matcher.
  - **Static-test SECURITY.md substring assertions need the exact rendered substring, NOT a paraphrase**: the matcher checks `strings.Contains(text, want)` with the literal string. If the doc says `internal/release/...static_test.go` (with the path prefix), the substring `static_test.go` (without prefix) fails the contains check ONLY if the prefix is required by the assertion. Lesson: write the assertion list as the EXACT substrings the doc must contain, then write the doc to match. My first pass listed the full path `` `internal/release/rate_limit_bypass_resistance_static_test.go` `` but wrote the doc as a two-clause phrase that broke the substring; reworded the doc to keep the bare backtick-fenced filename `` `rate_limit_bypass_resistance_static_test.go` `` and added a "(under `internal/release/`, BE-0363)" follow-up — both halves now match independently.
  - **The BE-0344 two-test pattern scales to "non-bypass" invariants**: BE-0363 is the EIGHTH worked instance, but the FIRST where the runtime half exercises an actual concurrent attacker (20 parallel goroutines through a production limiter). The pattern absorbs the new shape with no template changes — the static half pins the structural invariants (single Exempt site, closed constant set, canonical 429 seam, per-route wrap), the runtime half pins the marker-based behavioural invariants (forged headers/path/IP cannot flip Exempt, concurrent burst cannot exceed cap, deny log redacts bucket identity, envelope body redacts bucket identity, anonymous request still consults limiter). Forward-applicable to any future "X must not be reachable via attacker-controlled input Y" gate.

- Added TestVerificationSuiteExemptionSetIsTight — companion test that every exempt entry (a) refers to a real directory and (b) still lacks tests, so a stale exemption fails the build.
- Added self-check TestVerificationSuiteUnitTestsAnalyzerDetectsRegressions with 8 sub-tests driving synthetic known-good AND known-bad fixtures through every matcher (missing-test tree, exempted tree, ignored-prefix tree, fully-tested tree, test-only dir, incomplete SECURITY.md substring set, complete substring set, PRD without/with the required command). Catches over-tightening AND under-tightening.
- Added internal/credentials/keyring_test.go (~70 lines) — tiny unit tests for IsNotFound, IsUnsupported, and the Store-interface compile-time pin on KeyringStore. The package was the only non-main, non-doc-only package without tests and would have required an exemption entry; adding three small tests preserves the every-real-package-has-tests posture without expanding the exemption set.
- Added new `## Unit Test Suite` section to SECURITY.md (~50 lines) explaining the scope (every Go package), determinism (fake Dokploy + opt-in YALLA_EXTERNAL_DOKPLOY smoke), actionable failures (request_id in envelopes), redaction (output.Redactor + BE-0359 fuzzing), and CI cadence (Every push and PR across 3 OS hosts).
- Updated internal/release/AGENTS.md with a new `## Verification suite: unit tests for every package (BE-0379)` section explaining the SIX surfaces, the exemption-set discipline, the self-check shape, and the "update both ends in one edit" rule for future contributors.
- Verification:
  - gofmt -l . → clean
  - go vet ./... → clean
  - go mod tidy → clean
  - go test ./internal/credentials/... -count=1 → PASS (3 test functions)
  - go test ./internal/release/... -run TestVerificationSuite -count=1 → PASS (7 test functions + 8 self-check subtests)
  - go test ./... → PASS (no FAIL lines)
  - go test -race ./... → PASS (no FAIL or DATA RACE lines)
- Remaining risks / follow-ups: none for this story. The pattern (verification-suite single-file multi-surface static-test with closed exempt set + self-check) is the structural template for BE-0380 (repository integration tests), BE-0381 (HTTP handler contract tests), BE-0382 (OpenAPI conformance), BE-0383 (policy matrix), BE-0384 (quota concurrency), BE-0385 (job worker leases), BE-0386 (fake Dokploy contract), BE-0387 (redaction), BE-0388 (validator fuzz), BE-0389 (migrations from empty DB), BE-0390 (migration downgrade), BE-0391 (race detector), and every future P=1 verification-suite story. The per-story knobs are: (1) the canonical suite command (e.g. `go test -run TestMigrations ./...`), (2) the scope predicate (which packages/files the matcher walks), (3) the doc heading constant, (4) the substring-set capturing the ACs of that story, (5) the per-story exemption set if any.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Verification-suite single-file multi-surface static-test (BE-0379 pattern, internal/release/verification_suite_unit_tests_static_test.go; structural template for BE-0380..BE-0408 sibling verification-suite stories and any future "the suite itself is part of the contract" verification). NINE load-bearing rules: (1) ONE file pins ALL surfaces of the meta-contract so a future contributor changing the CI step name, the verify.sh step header, the CONTRIBUTING numeric prefix, the SECURITY row, or the PRD verification-loop array fails ONE test, not five. The single-file shape is the BE-0354 dependency_scan pattern carried forward to the verification-suite family. (2) CLOSED exempt set with rationale — every exemption MUST carry a rationale that points to where coverage actually lives, not just a "thin entrypoint" hand-wave. The rationale is what makes a future review decide whether to keep, extend, or remove the entry; without it the set drifts. (3) STALE-exemption guard (TestVerificationSuiteExemptionSetIsTight) — assert every exempt dir (a) exists and (b) still lacks tests. Otherwise a package that gains tests silently keeps its exemption and the discipline rots. (4) IGNORED-prefix walker — the package coverage walker MUST skip `.git/`, `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `outputs/`, `tmp/`, `bin/`, `vendor/` via prefix-with-trailing-slash check so a hypothetical `output/` package (without the trailing s) is still scanned. (5) PURE function split — findPackagesMissingTests takes (root, exempt, ignored) and is called once by the runtime test against the real repo AND multiple times by the self-check with synthetic trees built via mkFile (t.TempDir + os.WriteFile). The self-check is what proves the walker doesn't false-positive on test-only dirs and doesn't false-negative on ignored subtrees. (6) CASE-SENSITIVE substring constants — `requiredSecuritySectionSubstrings` are matched verbatim against the doc, so a substring like "every Go package" will NOT match a sentence-start "Every Go package". When the doc text naturally starts a sentence with the substring, use the capitalised form in the constant. The first run caught this: the test failed with `missing required substring "every Go package"` and the fix was to align the constant with the doc, not the doc with the constant. The self-check fixture must also be updated in the same edit (the synthetic SECURITY.md fixture in TestVerificationSuiteUnitTestsAnalyzerDetectsRegressions). (7) NON-MAIN, NON-DOC-ONLY package without tests is NEVER exempt-worthy — prefer adding 2-3 small tests (e.g. `internal/credentials` IsNotFound + IsUnsupported + Store-interface compile-time pin) over expanding the exemption set. The exemption set is reserved for thin main-glue and `doc.go`-only placeholders. (8) PRD as a verification surface — the prd.json's `verificationLoop.requiredLocalCommands` array is itself part of the contract. An AI agent reads the PRD before picking up a story; pinning the suite command there guarantees the agent sees it without needing to discover CI workflows or shell scripts. The matcher uses encoding/json with a partial struct so a future PRD schema extension doesn't break it. (9) CI MATRIX as part of the contract — pinning ubuntu-latest + macos-latest + windows-latest is what prevents a silent "we only test on Linux now" regression. The matrix dimension is a separate substring assertion per host so the failure diagnostic names the missing host explicitly.
  - The pattern is the next-strongest form of the BE-0354 (dependency_scan) single-file multi-surface pattern, applied to a meta-contract whose subject is the test suite itself rather than a specific security control. The two pattern families share: (a) single file, (b) closed substring/constant set per surface, (c) self-check with synthetic fixtures driving every matcher. They differ in: (a) BE-0379-family stories have a `findPackagesMissingTests`-style repo walker as their primary matcher (the security-control family has no such walker; their primary matcher is an AST scan over package source); (b) BE-0379-family stories pin the PRD itself (security-control stories generally don't); (c) BE-0379-family stories use a closed exempt set with per-entry rationale (security-control stories use closed constant lists like `forbiddenSecretEnvFragments` but no per-entry rationale).

  - The PRD's `-run TestPolicyMatrix ./...` filter form is a SECOND
    legitimate canonical-command shape (alongside the package-narrowed
    `go test ./internal/<pkg>/...` shape BE-0381/BE-0382 used). When
    inheriting an existing PRD entry that uses `-run`, the dedicated CI
    step and verify.sh step should mirror it verbatim — there is no
    additional package-narrowing layer.

    cross-tenant matrix that assumes Support is allowed for every action

    etc. ALWAYS trace engine.Decide before writing the expected-verdict
    switch — the engine's exact clause is authoritative.

    test (like TestPolicyMatrix), enriching the canonical with a sibling
    that captures a DIFFERENT engine invariant (in-tenant vs cross-tenant)
    is a strictly better outcome than pinning a single function — the
    canonical-funcs PAIR (rather than single) raises the bar a future
    regression must cross to silently leak.
  - The BE-0382 closing line "Future verification-suite subset stories
    adding a required step should follow the same pattern" was honoured
    verbatim: BE-0383's edit renumbered verify.sh optionals 9→10/10→11/
    11→12/12→13 in lockstep with the static test's
    policyMatrixVerifyShStepHeader = "# 9. Required: policy matrix tests"
    constant. No drift between the script and the matcher.

  - The BE-0384 instance refined the BE-0383 sub-pattern: the PRD's `verificationLoop.requiredBackendCommands` ALREADY contained `go test -run TestQuotaConcurrency ./...` before this story landed (same as BE-0383's policy-matrix entry). The matcher is satisfied without a PRD edit; if a future contributor "cleans up" the array they MUST run the static test first to learn that the entry is load-bearing.
  - The canonical-funcs pair were ADDED (not renamed) — the existing `TestCheckerReserveConcurrentRespectsLimit` is sibling, NOT the canonical function the `-run TestQuotaConcurrency` filter binds to. The naming pattern is: each verification-suite story whose canonical command is `-run TestXxx…` either (a) renames an existing test to match the `Xxx…` prefix (intrusive, breaks history) or (b) adds NEW canonical-pair tests next to existing siblings (additive, preserves history). BE-0384 chose (b) for the same reason BE-0383 did: the existing tests stay, the canonical ones name the invariants explicitly.
  - The verify.sh renumber pattern: every required-block insertion BEFORE the optionals block renumbers EVERY trailing optional in the same edit. BE-0384 inserted #10 and renumbered 10→11, 11→12, 12→13, 13→14. The static test's `quotaConcurrencyVerifyShStepHeader` (#10) and the existing `policyMatrixVerifyShStepHeader` (#9) confirm both numeric prefixes; the other static tests' optional-numbered headers must NOT be pinned because they shift on every required-block insertion.
  - The `-run TestQuotaConcurrency` filter binds to BOTH new tests via the `TestQuotaConcurrency` prefix (substring match); the analyzer self-check's `TestQuotaConcurrency prefix locks the -run filter contract` subtest pins this with a `strings.HasPrefix(..., "func TestQuotaConcurrency")` assertion so a rename to e.g. `TestConcurrentQuota…` would fail the gate before CI.
  - The TenantIsolation test's inner closure must NOT alias `t` (the testing.T) to a per-tenant tally bucket — Go's variable-shadowing rules make `t := results[orgID]` shadow the outer `t *testing.T`, silently breaking `t.Errorf` inside the closure. Used `bucket := results[orgID]` to make the alias explicit and the testing.T accessible for actionable diagnostics.
  - The SECURITY.md substring matcher set MUST include `FOR UPDATE` (the lock the hard-limit invariant rests on) and `organization_id` (the predicate the cross-tenant invariant rests on) — these are the two load-bearing engine details an auditor must see to verify the invariant from the documented contract alone, without opening the test file. The 13-substring set is the minimum that pins every BE-0384 AC.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0122
- Added internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_create_contract_test.go with three contract tests for POST /v1/projects:
  - TestCreateProjectServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter: served POST writes nothing to process stdout/stderr; the response data and request_id go through the http.ResponseWriter only; structured logger sink receives one record (the only sanctioned writer).
  - TestCreateProjectRequestLogRedactsBearerToken: per-request structured log never carries the bearer credential on the success path OR the authorization-failure path (viewer role, RoleViewer is denied by RBAC project.create); the response body never echoes the bearer either; a creator that errors-on-call proves the deny path short-circuits at policy.
  - TestCreateProjectErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause: apierr.StoreUnavailable surfaces as 503 E_UNAVAILABLE with a stable generic message; neither the wrapped cause string nor the datastore host:port appears in the response body.

- Results: PASS. 308 stories remain open.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: none for this story.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The contract-test extension pattern (BE-0080 -> BE-0122) re-applies cleanly to any POST endpoint that already has a non-contract test file pinning the happy/error paths. The recipe is: (a) introduce a per-endpoint XHandlerForWithLogger that mirrors the existing XHandlerFor but threads a *slog.Logger into NewHandler, (b) introduce a per-endpoint contract secret constant (yk_live_...), (c) write three tests with the exact names: TestXServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter (NOT t.Parallel because captureProcessOutput swaps global os.Stdout/os.Stderr), TestXRequestLogRedactsBearerToken (sub-tests for success path AND authorization-failure path), TestXErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause (apierr.StoreUnavailable + cause string with bare host:port). The authorization-failure sub-test for the redaction test should use a role-denied principal (RoleViewer here, disabled-principal in BE-0080) plus a denyCreator that errors-on-call to prove the short-circuit happens at policy, not at the port.
  - Reuse existing helpers from sibling test files: postProjects, createProjectRequestBody, decodeCreateProject, decodeError (from middleware_test.go, returns errorEnvelope with schema/ok/request_id assertions baked in), captureProcessOutput (from me_contract_test.go), orgPrincipal (RBAC role helper). Do not duplicate or shadow these — projects_create_test.go already declares fakeProjectCreator and the request helpers.
  - apierr.StoreUnavailable maps to HTTP 503 with stable code E_UNAVAILABLE; the wrapped error's Error() string MUST NOT appear in rec.Body — the contract test must check for both the full cause AND the bare host:port substring to catch partial leakage.
  - NewHandler's full positional argument list is long; mirror api_keys_create_contract_test.go's createAPIKeyHandlerForWithLogger formatting (one logical group per line) for readability and so that future param insertions in NewHandler stay diff-friendly. The logger is the second-to-last positional argument; rateLimiter (nil here) is the last.

TestDeleteOrgVariableServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter — captureProcessOutput swap pins that the HTTP server writes the deleted-variable payload only through http.ResponseWriter; stdout/stderr stay empty; structured logger goes to its own buffer; deleter receives the {org_id} and {key} path parameters verbatim.
  2. TestDeleteOrgVariableRequestLogRedactsBearerToken — table-driven (success path + authorization-failure path with a Disabled owner); a deleter that errors-if-invoked proves the deny short-circuits at policy so a "deleter error" can't be the leak source. Asserts deleteOrgVariableContractSecret (suffix FACEFEED) appears in neither the structured log nor the response body on either leg.
  3. TestDeleteOrgVariableErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause — apierr.StoreUnavailable wrapping "connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432" lands as 503/E_UNAVAILABLE with a non-empty stable Message; asserts the wrapped cause string and the bare datastore address "10.0.0.5" never appear on the wire.
- Per the WRITE-endpoint contract-quadruple pattern, pin (3) "submitted-secret value is not logged" is dropped because DELETE has no request body — no customer-supplied value enters the handler, so the variables-specific extra surface that BE-0110/BE-0113 cover does not apply.
- Verification run:
  - gofmt -w (clean)
  - go vet ./... (no findings)
  - go test ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... (PASS, 1.174s)
  - go test ./... (all packages PASS)
  - go test -race ./... (all packages PASS)
  - Focused: go test -run 'TestDeleteOrgVariable(ServerWrites|RequestLogRedactsBearerToken|ErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause)' (PASS, both with and without -race)
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The DELETE-endpoint contract-triple variant of the WRITE contract-quadruple pattern (BE-0110/BE-0113 -> BE-0116) is the structural template for every P=2 "Add contract tests for DELETE .../{org_id}/X/{id}" story whose endpoint mutates state through a single deleter port without a request body. THREE named tests cover the contract gaps the base *_test.go + *_policy_test.go pair leaves open: (1) "server writes response data only through ResponseWriter" with captureProcessOutput; (2) "per-request structured log redacts the bearer credential" with success + auth-failure legs (the deny leg uses a deleter that errors-if-invoked so a logged "deleter error" cannot be the leak source); (3) "error envelope built from a wrapped dependency cause never leaks that cause onto the wire" using apierr.StoreUnavailable with a host:port-bearing cause string and probing both the cause and the bare address. Pin (4) — "submitted is_secret=true value is not logged" — is dropped from the DELETE variant because DELETE has no body. The per-story knobs are: deleter port type (OrganizationVariableDeleter), the fake deleter's field names (v/err/got), and a distinct bearer-credential suffix per story so a regression that swaps two surfaces fails loudly (BE-0110 = CAFEBABE, BE-0113 = BEEFDEAD0123456789, BE-0116 = FACEFEED0123456789, BE-0107 = different). The handler-builder seam (a "WithLogger" clone of deleteOrgVariableHandlerFor that swaps the second-to-last NewHandler nil slot for the caller-supplied *slog.Logger) is identical across every write endpoint because the logger seam lives at the same position in NewHandler's parameter list.
  - When deciding the contract-test count for a write-endpoint story, the rule is: read endpoints get the triple (BE-0095/BE-0101/BE-0107) which is 2-3 tests; write endpoints whose body carries a customer-submitted secret value get the quadruple (BE-0110/BE-0113) which is 4 tests; write endpoints with NO body get the triple variant proven by BE-0116 which is 3 tests (drop the "submitted-secret" pin). Future stories to apply the DELETE-no-body variant to: every "Add contract tests for DELETE .../{X}" story whose route signature is path-only with no body, e.g. BE-0131 (DELETE /v1/projects/{project_id}), the eventual DELETE /v1/projects/{project_id}/grants/{grant_id} if it exists, DELETE single-API-key, etc.
  - The probe constants (cause "connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432", probe host "10.0.0.5") are deliberately identical across sibling contract tests so the invariant is a single closed regression set, not a per-endpoint variant — keep using them verbatim when adding more contract triples/quadruples.

      contract-test story should bind to the package whose contract

    - **CANONICAL PAIR NAMING — DUAL INVARIANTS: DETERMINISM ×
      RECORDER-REDACTION.** The pair encodes the two load-bearing
      invariants the fake MUST keep so a consumer test can rely on
      both: determinism (so the fixture is reproducible across runs
      and goroutines) and recorder-redaction (so the bearer never
      leaks through `Server.Requests()`). The pair pattern
      established in BE-0383/0384/0385 carries over verbatim with
      this domain-appropriate dual.
    - **PRE-EXISTING -RUN FILTER IN PRD** — the PRD's
      `verificationLoop.requiredBackendCommands` already contained
      `go test -run TestFakeDokploy ./...` before this story
      landed (BE-0383/0384's `EXISTING-TEST-SATISFIES-RUN-FILTER`
      sub-pattern). BE-0386 adds value via (a) creating the
      canonical TestFakeDokploy* pair (the prefix had ZERO existing
      bindings — no `TestFakeDokploy…` function existed anywhere

      silently matched no tests), (b) wiring CI/verify.sh/
      CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY/AGENTS surfaces as named gates, (c)
      adding the static defence.
    - **VERIFY.SH RENUMBER OF OPTIONALS BLOCK CONTINUES — SIX
      INSERTIONS NOW (#6→#12).** This brings the count to SEVEN
      consecutive required-step insertions with optional
      renumbering. BE-0387 (redaction tests) should follow the
      same edit shape: insert `# 13. Required` block AND renumber
      the four optional headers in the same Edit call.
    - **AC2 `OPT-IN EXTERNAL` IS A REQUIRED SUBSTRING.** The fake-
      Dokploy story uniquely satisfies AC2's "explicitly marked

    `go test -run TestFakeDokploy ./...` command); the reminder

    pattern: ignore the reminder when the edit is a pure-literal

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - `EXISTING-CALLERS-BIND-TO-NEW-PREFIX` — sibling of
    BE-0382's `EXISTING-TEST-SATISFIES-RUN-FILTER`. The
    `TestRedaction` prefix the PRD's
    `-run TestRedaction ./...` filter binds to was NOT
    pre-existing in `requiredBackendCommands` (only the existing
    `Environment variable redaction` SECURITY.md gate already
    used the prefix scoped to `internal/controlplane/variables`),
    but seventeen TestRedaction* tests already existed across
    three packages (`internal/output/redact_test.go`,
    `internal/controlplane/variables/env_var_redaction_*_test.go`,
    `internal/cli/redaction_security_*_test.go`). The canonical
    pair this story adds binds to the SAME prefix without
    renaming any of the existing callers — every existing test
    is now part of the gate the moment BE-0387 lands, AND the
    canonical pair pins the structural-net invariant the central
    Redactor MUST keep across every other caller. Forward-applicable:
    when picking up a verification-suite story whose `-run` filter
    matches existing tests across multiple packages, the canonical
    pair should live in the package that owns the contract (here
    `internal/output` where the `Redactor` type and `Sentinel`
    const are defined) rather than in any downstream consumer; the
    static defence then asserts both the canonical pair and the
    PRD command, so future regressions in either the central
    contract or a downstream consumer trip the same gate.
  - `SEVENTEEN-EXISTING-CALLERS-NUMBERED-ENTRY-#13` — sibling of
    BE-0386's `OPT-IN BLOCK — SEVEN INSERTIONS NOW`. Now EIGHT
    consecutive required-step insertions (BE-0379..BE-0387) with
    optional renumbering; the verify.sh optional band has shifted
    from #11..#14 (pre-BE-0383) to #14..#17 (post-BE-0387). The
    next contributor adding required step #14 (BE-0388 fuzz tests
    for validators, canonical `go test -run TestValidator ./...`
    if PRD names that filter) should follow the same edit shape
    AND prepare for an optional-band renumber to #15..#18.
  - `SENTINEL-CANNOT-BE-RE-REGISTERED-AS-SECRET` — the redactor's
    `minRedactableLen = 4` constant happens to be exactly the length
    of `"REDACTED"` (8) and `"[REDACTED]"` (10) so registering the
    sentinel as a secret would, in principle, cause the Redactor to
    scrub its own marker. The canonical pair's
    `r2 := NewRedactor(Sentinel, "REDACTED")` probe pins this case
    explicitly: if a future refactor lowers `minRedactableLen` or
    relaxes the dedupe filter, the test fails because the Redactor
    would scrub its own sentinel and make redacted output
    indistinguishable from never-redacted output. The probe deserves
    a place in the canonical pair so the regression surfaces in the
    public contract, not buried in an internal helper test.
  - `THREE-PACKAGE REDACTION-PREFIX BINDING` — the
    `TestRedaction` prefix binds across `internal/output`
    (central Redactor + canonical pair), `internal/controlplane/variables`
    (per-tenant LogValue, ScopedVariable, ResolvedVariable,
    ExplainProjection, plus the env_var_redaction static
    analyzer), and `internal/cli` (CLI envelope, dry-run, multipart
    upload). The dedicated `Redaction tests` CI step exercises
    every package in one shot; a regression in any one tearing
    the secret-leak posture fires the same gate. When adding a
    new redaction surface (e.g. an audit pipeline, a new
    transport like a custom header) name the test
    `TestRedaction_<Surface>...` so the prefix continues to bind
    across packages without modifying the static defence.

  name.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Multi-word invariant substrings MUST be quoted in the doc.**
    The first run failed with `missing required substring "no panic"`
    because the SECURITY.md text used "no-panic" (hyphenated,
    sentence-internal). The fix wrapped the literal as
    `"no panic"` in the section body so the matcher and the
    human-readable doc agree on one literal. Forward pattern: when
    pinning a multi-word phrase as a closed substring, prefer
    quoting the phrase in the doc (`"no panic"`, `"opt-in
    external"`, `"every push and PR"`) so the matcher binds to the
    literal a reviewer is most likely to write — and the matcher
    constant matches the quoted form verbatim. Hyphenation drift
    is a common false-positive.
  - **Multi-target surfaces: list EVERY target name explicitly.**
    SECURITY.md initially wrote "(`Name`, `Path`, `Domain`, ...)"
    which didn't satisfy a matcher pinning on the literal "FuzzName"
    substring. Fix: list the full nine-target FuzzXxx set verbatim
    so the doc names every load-bearing fact. Forward pattern: when
    a verification story's surface is a SET of N targets sharing one
    invariant, list ALL N target names verbatim in the SECURITY.md
    section (don't abbreviate with `...`) and pin a representative
    subset (first + middle + last) in the matcher's substring set
    so deleting an interior target trips the gate too.
  - **Canonical pair = closed-set coverage × runtime invariant.**
    BE-0388's design splits the load-bearing surface into two
    orthogonal invariants pinned by two canonical functions:
    `TestFuzzValidatorContractCoversExpectedValidators` (the
    closed-set coverage matcher, asserted by reading the file's
    own source via `runtime.Caller` so a future package move
    auto-updates the lookup) and
    `TestFuzzValidatorContractSeedCorpusRejectsHostileInputs`
    (the runtime no-panic matcher, asserted by `recover()`-wrapped
    invocations across the shared seed corpus). This split is the
    template for any verification story whose surface is a SET of
    targets sharing one invariant + a closed-set coverage rule.
    Sample siblings: BE-0394 (chaos Postgres disconnects), BE-0395
    (idempotency replay), BE-0398 (tenant isolation).
  - **FuzzXxx targets bind to BOTH `-run` and `-fuzz=`.**
    Go's fuzz tests run their seed corpus deterministically under
    `go test -run FuzzXxx` AND drive the randomised engine under
    `go test -fuzz=FuzzXxx`. The BE-0388 design keeps the existing
    FuzzXxx targets unchanged (they continue to support the
    optional `-fuzz=` driver for soak runs) AND adds a
    TestFuzzValidator-prefixed wrapper pair that binds to the
    `-run TestFuzzValidator ./...` filter on every `go test ./...`
    invocation. The wrapper complements, not replaces, the FuzzXxx
    targets. Document the `-fuzz=` driver as the opt-in escape
    hatch in SECURITY.md so an operator running a soak knows the
    entry point.
  - **Sandbox does NOT compile Go modules.** The
    `ctx_execute(language: "shell")` sandbox runs commands in a
    temporary directory that lacks the module's `go.mod`, so
    `go test ./internal/...` fails there with
    `ignoring go.mod in system temp root`. Run all `go test`,
    `go vet`, and `gofmt` commands via direct Bash (the project
    working directory). Use `ctx_execute_file` / `ctx_execute`
    ONLY for analysis/processing where stdout is the only signal
    needed (file slicing, JSON edits, grep summaries).
  - **Workflow Edit hook surfaces a generic command-injection
    reminder on first attempt.** The Edit hook on
    `.github/workflows/ci.yml` surfaced a generic "command
    injection" security reminder despite the inserted line
    containing zero untrusted input (a static
    `go test -run TestFuzzValidator ./...` command); the reminder
    is non-blocking and the second attempt succeeded. Forward
    pattern: ignore the reminder when the edit is a pure-literal
    `run:` insertion with no `${{ }}` expression. Established by
    BE-0386's commentary; this is now a second instance of the
    same gotcha.
  - **Per-story prediction for BE-0389 (migration tests from
    empty DB).** The PRD's `verificationLoop.requiredBackendCommands`
    already carries `go test -run TestMigrations ./...` from
    BE-0380; the canonical reference test
    `TestMigrations` already exists in
    `internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrate_test.go`. BE-0389
    is a renamed verification of the same gate from the
    bootstrap-from-empty-DB angle. Expected per-story knobs:
    canonical command unchanged (`go test -run TestMigrations`),
    new CI step name something like `Migration ladder tests`,
    verify.sh prefix #15 (next after BE-0388's #14), SECURITY.md
    section `## Migration Ladder Tests`. Static defence file
    `verification_suite_migrations_static_test.go`. Likely needs
    to ADD canonical TestMigrations* siblings (e.g.
    `TestMigrationsFromEmptyDatabase`) that exercise the
    empty-bootstrap path explicitly.

  - When the canonical pair contract spans BOTH deterministic
    (no infra) AND infrastructure-required substrates, ALWAYS
    encode each substrate in a separate member of the pair. A
    single combined test that branches on env-var presence
    would silently skip the deterministic gate when Postgres
    is unavailable. Two members keep the deterministic front
    line firing on every developer machine while the
    infrastructure gate covers the runtime contract in CI.
  - The closed-set coverage matcher MUST mirror the loader's
    filename grammar in a regex local to the test — not import
    a shared constant — so a future loader-grammar change
    touches BOTH sides in the same edit. Mirroring is the
    correct pattern; sharing would let a loader change silently
    relax the coverage gate.
  - When the apply-cleanly test reads the ledger back, sort by
    `ORDER BY version` and assert the FULL row by index against
    the loader's Migration slice — index-by-index name/version/
    checksum match, not just count. A count-only assertion
    would let a row insertion in the wrong order pass silently.
  - The `resource_id` actionable-failure identifier for
    migration errors is `schema_migrations.version=N` — a
    canonical, greppable form an operator can map back to the
    exact migration file. Forward-applicable: any future
    persistence-layer story whose row-level failures need an
    actionable identifier should use the
    `<table>.<column>=<value>` form.
  - When BE-0380's `-run TestMigrations` filter already
    matches the broader migrate tests, naming the BE-0389
    pair with the `EmptyDB` infix (so its `-run
    TestMigrationsEmptyDB` filter is strictly narrower) lets
    both filters coexist without collision. Forward-applicable
    to BE-0390 (canonical `TestMigrationsDowngrade*`?) and
    BE-0391 (canonical `TestMigrationsRace*`?).
  - Pre-existing test pollution warning carried from BE-0385
    still applies: the shared docker compose Postgres DB used
    via YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL has flaky failures in
    internal/controlplane/store/... outside the migrate
    package. BE-0389 runs a fresh throwaway DB per test
    invocation (testPool's crypto/rand-named DSN) so it is
    isolated from the pollution. Forward-applicable: every
    new Postgres-touching test should use testPool, never the
    raw DSN directly.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The single-resource GET contract test (BE-0125) does NOT need its own
    *HandlerForWithLogger helper. The corresponding list endpoint's helper
    (here listProjectsHandlerForWithLogger) constructs the full NewHandler
    with all 60+ fakes and the projects route table, and the path mux picks
    GET /v1/projects/{project_id} from the same handler. Reusing the helper
    avoids the 60-line fake-list duplication that would otherwise drift if
    NewHandler grows another port. Forward-applicable: every BE-01xx
    sibling for a {resource_id} GET endpoint (BE-0125 projects, BE-0155
    environments, BE-0185 services, etc.) should reuse its list endpoint's
    *HandlerForWithLogger rather than introduce a getXHandlerForWithLogger
    twin — the existing organizations_get_contract_test.go is the structural
    exception only because organizations has BOTH an org-id-less list AND
    an org-id GET that resolve through different reader-call shapes.
  - The closest twin for a {resource_id} GET contract test is
    organizations_get_contract_test.go. The shape is identical: three
    tests (stdout/stderr writer, bearer-redaction success+denial,
    dependency-cause non-leakage), one bearer constant, two
    captureProcessOutput-flavoured tests run NON-parallel (the global
    os.Stdout/os.Stderr swap is process-global), and decodeError(t, rec,
    "E_UNAVAILABLE") for the 503 wire check.
  - The "must not echo caller input" guard in services_logs_test.go does a
    full-body substring scan. Random request_id hex strings can produce
    coincidental substring matches with short caller inputs ("abc", "def",
    "bad", etc.). Future tests that pin "value not echoed" should scope
    the scan to the error.message or error.hint field, not the whole
    response body — the request_id is a generated value with no
    redaction obligation.
  - PRD-edit gotcha: do NOT use Node JSON.parse + JSON.stringify to flip a
    passes flag in ralph/prd.json. JSON.stringify renders non-ASCII chars
    as their literal UTF-8 form (em-dash, smart quotes), while the
    committed file uses \uXXXX escapes throughout the notes/description
    text. The round-trip rewrites thousands of bytes across the file as a
    side effect of flipping a single boolean. Use a targeted Edit tool
    operation anchored on the surrounding 3 lines of the target story
    block instead — diff stays at 1 insertion + 1 deletion. (The BE-0389
    progress entry says "MUST add via Node fs round-trip" for the
    requiredBackendCommands list ADDITION case; that case needs JSON
    structure-aware editing because the addition is a new array element
    whose position is determined by JSON ordering. The PASSES-flag-flip
    case is different — it's a single-token swap on a single line and the
    targeted Edit anchored on 4 surrounding lines is uniquely safe.)

  go vet ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ (clean)
