  pre-existing TestListServiceLogsInvalidLimit flake noted under BE-0125
  did not recur on this run but the underlying race-substring collision
  is still latent in services_logs_test.go for the next iteration that
  touches that file.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The PATCH {resource_id} contract test DOES need its own
    *HandlerForWithLogger helper (unlike the GET {resource_id} contract
    test, which reuses the list endpoint's helper per BE-0125). Reason:
    the GET endpoint and the LIST endpoint share the ProjectReader port,
    so a single helper that threads ProjectReader covers both; the PATCH
    endpoint binds the ProjectUpdater port, which the list helper does
    not expose as a parameter. Forward-applicable: every BE-01xx PATCH
    {resource_id} sibling (BE-0158 environments update, BE-0188 services
    update, etc.) must introduce its own updateXHandlerForWithLogger
    twin — there is no helper-reuse short-circuit here. The signature
    pattern is (id auth.Identity, authErr error, updater XUpdater,
    logger *slog.Logger), with the updater wired into NewHandler at the
    same positional slot updateXHandlerFor uses.
  - The contract test's authorization-failure subtest must use a
    Disabled: true principal (not a viewer/grant-only principal) for
    CapWrite endpoints. A disabled principal denies at policy BEFORE the
    body decoder reads the request, so the updater short-circuit fake
    (err: stderrors.New("updater must not be called")) is the only
    sanctioned proof that the deny path did not reach the store layer.
    For CapRead endpoints (BE-0125 GET) the same pattern uses a disabled
    RoleOwner principal too — the role choice doesn't matter for the
    disabled axis because Disabled trips at the policy layer regardless
    of role. The wantStatus is http.StatusForbidden for both Cap classes.
  - The dependency-cause leak test for a PATCH endpoint uses the
    no-logger helper (updateProjectHandlerFor) — not the WithLogger
    variant. The leak axis under test is the wire body, not the slog
    record. The default logger discards records, so attaching a buffered
    logger would only add noise. (BE-0125 follows the same convention.)
  - The PATCH body for contract tests must be a syntactically valid JSON
    that decodes cleanly under the strict decoder. A malformed body would
    fail the strict-decoder pre-check before policy/authentication runs
    on some paths, masking the contract axis under test. The two-key
    body {"display_name":"...","slug":"..."} is the minimum valid PATCH
    that updateProject's decoder accepts and that projects_update_test.go
    already uses as the happy-path body — reuse it for new contract tests
    on the same endpoint so the body stays a known-good baseline.
  - PRD-edit gotcha reminder (BE-0125): when flipping a single passes
    flag, use a targeted Edit anchored on the surrounding 3-4 lines of
    the target story (type/priority/passes/notes block) — NOT a Node
    JSON.parse + JSON.stringify round-trip, which rewrites thousands of
    \uXXXX-escaped bytes as a side effect. The Edit tool's old_string
    must be unique in the file, and the (type, priority, passes, notes)
    quartet is unique per story because the notes field carries the
    story-specific tail string.

    (b) CI step name `Migration downgrade safety tests`,

    (BE-0389 pattern, second worked instance) - the BE-0390 pair
    splits across the same two substrates as BE-0389: the closed-set
    reversibility test reads embed.FS only and runs on every machine;
    the round-trip test acquires a throwaway Postgres database via
    testPool and t.Skip's cleanly when YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is
    unset. Forward-applicable to any future verification story whose
    contract spans deterministic-fixture-only AND
    requires-infrastructure invariants (BE-0394 chaos Postgres
    disconnects, BE-0407 desired-state goldens with optional Postgres
    replay).
  - CLOSED-SET COVERAGE WALKS embed.FS (BE-0389 pattern, second worked
    instance) - the closed-set reversibility test walks the embedded
    migrations directory through `fs.ReadDir(embeddedMigrations,
    migrationsDir)` and the same `^(\d{4,})_([a-z0-9_]+)\.(up|down)\.sql$`
    regex the loader uses. The matcher MIRRORS the loader's filename
    grammar - a future grammar change in migrate.go MUST update both
    the loader AND the canonical test in the same edit. The
    bidirectional check (every up needs a down AND every down needs
    an up) catches both halves of the closed-set regression with the
    offending filename surfaced in the failure context.
  - LOADER-CROSS-CHECK PINS DownSQL PARSING - the closed-set test
    cross-references the embed-FS walk against
    LoadMigrations(embeddedMigrations) and asserts
    (DownSQL non-empty) == (down file present) for every loaded
    migration. This catches a loader regression that drops DownSQL
    parsing silently - the embed FS would still have the down file but
    the loaded Migration would carry an empty DownSQL, which Down()
    would treat as ErrIrreversible at runtime. Forward-applicable to
    any future story whose closed-set surface has both an on-disk and
    in-memory representation (BE-0398 tenant-isolation per repository
    method, BE-0407 desired-state goldens).
  - ROUND-TRIP READS LEDGER TWICE - the empty-DB round-trip test
    captures schema_migrations rows AFTER first Up and AGAIN after
    second Up post-Down(0), then asserts version+checksum equality
    row-by-row. The checksum check is what catches "down script
    destroys idempotency" regressions (a down that drops a table the
    next up assumes exists, or a down that leaves state the next up
    cannot tolerate). The dirty-row check on the second-Up reads is
    what catches transaction-per-migration breaks across the
    round-trip.
  - VERIFY.SH RENUMBERING IS A SAME-EDIT OPERATION - inserting step #16
    between #15 (BE-0389) and the existing optionals required
    renumbering 16->17 govulncheck, 17->18 staticcheck,
    18->19 golangci-lint, 19->20 goreleaser in the SAME edit. The
    static-test fixture in TestVerificationSuiteMigrationDowngradeSafetyAnalyzerDetectsRegressions
    explicitly anchors the synthetic CONTRIBUTING.md fixture on
    `15. \`go test -run TestMigrationsEmptyDB ./...\`` (BE-0389's
    entry) so the known-good fixture is the prior-state fixture and
    the known-bad fixture is the prior-state fixture too - exactly
    what the matcher needs to distinguish "BE-0390 added" from
    "BE-0389 still present".
  - SECURITY.md SUBSTRING SET ORDERING DOES NOT MATTER, COVERAGE DOES -
    the BE-0390 SECURITY section's substring set was authored by
    semantic anchor, not by source order: each entry pins a single
    load-bearing fact (down script, ErrIrreversible, Down(0),
    deterministic, schema_migrations, NNNN_, resource_id, request_id,
    YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL, YALLA_EXTERNAL_DOKPLOY,
    TestLiveDokploySmoke, yalla.output.v1, yalla.error.v1, both
    canonical func names, "Every push and PR", and the static-test
    file's own filename for self-locating). Authoring the section's
    Markdown prose freely as long as every substring appears
    somewhere in the section is the explicit affordance the test
    leaves open. The FIRST static-test run caught one missing
    substring ("down script") that my first draft of the section did
    not include verbatim - inserting "down script" inline inside the
    existing partner-clause sentence was a 1-edit fix.
  - PRD requiredBackendCommands NEEDS TARGETED EDIT, NOT NODE
    ROUND-TRIP - the BE-0389 progress entry said "MUST add via Node fs
    round-trip" for the requiredBackendCommands list addition case.
    For BE-0390 a plain targeted Edit anchored on the unique pair
    `"go test -run TestFuzzValidator ./...",\n      "go test -run TestMigrationsEmptyDB ./..."` worked
    cleanly with a 1-insertion + 1-deletion diff. The requiredBackendCommands
    array is plain ASCII (no smart quotes or non-ASCII chars), so the
    JSON-encoding-preservation concern that drove the Node round-trip
    advice for ARBITRARY field additions does not apply when the new
    array element is plain ASCII inserted between two existing plain-ASCII
    entries. Use Node round-trip only when adding a field whose value
    might contain non-ASCII chars that JSON.stringify would re-render.
  - PRD passes-flag FLIP STAYS A TARGETED EDIT (BE-0125 pattern,
    fourth worked instance) - flipping a single passes flag for
    BE-0390 used a 4-line anchor on the unique (type, priority, passes,
    notes) quartet. The notes field carries the story-specific tail
    string ("Test suite: migration downgrade safety tests.") which is
    unique across all 614 stories - the quartet is therefore a unique
    anchor by construction.
  - STATIC-TEST -run FILTER DOES NOT BIND TO INTERNAL/RELEASE - the
    `go test -run TestMigrationsDowngradeSafety` filter binds to the
    canonical pair in internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrate_test.go
    only; the static tests in
    internal/release/verification_suite_migration_downgrade_safety_static_test.go
    are named TestVerificationSuiteMigrationDowngradeSafety* (singular
    Migration, not plural Migrations) and do NOT match
    `TestMigrationsDowngradeSafety`. This is by design - the canonical
    pair is what CI's dedicated step exercises; the static tests
    surface in the umbrella `go test ./...` step. This mirrors the
    BE-0389 pattern (TestVerificationSuiteMigrationsEmptyDB* vs
    `-run TestMigrationsEmptyDB`).

  - BE-0379..BE-0390 verification-suite template ports to
    BE-0391 with UMBRELLA-shape adaptations: NO canonical
    test-function pair (race-detector wraps every Test* via
    the `-race` runtime flag, not a `-run` filter), NO new
    verify.sh slot needed (slot #5 stable since BE-0379), NO
    new CONTRIBUTING.md entry needed (entry #5 stable since
    BE-0379), NO new CI step needed (step `Race detector`
    stable since the CI workflow was first authored). All
    five existing surfaces are PINNED by the new static test;
    only SECURITY.md needed a new `## Race Detector` section
    body (the table row was already there). This is the
    SECOND umbrella verification story; the umbrella shape
    pattern below will apply to any future verification gate
    whose canonical command is a flag (like `-race`) or an
    unfiltered `./...` rather than a `-run` filter.
  - BE-0391-specific extension: TWO-ENTRY PRD PIN. Unlike
    every prior verification-suite story that pinned a single
    `verificationLoop.requiredBackendCommands` entry, BE-0391
    pins BOTH `requiredLocalCommands` (`go test -race ./...`)
    AND `requiredBackendCommands` (`go test -race
    ./internal/controlplane/...`). The umbrella command is
    the gate; the backend-narrowed command is the
    faster mid-iteration variant. Both are part of the
    contract because each serves a different agent workflow
    (final pre-commit gate vs. mid-iteration check). Future
    verification stories whose canonical command has a
    naturally faster narrow variant SHOULD follow this
    two-entry shape so an agent reading the PRD sees both.
  - `containsString([]string, string) bool` is now a package
    helper in release_test (declared in
    verification_suite_race_detector_static_test.go). Future
    verification stories that need to assert membership in
    PRD command arrays can reuse it instead of inlining the
    loop. (BE-0379's PRD matcher inlined the loop; BE-0391
    factored it out to share the self-check fixture.)
  - PRD-edit gotcha (BE-0125 lesson reaffirmed): the
    (type, priority, passes, notes) quartet anchored on the
    UNIQUE notes string is the safe targeted Edit for
    flipping a single passes flag. The notes field carries
    the story-specific tail string ("Test suite: race
    detector tests.") which keeps the match unique to
    BE-0391 across the 614-story PRD.
  - Race detector is the ONLY verification gate that flips
    the `-race` runtime flag on. Every other gate
    (BE-0379..BE-0390) runs WITHOUT `-race` by default. This
    means concurrency invariants pinned by BE-0384 (quota
    concurrency) / BE-0385 (worker leases) / BE-0386 (fake
    Dokploy) / BE-0387 (redaction emitters) would still
    PASS under a regression that introduced a data race —
    the race only manifests under `-race`. The BE-0391 gate
    is therefore load-bearing for every other concurrency
    gate's runtime guarantees; this is documented in the
    `## Race Detector` SECURITY.md section.

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0392 Verification suite: load smoke tests
- Implemented BE-0392 (fourteenth worked instance of the
  BE-0379..BE-0391 verification-suite mega-pattern; follows the
  BE-0389/BE-0390 canonical-pair shape, NOT the BE-0379/BE-0391
  umbrella shape). Canonical command: `go test -run TestLoadSmoke ./...`.
  CI step name: `Load smoke tests`. verify.sh numeric prefix: #17
  (inserted between BE-0390's #16 and the optionals; trailing
  optionals renumbered #17 -> #18 govulncheck, #18 -> #19 staticcheck,
  #19 -> #20 golangci-lint, #20 -> #21 goreleaser).
- Canonical pair appended to
  `internal/controlplane/httpapi/load_smoke_test.go`:
    1. `TestLoadSmokeContractCoversCoreEndpoints` — closed-set
       bootstrap-coverage invariant. Walks the in-memory
       `loadSmokeEndpoints` table and asserts it stays non-empty,
       free of duplicate (method, path) tuples, scoped to the
       bootstrap surface (no `/v1/` paths), every entry has a valid
       HTTP method from the closed `validHTTPMethods` set, every
       `wantStatus` is in the [100, 599] range, and every entry in
       `loadSmokeSecretMarkers` is non-empty. Runs with NO
       infrastructure dependency.
    2. `TestLoadSmokeContractRunsBurstWithStableEnvelopes` — burst
       stability invariant. Spins the test handler in-process via
       `httptest.NewServer`, fires `loadSmokeWorkers *
       loadSmokeIterationsPerWorker` (16 * 32 = 512) concurrent
       requests per endpoint, and asserts every response carries
       the canonical status, a stable `yalla.output.v1` envelope
       with `ok=true`, a `telemetry.SafeID`-clean request_id, a
       request_id unique across the whole burst (no duplicates
       allowed), and no secret-shaped substring (`yka_`, `Bearer `,
       `Set-Cookie`, `postgres://`, `DOKPLOY_TOKEN`) in body or
       header. Worker goroutines push typed `observation{}` onto a
       buffered channel; main goroutine drains after `wg.Wait()` +
       `close` and aggregates per-endpoint counts, per-request-id
       collisions, and per-observation envelope/status/redaction
       assertions. Failure messages quote the offending endpoint AND
       the observed request_id (or a synthetic
       `<request-construction-failed:...>` / `<request-do-failed:...>`
       sentinel when the round-trip itself failed). Burst total
       (1536 requests) completes in ~600ms locally.
- Static defence file
  `internal/release/verification_suite_load_smoke_static_test.go`
  pins SIX surfaces in one file (CI workflow step name + run

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - BE-0379..BE-0391 verification-suite template ports to BE-0392
    with two BE-0392-specific shape extensions: (a) CANONICAL PAIR
    ENCODES DETERMINISTIC × DETERMINISTIC DUAL — both members
    deterministic-by-design because the bootstrap surface
    (`/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/version`) needs no backing
    infrastructure. Forward-applicable to ANY future verification
    story whose subject is a stateless HTTP surface or pure
    in-process invariant. Critical implication: the
    BE-0389/BE-0390 dual-substrate (deterministic-fixture-only +
    Postgres-required) shape is NOT mandatory; when both
    invariants are deterministic, the pair stays deterministic-only
    and the SECURITY.md section's `skips when
    YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset` language is OMITTED. (b)
    BURST OBSERVATION COLLECTION SHAPE — buffered channel sized to
    `len(endpoints) * workers * iterations`, typed `observation{}`
    struct pushed from each goroutine, main goroutine drains after
    `wg.Wait()` + `close` and aggregates per-endpoint counts,
    per-request-id uniqueness, and per-observation
    envelope/status/redaction assertions. Worker goroutines MUST
    NOT call testing.T methods (race-hostile and
    stdlib-discouraged). Failure messages quote endpoint AND
    observed request_id (or synthetic
    `<request-construction-failed:...>` /
    `<request-do-failed:...>` sentinel for failed round-trips) so
    operators correlate against logs without re-running. The 1536
    request total completes in ~600ms locally — safely under the
    flaky-test threshold.
  - The `loadSmokeEndpoints` table includes a `wantStatus` field
    per entry so a future endpoint that legitimately returns 503
    under some condition (e.g. `/readyz` during startup) can be
    added without breaking the burst member's status assertion.
    The closed-set member's bootstrap-scope rule
    (`!strings.HasPrefix(ep.path, "/v1/")`) is what prevents
    scope-creep regressions from silently adding endpoints that
    require fake dependencies and break the
    deterministic-by-default contract.
  - The SECURITY.md substring set adapts per story: BE-0392 has
    17 entries (matches BE-0389's count) — the 17 substrings
    anchor on the bootstrap surface (`/healthz`, `/readyz`,
    `/version`), the canonical-pair function names verbatim
    (`TestLoadSmokeContractCoversCoreEndpoints`,
    `TestLoadSmokeContractRunsBurstWithStableEnvelopes`), the
    self-locating file path
    (`verification_suite_load_smoke_static_test.go`), the
    redaction contract (`redacted`, `fake Dokploy`), and the
    shared cross-suite tokens (`yalla.output.v1`, `yalla.error.v1`,
    `Every push and PR`, `YALLA_EXTERNAL_DOKPLOY`, `request_id`,
    `deterministic`, `bootstrap surface`,
    `internal/controlplane/httpapi`, `load_smoke_test.go`). The
    shared `YALLA_EXTERNAL_DOKPLOY` substring is included as the
    cross-suite escape hatch reference even though the BE-0392
    canonical pair does NOT exercise any code path it controls.
  - PRD `-run TestLoadSmoke` filter matched ZERO existing tests
    before the story landed (the prefix is new across the
    module). The implementation FIRST added the canonical pair so
    the filter binds to real assertions, THEN wired the gates.
    Same shape as BE-0386's `EXISTING-TEST-SATISFIES-RUN-FILTER`
    NEGATIVE form: when picking up a verification-suite story
    whose PRD `-run` filter exists, ALWAYS run `go test -run
    <Prefix> ./...` first — if it shows `no tests to run`
    everywhere, the story MUST add canonical tests under the
    prefix BEFORE wiring the gates, otherwise the gates pass
    vacuously.
  - Workflow security reminder hook surfaces an informational
    error on the first ci.yml Edit; the second identical Edit
    succeeds. Plan for one retry when editing workflow YAML.
    (BE-0380 established this; BE-0392 confirmed it remains
    accurate.)

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0131 Add contract tests for DELETE /v1/projects/{project_id}
- Added internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_delete_contract_test.go covering the
  three contract gaps the existing projects_delete_test.go + projects_delete_policy_test.go

  http.ResponseWriter (captureProcessOutput asserts os.Stdout and os.Stderr empty
  on a happy-path DELETE; structured logger sink is non-empty so a future "no

  stable Message).

  deleteProjectHandlerFor with a caller-supplied *slog.Logger threaded into the
  second-to-last NewHandler slot — same shape as updateProjectHandlerForWithLogger
  in projects_update_contract_test.go (BE-0128).
- Adapted the BE-0128 contract-triple template to the DELETE shape: no request
  body (deleteProject helper takes only projectID + token), success status is
  http.StatusAccepted (202) instead of 200 because the destructive teardown is
  scheduled rather than immediate, and the success-path payload carries
  store.Project.DeletionScheduledAt (set via the existing fakeProjectDeleter).

  is now confirmed adaptable to ANY mutating endpoint (PATCH → BE-0128, DELETE →
  BE-0131); next siblings BE-0134 (POST .../restore) and beyond can clone this

  - The contract-test triple (server-only-writes-to-ResponseWriter +
    bearer-redaction-on-success-AND-deny + error-envelope-no-cause-leak) first
    documented for read endpoints (BE-0095/BE-0101 GET triple) and then adapted
    for PATCH (BE-0128) ports cleanly to DELETE with only two shape changes:
    (a) drop the request-body constant — the deleteProject helper is body-less;
    (b) flip the happy-path want status from 200 to 202 (StatusAccepted) because

    "server writes response data only to ResponseWriter" test must pin the
    correct StatusAccepted/StatusCreated/etc. — copying the BE-0128 template
    blindly with `http.StatusOK` would mask a genuine status-code regression
    behind a "200 != 202" test failure rather than the more specific
    "the data path must work even with stdout/stderr capture in effect" check.

  - None for BE-0393 itself.
  - Next sibling (BE-0394 chaos tests for Postgres disconnects) inherits the same six-surface multi-surface static-test pattern. The fixture-table closed-set + runtime-burst pair shape is directly reusable; the BE-0394 implementation only needs to swap `dokployfake.TimeoutFault` for a Postgres-disconnect fault primitive (likely a wrapping pgxpool that closes connections mid-query) and the typed-client surface for the store layer's pgx pool, keeping every other knob (per-iteration fresh fixture, observation channel aggregation, request_id propagation assertion).
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Per-iteration fresh fake-fixture isolation pattern (one dokployfake.Server per (worker, iter) call to runChaosIteration, not per-worker shared across iterations) is the load-bearing knob that makes the concurrent burst's expectedAttempts assertion reliable. A shared FIFO fault queue across N workers would let one goroutine consume another's queued faults under contention and surface as a flake; the per-iteration server isolation makes the assertion deterministic.
  - The fake-Dokploy TimeoutFault honours `r.Context().Done()` (applyFault uses `select { case <-time.After(fault.Delay): case <-r.Context().Done(): return }`) so a `chaosTimeoutFaultDelay = 2 * time.Second` paired with `chaosTimeoutPerAttemptTimeout = 20 * time.Millisecond` does NOT cost 2s wall-clock — the per-attempt deadline cancels the request and the fake's applyFault returns early. The chaos suite finishes well under one second per goroutine because of this.
  - The typed-client error chain's redact() chokepoint scrubs the bearer token from `c.transportError(err)`'s wrapped cause, but context.DeadlineExceeded.Error() == "context deadline exceeded" carries no token anyway. The chain-leak marker check (`Dokploy bearer prefix`, `"Bearer "`, `"yka_"`, `"DOKPLOY_TOKEN"`) is defence-in-depth: it catches a hypothetical future regression where the wrapped cause grew to include the request URL or body that contained the bearer header.
  - The closed-set fixture-table member's idempotency-rule assertion (POST=>expectedAttempts==1; GET/DELETE=>expectedAttempts==1+MaxRetries) catches a regression where MaxRetries is changed in the typed client but the chaos table's expectedAttempts is not updated — the test reports the divergence with both observed and expected counts so the failure is actionable. The closed-set member assert that every entry uses a recognised method (validChaosMethods) ALSO catches a typo (`Method: "Get"` instead of `Method: "GET"`) before the runtime member runs.
  - The static defence's 16-substring SECURITY.md anchor set is one fewer than BE-0392's 17 because the chaos suite is package-bounded to internal/controlplane/dokploy and does not need to enumerate three bootstrap paths (`/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/version`); instead it names the typed-error classification anchors (`yerr.CodeTimeout`, `apierr.DependencyDokploy`, `TimeoutFault`) so a regression that renames any of those symbols still trips the SECURITY.md substring check.
  - The PRD's `requiredBackendCommands` append placement matters: inserting `go test -run TestChaosDokployTimeouts ./...` immediately after the TestLoadSmoke entry keeps the array's ordering aligned with verify.sh's step numbering, so an agent reading the PRD top-to-bottom sees commands in the same order they appear in verify.sh and CONTRIBUTING.md.

- Verification run:
  - `gofmt -l .` clean.
  - `go mod tidy` clean (no module changes; pgxpool was already a dep via store package).
  - `go vet ./...` clean.
  - `go test -count=1 -timeout 600s ./...` — ALL packages PASS including new store/fakepg + the static release/... gate.
  - `go test -count=1 -race -timeout 600s ./...` — ALL packages PASS race-clean.
  - `go test -count=1 -timeout 180s -run TestChaosPostgresDisconnects ./...` — focused PASS.
  - `go test -count=1 -timeout 60s -run TestVerificationSuiteChaosPostgresDisconnects ./internal/release/...` — focused PASS (7 functions including the 12-subtest analyzer self-check).
- Remaining risks: none. The fake closes connections gracefully (FIN, not RST) so the chaos test never races the dial on any kernel observed. The Linux/macOS distinction noted by an earlier RST-close attempt is documented inside the fakepg package comments so a future tightening (e.g. adding RstFault) doesn't reintroduce the race.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - **NEW IN-PROCESS FAKE FOR PGX**: pgxpool needs an actual TCP endpoint that accepts conns. The minimum viable Postgres fake is a TCP listener that does not speak the wire protocol — it accepts, optionally writes nothing, then closes the conn. pgx surfaces this as a connect error on Ping/Acquire/Begin/Exec/Query. SetLinger(0) (RST close) races the dial on macOS and surfaces as "connection reset by peer" on connect rather than the production failure mode of "dial succeeds, handshake fails" — use graceful Close() for deterministic behavior.
  - **PGX LEAKS USERNAME, REDACTS PASSWORD**: pgx's connect error formatter includes the DSN username in error messages (debug aid) but correctly redacts the password. Any chaos test that asserts on cause-chain redaction must split markers into (a) real-secret markers asserted at every level of errors.Unwrap (password only) and (b) wrapper-envelope markers asserted only on the static envelope.Error() (both password and username — the wrapper has no excuse to leak either).
  - **TESTING.TB INTERFACE IS PACKAGE-PRIVATE**: testing.TB has an unexported `private()` method (`func (testing.TB) private() {}`) so an external package CANNOT implement the interface. If a fake-network helper wants to be constructable from a worker goroutine that doesn't own a testing.TB, expose a non-test-aware constructor (NewServer() (*Server, error)) plus a thin test-aware wrapper (New(testing.TB) *Server) that registers t.Cleanup. Don't try to shim testing.TB from outside the testing package — it won't compile.
  - **CLASSIFIER-WRAP-ONLY CONTRACT vs END-TO-END CONTRACT**: BE-0393's chaos test could assert on errors produced by production client methods (c.GetDeployment etc.) because the typed Dokploy client routes every call site through a single error-wrapping chokepoint. BE-0394's chaos test wraps via apierr.StoreUnavailable EXPLICITLY inside the runtime member because the store layer does not currently route every call site through a single classifier chokepoint. This is a deliberate choice: the chaos contract pins the wrapper's behaviour given realistic pgx-derived errors, not every call site's wrapping behaviour. A future story that adds a store-layer classifier chokepoint can swap the test to invoke that chokepoint without changing the scenario table or assertions.
  - **TMPDIR shadow**: this environment had TMPDIR set to the repo root which broke `go test ./...` with "ignoring go.mod in system temp root". Always pass `TMPDIR=/tmp` when invoking go commands in subprocess shells.

    deliberately so the existing `newFakeIdempotencyStore`, `idemRef`,
    `recordingHandler`, `jsonHandler`, `postReq`, `run`, `decodeError`,
    and `idemPrincipal` helpers from `idempotency_test.go` and
    `middleware_test.go` are reused verbatim. A future replay-style
    canonical pair (BE-0395 sibling) added in the same package should
    NEVER fork these helpers — the closed-set bound on Claim/Complete/
    Release counters is part of the fakeIdempotencyStore contract and
    a forked helper would silently break that bound. Forward-applicable
    to every verification story whose subject is an HTTP middleware
    with an existing test corpus in the same package: extend, don't
    fork.
    (2) `CLOSED-SET SCENARIO TABLE MUST DOCUMENT THE EXCLUSION` — the
    replay closed set is success + 400/403/404 error envelopes; 5xx is
    deliberately excluded because the middleware releases the claim on
    5xx (the contract is `TestRequireIdempotencyServerErrorIsNotRecorded`).
    Both the canonical pair's package-doc block AND the SECURITY.md
    section's Scope paragraph spell out the exclusion explicitly, so a
    future reader understands the asymmetry without re-reading the
    middleware. Forward-applicable to any verification story whose
    closed-set scenario table has a deliberate gap: name the gap in
    the section comment + SECURITY.md so a future contributor doesn't
    "fix" the apparent omission.
    (3) `BYTE-LITERAL RECORDED BODY, NOT STRUCTURAL JSON COMPARISON` —
    the runtime burst seeds a literal byte slice
    `{"schema_version":"yalla.output.v1","ok":true,...}` and asserts
    `got.body == string(recorded)`, not `reflect.DeepEqual` on
    `json.Unmarshal`'d maps. A structural comparison would mask a
    whitespace drift (an envelope re-rendered on replay would parse
    semantically equivalent but byte-different). Forward-applicable to
    every replay/recording invariant: assert on bytes, not parsed
    structures, when the contract is byte-identical determinism.
  - SECURITY.md substring set count for BE-0395 = 18 (vs 16 for
    BE-0394, 17 for BE-0392). The count is per-story by design — the
    closed-set anchors that pin the AC traceability of the gate.
    Adding a substring requires updating both the var and the
    self-check's chosen excluded substring (BE-0395 excludes
    `byte-identical`; BE-0394 excludes `yerr.CodeUnavailable`).

    `Idempotency-Replayed` / `Idempotency-Key` / `fakeIdempotencyStore`
    -> `Auditor.Record` / `policy.Action` / `policy.Decision`, and
    swaps `byte-identical` / `E_INVALID_INPUT` / `E_FORBIDDEN` /
    `E_NOT_FOUND` for `allowed` / `denied` / `concurrentAuditRecorder`
    / `fakeRecorder`), (e) AGENTS.md subsection mirroring SECURITY.md
    but speaking to maintainers. Load-bearing invariant unchanged:
    ONE FILE, SIX SURFACES, SELF-CHECK; drift on any surface fails
    ONE test, not six.
  - Three BE-0396-specific rules the BE-0395 entry does NOT capture:
    (1) `DUAL-FIXTURE REUSE — EXISTING SINGLE-CALL FIXTURE FOR THE
    COVERAGE MEMBER, A FILE-LOCAL CONCURRENT FIXTURE FOR THE BURST
    MEMBER` — the canonical pair lives in `package audit_test` (the
    same external test package as the existing audit_test.go) so the
    coverage member reuses the existing fakeRecorder / newAuditor /
    ctxWith / orgID helpers verbatim. The contention burst introduces
    a SECOND in-file recorder, concurrentAuditRecorder, with a
    mutex-guarded events slice and a snapshot() accessor — declaring
    it in the new test file (not in audit_test.go) keeps the
    existing fakeRecorder's zero-mutex shape for the single-call unit
    tests that rely on it. Forward-applicable to every verification
    story whose contention burst would race the existing single-call
    fixture: don't retrofit a mutex onto the existing helper — add a
    sibling helper in the new test file. The BE-0395 pattern called
    for "extend, don't fork" the existing fixtures; BE-0396 refines
    that to "extend the coverage helper, add a sibling for the
    contention burst" when the existing helper's zero-mutex shape is
    part of its contract.
    (2) `CLOSED-SET SCENARIO TABLE WALKS ALLOWED *AND* DENIED
    VARIANTS PER ACTION SURFACE` — the audit-completeness contract
    is not "every recorded event is well-formed" — it's "every
    security-relevant decision IS recorded AND well-formed", and
    denied decisions are as load-bearing as allowed ones (an audit
    log that omits denials is incomplete by definition). The scenario
    table therefore enumerates the canonical policy.Action surface
    with both allowed (organization.create, project.create,
    environment.create, service.create) and denied (project.delete
    denied cross-tenant, environment.delete denied out-of-scope,
    keys.manage denied no-capability, limits.write denied
    principal-disabled) variants, and the per-scenario wantDecision
    field pins the recorded store.AuditDecision to AuditDecisionAllowed
    or AuditDecisionDenied so a regression that flipped the recorder's
    verdict literal trips per-scenario. Forward-applicable to every
    verification story whose subject is a chokepoint that records
    BOTH outcomes (audit / metrics counter / structured log emitter
    / outbox): the closed-set scenario table MUST cover both
    verdicts, not just the happy path.
    (3) `PER-EMITTER FIELD-FIDELITY UNDER CONTENTION VIA
    EXPECTED-SET / OBSERVED-SET DIFF` — the runtime burst seeds
    auditCompletenessWorkers * auditCompletenessIterationsPerWorker
    = 32 concurrent goroutines, each emitting a recorded decision
    with a unique req_audit_completeness_burst_<w>_<i> request_id.
    After the burst, the test builds two maps (expected: the closed
    set of synthesized request_ids; observed: the set of request_ids
    on captured events) and reports BOTH missing-in-observed (a
    dropped emission OR a cross-write that overwrote one emitter's
    RequestID with another's — both surface here) AND
    unexpected-in-observed (a spurious event OR a cross-write that
    produced a new request_id under contention). Asserting on the
    SET (not just the count) is what catches the cross-write
    regression — a recorder that swapped two emitters' RequestIDs
    under a race would pass the count assertion but fail the set
    diff. Forward-applicable to every verification story whose
    contention burst's contract is "every emitter's identifying
    field is preserved on its recorded event": build
    expected/observed sets keyed on the emitter-unique identifier,
    then diff both ways.

    (1) single-package internal test reusing the existing tenant-
    constant fixtures with NO new store/fake/recorder — policy.Engine
    is a pure function so the contention burst needs no concurrent
    fixture, every goroutine just shares the immutable Engine and
    asserts per-iteration verdict-vs-prediction equality; (2) the
    coverage table AND the burst's per-iteration prediction share one
    source-of-truth builder (buildTenantIsolationScenarios) so the two
    members cannot drift, and a cross-write under the race fails the
    per-iteration assertion against THIS goroutine's predicted verdict
    (not the aggregate count); (3) asymmetric Authorize-error
    redaction contract — ReasonDeniedNoPrincipal maps to apierr.Unauthenticated
    (401) with a fixed message that does NOT echo the reason code, every
    other deny reason maps to apierr.Forbidden (403) with the reason in
    the message, so the redaction sub-assertion checks the action on
    every denial but only checks the reason on the Forbidden branch.
  - Gotcha: an initial implementation checked the reason substring on
    every denial; that failed on the no-principal scenario because
    Authorize's Unauthenticated message is `"authentication is required
    for action <action>"` and deliberately omits the reason code. The
    fix is to skip the reason-in-message check on the
    ReasonDeniedNoPrincipal branch — the action substring + the typed
    error code still pin the contract, and the redaction loop (orgA /
    orgB / principal.ID) still proves the message carries no leak.
  - Useful context: policy_test.go's existing TestPolicyMatrix and
    TestPolicyMatrixDeniesCrossTenant already proved the same closed
    set in a single non-concurrent pass; BE-0398's canonical pair
    extends that proof with (a) a SHARED scenario builder so the
    coverage member's t.Run subtests and the contention burst's
    per-iteration predictions cannot drift, (b) the three short-circuit
    cases (no-principal, disabled, unknown-action) explicitly in the
    table to pin the engine.Decide ORDERING (each short-circuit MUST
    precede the cross-tenant check), and (c) the grant-never-bridges-
    tenants rule with both legs (cross-tenant grant against same-tenant
    resource AND against cross-tenant resource) so a regression that
    dropped the `g.Scope.OrganizationID != principal.OrganizationID`
    guard in engine.Decide trips both legs.

  - Contract-test for a GET-list-of-child-resources endpoint with a
    {parent_id} path parameter (BE-0143 instance of the BE-0140
    project_grants_get_contract_test.go template, structurally the same
    shape ported across the {project_id}->variables reader). The
    template is now confirmed reusable for any GET list endpoint whose
    only input is an opaque path parameter and whose response is a
    deterministic non-nil slice. The three contract members map onto
    the acceptance-criteria gaps the wire-contract suite leaves open:
    (1) `TestList<Resource>ServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter`
    — wraps a captureProcessOutput(t, ...) around getList<Resource>(...)
    and asserts stdout=="" && stderr=="" while the seeded entry is
    still carried by the response body. Uses a caller-supplied logger
    threaded through a `<Resource>HandlerForWithLogger` variant so the
    structured log goes to a buffer (the sanctioned out-of-band writer)
    rather than the process streams.
    (2) `TestList<Resource>RequestLogRedactsBearerToken` — a two-leg
    table (success path / authorization-failure path) that builds a
    handler with a JSON-handler logger at slog.LevelDebug, sends the
    bearer credential as Authorization: Bearer <token>, then asserts
    neither the log buffer nor the response body contains the literal
    bearer. The deny leg uses `principal.Disabled = true` so policy
    short-circuits before the reader, and the reader's err is
    `stderrors.New("reader must not be called")` to prove the deny
    path never reached the store.
    (3) `TestList<Resource>ErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause` —
    seeds the reader's err with `apierr.StoreUnavailable(
    stderrors.New("connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432"))`, then
    asserts the 503 response body contains neither the wrapped cause
    string NOR the datastore address substring "10.0.0.5". This is
    the chokepoint for "an error envelope leaked the internal-network
    detail" regressions.
  - The handler-builder fanout for a new `<Resource>HandlerForWithLogger`
    helper is the SAME 60-argument NewHandler call as the existing
    `<Resource>HandlerFor`, but with `logger` substituted for the
    second-to-last `nil` argument. The argument-positional slot for
    the resource's own port stays unchanged (here `reader` lives in
    the projectVariables slot of the projects/grants/variables/replacer
    quad on the NewHandler line). Forward-applicable to every future
    GET list contract test: build a `WithLogger` sibling once per
    resource, reuse it across all three contract members.
  - The contract-test bearer constant is namespaced per endpoint
    (`listProjectVariablesContractSecret`) so a future analyzer can
    grep for any byte of it leaking into logs / response bodies.
    Convention: `yk_live_supersecret_<resource>_<method>_DEADBEEF...`.
    The DEADBEEF suffix makes accidental collisions across files
    impossible.

- Remaining risks / follow-ups: the live-path branch of TestLiveDokploySmokeExercisesLiveEndpoint can only be exercised
  end-to-end against a real Dokploy. The nightly external-smoke workflow needs three repository secrets configured
  (YALLA_EXTERNAL_DOKPLOY_BASE_URL, YALLA_EXTERNAL_DOKPLOY_TOKEN, optional YALLA_EXTERNAL_DOKPLOY_PROBE_SERVICE)
  before its first scheduled run actually hits a Dokploy host; until then both manual and scheduled runs will
  surface as deterministic skips that still report green. This matches the documented contract — the smoke is
  opt-in by design.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Patterns discovered:
    - First opt-in verification-suite story. The BE-0379..BE-0399 template required two key shifts: (a) the
      command lives in verificationLoop.optionalWhenConfigured, NOT requiredBackendCommands — and the static
      test ASSERTS BOTH presence in optional AND absence from required; (b) the CI surface is a dedicated
      workflow file with workflow_dispatch + schedule triggers, NOT a step in ci.yml's test job — pinning the
      env-injection literal `YALLA_EXTERNAL_DOKPLOY: "1"` is essential because without it the smoke would
      t.Skip silently and the workflow would always report green; (c) verify.sh optional step gated on the
      env var so it doesn't bleed into the default gate (`if [[ "${YALLA_EXTERNAL_DOKPLOY:-}" = "1" ]]; then`
      — the same env value the test reads at runtime); (d) CONTRIBUTING.md entry lives in the Optional Tools
      section, not the numbered required list — a NEW "Opt-in external suites" subsection keeps it
      discoverable; (e) SECURITY.md row's When column says "Opt-in (...), nightly + manual" rather than the
      uniform "Every push and PR" used by every other gate.
  - Gotchas encountered:
    - The Dokploy client maps a 401/403 from the upstream to `apierr.Internal()` → `yerr.CodeInternal`,
      NOT `CodeAuth` or `CodeForbidden`. The reason is documented in client.go's statusError: a 401 from
      Dokploy means Yalla's OWN credentials are bad — that's a Yalla misconfiguration the customer cannot
      act on, so it's surfaced as an internal error. The smoke's redaction-contract branch had to assert
      `CodeInternal`, not `CodeUnauthenticated`. This is itself a load-bearing contract worth pinning: a
      regression that exposed upstream auth failures as customer-actionable codes would mislead the caller
      into thinking THEIR credentials were wrong.
    - The GitHub Actions write-hook fires on any `.github/workflows/*.yml` write and emits a security
      reminder about injection patterns. The fix is to bind ${{ secrets.* }} only to `env:` and then run
      the command without interpolating user-controlled inputs into the shell — even though `secrets.*` is
      not in the GitHub-listed risky inputs, the hook still nudges. Putting the env block on the step
      (not the job) keeps the secret scope minimal.
    - `t.Setenv("", "")` does NOT unset the variable — it sets it to the empty string. The smoke loader's
      contract distinguishes empty-string from unset (both should t.Skip), but to test the "unset" case the
      test calls `os.Unsetenv` AFTER `t.Setenv` (the t.Setenv registers the cleanup so the post-test state
      is consistent). This is the right shape for any future test that needs to exercise both unset and
      empty-string paths against an env-var loader.
  - Useful context:
    - The PRD's `optionalWhenConfigured` already contained the canonical opt-in command BEFORE this story
      was implemented. The static test just had to enforce the invariant; no PRD schema mutation was
      needed. Future verification stories that add new entries to optionalWhenConfigured should follow the
      same shape — the array is the single discoverable surface AI agents read first.
    - verify.sh's trailing optionals block (currently #25 govulncheck, #26 staticcheck, #27 golangci-lint,
      #28 goreleaser) now also carries #29 external live-Dokploy smoke. The block grew by one slot
      without renumbering any existing step; future trailing-optional stories should append at the next
      free number rather than inserting in the middle (which would force a renumber-everywhere edit).

## 2026-05-17 - BE-0146 — Add contract tests for PUT /v1/projects/{project_id}/variables
- Implemented the load-bearing public-API contract coverage for
  PUT /v1/projects/{project_id}/variables as the structural twin of
  variables_put_contract_test.go (BE-0110, the org-variables WRITE
  contract) and project_variables_get_contract_test.go (BE-0143, the
  project-variables READ contract). Added one new test file with four
  tests:
    1. TestReplaceProjectVariablesServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter
       — captureProcessOutput wraps a served PUT and pins that nothing
       reaches os.Stdout / os.Stderr; the post-write variables payload is
       carried by the response body; the captured store.ReplaceProjectVariablesInput
       carries the principal's home org and the {project_id} path
       parameter verbatim; the structured logger is the only sanctioned
       out-of-band writer and writes go to its own buffer.
    2. TestReplaceProjectVariablesRequestLogRedactsBearerToken — twin
       legs (success path with allowed Developer; deny path with a
       disabled principal that short-circuits at policy and an err-on-call
       replacer to prove the deny leg can't be the leak source). Pins the
       bearer credential never appears in the structured log buffer NOR
       the response body.
    3. TestReplaceProjectVariablesRequestLogRedactsSubmittedSecretValue —
       the variables-WRITE-specific extra pin. Same twin legs (success +
       deny). The customer's submitted is_secret=true value never reaches
       the per-request log buffer NOR the response body, including the
       deny-leg case where the value never reached the store at all but
       can still leak via the operational log if a future regression
       starts dumping the decoded request body.
    4. TestReplaceProjectVariablesErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause
       — a fakeProjectVariableReplacer{err: apierr.StoreUnavailable(...)}
       surfaces as a typed 503 whose error envelope carries a stable
       generic message; the wrapped driver cause ("connection refused
       dialing 10.0.0.5:5432") and the bare datastore address never reach
       the wire.
- Files changed:
  - NEW internal/controlplane/httpapi/project_variables_put_contract_test.go
    (four contract tests + replaceProjectVariablesHandlerForWithLogger
    helper + three module-scope constants: bearer credential, submitted
    secret marker, canonical replace body)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0146.passes -> true)
  - ralph/progress.txt (this entry + Codebase Patterns new bullet)
- Verification run (from repo root):
  - gofmt -l .                                              -> clean
  - go vet ./...                                            -> clean
  - go mod tidy                                             -> no-op
  - go test -count=1 -run TestReplaceProjectVariables ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/
                                                            -> green (~0.55s)
  - go test -count=1 ./...                                  -> all green
  - go test -race -count=1 ./...                            -> all green
  - goimports not installed (documented gap, gofmt -l clean).
- Results: green across the board. No live Postgres or live Dokploy
  required — the suite stays a pure unit-test suite of the HTTP wire
  path against fake store doubles.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - None for BE-0146 itself. Forward-applicable to the BE-0149..BE-0200
    chain of contract-test stories for the environment / service /
    backup endpoint families: each one will need (a) a server-stdout/
    stderr pin, (b) a bearer-credential redaction pin on both legs,
    (c) for WRITE endpoints whose body carries is_secret=true items,
    a submitted-secret redaction pin on both legs, and (d) a
    dependency-cause leak pin including the bare datastore address.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Patterns discovered:
    - The BE-0110 / BE-0143 / BE-0146 contract-test trio establishes a
      stable four-test shape for every public PUT contract story whose
      body can carry is_secret=true values. The fourth test (submitted-
      secret redaction on BOTH success and deny legs) is the differentiator
      from the BE-0140 / BE-0143 read-only contract shape, which only
      needs three tests. The "deny leg also pins the redaction" choice is
      load-bearing: the deny path is precisely where a future regression
      that dumps the decoded body is most dangerous (the secret never
      reached the store but still reaches the operator log).
    - principalForProjectVariables returns a Developer in the principal's
      home org, which clears env.write (CapWrite) at the policy boundary.
      The deny leg sets denied.Principal.Disabled = true on a fresh copy
      so the policy short-circuit fires before any handler logic runs;
      this is the same shape BE-0143 uses on the READ endpoint and is
      forward-applicable to every project / environment / service
      WRITE contract test that does NOT need the full role matrix
      (the role matrix is the put_policy_test sibling's job, not the
      contract test's).
    - The PUT-contract NewHandler call site mirrors the GET-contract one
      with exactly two swaps: fakeProjectVariableReader{} stays in the
      reader slot, and replacer replaces fakeProjectVariableReplacer{}
      in the replacer slot. The remaining ~70 fake-port positional
      arguments are bit-identical to the GET sibling, so a sweep that
      adds a trailing positional NewHandler parameter (per
      internal/controlplane/httpapi/AGENTS.md "Adding a positional
      parameter to NewHandler") need only touch both contract helpers
      identically.
  - Gotchas encountered:
    - The fakeProjectVariableReplacer{} returns nil/nil from Replace by
      default; this is the right zero value for tests that never reach
      the handler (the deny-leg case). For the success-leg case we set
      .vars to the simulated post-write entries AND optionally .got to
      capture the input. Forgetting to set .vars in the success leg
      yields an empty Variables[] in the response, which would fail the
      "want two post-write entries" assertion — useful early signal that
      the success-leg fixture is misconfigured.
    - The submitted secret marker MUST be a distinct, recognisable
      literal (no overlap with natural test values). The 16+ hex-suffix
      shape (yallaprojectsubmittedsecretMARKER0123456789C0FFEE) makes a
      substring match in either the log buffer or the response body
      decisive. Reusing the bearer-credential constant would conflate
      two distinct contract surfaces and cause one test to mask the
      other's regression.
  - Useful context:
    - The captureProcessOutput helper swaps the global os.Stdout and
      os.Stderr, so any test using it MUST NOT call t.Parallel() (the
      swap would race with sibling tests). The other three tests in
      this file DO call t.Parallel() because they use a buffered slog
      handler, never the process streams.
    - The four contract assertions complete BE-0146's acceptanceCriteria
      list:
        * httptest coverage of success envelope (project_variables_test.go's
          existing TestReplaceProjectVariablesHappyPath family) + error
          envelope (this file's dependency-cause leak test) +
          request_id propagation (decodeReplaceProjectVariables's
          existing pin) + OpenAPI operation registration
          (project_variables_test.go's existing
          TestPutProjectVariablesOpenAPIRouteIsRegistered).
        * Unauthenticated / unauthorized / invalid input / not found /
          happy path coverage from existing sibling tests plus the
          policy matrix from projects_variables_put_policy_test.go.
        * stdout/stderr never used for response data (this file's
          test #1).
        * Logs remain redacted (this file's tests #2 and #3).
        * Isolated fixtures, fake Dokploy where provisioning is
          involved (the endpoint persists desired state only — no
          Dokploy call until a subsequent deployment / variable
          rendering job — so the fake store double is sufficient
          for the contract test).
        * Stable JSON envelopes with yalla.output.v1 /
          yalla.error.v1 (decodeReplaceProjectVariables and
          decodeError pins).
        * Secrets / tokens / API keys / cookies / rendered values
          redacted in logs, errors, audit metadata, and test output
          (tests #2, #3, #4 plus project_variables_test.go's existing
          response-body sentinel pin).

  - Useful context: `denied.Principal.Disabled = true` is the canonical knob to force a CapRead policy short-circuit before the reader runs; the deny-leg reader returns stderrors.New("reader must not be called") and the test relies on policy never invoking it.

The contention member fires `releaseBuildWorkers * releaseBuildIterationsPerWorker` = 4096 goroutines against a shared slice and asserts each derives its OWN scenario's predicted projection.

### Remaining risks or follow-ups
- None. The static gate is self-pinning; future drifts in any of the six surfaces will trip the analyser on the offending fixture before they can ship.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Inserting a required verify.sh step at position #N forces a renumber of every optional step #N..end AND a synchronised constant update in every prior static test that pinned an affected step header.** For BE-0401, that meant updating BE-0400's external-smoke static test (`externalDokploySmokeVerifyShStepHeader` from `# 29` to `# 30`; the synthetic-fixture strings inside the analyser self-check from `# 28`/`# 29` to `# 29`/`# 30`) in the same edit. The renumber cost is bounded: only static tests that pin step headers in the affected range need updates, and the existing matchers fail loudly on drift so the renumber lands deterministically. Forward-applicable to every future required-step insertion: grep all `# N. Optional` and `# N. Required` literals in `internal/release/verification_suite_*_static_test.go` for the renumbered range and update each in the same commit.
- **Pure projection helpers (no live infrastructure) still benefit from a contention-burst member of the canonical pair.** The release package's `ArchiveExt`/`BinaryName`/`ArchiveName`/`ChecksumsName` are pure functions today, so the contention member would seem redundant. But the burst is the load-bearing stability check the gate's wire contract requires: a future regression that introduced shared mutable state (a cached lookup table, a global builder, a sync.Once that mutated a shared map) would surface here before reaching the GoReleaser pipeline. Keeping the pair shape consistent across every BE-0379..BE-0401 verification gate makes the static analyser's canonical-funcs matcher reusable and the operator-facing AGENTS.md narrative consistent. Forward-applicable: every future verification-suite gate (pure-function or stateful) keeps the closed-set-coverage + per-decision-stability pair shape so the `-run TestX` filter binds to a two-function fixture the static gate can name.
- **The static gate's SECURITY.md substring matcher tolerates 14 anchor substrings without the inline pattern feeling brittle.** Using semantically anchored substrings (function names, type names, file names, contract keywords) instead of whole sentences keeps the matcher robust to Markdown line wrap while still pinning every AC. The choice to exclude `policy.Engine`-style backtick-quoted code spans from the substring set when they don't apply to the gate (release-build has no policy boundary) keeps the matcher focused on the load-bearing facts.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The canonical pair shape for a PURE FUNCTION VALIDATOR with a CLOSED-SET SCENARIO TABLE is the simplest instance of the BE-0379..BE-0401 family.** `config.Load` is a pure function from an env map to a `*Config` or a typed `*yerr.Error` value. The contention burst's "shared mutable state" target is therefore hypothetical (today the validator has none), but keeping the pair shape consistent across every BE-0379..BE-0402 gate keeps the static analyser's canonical-funcs matcher reusable. The burst still has real defensive value: a future regression that introduced a cached profile-defaults table, a global rate-limit builder, or a sync.Once mutating a shared map would surface in the 2048-goroutine burst before reaching either backend binary. Forward-applicable: every future pure-function verification gate keeps the closed-set-coverage + per-decision-stability pair shape; the burst's per-iteration assertion key is `scenario.predicate(scenario.input)` not the aggregate pass count, so a cross-write fires deterministically.
- **The SECURITY.md substring set MUST match the prose's actual phrasing — a hyphenated `strict-profile` matcher fails if the prose says `strict profile` with a space.** Caught at first test run; flipped both the constant and the doc comment to `strict-profile` to align with the established `strict-profile presence check` phrasing already used in BE-0399's section. Forward-applicable to every future SECURITY.md substring matcher: when the analyser fires on a missing substring, the fix is to align EITHER the constant OR the doc, never both — pick whichever phrasing is the established convention in the existing sections.
- **`json.dump` with `ensure_ascii=False` strips the PRD's `—` em-dash escape style and produces ~50 lines of cosmetic diff.** The fix is `ensure_ascii=True` (the default) which preserves the original escape style. The PRD's em-dashes are written as `—` literals because that keeps the JSON file ASCII-safe for grep / sed / non-UTF8 viewers; never re-serialise the PRD with `ensure_ascii=False`. Forward-applicable: every future PRD edit that round-trips through json.load+json.dump should keep `ensure_ascii=True` (default) and `indent=2` to match the existing style. Better still: prefer minimal Edit calls on the specific line rather than a full re-serialisation when only one or two lines change.
- **Reusing the same `_test.go` file's package-internal `strictEnv()` helper from a sibling `_test.go` file in the SAME package keeps the contract test self-contained.** The new `config_validation_test.go` is in `package config` (same as `config_test.go`), so it sees `strictEnv()`, `MapLookup`, and every constant directly. No new fixture file, no exported-for-test seam, no module-scoped helper duplication — the closed-set scenario table is the only new code. Forward-applicable: when a new verification story's pair lives in the same package as an existing test fixture, use `package <pkg>` (not `package <pkg>_test`) so the canonical pair can reuse the existing test helpers without exposing them as a public API surface.
- **The 30-scenario table sized at `workers=32 * iters=64 = 2048` is the right contention burst for a pure validator.** Larger bursts (BE-0401's 4096) are overkill for a function that does no I/O and allocates only a small env map per iteration; smaller bursts (under 1024) wouldn't reliably trip a future regression that introduced shared mutable state. The 30-scenario closed-set table mod-indexed into the burst means each scenario is exercised ~68 times across the 2048 iterations — enough to surface a per-scenario regression deterministically without bloating the suite's wall-clock time. Forward-applicable: pure-function verification suites pick burst counts in the 1024..2048 range and use mod-indexing so every scenario gets sufficient repetitions.

## 2026-05-18 - BE-0152 — Add contract tests for POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments
- Implemented the BE-0152 contract suite as a structural twin of the BE-0146 PUT-contract four-test shape, adapted to the project environments WRITE endpoint (POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments). The BE-0149 progress note explicitly directed BE-0152 to follow the BE-0146 four-test shape rather than the BE-0149 read-only three-test shape, because POST bodies carry caller-supplied request material that must be redaction-proven on both legs.
- Created internal/controlplane/httpapi/project_environments_create_contract_test.go with four tests pinning the four contract surfaces project_environments_create_test.go (BE-0151) and projects_environments_create_policy_test.go do not assert directly:
  - (1) TestCreateProjectEnvironmentServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter (NOT t.Parallel; uses captureProcessOutput): proves stdout and stderr are empty after a 201 success leg, the created-environment payload is carried by the response body, the creator was driven with the principal's home org + path project_id (so a future refactor that bypasses the EnvironmentCreator path fails this story in two places), and the structured log buffer is non-empty (the only sanctioned out-of-band writer).
  - (2) TestCreateProjectEnvironmentRequestLogRedactsBearerToken (both legs): a recognisable bearer credential createProjectEnvironmentContractSecret never appears in the per-request structured log or the response body, on the happy path AND on the authorization-failure path. The deny leg uses a Disabled principal so policy short-circuits before the creator runs, and the creator's Create path errors if invoked ("creator must not be called"), proving any logged "creator error" cannot be the leak source.
  - (3) TestCreateProjectEnvironmentRequestLogRedactsSubmittedBodyMaterial (both legs, asymmetric body-echo assertion): a recognisable display_name marker createProjectEnvironmentContractSubmittedDisplayName placed in the request body never appears in the per-request structured log on either leg. The success leg legitimately echoes display_name back in the response body (the created row), so the body-echo assertion fires only on the deny leg — where echoing decoded body material would prove the handler decoded the body before short-circuiting at the policy gate. This is the POST-write-specific extra surface vs the read-only sibling (BE-0149's three-test shape).
  - (4) TestCreateProjectEnvironmentErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause: apierr.StoreUnavailable wraps a "connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432" cause; the typed 503 envelope carries a stable generic E_UNAVAILABLE message, and neither the bare cause string nor the datastore address 10.0.0.5 ever reaches the response body.
- Helper pattern: one new createProjectEnvironmentHandlerForWithLogger that mirrors the existing createProjectEnvironmentHandlerFor (project_environments_create_test.go) with the final two NewHandler positional args swapped from (nil, nil) to (logger, nil). Constant pattern: three module-scope constants per file — bearer credential with endpoint-specific hex suffix (CAFED00D), submitted body marker with endpoint-specific hex suffix (F00DCAFE), canonical happy-path request body string.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/project_environments_create_contract_test.go (NEW)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0152.passes -> true)

  - None for BE-0152 itself. Forward-applicable to the BE-0155..BE-0200 chain of environment / service / backup write-endpoint contract-test stories: each one follows the same four-test shape with helper/path/decoder/marker substitutions. BE-0155 (GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}) is a read-only sibling so it should follow the BE-0149 three-test shape (no test #3 body-redaction pin, only stdout/stderr + bearer redaction + dependency-cause). The next write-endpoint contract story (BE-0158 PATCH /v1/environments/{environment_id}, BE-0161 DELETE /v1/environments/{environment_id} for "no body", BE-0164 POST clone, etc.) re-use the four-test shape verbatim; DELETE endpoints with no caller-supplied body can drop test #3.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Patterns discovered:
    - The BE-0146 / BE-0152 contract-test pair generalises the PUT-contract four-test shape to every WRITE endpoint that decodes a caller-supplied body. For an endpoint whose response legitimately echoes the submitted material (POST create rows like environments, projects, services, where display_name / slug / name are public fields), the body-redaction test #3 splits its assertion asymmetrically: log buffer NEVER contains the marker on either leg, response body MUST NOT contain the marker on the DENY leg only. This is the new structural variant: success-leg body-echo is by-design, deny-leg body-echo is a regression. Forward-applicable to every BE-0152-style POST-create contract story (BE-0164 clone, project create, service create, backup create, deployment create, member create, organization create, api-key create — the entire create-row family).
    - The "deny leg uses a Disabled principal + err-on-call port" mechanism transfers verbatim from BE-0146's denyReplacer to BE-0152's denyCreator. The deny port's err message ("X must not be called") is the load-bearing assertion: any logged "X error" in either surface fails the redaction pin, so a regression that wires up the port behind the policy gate fails this story in two places (the wantStatus check AND the redaction substring check).
    - For POST endpoints where the response body legitimately echoes one of the submitted fields, picking a recognisable hex-suffixed marker for that field (display_name marker yallaprojectenvsubmittedbodyMARKER...F00DCAFE) lets the body-not-logged contract still pin redaction on the success leg via the log buffer alone — the response body assertion gracefully degrades to "deny leg only" without losing the headers-not-logged / body-not-logged contract on the happy path. The marker discipline (distinct hex suffix per endpoint per surface — CAFED00D for the bearer, F00DCAFE for the body marker) prevents cross-pollination from a future regression that swaps any two surfaces.
    - Endpoint-specific NewHandler arg list: POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments threads the EnvironmentCreator through the 30th positional argument slot (after fakeProjectEnvironmentReader{}, before fakeEnvironmentReader{}). The full positional list of NewHandler is mechanically identical across every contract-test helper — the only varying slot is the port the test owns. Copy-and-paste the existing createProjectEnvironmentHandlerFor body, swap (nil, nil) for (logger, nil) at the tail, done.
    - The route is environment.create, a CapWrite action, and routes.go documents the admit-list verbatim (owner, admin, developer, ci). principalForProjectEnvironments returns a RoleDeveloper identity, which is sufficient for the success leg; the deny leg only needs Disabled=true on the same identity to flip wantStatus from 201 to 403 — the role matrix is BE-0150's job, not this contract suite's.
  - Gotchas encountered:
    - The BE-0152 file name follows the project_<scope>_<verb>_contract_test.go convention used by BE-0146 (project_variables_put_contract_test.go) and BE-0149 (project_environments_get_contract_test.go). For POST/create endpoints whose existing handler-driver test file is named project_environments_create_test.go (BE-0151), the contract twin lives at project_environments_create_contract_test.go — the trailing "_contract_test" suffix is what distinguishes the contract layer from the existing handler-driver coverage. Forward-applicable to every BE-0152-style POST-create contract story.
    - The success leg's HTTP status is 201 Created (StatusCreated), not 200 OK. This is endpoint-specific: project_environments_create_test.go's happy path uses 201, so the contract twin must too. Other POST endpoints in the chain may also use 201 — always check the existing handler test's wantStatus before authoring the contract twin.
    - The createProjectEnvironmentRequest body shape is {environment_id, slug, display_name} — no organization_id (derived from authenticated principal) and no project_id (derived from path parameter), both of which are deliberately ignored if the caller sends them (pinned by BE-0151's existing TestCreateProjectEnvironmentIgnoresOrganizationIDInBody / TestCreateProjectEnvironmentIgnoresProjectIDInBody). The contract twin's canonical body uses the happy-path shape so a failure can never be blamed on body validation.
  - Useful context:
    - Sibling write-endpoint contract-test stories that reuse this exact four-test shape (with helper/path/decoder substitutions): BE-0158 (PATCH /v1/environments/{environment_id}), BE-0161 (DELETE /v1/environments/{environment_id} — drop test #3 if no body), BE-0164 (POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/clone), BE-0170 (PUT /v1/environments/{environment_id}/grants), BE-0176 (PUT /v1/environments/{environment_id}/variables — has secrets so re-include the BE-0146 in-body is_secret=true value pin instead of the BE-0152 display_name marker pin), and every create-row / write-shape story in the BE-0179..BE-0200 chain.
    - Sibling read-endpoint contract-test stories that follow the BE-0149 three-test read-only shape (no test #3): BE-0155 (GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}), BE-0167 (GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/grants), BE-0173 (GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/variables), BE-0179 (GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/services).
    - The BE-0146 / BE-0152 four-test shape's invariant: test #1 NOT t.Parallel (captureProcessOutput swaps os.Stdout/os.Stderr globals), tests #2 / #3 / #4 ARE t.Parallel. The deny-leg fake-port message convention is "<X> must not be called" — single string, present-tense, no period.

file). Canonical pair TestAdminEndpointCoversCallSites +
TestAdminEndpointPreservesContractUnderContention at
internal/controlplane/policy/admin_endpoint_policy_test.go walks a
closed-set cartesian table over every tagged-admin HTTP route × every
built-in role × {same-tenant, cross-tenant} × {no grant, project /
environment / service-scoped grant} and asserts policy.Engine.Decide
returns the predicted (Allow, Reason); the 2048-goroutine burst hammers
the same table by deterministic mod-index against a single shared
Engine instance.

- go test ./internal/release/ → ok 0.314s
- go test -run 'TestVerificationSuite(Admin|External)' ./internal/release/ → ok 0.523s
- Full verification (gofmt, go vet, go test ./..., go test -race ./...) → see commit message.

### Results
The closed-set table generates len(adminEndpointCallSites) ×
(2 × len(adminEndpointBuiltinRoleVerdicts) +
len(adminEndpointGrantContainments)) = 6 × (12 + 3) = 90 rows; the
contention burst draws each row ~22 times across 2048 iterations and
every iteration asserts the row's per-scenario predicted (Allow,
Reason). The closed-set self-checks at the head of
TestAdminEndpointCoversCallSites pin (1) every endpoint binds to one
of the four ActionAdmin* constants and every action is bound,
(2) every admin action is catalogued as CapSupport, (3) builtinRoleCaps
admits CapSupport only for RoleSupport. The contention burst's
ADMINENDPOINTSECRETMARKER canary scans the Reason field on every
iteration as a structural redaction predicate against a future engine
change that widened Reason to caller-supplied data.

### Remaining risks or follow-ups
- The closed-set adminEndpointCallSites slice MUST stay in lockstep
  with internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go's tagged-admin routes.
  A new admin endpoint (e.g. a future POST /v1/admin/users/disable)
  added without a row fails the exhaustiveness self-check; conversely,
  retiring an admin endpoint without dropping its row fails the same
  self-check. The pair binds to the wire surface via the action set,
  not the route registration, so the binding is structural rather
  than literal: a future regression that registered an admin endpoint
  resolving to a non-ActionAdmin* constant would fail the first
  self-check before the table walk.

### Learnings for future iterations
- The BE-0379..BE-0402 verification-suite mega-pattern continues
  to apply verbatim at BE-0403. The per-story knobs that move are:
  (a) the family prefix (`AdminEndpoint`/`adminEndpoint`),
  (b) the verify.sh step number (#27 here, #N+1 for the next), and
  (c) the BE-0400 optional renumber (here `# 31`→`# 32` and synthetic
  `# 30`→`# 31`).
- The closed scenario table for admin endpoints is generated rather
  than handwritten: a per-endpoint loop over role + axis +
  containment matrices yields 90 rows from ~30 lines of structural
  fixtures. The deterministic mod-index in the contention burst
  draws every row across 2048 iterations without ever calling rand,
  so two consecutive `go test -race` invocations exercise identical
  scenarios per goroutine — a regression that swapped goroutines'
  scenarios under contention surfaces as a SAME-iteration mismatch
  across runs, not a flaky one-in-N race.
- The Principal struct uses `Disabled bool` (default false = enabled).
  Do not invent an `Enabled` field; the existing `principalIn` helper
  in policy_test.go relies on the zero-value-is-enabled invariant.
- `roleCaps(role Role)` returns (zero capSet, false) for unknown
  roles. A Principal with Role="" + Grants only never trips the
  unknown-role guard at line 109 of engine.go because the guard is
  conditional on `principal.Role != ""`. Tests that exercise grant-
  only principals MUST therefore leave Role unset (the empty string),
  not set Role to a sentinel string the engine would reject.

The burst's value is the assertion that the package has no shared state. This is different from BE-0395..BE-0398 (shared chokepoint instance with documented mutable state) and from BE-0404 (shared *BreakGlassService).
  - When a closed-set scenario table predicates an output field that ONLY some scenarios populate (here: env-var rows route a value through `Action.DesiredValue`; service / domain / unmanaged rows do not), gate the redaction canary per-row via a row-level flag, NOT a generic pre-mutator pass. A generic pass bleeds marker into untouched baseline fields and produces unintended drift (here it would turn the env_var_missing row into env_var_changed and false-positive the row's "missing" prediction).
  - Determinism is structurally different from the closed-set tag — pin it as its own head-of-test self-check, not folded into the per-row verdict. The reconcile coverage member calls `Diff(desired, actual)` twice per scenario and `reflect.DeepEquals` the plans; a future regression that introduced map-iteration ordering into the planner output would surface here as a fast targeted failure rather than a confusing per-iteration burst mismatch many lines later.
  - The sandbox's TMPDIR collision with the Go module's path triggers `pattern ...: directory prefix ... does not contain main module` warnings. Wrapping invocations with `TMPDIR=/tmp go test ...` from `ctx_execute(language: "shell")` is sufficient — the harness's normal `Bash` tool already runs in the right working directory without that prefix.

Don't assert on the absence of an observable side-effect (a state diff would silently pass when the planner reads but does not write — which is itself a regression for pending-owner rows).
