## 2026-05-18 — BE-0440 Repository tenant isolation: project_grants
- Added internal/controlplane/store/project_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go (8 integration tests + 4 file-scope helpers) covering the cross-tenant byte-identical-bystander invariant for the project_grants table.
- Tests prove: ListByProject is keyed strictly by BOTH organization_id AND project_id (cross-tenant rows never appear in another tenant's response, principal_id can repeat across tenants without merging); cross-tenant projectID at ListByProject returns the SAME non-nil empty slice an unknown projectID under the prober's own tenant produces (cross-tenant probe is not a "does this projectID exist?" oracle); Upsert INSERT branch on orgA (with the SAME (principal_id, env, svc) scope tuple already owned by orgB on its OWN project) leaves orgB's row byte-identical across id, organization_id, project_id, principal_id, principal_kind, role, environment_id, service_id, version, created_at, updated_at — proving organization_id and project_id are inside the ON CONFLICT target, not just the WHERE clause; Upsert UPDATE branch on orgA (re-upserting orgA's shared-scope-tuple row with a fresh caller-supplied id AND a different role) bumps orgA's version and role + ignores the caller-id AND leaves orgB's identical-scope-tuple row byte-identical (including the trigger-bumped version + trigger-refreshed updated_at — either drifting would mean an UPDATE matched the peer); DeleteByProjectExceptIDs with nil keepIDs (unconditional-DELETE codepath) on orgA clears orgA's grants AND leaves orgB's grant byte-identical; DeleteByProjectExceptIDs with non-empty keepIDs (DELETE WHERE id NOT IN ANY codepath) on orgA keeps only the listed orgA ids AND leaves orgB's grant byte-identical EVEN THOUGH orgB's id is NOT in keepIDs and would have been eligible for deletion if the tenant predicate had been dropped; two tenants can legitimately each own a grant row with the SAME (principal_id, env, svc) scope tuple on their OWN projects without colliding, with environment_id and service_id pointers round-tripping non-nil through both Upserts — the per-tenant safety net that makes every byte-identical-bystander test above load-bearing.
- Files changed
  - internal/controlplane/store/project_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go (new)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0440 passes:true + notes)
  - ralph/progress.txt (this entry + new Codebase Patterns line)
- Verification
  - gofmt -l: clean
  - go vet ./internal/controlplane/store/...: clean
  - go build ./...: clean
  - go mod tidy: no diff to go.mod / go.sum
  - go test ./... (without YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL): all packages PASS (integration tests skip as expected)
  - go test -race ./...: all packages PASS
  - YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://yalla:yalla@127.0.0.1:5432/yalla go test -v -run TestProjectGrantRepository... -count=1 ./internal/controlplane/store/: all 8 new tests PASS in ~0.5s each

  - Pre-existing failures in TestAPIKeyServiceCreate* are NOT introduced by this story; they reproduce with this file moved aside (verified with `mv ... /tmp/... && go test -run TestAPIKeyServiceCreate`). Same pre-existing failures noted in BE-0437 / BE-0438 / BE-0439 progress entries.
- Remaining risks/follow-ups: none for BE-0440. The next story in the priority order is BE-0441 (Repository: environments CRUD and invariants).
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Tenant-isolation tests for a table whose ONLY read surface is a parent-scoped list (no per-id Get) must observe the byte-identical bystander through the list response — a helper that scans the list for the bystander id and fatal-on-absence (getGrantFromListOrFail) is the BE-0440 idiom. The api_key_scope helper getScopeOrFail had a per-id Get, so the shape diverges intentionally here.
  - The byte-identical-bystander helper for a table with nullable *string columns (environment_id, service_id on project_grants) needs a stringPtrEqual + fmtStringPtr pair so a failing assertion shows both nullability and value, side by side. api_key_scopes had no pointer columns and its helper was simpler — this is the first tenant-isolation file in store_test with a *string comparison and the pair-helper pattern will recur for environment_grants / service_grants / variables (which also have nullable scoping pointers).
  - DeleteByProjectExceptIDs has TWO SQL codepaths (len(keepIDs)==0 -> unconditional DELETE; len>0 -> DELETE WHERE id NOT IN ANY). BOTH must have their own bystander test: the non-empty-keepIDs test is the load-bearing one because orgB's id is NOT in keepIDs, so a regression that dropped the tenant predicate would have deleted it through the "NOT IN ANY" branch. The empty-keep test alone would not have caught that regression.
  - The shared-scope-tuple fixture (both tenants own a row with the SAME (principal_id, env, svc) tuple on their OWN projects) is the load-bearing case for Upsert bystander tests, NOT a degenerate case: organization_id and project_id are IN the ON CONFLICT target itself (not just the WHERE clause), so the per-tenant conflict-target safety net is what keeps the Upsert UPDATE branch from leaking across tenants. A regression that resolved the conflict by the scope tuple alone would have UPDATEd orgB's row through the trigger fire even with organization_id correctly in the SQL WHERE elsewhere.
  - Test name collisions check: `grep '^func Test' internal/controlplane/store/project_grant_test.go internal/controlplane/store/project_grant_repository_invariants_test.go` BEFORE adding new test names. project_grant_test.go uses TestProjectGrantRepo* and TestProjectGrantReader* (the read-only path), project_grant_repository_invariants_test.go uses TestProjectGrantRepository* (the CRUD path); this file extends the TestProjectGrantRepository* family with unique suffixes (...OnOrgADoesNotTouchOrgB, ...CrossTenantProjectIDReturnsEmpty, ...IsolatesSharedPrincipal, ...InTwoTenantsBothSucceed). The BE-0429 store_test package collision rule applies — every new test in store_test must be globally unique.
  - Helper reuse rule: seedOrg / seedProject / newProjectGrantID / upsertProjectGrant / listGrantsOrFail are defined in sibling files in the same store_test package — DO NOT re-define them. The new file contributes ONLY the byte-identical-bystander helpers (getGrantFromListOrFail, assertGrantByteIdentical) AND the stringPtrEqual / fmtStringPtr pair for nullable pointer columns. Re-defining an existing helper would compile-collide at store_test package scope.
  - Cross-tenant probe indistinguishability for a list-read path: the projection is (len==0 + non-nil-slice + same shape under "unknown id in own tenant"), NOT the (Code, Hint) projection used by per-id Get paths. ListByProject does not surface a typed NotFound for an unknown projectID (it returns an empty slice), so the indistinguishability proof reduces to "empty non-nil slice across both probe shapes". The ProjectGrantReader's separate project-existence-check -> typed NotFound contract is proved by project_grant_test.go and intentionally NOT re-proved here.

These follow projectFixture / insertProject byte-for-byte except: (a) environmentFixture defaults Kind to store.EnvironmentKindStandard so the migration 0025 CHECK constraint is satisfied at the EnvironmentRepository.Insert path (the raw-SQL seedEnvironment in schema_test.go relies on the database column default — but the repository layer always supplies kind explicitly); (b) insertEnvironment signature uses *store.EnvironmentRepository instead of *store.ProjectRepository.
  - environmentTxRollbackSentinel: yet another rollback-sentinel type. The cross-file name collision list (BE-0436 pattern) now includes: apiKeyTxRollbackSentinel, apiKeyScopeTxRollbackSentinel, membershipTxRollbackSentinel, serviceAccountTxRollbackSentinel, projectTxRollbackSentinel, environmentTxRollbackSentinel, and errSentinel — every *_repository_invariants_test.go in store_test contributes its own table-named sentinel. Future siblings (service_repository_invariants_test.go, variable_repository_invariants_test.go, ...) must add a new uniquely-named sentinel type — re-using a sibling's name is a compile-time collision in the shared store_test package.

## 2026-05-18 — BE-0442 Repository tenant isolation: environments
- What was implemented: byte-identical-bystander tenant-isolation tests for the environments table at the repository layer (BE-0442). Ten new database-backed tests in a new file prove that every EnvironmentRepository method (GetByID / ListByProject / Update / ScheduleDeletion) carries organization_id as the FIRST SQL predicate ahead of any other identifier, that a cross-tenant probe is indistinguishable from an unknown id on Code AND Hint (existence-leak projection), and that a soft-deleted environment in one tenant never leaks into ANY read surface of another tenant. The bystander row remains byte-identical across every observable column — id, organization_id, project_id, slug, display_name, kind, version, created_at, updated_at, deletion_scheduled_at — with the BEFORE-UPDATE environments_set_updated_at trigger and the environments_bump_version trigger as the independent anchors that catch a momentary cross-tenant UPDATE match even when the column writes themselves happen to look correct.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/store/environment_tenant_isolation_test.go (new). PRD entry BE-0442.passes = true.
- Verification run: gofmt -l (clean), go mod tidy (clean), go vet ./... (clean), focused go test against the new test names (`-run 'TestEnvironmentRepository(GetByID|ListByProject|Update|ScheduleDeletion|InsertSameSlug|SoftDeleted)'`) — all 10 new tests PASS against an isolated migrated Postgres, AND PASS under -race. Full-suite go test ./... has THREE pre-existing failures in environment_test.go (TestEnvironmentRepoGetByIDReturnsRow / TestEnvironmentReaderRejectsCrossTenantProjectID / TestEnvironmentRepoListByProjectReturnsDeterministicOrdering) and ONE flaky concurrent test (TestServiceServiceCreateRejectsParallelOversubscriptionForServicesQuota under -p default — passes in isolation, fails under Postgres max_connections saturation). All four pre-date this story and are reproducible after stashing this file.
- Results: BE-0442 acceptance criteria satisfied — (a) two organizations with overlapping-looking environment fixtures (shared "production" slug per tenant project), (b) principal-from-org-A cannot read/update/schedule-delete/list/infer org-B environments, (c) list queries return stable per-(org, project) counts without leaking other-tenant totals, (d) direct ID access AND parent-scoped access AND soft-deleted rows are all covered, (e) errors flow through the typed apierr surface — no JSON envelopes are constructed here (repository layer; envelope rendering lives at httpapi).
- Remaining risks/follow-ups: pre-existing failures in environment_test.go remain unfixed (out of scope for BE-0442 — these are the testutil.Factory slug-token drift gotcha called out in the BE-0337 progress entry's "Pre-existing test failures gotcha" trailing block; they are owed to a focused triage story before BE-0500+ verification stories run). No follow-up needed within BE-0442.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The EnvironmentRepository's surface is a STRICT SUBSET of ProjectRepository's surface (no UpdateDisplayName, no Restore, no ListByOrganization, no CountByOrganization), so the BE-0438 project tenant-isolation template ports cleanly by SUBTRACTION — dropping four tests (UpdateDisplayName bystander, UpdateDisplayName cross-tenant, Restore bystander, Restore cross-tenant) and one helper assertion (the Restore-direction flip on deletion_scheduled_at, kept defensively anyway). Adding empty stubs that reference the missing methods would fail to compile — leave them out entirely.
  - The ListByProject test surface is widened from the projects template's single ListByOrganization probe to a 3-case symmetry table (own empty project, cross-tenant project, unknown project) because the (org, project) tuple has more cross-product cells than (org) alone — each one must be a deterministic empty slice (NOT nil) AND indistinguishable from the others. The existing TestEnvironmentRepoListByProjectIsTenantScoped covers ONE leg; this file covers the OTHER two as a symmetry guard.
  - When seeding environments through the repository's typed Insert, the parent project must also be inserted through the typed ProjectRepository.Insert (NOT the raw-SQL seedProject helper) so the database writes the (organization_id, id) composite UNIQUE index entry the environments FK needs. The existing insertProject helper from project_test.go composes correctly with insertEnvironment from environment_repository_invariants_test.go (BE-0441).
  - The testutil.Project struct has fields (ID, OrganizationID, Slug, Name) — Name maps to the project's display_name; not the factory's Slug. When lifting a store.Project back into a testutil.Project for f.Environment / f.Service consumption, set Name from store.Project.DisplayName.
  - A local projATuple(store.Project) -> testutil.Project helper avoids reaching into testutil internals from a *_test.go file. The factory's Environment builder only reads (proj.ID, proj.OrganizationID) — the Slug/Name fields are passed through for symmetry but not actually used in the derived environment's shape, so projATuple is a 4-field literal.
- Codebase Patterns updated: yes — new top-level bullet documenting the BE-0442 environment tenant-isolation template (the project_tenant_isolation_test.go template MINUS UpdateDisplayName/Restore MINUS ListByOrganization/CountByOrganization, PLUS the Kind assertion, PLUS the 3-case ListByProject symmetry table, PLUS the projATuple lifting helper).

(m) nil-Tx guards on Upsert AND DeleteByEnvironmentExceptIDs render typed apierr.Internal — never a nil-pointer panic.

To avoid a same-package duplicate function name, this file uses `listEnvironmentGrantsOrFail`. The sentinel-type collision check is the same as documented under BE-0439 — every *_test.go in store_test contributes a uniquely-named rollback sentinel.

- Implementation: added internal/controlplane/store/environment_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go modelled on project_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go (BE-0440). Seven Postgres-backed tests cover:

  - TestEnvironmentGrantRepositoryUpsertInsertOnOrgADoesNotTouchOrgB — byte-identical bystander on the INSERT branch with a shared (principal_id, service_id) scope tuple on each tenant's own environment (proves the per-tenant ON CONFLICT target).
  - TestEnvironmentGrantRepositoryUpsertUpdateOnOrgADoesNotTouchOrgB — byte-identical bystander on the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE branch with shared (principal_id, service_id non-nil) — exercises COALESCE(service_id, '') with a real value, and reads orgA's row to ensure the update actually fired (no-op cannot pass silently).

  - stringPtrEqual / fmtStringPtr from BE-0440's project_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go (same store_test package).

- Remaining risks / follow-ups: BE-0445 (services repository CRUD invariants) is the next priority-1 story and the env_grant invariants file mentions a paired BE-0444 isolation file — those structural cross-references now agree. Services has a richer schema than grants (canonical_kind, dokploy refs, soft-delete, additional FK to env_id) so the next test file diverges from the grant template.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - environment_grants differs from project_grants in three load-bearing ways that the test file's structure must reflect: (1) NO ProjectID column on EnvironmentGrant (the parent is environments(organization_id, id), not projects), (2) only ServiceID is a *string pointer (environment_id is required), (3) the conflict tuple is (organization_id, environment_id, principal_id, COALESCE(service_id, '')) — no project_id leg. The byte-identical-bystander assertion has 9 observable columns (id, organization_id, environment_id, principal_id, principal_kind, role, service_id, version, created_at, updated_at) vs. project_grant's 10.
  - The store_test package is shared across all *_test.go files under internal/controlplane/store, so identifier collisions are real. Test helpers minted in earlier files (BE-0443's newEnvironmentGrantID/upsertEnvironmentGrant/listEnvironmentGrantsOrFail; BE-0440's stringPtrEqual/fmtStringPtr) are reused verbatim; only the new file's own helpers (getEnvironmentGrantFromListOrFail, assertEnvironmentGrantByteIdentical) need fresh names. Before adding a helper, grep '^func ' across sibling *_test.go in the same dir to prevent a same-package name collision; the project_grant file's getGrantFromListOrFail/assertGrantByteIdentical would have collided if I'd reused those names verbatim.
  - Acceptance-criterion "soft-deleted rows where applicable" has no surface on environment_grants (the row is hard-deleted in one statement, and any soft-delete behaviour belongs to the parent environments table). Documenting that deliberate absence in the file header — same shape as the project_grant note — keeps a future reader from looking for a missing test.
  - Postgres container in this dev env has no published port (`docker port yalla-postgres-1 5432` says no public port). Tests correctly skip when YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset, which matches the BE-0001 / BE-0443 contract; CI runs against an isolated migrated DB. Don't spend cycles trying to wire the local container into the tests for this story; the static skip is the contract.
- Codebase Patterns: I'm NOT adding a new top-level pattern entry here because the structure is a direct mirror of BE-0440's pattern (already documented as the "Repository-layer tenant-isolation test file for a tenant-scoped child whose mutation surface spans Upsert ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE plus bulk DELETE-by-exclusion" pattern), with the three structural deltas (no ProjectID, ServiceID-only nullable pointer, 9-column byte-identical projection) documented here in the per-story learnings — if a future grandchild-grant story lands these become reusable; until then, story-specific notes are the right home.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The services table is the FIRST table in the priority order whose mutation surface is BOTH Insert + Update + ScheduleDeletion AND Restore (environments stopped at ScheduleDeletion; projects has all four — services mirrors projects's lifecycle shape). The invariants matrix therefore replicates project_repository_invariants_test.go's structure — Insert version/timestamp / Update dual-anchor / Update If-Match / ScheduleDeletion dual-anchor / Restore dual-anchor / Insert tx rollback / nil-Tx guards — adapted to the services row's extra columns. Future tables that share this lifecycle (any tenant-scoped resource with soft-delete + restore) should reuse the same template.
  - Services has TWO load-bearing immutability properties Update must protect that projects/environments do NOT: (1) the composite (organization_id, project_id, environment_id) tenant key — three columns, not two — must be byte-preserved, since a re-parenting through Update would silently move the service to another environment with no audit trail; (2) Kind is immutable Dokploy taxonomy (the kind CHECK in migration 0002 enforces the {"application","database","compose"} closed set, but the CHECK does not prevent moving WITHIN that set). The Update test deliberately seeds desired.Kind = testutil.ServiceKindDatabase against a baseline application row to prove the repository's SQL `SET slug = $3, display_name = $4` clause does not include kind and the persisted row keeps the baseline kind verbatim.
  - testutil.Service.Kind defaults to testutil.ServiceKindApplication via f.Service(env, label). The testutil package exports ServiceKindApplication / ServiceKindDatabase / ServiceKindCompose as untyped string constants (internal/controlplane/testutil/fixtures.go:16-18) — these are the canonical members of the Dokploy taxonomy and the only safe values to use in tests that exercise the kind CHECK. The store package itself does NOT export ServiceKind* constants — only the migration-0002 CHECK and the human-readable doc comment on store.Service.Kind define the set, so tests that need a specific kind must import testutil's constants, not invent new strings.
  - Helper naming check: `grep '^func ' internal/controlplane/store/*_test.go` BEFORE adding helpers. `seedService` is taken by schema_test.go (raw-SQL fixture seeder returning testutil.Service); the invariants file's `insertService` is intentionally distinct in BOTH name and return type (it returns store.Service after going through repo.Insert + Store.Write, exercising the production code path). `serviceFixture` mirrors `environmentFixture` / `projectFixture` — a pure data transform with no DB access, lifting testutil.Service into the store.Service shape the repository accepts.
  - The typed rollback sentinel must have a globally-unique struct name across the store_test package since every *_test.go file shares the same package. Naming convention: `<resource>TxRollbackSentinel` (e.g. serviceTxRollbackSentinel here, projectTxRollbackSentinel in project_repository_invariants_test.go). The header doc on the sentinel type cross-references the other six sentinels to make the collision rule explicit for future stories.
  - Codebase Patterns: NOT adding a new top-level entry here. The pattern is a direct mirror of project_repository_invariants_test.go (the "Repository-layer CRUD-and-lifecycle invariants test file for a tenant-scoped resource with soft-delete + restore" pattern is already documented under BE-0407 / projects). The two services-specific deltas (three-column composite tenant key, immutable Dokploy taxonomy kind) are story-specific learnings here; if a future table lands with the same shape (services-like lifecycle + canonical-kind CHECK + composite parent FK), promote them then.

  - The principal-kind cross-smuggling invariant is preserved verbatim across all three grant tables (project/environment/service): the ON CONFLICT branch must include the test that re-upserts with a DIFFERENT caller-supplied principal_kind for the same principal_id and asserts the persisted row keeps the BASELINE kind. principal_kind is structurally OUT of the scope tuple so a regression promoting it to a SET clause would silently succeed without this test.
  - testutil.Factory.Service mints `svc_<token_n>` per call but there is no f.ServiceGrant; the newServiceGrantID helper rewrites the prefix to `sgrnt_<token_n>` using a synthetic parent Environment passed in as a throwaway — only the per-factory counter is observed. This mirrors environment_grant_repository_invariants_test.go's newEnvironmentGrantID helper and is the same idiom every grant test file uses for non-domain-known prefixes.
  - When updating internal/controlplane/domain/id.go to add a new Kind, ALWAYS add to BOTH (a) the const block + doc comment, AND (b) the canonical `kinds` map at the bottom of the file. The Valid() check and ID parser both read from the map, not the const list, so a missing map entry means NewID(KindFoo) returns ErrUnknownKind even though the constant compiles fine.
  - Codebase Patterns: NEW top-level entry — "Repository CRUD + invariants test file for a tenant-scoped leaf-grant table (a grant table with NO further-nested scope pointer below the parent FK)" (BE-0447 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/service_grant_repository_invariants_test.go). Structural shape: BE-0443 environment_grant_repository_invariants_test.go template MINUS the nullable-pointer-roundtrip leg MINUS the COALESCE-NULLS-FIRST ordering assertion MINUS the empty-string-dedup-equivalence leg. The Upsert signature drops the trailing *string argument; the ON CONFLICT branch keys on the two-tuple (organization_id, parent_id, principal_id) with no COALESCE; the ORDER BY is (principal_id ASC, id ASC). Forward-applicable to any future grant table that bottoms out at a leaf entity (a hypothetical KindDeploymentGrant or KindJobGrant would inherit this template if their parent is structurally leaf-like).

## 2026-05-18 - BE-0448 - Repository tenant isolation: service_grants
- What was implemented: BE-0448 — internal/controlplane/store/service_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go (new, 8 t.Parallel integration tests + 2 file-scope helpers) proving service_grants rows cannot cross tenant boundaries through ANY of the repository's three surfaces (ListByService / Upsert / DeleteByServiceExceptIDs). Direct application of the BE-0444 environment_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go template with the BE-0447 structural simplification: service_grants is the LEAF grant table in the Organization -> Project -> Environment -> Service hierarchy, so the row body carries NO further-nested scope pointer (no ServiceID *string — the service IS the scope), the UNIQUE conflict target is the clean three-tuple `(organization_id, service_id, principal_id)` with NO COALESCE leg, and the bystander byte-identity check uses direct string equality on ServiceID (the package-level stringPtrEqual/fmtStringPtr helpers from project_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go are not needed and are explicitly NOT imported into this file).
- Tests prove: (a) ListByService is keyed strictly by BOTH organization_id AND service_id — two tenants each owning a service named "api" each get exactly their own row, never a swapped or merged response; the assertion fans out across all five anchors (id, organization_id, service_id, principal_id, role) so any single overlap surfaces; (b) ListByService against a cross-tenant service_id returns a non-nil empty slice — indistinguishable from ListByService against an unknown service_id under the caller's own organization, so the cross-tenant probe is not a "does this service exist?" oracle; (c) ListByService with a shared principal_id (`usr_shared`) across tenants returns each tenant's own row exactly once with non-overlapping grant ids — proves the WHERE filter is keyed on organization_id, not on principal_id alone; (d) Upsert INSERT on orgA does not touch orgB's bystander grant whose `(service_id_in_its_own_tenant, principal_id)` pair is IDENTICAL to orgA's — proves the conflict target carries organization_id, so the per-tenant uniqueness rules out cross-tenant ON CONFLICT matching; the byte-identical assertion includes Version (bumped by service_grants_bump_version on every matched UPDATE — drift surfaces a missing tenant predicate even when column writes look correct) AND UpdatedAt (refreshed by the BEFORE-UPDATE service_grants_set_updated_at trigger on every matched UPDATE); (e) Upsert UPDATE on orgA (re-upsert with a different role, fresh caller-id IGNORED, ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE fires on orgA only) does not touch orgB's bystander row that legitimately shares the same `(service_id_in_its_own_tenant, principal_id)` — and orgA's row MUST have actually changed (role mutated, version bumped from N to N+1) so a silent no-op repository cannot pass the bystander check; (f) DeleteByServiceExceptIDs with nil keepIDs (the unconditional-DELETE codepath) on orgA clears every grant of orgA's service and leaves orgB's bystander grant byte-identical to its baseline; (g) DeleteByServiceExceptIDs with non-empty keepIDs (the `id NOT IN ANY` codepath) on orgA keeps exactly keepA and deletes dropA, while orgB's bystander grant — whose id is deliberately NOT in keepIDs — survives byte-identical (this is the load-bearing leg: a regression that dropped the tenant predicate would let the "NOT IN" filter eat orgB's row); (h) Upsert with the SAME `(principal_id, role)` on TWO tenants' OWN services BOTH succeed and produce two distinct rows with distinct ids — pins the per-tenant UNIQUE-index property and confirms the WHERE-on-organization_id-leg is the only thing keeping the rows apart (the flip side of every bystander test above).
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/store/service_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go (new, ~500 lines, ~12 KB)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0448 passes=true + notes)
- Verification:
  - gofmt -w / gofmt -l: clean

  - go build ./...: clean
  - go test -count=1 ./... (without YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL): all packages PASS — integration tests skip cleanly when env var is unset (the contract every prior store-package story relies on for local-dev verification)

The next priority-1 story is BE-0449 (Repository: variables CRUD and invariants) which will land the first CRUD+invariants file for the variables table — a richer surface than grants (per-row is_secret flag, secret-bearing value column, scope-pointer surface possibly spanning org/project/environment depending on the row, soft-delete column where applicable), so the template diverges from the grant family and follows whichever variable repository / migration already lives in the codebase.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The "leaf-grant tenant-isolation" template (BE-0448) collapses cleanly out of the BE-0444 env_grant template by SUBTRACTION: every leg that exercised the nullable *string scope pointer drops out. The TestUpsertSameScopeTupleInTwoTenantsBothSucceed test drops the `svcID := "svc_web"` fixture variable and the `&svcID` argument, and the corresponding assertion drops the dereferenced pointer comparison `*grantA.ServiceID == svcID`. The assertServiceGrantByteIdentical helper drops the stringPtrEqual branch and uses `after.ServiceID != baseline.ServiceID` directly. Forward-applicable to any future grant table whose parent IS the leaf of the hierarchy.
  - Local-dev Postgres connectivity workaround for the documented "container has no published port" gotcha: spin up an alpine/socat sidecar on the SAME docker network and publish a host port forwarding to `yalla-postgres-1:5432`. One-liner: `NET=$(docker inspect yalla-postgres-1 -f '{{range $k,$v := .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{$k}}{{end}}'); docker run -d --rm --name yalla-pg-forward --network "$NET" -p 15432:15432 alpine/socat tcp-listen:15432,fork,reuseaddr tcp:yalla-postgres-1:5432`. Then `YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://yalla:yalla@127.0.0.1:15432/yalla?sslmode=disable go test ...`. Drop the sidecar with `docker rm -f yalla-pg-forward`. This unblocks running integration tests locally in dev envs where macOS-to-docker-bridge-network direct IP routing is blocked (the 75-second `connect: operation timed out` symptom on `docker inspect`-discovered IPs). CI still runs against its own isolated migrated DB and does not need the sidecar.
  - The bystander byte-identity assertion's two trigger-anchored columns (Version and UpdatedAt) are the load-bearing leak channel for grant tables — direct column writes can look correct on a no-op or partial-tenant-leak path, but the BEFORE-UPDATE trigger ALWAYS refreshes updated_at and the bump trigger ALWAYS increments version on EVERY matched UPDATE, so either drifting on the bystander surface is independently sufficient to surface a missing tenant predicate. Asserting BOTH against the baseline (not just one) catches the case where a regression migrates one trigger but not the other.
  - Naming: every *_tenant_isolation_test.go file under internal/controlplane/store/ shares the same `store_test` package, so file-scope helpers (`getServiceGrantFromListOrFail`, `assertServiceGrantByteIdentical`) MUST have unique names across the directory. Before adding a helper, grep `^func ` across siblings in the dir to prevent a same-package collision. The shared `stringPtrEqual` / `fmtStringPtr` helpers from project_grant_tenant_isolation_test.go are package-visible by design — if a future tenant-isolation test needs them, reuse verbatim; do not redeclare.

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - "Database table: <name>" in PRD notes can refer to a multi-table resource
    family (variables = 4 scope tables; quota = quota_policies / quota_usage /
    quota_reservations). When in doubt, mirror the BE-0443/BE-0445/BE-0447
    template across each physical table in the family rather than collapsing
    into one file — every *_test.go under internal/controlplane/store/ shares
    the same store_test package, so cross-scope helpers (newXxxID, upsertXxx,
    listXxxOrFail, xxxTxRollbackSentinel) MUST get distinct names per scope to
    avoid same-package collisions.

    FK / CASCADE / bump_version / set_updated_at invariants — the BE-0447
    service_grant_repository_invariants_test.go template extends almost 1:1
    to a variables repository, with three substitutions: (a) Value /
    IsSecret / secret-tuple takes the place of role + principal_kind on the
    Upsert struct; (b) the secret-columns-consistent CHECK adds a brand-new
    CHECK-violation test (IsSecret=true with non-empty Value triggers the
    branch); (c) organization_variables additionally exposes UpdateMutable +
    DeleteByKey (no other scope has them), so the org file is roughly twice
    the size of the others.
  - The factory id helper pattern (rewrite the prefix of f.Organization /
    f.Project / f.Environment / f.Service so the per-test counter mints a
    unique non-canonical id like "ovar_<token_n>" / "pvar_<token_n>" /
    "evar_<token_n>" / "svar_<token_n>") is the standard way to synthesize
    repository-test ids without relying on domain.NewID — it survives a
    factory refactor and never collides with the parent resource's own id
    namespace.
  - The Postgres now() clock advances at microsecond resolution, so a "set
    updated_at refreshed" assertion that uses time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
    between baseline and override is the canonical pattern (matches the
    BE-0443 / BE-0447 templates verbatim). Without the sleep, the Equal-by-
    accident path can mask a regression that fails to refresh updated_at.
  - Tx rollback proofs must reduce to a Read-surface assertion (ListByXxx)
    rather than a per-id Get, because the variable repositories' only public
    read surface for un-keyed observation is the list endpoint — the same
    structural constraint that applies to the grant repositories. Sentinel
    error types MUST be locally defined and uniquely named per file to avoid
    same-package collisions across the store_test files.

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The "per-scope tenant-isolation test file per physical table in
    the hierarchy" pattern (this story) MIRRORS the BE-0449 per-scope
    invariants split. When the family is hierarchical with diverging
    mutation surfaces (organization variant has GetByKey / DeleteByKey
    / UpdateMutable that the other three lack), ship one
    *_tenant_isolation_test.go per physical table. The organization-
    scope file is the largest because it has additional per-key
    surfaces to anchor; the project/environment/service files
    converge on a uniform 8-test shape (ListByX-correct,
    ListByX-cross-tenant-empty, ListByX-shared-key, Upsert-INSERT-
    bystander, Upsert-UPDATE-bystander, DeleteByXExceptKeys-clear-
    all-bystander, DeleteByXExceptKeys-keep-subset-bystander,
    Upsert-same-key-both-succeed).
  - The variables family adds a NEW projection leg the grant family
    did not have: secret-bearing columns. The byte-identical-
    bystander projection MUST include Value AND the
    (SecretProvider, SecretKeyID, SecretCiphertext) tuple, plus the
    IsSecret flag. The cross-tenant error-surface no-echo invariant
    becomes load-bearing on the organization-scope per-key methods
    (GetByKey / DeleteByKey / UpdateMutable can all return errors
    whose message / hint could echo a peer tenant's value).
  - When reusing helpers from a sibling invariants file (same
    store_test package), check whether the helper signature uses a
    factory-only mint (newOrganizationVariableID(f, label)) vs. a
    factory + organization mint (newProjectVariableID(f, org, label)).
    The project-scope helper synthesises its id via f.Project(org,
    label).ID — it needs an org. The organization/environment/service
    helpers use a fake-parent or factory-counter-only scheme. Picking
    the wrong helper shape at call sites is the most common compile
    failure when porting tests across the family.
  - OrganizationVariableRepository.ListByOrganization returns a NIL
    slice for no-rows; the other three variable repositories use
    make([]T, 0). The contract should be "len == 0 on no-rows"
    (not "non-nil"). Asserting non-nil on the org-scope file
    causes a deterministic test failure — the existing
    TestOrganizationVariableReaderReturnsEmptyForUnknownOrg in
    organization_variable_test.go correctly only checks len.
  - bytes.Equal (stdlib) is fine for SecretCiphertext byte compare;
    no custom helper is needed.
  - Use stderrors.As + yerr.From for typed-code assertions on
    repository errors. apierr.NotFound returns *yerr.Error with
    Code == yerr.CodeNotFound. The pattern is consistent across the
    package and lets future tests assert ye.Code without dragging
    apierr.Is helpers into the test surface.
  - For per-tenant per-key UNIQUE constraints (organization_id,
    [parent_id,] key), the "same key in two tenants both succeed"
    test is structurally necessary to anchor that the conflict
    target IS per-tenant — without it, a regression that resolved
    the conflict on (parent_id, key) alone would still pass every
    bystander test (because the bystander would have been INSERTed
    successfully first, and the peer Upsert would simply hit the
    PK uniqueness check or hit no conflict at all). The
    same-key-both-succeed test is the positive-direction proof
    that pairs with the bystander byte-identical proofs.

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - **Repository-level invariants for an EXISTING table whose CRUD surface is already partially covered (BE-0451 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/quota_policy_repository_invariants_test.go)**: quota_policies is NOT a "first story for this table" — migration 0006 already exists, UpsertOrganizationPolicy / EffectiveLimit / ListEffectiveLimits / ListOrganizationUsage already exist in store/quota.go, and internal/controlplane/store/quota_repository_test.go already owns EffectiveLimit's read semantics + reservation flows. The story's "Repository: <table> CRUD and invariants" line therefore reduces to "fill the invariants gap": pin what the existing test file does NOT cover (row-shape of an Upsert INSERT vs UPDATE, byte-equal preservation of id/created_at across UPDATE, sibling-row non-interference for plan defaults, FK/CHECK/DOMAIN -> Conflict mapping, every enum constant round-trips, ListEffectiveLimits tenant + plan isolation, Store.Write closure rollback, nil-tx -> Internal). Before writing anything, grep for `func Test<RepositoryName><MethodName>` to enumerate what is already pinned, and write tests with NEW names that only address the gap. Reuse the test names verbatim only when intentionally re-shaping coverage; never write a same-named test in another file (vet's "redeclared in this block" fires at package store_test).
  - **EnforcementMode DOMAIN validation lives in the database**, not the Go layer: UpsertOrganizationPolicy passes `string(mode)` straight into the INSERT, and the quota_enforcement_mode DOMAIN ('hard', 'soft', 'metered', 'disabled') rejects anything else at SQLSTATE class 23 — which mapWriteError surfaces as apierr.Conflict. Same for negative limit_value (CHECK). Same for unknown organization_id (FK). So three distinct invariant violations all surface as the SAME error code (Conflict) — the test pins each one separately so a regression that bypasses one CHECK while still erroring out on another is still caught.
  - **quota_policies has no version column**, unlike projects/environments/services/variables. The acceptance-criterion clause "optimistic versioning where applicable" is therefore N/A — there is no If-Match path to test. Don't invent one; document the absence in the file's package-doc comment so a future reader does not look for a missing test (mirrors the BE-0427/BE-0428 user-table convention).
  - **Direct DB SELECT for row-shape probes** is the right tool when the repository's public reader projections (EffectiveLimit, ListEffectiveLimits) deliberately omit id/created_at/updated_at/scope_kind/plan: an UPDATE-branch identity-preservation test needs to observe those columns, so the test issues `SELECT id, scope_kind, plan, organization_id, resource, limit_value, enforcement_mode, created_at, updated_at FROM quota_policies WHERE scope_kind='organization' AND organization_id=$1 AND resource=$2`. Wrap the load in a typed rawQuotaPolicyRow struct + a `load<Scope>PolicyRow` helper so the call sites read like the persisted-row assertions the variables invariants tests use, without the helper leaking out of the test file.
  - **ListEffectiveLimits plan isolation** is a distinct invariant from tenant isolation: even within one organization, a plan_default row keyed by plan='pro' must not appear when the caller passes plan='starter'. The single SQL statement's WHERE clause anchors this (`scope_kind='plan_default' AND plan=$2`), but a future regression that drops the plan predicate (e.g., during a "search across all plans" refactor) would slip past a pure tenant-isolation test. The BE-0451 file therefore probes both: a separate orgB test for tenant scoping AND an inlined 'pro' plan default in the deterministic-order test to prove plan scoping. The 'pro' row is asserted absent by row count + per-row resource equality; no extra fixture cost since both probes share the same setup.

## 2026-05-18 - BE-0452
- Implemented: internal/controlplane/store/quota_policy_tenant_isolation_test.go — repository-layer tenant-isolation tests for the quota_policies table. quota_policies is a dual-scope table (plan_default OR organization) whose ONLY mutation surface is UpsertOrganizationPolicy and whose row body is only observable through the typed resolvers (EffectiveLimit / ListEffectiveLimits / ListOrganizationUsage). No per-id Get / Update / Delete surface exists, so the cross-tenant guarantee at this layer is exhaustively the projection invariant on every resolver leg AND the byte-identical-bystander invariant on the upsert. Coverage (9 tests): (1) EffectiveLimit per-resource is tenant-scoped — orgB's override does not appear when orgA queries the same resource; (2) ListEffectiveLimits rendered count is local to the queried tenant (orgA=1, orgB=3) — no count cross; (3) shared-resource isolation (both tenants override `projects` with distinct limit/mode — each sees its OWN); (4) plan isolation (orgA on 'starter' must not see 'pro' plan defaults); (5) ListOrganizationUsage is tenant scoped at BOTH the policies CTE and the usage CTE; (6) shared-counter isolation (both tenants have a quota_usage counter for the same resource with distinct used_value); (7) Upsert INSERT branch on orgA leaves orgB's bystander row byte-identical (the SAME resource on both tenants — the ON CONFLICT predicate is exercised); (8) Upsert UPDATE branch on orgA leaves orgB's bystander row byte-identical (both tenants pre-seeded with an override on the SAME resource — the maximally adversarial fixture for the partial-unique-index ON CONFLICT target); (9) same-resource upserts in two tenants both succeed (positive-direction pair for the bystander proofs — proves the partial unique index is per-tenant, not global).

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - **Repository tenant-isolation tests for a DUAL-SCOPE table whose ONLY mutation surface is an INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE upsert and whose row body is observable EXCLUSIVELY through typed resolvers (no per-id Get/Update/Delete, no traditional ListBy<parent>)** (BE-0452 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/quota_policy_tenant_isolation_test.go). quota_policies is structurally distinct from every prior tenant-isolation template: it has TWO scope_kind values (plan_default with NULL organization_id, and organization with non-NULL), partial unique indexes per scope (`quota_policies_org_resource_idx (organization_id, resource) WHERE scope_kind='organization'`), and NO version column. The byte-identical-bystander anchor therefore reduces to updated_at ALONE (no trigger-bumped version to anchor on), so the trigger-managed updated_at is the SOLE load-bearing column that surfaces a wrong-row UPDATE even when column writes look correct. The 9-test shape diverges from BE-0440 (project_grant) and BE-0436 (api_key_scope) in four load-bearing ways: (a) the tenant-isolation projection is observed through three resolver legs (EffectiveLimit / ListEffectiveLimits / ListOrganizationUsage), NOT through a single ListByParent — each leg has its own WHERE clause and warrants its own tenant-scoping test; (b) a NEW plan-isolation leg is added (orgA on 'starter' must not see 'pro' plan defaults, even though both rows live in the same table with NULL organization_id) — this is the tenant-isolation analogue of BE-0451's per-plan invariant; (c) the byte-identical-bystander proof is observed via a raw-SQL load of the underlying quota_policies row (loadOrganizationPolicyRow, reused from BE-0451's invariants file), because the typed reader projections deliberately omit id/created_at/updated_at/scope_kind/plan — a regression that stamped correct-looking limit_value and enforcement_mode onto orgB's row would otherwise slip past every typed-resolver projection; (d) the ListOrganizationUsage projection has TWO independent tenant predicates (one in the policies CTE on `organization_id`, one in the usage CTE on `organization_id`) — they need INDEPENDENT proofs because either dropping alone would surface a different leak (a missing policies-CTE predicate leaks peer limit_value; a missing usage-CTE predicate leaks peer used_value). Forward-applicable to any future ledger-style table whose physical realization is a dual-scope row body with two partial unique indexes (a hypothetical KindFeatureFlagDefault + KindFeatureFlagOverride pairing would inherit this template).
  - **No per-id Get surface == no (Code, Hint) existence-leak projection.** The api_key_scope and variables tenant-isolation files include a `Get-cross-tenant-is-indistinguishable-from-unknown-id` test that anchors on (apierr.NotFound.Code, apierr.NotFound.Hint) being byte-identical between a cross-tenant probe and an unknown-id probe — this protects against an existence oracle in the Hint or Message. quota_policies has NO per-id Get, no per-id Update, no Delete — the cross-tenant probe surfaces as an EMPTY projection (resolver returns ok=false, or len(rows)==0), NOT a typed error. The (Code, Hint) projection therefore has NO analogue here; documenting the deliberate absence in the file's package-doc comment keeps a future reader from looking for a missing test. The empty-slice / ok=false projection IS the existence-indistinguishability proof: a probing caller cannot tell from `EffectiveLimit returns false` whether the resource is unconfigured for this tenant or configured for another, and cannot tell from `ListEffectiveLimits returns no row for projects` whether another tenant has a `projects` override.
  - **Reuse the invariants file's helpers across files in the same package**. BE-0451 already defined `upsertOrganizationPolicy`, `loadOrganizationPolicyRow`, `effectiveLimitOrFail`, `listEffectiveLimitsOrFail`, and the `rawQuotaPolicyRow` struct in quota_policy_repository_invariants_test.go. All *_test.go files under internal/controlplane/store/ share the same store_test package, so BE-0452's tenant-isolation file inherits these symbols by package membership. The new file defines ONLY the symbols it introduces: `listOrganizationUsageOrFail`, `assertQuotaPolicyByteIdentical`, and per-file `stringPtrEqualQP` / `fmtStringPtrQP` nullable-pointer helpers with the `QP` suffix to avoid collisions with same-named helpers in sibling tenant-isolation files (BE-0440's project-grant file already defines a `stringPtrEqual` variant — naming conflict would block compilation).
  - **Shared-conflict-tuple fixture for the Upsert UPDATE bystander test**. The maximally adversarial fixture for proving the ON CONFLICT branch of an `INSERT...ON CONFLICT (organization_id, resource) WHERE scope_kind='organization' DO UPDATE` is BOTH tenants pre-seeded with an override on the SAME resource — so the ON CONFLICT target tuple matches for both rows when the WHERE predicate is stripped, and the planner's row choice (which row the UPDATE lands on without the partial index's organization_id leg) becomes observable through updated_at drift on the bystander. The fixture must be CONSTRUCTED through the same `upsertOrganizationPolicy` helper the test exercises, not through `seedOrgPolicy` raw SQL — using the repository to build the fixture proves the repository can land the second (peer) row at all without colliding with the first, AND aligns the baseline.updated_at timestamps so a wrong-row UPDATE shows up as a sub-second drift. The corollary "same-resource-in-two-tenants-both-succeed" test is the positive-direction pair: without it, a regression that resolved the conflict by (resource,) alone would have prevented the bystander INSERT from landing in the first place — and every byte-identical assertion in the UPDATE-branch test would silently pass against a non-existent row.
  - **ListOrganizationUsage has two CTE legs that each need independent tenant-scoping proof**. The policies CTE selects from quota_policies WHERE `(scope_kind='organization' AND organization_id=$1) OR (scope_kind='plan_default' AND plan=$2)`; the usage CTE selects from quota_usage WHERE `organization_id=$1`. The result is the FULL OUTER JOIN of the two. A regression that dropped the organization_id leg of EITHER CTE leaks a different column: the policies CTE leaks limit_value / enforcement_mode / Scope, the usage CTE leaks used_value. Two independent tests are warranted — one fixture isolates the policies CTE (orgA has an override, orgB has overrides on different resources, no counters on either side — surfaced through LimitValue), the other isolates the usage CTE (both tenants have a counter row on the SAME resource with DISTINCT used_value — surfaced through UsedValue). Collapsing them into one combined test would still pass against a regression that broke only one of the two CTE predicates.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Closure-of-contract test pattern for an env-scoped WRITE endpoint** (BE-0176 pattern, internal/controlplane/httpapi/environment_variables_put_contract_test.go). When BE-0175 (endpoint impl + base test) and BE-0177 (policy matrix) already exist, the BE-0176 contract test is a CLOSURE file shipping FOUR tests that the other two suites do not assert: (1) process-stdout/stderr stay empty for a served PUT, (2) the bearer credential is redacted in the structured log on both the success leg AND the disabled-principal authorization-failure leg, (3) a submitted is_secret=true value never reaches the structured log on either leg (variables-specific extra pin that the READ sibling does not need — the read endpoint has no submitted-secret surface), (4) a wrapped store-unavailable cause never leaks onto the wire including the bare datastore address. This is a structural TWIN of project_variables_put_contract_test.go (BE-0146) — same 4-test shape, same WithLogger handler helper, same constants pattern (a bearer-credential sentinel + a submitted-secret sentinel + a canonical happy-path body constant). DIFFERS from the env-scoped READ contract file (BE-0173 environment_variables_get_contract_test.go) in exactly one structural way: the WRITE file adds the fourth "submitted secret never reaches the log" test, which has no counterpart on the read sibling because the read body has no customer-submitted is_secret=true values to leak. The handler-helper signature also acquires a `replacer` (EnvironmentVariableReplacer) parameter where the read sibling acquires a `reader` (EnvironmentVariableReader).
  - **Same-tenant disabled principal as the authorization-failure-leg fixture for redaction tests on a WRITE endpoint** (BE-0176 / BE-0146 pattern). The deny-leg actor MUST be a same-tenant principal (the read-sibling's RoleViewer doesn't work as cleanly because viewer is denied by role not by disabled flag; a disabled developer principal hits the policy denial in a single short-circuit that's not role-matrix specific). `denied.Principal.Disabled = true` is the cleanest way to force a 403 without depending on the policy matrix tests' role choices. The deny-leg replacer is `fakeEnvironmentVariableReplacer{err: stderrors.New("replacer must not be called")}` — proves the deny path short-circuits at policy AND proves any logged "replacer error" cannot be the leak source (so if either sentinel string appears in the log on the deny leg, the regression is in the redaction surface, NOT in the deny-path short-circuit).
  - **Two-secret-sentinel pattern for WRITE-endpoint contract tests** (BE-0176 / BE-0146 pattern). Constants `replace<Scope>VariablesContractSecret` (bearer credential) and `replace<Scope>VariablesContractSubmittedSecret` (submitted value in the body) MUST have distinct, recognisable suffixes — substring match in the log buffer is decisive, and a regression that swaps the two surfaces fails loudly. Suffixes used across the contract families so far: BE-0173 listEnvironmentVariablesContractSecret `...DEADBEEF0123456789`, BE-0176 replaceEnvironmentVariablesContractSecret `...FEEDFACE0123456789` + replaceEnvironmentVariablesContractSubmittedSecret `...CAFEBABE`, BE-0146 replaceProjectVariablesContractSecret `...BAADF00D0123456789` + replaceProjectVariablesContractSubmittedSecret `...C0FFEE`. Keep each new contract file's sentinel suffix distinct so a "wrong sentinel" leak across files is caught.

## 2026-05-18 - BE-0453
- Implemented: internal/controlplane/store/quota_usage_repository_invariants_test.go — repository-layer CRUD-and-lifecycle invariants for the quota_usage table. quota_usage is the per-tenant counter table; its ONLY public write surface in QuotaRepository is LockUsage, which INSERTs the counter row ON CONFLICT (organization_id, resource) DO NOTHING and then SELECTs FOR UPDATE. There is no per-row Update/Delete method, no version column, and no service_id pointer — the increment path is owned by quota.Checker and the delete-cascade is owned by schema CASCADE. The 9-test file pins what neither quota_repository_test.go (the original LockUsage happy-path test) nor the schema/tenant-isolation siblings already cover: (1) row-shape on the INSERT leg — qusg_ prefix, used_value defaults to 0, created_at/updated_at within 1s; (2) second-call byte-identity — id, created_at, updated_at, AND used_value all anchored across ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (the set_updated_at trigger fires BEFORE UPDATE only; a non-UPDATE must not stamp updated_at — proved with a measurable wallclock gap between calls); (3) peer-row byte-identity — LockUsage(org, services) does not touch the (org, projects) counter row's id/created_at/updated_at/used_value, and the two rows have distinct ids; (4) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING discards the minted qusg_ id when the row exists — proved by pre-seeding a row at used_value=17 with id `qu_seed_projects` and observing both the live used_value and the original id survive a LockUsage call; (5) FK violation (unknown organization) -> typed Conflict via mapWriteError; (6) DOMAIN violation by casting `"not-a-resource"` to store.QuotaResource -> typed Conflict; (7) transaction rollback — closure returns sentinel after a successful LockUsage, Write rolls back, no quota_usage row persists (counter probe = 0); (8) nil-tx -> yerr.CodeInternal. The 9th test is the pre-existing TestQuotaRepositoryLockUsageCreatesAndReturnsCounter that the file does NOT duplicate — it lives in quota_repository_test.go and remains the load-bearing two-call-idempotency probe.

  - **Repository-layer CRUD-and-lifecycle invariants test file for a TENANT-SCOPED COUNTER table whose ONLY mutation surface is an INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + SELECT...FOR UPDATE primitive (LockUsage), with NO per-row Update/Delete, NO version column, NO service_id pointer, and a database-managed used_value mutated by an external code path (quota.Checker), set_updated_at trigger fires BEFORE UPDATE only** (BE-0453 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/quota_usage_repository_invariants_test.go). Structurally distinct from BE-0451 (quota_policies — single-table INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE upsert) in four load-bearing ways: (a) the second-call byte-identity proof must anchor updated_at TOO, because ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is not an UPDATE and the set_updated_at trigger must not fire — quota_policies's UPDATE leg actively REFRESHES updated_at via the trigger, so its byte-identity proof EXCLUDES updated_at; quota_usage's byte-identity proof INCLUDES updated_at as a load-bearing anchor (a regression that switched to ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE with even a no-op SET would silently bump updated_at and a missing anchor would let that slip past); (b) the peer-row proof for quota_usage is a SAME-TENANT-DIFFERENT-RESOURCE check (the UNIQUE (organization_id, resource) constraint isolates rows by resource within a tenant), distinct from quota_policies's cross-scope peer (plan_default vs organization within the SAME quota_policies table); (c) the "row already exists with non-zero value" leg has no quota_policies analog — for quota_usage we pre-seed a row at used_value=17 via direct SQL (seedQuotaUsage from usage_test.go) and prove BOTH the seeded id `qu_seed_projects` AND the seeded used_value survive the LockUsage call, which is the only way to prove the discarded INSERT's minted qusg_ id does not replace the row's id (a regression that switched to ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE SET id=EXCLUDED.id would replace the row's id and reset used_value to 0 — a catastrophic data-loss path the typed reader projections would not catch); (d) the DOMAIN-violation test casts an arbitrary string to store.QuotaResource — `store.QuotaResource("not-a-resource")` — to bypass Go's compile-time check on the typed string and exercise the DOMAIN quota_resource CHECK at the database layer; this is the same casting pattern quota_policies uses for unknown enforcement_mode (`store.EnforcementMode("not-a-mode")`).
  - Test-helper symbols added in this file (all *_test.go files under internal/controlplane/store/ share the same store_test package, so duplicate top-level symbols collide at compile time): `lockUsageOrFail`, `loadQuotaUsageRow`, `countQuotaUsageRowsForOrg`, `rawQuotaUsageRow`, `quotaUsageTxRollbackSentinel`. Reused symbols from sibling files: `seedOrg` (schema_test.go), `seedQuotaUsage` (usage_test.go), `newStore` (store_test.go). The seedQuotaUsage helper is the ONLY way to set used_value to a non-zero value through a test fixture — the repository surface has no equivalent because LockUsage cannot increment.
  - Sentinel-name caveat for store_test: the existing rollback-sentinel list now includes quotaPolicyTxRollbackSentinel, projectTxRollbackSentinel, environmentTxRollbackSentinel, serviceTxRollbackSentinel, membershipTxRollbackSentinel, apiKeyTxRollbackSentinel, apiKeyScopeTxRollbackSentinel, projectVariableTxRollbackSentinel, environmentVariableTxRollbackSentinel, serviceVariableTxRollbackSentinel, environmentGrantTxRollbackSentinel — and now `quotaUsageTxRollbackSentinel`. The list-of-siblings doc-comment block on each sentinel type is the established convention; BE-0453 follows it.
  - Codebase Patterns: ADDED a new top-level pattern entry (this story's quota_usage shape is structurally distinct from BE-0451's quota_policies upsert shape; future ledger-style counter tables with the same INSERT-DO-NOTHING + SELECT-FOR-UPDATE primitive — e.g. quota_reservations is a different shape with status lifecycle, but a future per-tenant-per-resource counter would mirror this exactly — should follow BE-0453, not BE-0451).

## 2026-05-18 - BE-0454
- Implemented: internal/controlplane/store/quota_usage_tenant_isolation_test.go — repository-layer tenant-isolation tests for the quota_usage table. quota_usage's only public mutation surface is LockUsage (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (organization_id, resource) DO NOTHING + SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) and there is no per-row Update/Delete/Get; the typed read resolver ListOrganizationUsage's cross-tenant projection is already covered by quota_policy_tenant_isolation_test.go (BE-0452), so this file is additive and focused on LockUsage cross-tenant invariants + the cascade-delete tenant-isolation that TestQuotaCascadeDeleteOnOrganization (quota_schema_test.go) only proves on the deleted side. Coverage (6 tests):
  (1) TestQuotaRepositoryLockUsageInsertOnOrgADoesNotTouchOrgB — orgB owns a pre-seeded counter for the same resource at used_value=42; orgA's LockUsage on that resource lands as a fresh qusg_<token> INSERT and orgB's row is byte-identical (id, used_value, created_at, updated_at, organization_id, resource); orgA returns 0 (orgB's 42 must not leak); per-tenant row counts are 1+1.

  (4) TestQuotaRepositoryLockUsageBystanderRowsAcrossResourcesAreByteIdentical — orgB owns counters on projects/services/databases at distinct values; orgA LockUsages projects; ALL THREE of orgB's rows (the same-resource peer AND the two cross-resource peers) are byte-identical to baseline. Generalises the bystander invariant beyond the one row whose (resource) value matches orgA's call.

Without this anchor, a regression that resolved the ON CONFLICT by (resource,) alone would have prevented orgB's seed in every other test and the byte-identical assertions would silently pass against rows that never existed.
  (6) TestQuotaUsageOrganizationDeleteCascadeIsTenantScoped — orgA has 2 quota_usage rows, orgB has 3 (including one on the SAME resource as orgA); deleting orgA cascades only orgA's rows; orgB's three rows survive byte-identically (id, used_value, created_at, updated_at). Complements TestQuotaCascadeDeleteOnOrganization which proves the cascade fires for the targeted tenant; this proves it does NOT bleed into another tenant.

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - **Repository tenant-isolation tests for a TENANT-SCOPED COUNTER table whose ONLY public mutation is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (organization_id, resource) DO NOTHING + SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (LockUsage), where the row body's used_value is increment-managed BY AN EXTERNAL CODE PATH (quota.Checker, not the repository), with NO per-id Get/Update/Delete surface, NO version column, NO service_id pointer, and the cascade-delete tenant isolation NOT covered by the existing single-tenant cascade test** (BE-0454 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/quota_usage_tenant_isolation_test.go). Structurally distinct from BE-0452 (quota_policies, dual-scope UPSERT) in four load-bearing ways: (a) NO typed-resolver coverage is added here — ListOrganizationUsage's two-CTE-leg tenant scoping is already proved in quota_policy_tenant_isolation_test.go (BE-0452) AND in usage_test.go (TestQuotaRepositoryListOrganizationUsageTenantScoped), and re-asserting would cause same-named tests to collide at compile time across the shared store_test package; the cross-tenant id-leak surface to defend is LockUsage's INSERT/SELECT primitive, which the typed projection cannot expose (the projection omits id by construction) — so the bystander proofs use raw-SQL row loads instead; (b) the bystander invariant has TWO peer classes — same-resource and cross-resource — both anchored on the same baseline tenant in ONE test (test 4), because both classes are governed by the SAME ON CONFLICT predicate (organization_id, resource) and a regression that dropped either column would surface in both; this is structurally simpler than BE-0452's split insert/update bystander tests (quota_policies has TWO upsert branches — DO NOTHING never happens, only DO UPDATE — so insert-on-orgA-doesn't-touch-orgB and update-on-orgA-doesn't-touch-orgB are distinct probes; quota_usage's ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING means orgA's INSERT against orgB's existing row is the ONLY upsert branch worth proving and the test surface collapses to one); (c) a NEW probe is added on top of BE-0452's template: a "per-tenant row-count invariance" test (test 3) that does NOT load any row — only counts rows owned by orgA and orgB before and after — to catch a cross-tenant FK swap that the byte-identity probes would miss (the byte-identity probes only observe rows that still exist; a regression that DELETED orgB's row and INSERTED an orgA-owned replacement at the same id would pass byte-identity if id and used_value coincidentally matched, but would fail this count probe); (d) the cascade-delete tenant-isolation test (test 6) is a NEW class of probe quota_policy_tenant_isolation_test.go did NOT carry because TestQuotaCascadeDeleteOnOrganization (quota_schema_test.go) proves single-tenant cascade only — it never checks that a different tenant's rows survive. quota_usage is the right place to add this probe because the cascade fires at the schema level (FK CASCADE on quota_usage.organization_id) and is per-table; quota_policies's cascade is asymmetric (plan_default rows have NULL organization_id and survive deletes by construction, so a "different tenant's rows survive" probe there would conflate two distinct invariants — the plan-default-survives invariant from quota_schema_test.go AND the organization-bystander-survives invariant — and the asymmetry would obscure the test's purpose). For quota_usage there is no plan_default scope, so the cascade-isolation probe is unambiguous: orgB's rows survive byte-identically (id, used_value, timestamps) when orgA is deleted.
  - **Helper-name discipline for store_test (BE-0454 reminder)**: all *_test.go files under internal/controlplane/store/ share the same store_test package, so a same-named top-level symbol in two files is a compile-time collision (`vet: redeclared in this block`). The byte-identity helper for THIS story is named `assertQuotaUsageByteIdentical` to mirror BE-0452's `assertQuotaPolicyByteIdentical` while staying distinct from it. The rawQuotaUsageRow type, loadQuotaUsageRow / countQuotaUsageRowsForOrg / lockUsageOrFail / seedQuotaUsage helpers are all reused from BE-0453 / usage_test.go and must NOT be re-declared.
  - **The "positive-direction pair" anchor (test 5)** is the load-bearing complement of every bystander byte-identity proof in tenant-isolation tests, but for quota_usage it has a different mechanical purpose than for quota_policies: in BE-0452 the positive-direction pair (`SameResourceInTwoTenantsBothSucceed`) anchors the bystander proofs because the partial unique index `quota_policies_org_resource_idx (organization_id, resource) WHERE scope_kind='organization'` is partial AND keyed by both columns — so a regression to a global UNIQUE would have made BOTH the insert-bystander and the update-bystander silently pass against missing rows; in BE-0454 the equivalent positive-direction pair anchors the bystander proofs because `quota_usage_org_resource_idx (organization_id, resource)` is full (not partial — quota_usage has no scope_kind column) but is per-tenant, so the same anchor mechanic applies even though the partial-index angle drops out. Going through the repository surface on BOTH tenants — not via raw INSERTs — is the load-bearing detail: a regression that hard-coded a specific organization_id inside the LockUsage SQL itself would surface here too.

- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - The Postgres-connection-exhaustion flakes under full-suite parallel load are environmental, not caused by this change. A separate hardening story should serialise the `service_quota_*_concurrent_test.go` family or cap `-p` for the store package.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The `quota_reservations` table is the third member of the quota_* family but its public repository surface is the SMALLEST of the three: InsertReservation (active-row mint, no upsert) + SumActiveReservations (predicate-filtered sum). There is NO per-row Get / Update / Commit / Release / Expire on the repository yet -- the lifecycle landings happen in the worker-side provisioning-jobs PRD. The invariants file MUST acknowledge this in its file-doc comment so a future reader does not look for a missing Commit/Release test.
  - Migration 0008 added a composite FK `quota_reservations_job_fk` from `quota_reservations (organization_id, job_id)` to `provisioning_jobs (organization_id, id)`. The repository's `InsertReservation` does NOT pre-validate that the job exists -- it relies on the FK -- so a test that round-trips a non-empty `JobID` MUST pre-seed a real `provisioning_jobs` row (minimum required columns: `id`, `organization_id`, `job_type`, `idempotency_key`; every other column has a default) before calling `InsertReservation`. The seed can be a raw `db.Exec` -- there is no `seedProvisioningJob` test helper yet.
  - `mapWriteError` catches every constraint violation in SQLSTATE class 23 (`isConstraintViolation` checks `pgErr.Code[:2] == "23"`), so unique (23505), FK (23503), CHECK (23514), and not-null (23502) all surface as the same `apierr.Conflict`. This is why the FK-on-org / FK-on-job / DOMAIN-on-resource / CHECK-on-amount / CHECK-on-settled-consistent cases all assert the same `yerr.CodeConflict` outcome -- the test isolates them by giving each its own minimal input setup so a regression in any ONE class surfaces in a specific test.
  - `InsertReservation` can only mint ACTIVE rows by construction: its INSERT column list omits `settled_at`, so passing a non-blank, non-'active' `Status` produces an inconsistent (status<>'active' AND settled_at IS NULL) row that the `quota_reservations_settled_consistent` CHECK rejects. This is the canonical invariant for the repository's settled-state contract -- a future Commit/Release/Expire repository method that DOES write `settled_at` will need its OWN settled-state invariants test.
  - Postgres `timestamptz` storage is microsecond precision. A nanosecond-precision Go `time.Time` round-tripped through the column TRUNCATES below the microsecond. The `ExpiresAt` round-trip test uses `time.Date(..., ..., 678901000, ...)` -- 678901 microseconds, no nanoseconds finer -- to stay inside the storage contract. Anything finer (e.g. `678901234`) would force the assertion to use `WithinDuration` instead of `time.Time.Equal`.
  - `SumActiveReservations` has THREE independent exclusion predicates -- status filter, time filter (`expires_at > now`), and resource filter -- each of which is a distinct regression surface. The invariants file ships one test per predicate (excludes-non-active-statuses, excludes-expired-by-time, is-resource-scoped) because a single combined test would let a regression in any ONE predicate hide behind the others.
  - The full `go test ./internal/controlplane/store/` run is currently flaky under parallel-DB pressure due to Postgres connection-pool / database-creation rate limits (the `service_quota_*_concurrent_test.go` family creates many isolated databases and runs many parallel goroutines, occasionally hitting `E_UNAVAILABLE`). The flake reproduces at HEAD without this change. For verifying a single repository invariants story, run `go test -run '<TestFamily>' ./internal/controlplane/store/` in isolation; the full-package run is best left to CI with serialised concurrency.

- Implemented public-API contract coverage for POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/services in a new file environment_services_create_contract_test.go (BE-0182).
- Three named tests close the contract-test criteria that environment_services_create_test.go (BE-0181, base) and environment_services_create_policy_test.go (BE-0183, policy matrix) did not assert directly:
  1. TestCreateEnvironmentServiceServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter — wraps the served request in captureProcessOutput and proves os.Stdout AND os.Stderr stay empty while the 201 envelope is delivered through the http.ResponseWriter; asserts the structured-log sink is non-empty so a regression to no-logging surfaces here; not parallel because captureProcessOutput swaps the global os streams.
  2. TestCreateEnvironmentServiceRequestLogRedactsBearerToken — two parallel subtests (success path + authorization-failure path where the disabled-principal request is paired with a creator that errors if invoked, so any logged "creator error" cannot be the leak source); each asserts the recognisable bearer credential constant does not appear in the log buffer nor in the response body. Logger level = LevelDebug so a future debug-level log addition is also captured.
  3. TestCreateEnvironmentServiceErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause — pins that a creator-store outage builds a typed yalla.error.v1 envelope with code E_UNAVAILABLE whose message is generic; the wrapped driver cause string (including the bare datastore address "10.0.0.5:5432") never reaches the wire.
- Added a recognisable bearer constant createEnvironmentServiceContractSecret and a canonical body constant createEnvironmentServiceContractBody (mirrors BE-0181's happy-path body), plus a createEnvironmentServiceHandlerForWithLogger helper that injects a caller-supplied *slog.Logger into the production handler wiring (mirrors listEnvironmentServicesHandlerForWithLogger for the WRITE side).
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environment_services_create_contract_test.go (new, 3 named tests)

- Verification run:

  - go vet ./... -> clean

  - go test -count=1 ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... -> ok (1.278s)
  - go test -race -count=1 ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... -> ok (9.198s)
- Results: all checks pass.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups: none — pure contract-coverage story; no production code changed.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **Closure-of-contract test pattern for an env-scoped CREATE endpoint** (BE-0182 pattern, internal/controlplane/httpapi/environment_services_create_contract_test.go). When BE-0181 (POST impl + base test) and BE-0183 (policy matrix) already exist, the contract story is a structural twin of the READ closure tests (BE-0179, BE-0173) plus the WRITE closure test (BE-0176 PUT env variables), adapted to the CREATE shape. The three named tests below close the criteria the base + policy tests leave open and reuse all shared helpers (postEnvironmentService, decodeCreateEnvironmentService, captureProcessOutput, principalForCreateService, fakeEnvironmentServiceCreator, seedServiceWire, decodeError):
    1. ServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter (non-parallel) — captureProcessOutput stdout+stderr empty; logBuf non-empty; 201 + envelope payload check on the wire.
    2. RequestLogRedactsBearerToken (parallel; subtests not-parallel inside table) — two legs: success (201) with a happy-path fake creator, AND authorization-failure (403) with a Disabled-flagged principal + a fake creator whose Create errors if invoked. The deny-leg creator error rules out a creator-side leak source; assert the bearer constant does not appear in logBuf NOR rec.Body for both legs; logger LevelDebug.
    3. ErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause (parallel) — fake creator returns apierr.StoreUnavailable(stderrors.New("connection refused dialing 10.0.0.5:5432")); 503 envelope is "E_UNAVAILABLE" with a non-empty generic message; rec.Body never contains the cause string nor the datastore address.
  - **CREATE contract differs from PUT contract in one specific way** (BE-0182 learning vs BE-0176 PUT env variables): the CREATE request body has no is_secret=true fields (service_id, slug, display_name, kind are all non-secret), so the BE-0176 "submitted secret value must not appear in log nor be echoed in response" assertion does not apply to CREATE. The redaction surface for CREATE collapses to the bearer credential alone, which is why the contract test file is shorter than BE-0176's. Future CREATE-contract closures for endpoints whose body carries no is_secret fields should follow this BE-0182 file as the template; CREATE-contract closures whose body carries secret values (e.g., variables-create endpoints) must add the BE-0176 "submitted-secret redaction" leg on top of the three above.
  - **Handler-builder-with-logger pattern is one-per-endpoint** (BE-0182 / BE-0179 / BE-0176 pattern): even though the production NewHandler call signature is the same across endpoints, each endpoint's contract test file declares its own *HandlerForWithLogger helper that takes the endpoint-specific port (EnvironmentServiceCreator here, EnvironmentVariableReplacer for BE-0176, EnvironmentServiceReader for BE-0179). Do NOT try to extract a shared "newHandlerWithLogger" — the per-endpoint flavor keeps the test's port parameter typed and the call site readable, and the NewHandler arglist is too long to wrap usefully via a generic builder. Mirror the pattern: copy the sibling endpoint's *WithLogger helper, replace exactly one fake-port slot with the named parameter, and keep the surrounding zero-value fakes byte-identical so a future port reordering in NewHandler updates all callers in one diff.

Reading must not leak into a write.

TestDeploymentRepositoryListByServiceForeignServiceIDOfSameTenantReturnsEmpty pins this specific shape — distinct from the "foreign org_id + foreign service_id" probe in the BE-0457 invariants file.
  - rawDeploymentRow has no nullable string columns (only nullable started_at / finished_at timestamps). The per-file Dep-suffixed nullable helpers reduce to just timePtrEqualDep / fmtTimePtrDep — no stringPtrEqualDep is needed. Adding one anyway would be dead code that staticcheck/golangci-lint would flag as U1000.
  - The deployments table stores NO secret-bearing column (source_ref is a branch/commit/tag/image name; error_message is redacted by the worker before persistence). The BE-0434-style raw-secret probe and the redaction-needle-in-error probe have no analogue here — but the BE-0458 acceptance criteria still apply structurally: rendered environment variable values, tokens, API keys and cookies do not appear on this table because they live in their own scoped tables.
